articles.title: VC funding dips in September despite big deals; More voices join the lineup at TechSparks 2026
articles.text:
VC funding dips in September despite big deals; More voices join the lineup at TechSparks 2026
Venture capital funding into Indian startups saw an 8.3% year-on-year dip in September, despite four $100 million deals. However, there were some positives. Meanwhile, here's a look at the speaker lineup for TechSparks 2026.
Dear Reader,
PhysicsWallah will no longer lend to students directly.
The edtech company’s wholly-owned subsidiary FinZ Finance has agreed to sell a Rs 95.79 crore loan portfolio to Auxilo Finserve, an RBI-registered NBFC focused on education finance. This is part of PhysicsWallah’s strategic move to focus on its core business and reduce balance-sheet and credit risks associated with lending. Going forward, lending will be facilitated through regulated third-party NBFCs.
In other news, TVS Automobile Solutions has raised Rs 425 crore in a Series D round of funding led by CE-Invests, the investment arm of UAE-based Crescent Enterprises. The funding will be used to expand the company’s myTVS aftermarket brand in overseas markets, starting with MENA.
Meanwhile, ecommerce marketplace Flipkart has picked up a minority stake in global B2B travel tech startup TravClan to strengthen international holiday offerings across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel and expand access to global suppliers and destination support.
Moving on, AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal, made a weak stock market debut on Monday, with its stock listing at Rs 28.32 on the NSE and Rs 28.30 on the BSE, down 11.5% from its issue price of Rs 32. This caught some investors off guard, especially as grey market trading had earlier indicated a 3% listing gain.
In global news, OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman has said we must accept some of the risks associated with AI for the greater good. The benefits outweigh the risks, he argued.
“We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency," Altman said in an interview with Politico's tech-centric newsletter Decoded.
In today’s newsletter:
- VC funding dips in September despite big deals
- More voices join the lineup at TechSparks 2026
Here’s your trivia for today: What did the letter ‘Q’ originally stand for in NASDAQ? (Scroll down for the answer)
Funding
VC inflow dips again, but there are some positives
Venture capital funding into Indian startups saw an 8.3% year-on-year dip in September, despite four $100 million deals. However, VC funding rose 15.5% compared to August, revealing the divergent trends in capital inflow into the startup ecosystem.
The total VC funding for September this year was $1.139 billion, compared to $1.242 billion in the same month last year, according to YourStory Research. The VC funding in August 2026 was $986 million.
Key takeaways
- There were some positives in September. The month marked the third time that VC funding crossed $1 billion this year. Also, four deals crossed the $100 million mark.
- The fintech segment raised the highest amount of funding in September at $251 million followed by electric vehicles at $222 million.
- Current trends indicate that 2026 may show a marginal improvement over 2025 in terms of overall funding. However, it will be challenging given that the last three months of the year are generally a period of slower activity.
TechSparks
More voices join the lineup at TechSparks 2026
At TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s flagship startup and technology summit, founders, investors, technology leaders, and policymakers will come together to discuss and deliberate on ‘The New Tech Order’.
The three-day summit will take place in Bengaluru from October 13 to 15. Karnataka ministers Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, IT, BT & E-Governance, and Krishna Byre Gowda, Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development, will join the conversations, alongside Pratyaya Amrit, Chief Secretary, Government of Bihar, and others.
Key takeaways
- With founders, investors, technology leaders and policymakers coming together, TechSparks 2026 will look at how technology is changing businesses, industries and the wider ecosystem.
- Here are some of the speakers joining TechSparks 2026: Ananth Narayanan, Founder and CEO of BRND.ME; Mohit Bhatnagar is Managing Director at Peak XV; Kalavathi G V is Executive Director and Head of the Global Development Center at Siemens Healthineers; and Rahul Chari is Founder and CPTO at PhonePe.
- The TechSparks 2026 lineup also features Nupur Goenka, Executive Director, Tally Solutions; Ankit Bagaria, Co-founder and CEO, Loopworm; Vikas Brahmavar, Founder and Director, Boson Whitewater; Chetan Maini, Chairman and Co-founder, SUN Mobility; Angad Daryani, Founder and CEO, Praan; Nikhil Rajpal, Founder, Qubo; Akshay Shekhar, CEO and Co-founder, Kazam; and Sharat Chandra, Founder, EmpowerEdge Ventures.
News & updates
- Debt financing: Quantum computing and artificial intelligence company QpiAI has secured Rs 50 crore in debt financing from InnoVen Capital India Fund II, with the Bengaluru startup allotting 5,000 Series B non-convertible debentures to the fund, per RoC filings.
- Rights issue: Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal has backed the company’s upcoming Rs 1,000 crore rights issue, pledging a 4.32% stake in the EV maker to fund his participation. This comes days after Ola Electric’s board okayed the plan to raise fresh capital through partly paid-up shares and appointed Deepa Bansal as its new compliance chief to boost governance.
- Beating forecasts: Taiwan’s Foxconn, the world's largest contract electronics maker, has reported a 47% jump in third-quarter revenue year-on-year that beat market estimates, fuelled by strong AI-related demand.

articles.title: Akasa Announces Euler MX2 Fanless Mini-ITX Case
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
Akasa Announces Euler MX2 Fanless Mini-ITX Case
Akasa, a leading provider of thermal solutions, introduced the Euler MX2, a premium aluminium fanless case for Mini-ITX motherboards. It supports Intel LGA1851, LGA1700, LGA1200 and LGA115X socket-based processors up to 35 W TDP and pairs an integrated 220 W DC-to-DC power converter with two internal 2.5" SATA drive bays. The Euler MX2 suits commercial systems that run unattended, such as industrial automation, point-of-sale (POS) and kiosks, surveillance, digital signage, and long-life edge computing.
Akasa's patented spring-loaded mounting system gives the Euler MX2 wide compatibility with Mini-ITX form factor motherboards and consistent, stable thermal contact across the supported socket range. The case supports Intel Core (8th-14th Gen) and Core Ultra (15th Gen) processors up to 35 W TDP. Its fully passive aluminium chassis dissipates heat from the CPU through the external fins. With no fans, the system minimizes noise and mechanical points of failure.Two internal bays support 2.5" SATA SSDs or HDDs up to 9.5 mm in height, giving system integrators storage capacity built into the case. For installations where a smaller footprint matters more than 2.5" storage, the 4.0L Euler CMX supports the same sockets and processors up to 35 W TDP, with onboard M.2 storage only.The internal 220 W DC-to-DC converter runs from a 12 V DC input via a 4-pin DIN connector and delivers +3.3 V, +5 V, +5 V standby, +12 V and -12 V rails. It has built-in over-voltage and over-power protection and is rated for operation from -25°C to 70°C. 24-pin and 4+4-pin ATX power cables are included for standard motherboard connection. An optional 150 W, 12 V external adapter is available for complete system builds (product code: AK-PD150-02K).For a clutter-free setup, the chassis supports VESA mounting, allowing direct installation to compatible displays or mounting arms.The front panel features two USB 3.2 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) Type-A ports, power and HDD LED indicators and a power button. The rear panel has an opening for the motherboard's rear I/O, two serial port openings, antenna fitting holes, a Kensington lock hole and the 4-pin DIN power port. Optional antennas (A-ATN01-BK) and pigtails (A-ATC01-150GR) are available for Wi-Fi connectivity.
Optional bespoke engraving and coloring are available to brand and differentiate system builds, subject to a minimum order quantity. To discuss customization, project details or OEM services, contact the Akasa team.
Applications
The Euler MX2 suits applications where silent operation and high mean time between failures (MTBF) matter:
- Industrial automation
- POS terminals and surveillance systems
- Digital signage and kiosk systems
- Edge computing and long-life deployment
Pricing and Availability

articles.title: OpenAI anuncia marca-d’água invisível para textos do ChatGPT • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
OpenAI anuncia marca-d’água invisível para textos do ChatGPT
Tecnologia textGrainm começará a funcionar no ChatGPT e Codex da União Europeia nesta fase inicial.
A OpenAI anunciou a implementação do textGrain no ChatGPT e no Codex. Trata-se de uma tecnologia de marca d’água invisível para textos que ajuda a identificar quando esse tipo de conteúdo é gerado por IA. Por ora, a novidade é restrita à União Europeia.
Essa não é uma tecnologia necessariamente nova. A OpenAI havia anunciado o desenvolvimento de um método de marca d’água em 2024, mas, desde então, nunca o adotou em larga escala para textos.
Nesse sentido, talvez o textGrain pudesse levar mais tempo para ser implementado. A OpenAI só o anunciou agora para se adequar à Lei de Inteligência Artificial da União Europeia (EU AI Act).
O regulamento europeu determina que organizações que oferecem serviços de IA generativa de qualquer formato (texto, imagem, áudio ou vídeo) implementem mecanismos que permitam que esse tipo de conteúdo seja marcado de modo a ser identificado como sintético por ferramentas de verificação.
Já existe um recurso do tipo para conteúdo de mídia no ChatGPT. Faltava a implementação para textos, que começa a chegar agora. Contudo, a marca d’água invisível em si não é obrigatória. Trata-se apenas do método que a OpenAI escolheu para se adequar à legislação europeia.
A própria OpenAI descreve o textGrain como um “sinal estatístico invisível”. Isso significa que o conteúdo resultante não recebe um caractere invisível ou espaços adicionais, por exemplo, mas ajustes sutis que alteram estatisticamente como o modelo de IA escolhe palavras para inserir no texto. Ainda de acordo com a OpenAI, isso é feito sem prejudicar a qualidade do resultado.
Nas próximas semanas, a tecnologia será implementada como padrão nos textos gerados pelo ChatGPT e o Codex em todos os planos de usuários baseados na União Europeia.
Um detalhe interessante é que, apesar da limitação regional da atual fase, desenvolvedores de qualquer parte do mundo que usam a API da OpenAI poderão ativar a marca d’água em determinados modelos para uso em suas aplicações.
Mas a própria OpenAI alerta que há limitações: a marca d’água pode ser “enfraquecida” com edições ou determinados tipos de texto, bem como pode não permitir uma detecção precisa em conteúdos curtos.
A organização também deixa claro que o textGrain não identifica o usuário que solicitou o texto, não pode validar se o resultado é verdadeiro ou equivocado, e não mede a proporção de trabalho humano em um conteúdo editado.

articles.title: « Il faut pénaliser celui qui consomme le flux pirate » : les clients d’IPTV illégales bientôt sanctionnés en France ?
articles.text:
Depuis le 5 août dernier, la loi n° 2026-725 est entrée en vigueur. Celle-ci est relative au sport professionnel et renforce la lutte contre les fournisseurs de flux IPTV et de streaming illégaux, mais aussi contre les moyens techniques permettant d’y accéder ou de contourner les mesures de blocage, notamment les VPN, les moteurs de recherche et les DNS alternatifs. Son mécanisme repose sur un blocage automatique et en direct des flux pirates.
Les sanctions peuvent monter jusqu’à 3 ans de prison et 300 000 € d’amende pour les personnes qui diffusent illégalement des compétitions. S’il est question d’une organisation, les sanctions peuvent même monter jusqu’à 7 ans d’emprisonnement et 750 000 € d’amende. Ceux qui font simplement la promotion de ce type de service risquent quant à eux 1 an de prison et 15 000 € d’amende. Quid des clients de ces services illégaux ? Certains veulent dorénavant les cibler.
Les appels à cibler les clients d’IPTV illégales se multiplient
Comme le rapporte L’équipe, Olivier Bramly, directeur général de LFP Media (une filiale commerciale de la Ligue de Football Professionnel), estime que la loi du 5 août ne va pas assez loin, puisqu’elle ne vise pas directement les clients des services IPTV illégaux et les consommateurs de flux en streaming illégaux. Il explique : « Il est trop peu compris dans l’opinion publique que l’usage d’une IPTV est illégal. À la fin des fins, il faut aller pénaliser celui qui consomme le flux pirate ; son acte ne peut pas rester sans conséquences ». Selon lui, les clients d’une IPTV illégale devraient être également pénalisés afin de faire prendre conscience à ceux-ci qu’il est question d’un service pirate.
Martin Ajdari, le président de l’Arcom, milite aussi pour cibler les clients des IPTV illégales, mais parle davantage de sensibilisation : « Il est important que les utilisateurs individuels soient sensibilisés sur la valeur des droits et le fait qu’Internet n’est pas un vaste magasin où tout est gratuit. Mais en même temps, il faut les responsabiliser, le cas échéant, en leur montrant que leur action n’est ni passée inaperçue, ni sans conséquences ». Il reste à savoir ce qu’il entend par des actions qui ne seraient pas « sans conséquences ».
Les clients d’IPTV illégales restent peu inquiétés, mais pour combien de temps encore ?
Les fournisseurs d’IPTV illégales sont bel et bien dans le viseur de la justice. Un couple du Vaucluse a par exemple été condamné à verser plus de 300 000 euros de dommages et intérêts à Canal+ pour avoir vendu plus de 8 000 abonnements IPTV illégaux. Un Britannique a, quant à lui, été condamné à 6 ans et demi de prison pour avoir généré près d’un million de livres grâce à un service IPTV illégal. Bref, les exemples ne manquent pas.
En revanche, les clients d’IPTV illégales restent pour l’instant peu inquiétés. Il serait faux de dire qu’ils le sont totalement : une vingtaine d’utilisateurs d’un service d’IPTV illicite ont par exemple été condamnés en France des amendes allant de 300 à 400 euros, mais les efforts de la justice se concentrent avant tout sur les fournisseurs. Pour l’instant, les condamnations de clients restent donc rares et ponctuelles.
Mais pour combien de temps encore ? Les appels au durcissement de la loi, comme celui d’Olivier Bramly, se sont multipliés ces derniers mois. Et si des dizaines de flux IPTV illégaux ont été fermés, des remplaçants arrivent en un rien de temps. En fin de compte, s’attaquer aux clients pourrait être l’arme ultime des ayants droit pour lutter contre ce type de service illégal.

articles.title: Robotics startup RobCo valued at $1B+ in $40M funding round - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Robotics startup RobCo valued at $1B+ in $40M funding round
Industrial automation startup RobCo Inc. today announced that it has closed a $40 million funding round.
Most of the shares that changed hands were sold by current and former employees. The investor consortium that bought the equity included Sequoia, Lightspeed and several other startup funds. RobCo is now valued at more than $1 billion, double what it was worth in January.
Germany-based RobCo sells more than a dozen robots designed to automate logistics and manufacturing tasks. Most of the machines are industrial arms. The largest, XL, can pick up 88 pounds and move payloads more than eight feet. It’s optimized for metalworking tasks.
RobCo’s lower-end robotic arms offer a different mix of features. Some have a complex set of joints that enables them to maneuver around obstacles, while others are optimized to pick up heavy items. RobCo’s simplest machine is a single-joint robotic arm designed to hold a camera above conveyor belts for quality inspection purposes.
The company’s flagship system is a two-armed, mobile robot called Alfie. It’s capable of automating tasks that can’t be performed by a traditional robotic arm. For example, an automaker could configure Alfie to stabilize a car part with one arm and use the other to apply paint.
The items that an industrial robot processes change on a regular basis. For example, a piece of merchandise might arrive in a larger box than usual or the number of components on a conveyor belt might suddenly increase. Historically, such changes required companies to update their industrial robots’ software. That slowed down production and increased operating costs.
RobCo says Alfie can adapt to changes without manual code updates. That versatility is made possible by an artificial intelligence engine called RobVision.
Customers can activate RobVision by uploading a photo of the item they plan to process with Alfie. The software creates synthetic, or AI-generated, variations of the photo and uses them to train a custom AI model. Once the model is installed on an Alfie robot, it automatically adapts to production line changes.
Companies can customize the behavior of RobCo’s machines using a development tool called RobFlow. It provides pre-programmed robot commands that each correspond to a specific motion, a pause or some other action. RobFlow enables users to mix and match those commands into multistep workflows without writing any code.
The third component of RobCo’s software stack, RobCo Studio, can be used to optimize a robot’s hardware configuration. It also eases related tasks such as scheduling maintenance work.
Today’s investment will help RobCo grow its U.S. presence. The company’s founding chief executive, Roman Hölzl, moved to San Francisco ahead of the funding round. RobCo. maintains a manufacturing facility in Austin and has customers across a dozen states.

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max : voilà que maintenant, certains appareils n'ont plus de réseau
articles.text:
L'iPhone 18 Pro Max a un nouveau problème. Oui, encore. Ça fait beaucoup là non ? Pour un premier smartphone lancé sous l'ère de John Ternus, l'iPhone 18 Pro Max enchaîne les déceptions avec cette fois-ci néanmoins, une "bonne nouvelle", si l'on peut la qualifier ainsi.
Ce sont maintenant des problèmes de réseau mobile qui touchent l'iPhone 18 Pro Max spécifiquement, mais Apple, n'allant pas se contenter d'une simple mise à jour, opte pour une mesure plus radicale, qui va ravir certains utilisateurs du smartphone de la marque. Les clients qui n'avaient pas mis de coque et qui sont déçus de la qualité vont pouvoir investir quelques euros et repartir de zéro.
Des problèmes de réseau chez un opérateur américain
Après des problèmes d'écran, des soucis de réseau font leur apparition. Depuis le lancement de l'iPhone 18 Pro Max début septembre, des clients du réseau américain AT&T signalent des soucis de connectivité. Apple a en effet finalement confirmé l'existence du problème à nos confrères de 9to5Mac.
Selon l'entreprise, un petit nombre de propriétaires d'iPhone 18 Pro Max sur le réseau d'AT&T ont perdu l'accès aux données cellulaires. Pour corriger cela, Apple a lancé iOS 27.0.1, une mise à jour qui est censée régler ce problème. Une mise à jour des paramètres de l'opérateur a également été effectuée.
Nous avons identifié un problème affectant un petit nombre d'utilisateurs d'iPhone 18 Pro Max sur le réseau AT&T pouvant entraîner une perte de service et l'impossibilité de passer des appels. - Apple
Un remplacement de l'iPhone en cas de problème
Pour les clients ayant déjà subi une perte totale de réseau cellulaire, une solution matérielle s'impose, le remplacement de l'iPhone. C'est là que quelques déçus par la qualité de l'appareil, qui n'avaient pas investi dans une coque de protection, pourraient être ravis.
Les propriétaires concernés sont invités à se rendre dans une boutique AT&T ou en Apple Store, ou à contacter le support de l'opérateur ou de la marque, pour un remplacement de leur smartphone.
- Design toujours réussi
- Un objectif principal très lumineux
- Les performances dingo
Des témoignages sur Reddit montrent que certains utilisateurs ont effectivement reçu un appareil de remplacement après avoir contacté Apple. Toutefois, les expériences rapportées ne sont pas uniformes, quelques propriétaires n'ayant pas eu accès à cette solution.
Un modem Qualcomm défectueux ?
Les problèmes de réseau en question semblent n'affecter que la version Pro Max. L'iPhone 18 Pro Max vendu aux États-Unis intègre le modem 5G Qualcomm X80, tandis que l'iPhone 18 Pro standard utilise un modem conçu par Apple, le C2. Bien que cette différence puisse constituer un élément de réponse, l'origine exacte du problème reste indéterminée.
Apple recommande pour l'instant à tous les utilisateurs d'iPhone 18 Pro Max sur le réseau d'AT&T de télécharger la mise à jour iOS 27.0.1, particulièrement pour ceux n'ayant pas encore rencontré de problèmes.

articles.title: La ‘papelera fantasma’ de WhatsApp: por qué borrar chats no libera espacio realmente
articles.text:
Borrar una conversación en WhatsApp no significa recuperar el espacio que ocupaba. Esa es la conclusión que se desprende del funcionamiento técnico de la aplicación: aunque el chat desaparece de la pantalla, buena parte de los archivos que contenía sigue almacenada en el teléfono.
El fenómeno se conoce como la ‘papelera fantasma’ de WhatsApp, y ocurre porque la app genera copias de caché, miniaturas y referencias cruzadas de cada imagen, video o documento que circula por los chats, elementos que no se eliminan solo con borrar la conversación desde la interfaz principal.
Para solucionarlo, WhatsApp incluye un gestor de almacenamiento interno, poco conocido por la mayoría de los usuarios, que permite identificar y borrar de forma definitiva los archivos pesados y duplicados que realmente consumen la memoria del dispositivo.
Por qué borrar un chat no elimina los archivos reales
WhatsApp necesita responder con rapidez cuando un usuario abre una conversación, revisa una foto antigua o busca un archivo enviado meses atrás. Para lograrlo, la aplicación no depende únicamente del mensaje original: crea miniaturas de vista previa, índices de búsqueda local y registros de medios que facilitan ese acceso inmediato.
A eso se suma otro factor habitual en el uso diario de la aplicación. Cuando un mismo archivo (un meme, un video o un documento) se reenvía a distintos contactos o grupos, el sistema no multiplica el archivo original en sí, pero sí mantiene referencias cruzadas y copias asociadas a cada chat por el que pasó.
El resultado aparece en el momento de borrar una conversación. El enlace visible del archivo dentro del chat desaparece, pero la miniatura almacenada en caché suele permanecer en el sistema de archivos del teléfono. Las copias vinculadas a otros chats donde ese mismo contenido fue reenviado tampoco se eliminan.
Borrar un chat en WhatsApp elimina la conversación visible, pero no borra automáticamente las miniaturas en caché ni las copias del mismo archivo reenviadas a otros chats, lo que explica por qué el espacio ocupado en el teléfono apenas se reduce tras ese borrado manual.
Esa diferencia entre lo que el usuario ve y lo que realmente queda almacenado es lo que da origen al término papelera fantasma: la app muestra un chat vacío, pero el peso total de WhatsApp en los ajustes del sistema operativo se mantiene prácticamente igual.
El gestor de almacenamiento que identifica los archivos pesados
A diferencia de la eliminación manual desde cada conversación, WhatsApp cuenta con un panel propio que organiza el contenido según el tamaño real que ocupa en el disco y según sus patrones de duplicación, no según la cantidad de mensajes enviados.
Dentro de ese panel existen dos categorías que concentran la mayor parte del espacio desperdiciado y que rara vez son revisadas por los usuarios.
La sección “Reenviados muchas veces” agrupa los archivos que circularon por múltiples chats. Eliminarlos desde allí desvincula de una sola vez el archivo original y todas sus copias en caché, en lugar de tener que borrarlo chat por chat.
La sección “Más de 5 MB” ordena de mayor a menor todos los videos, documentos y audios pesados guardados en la base de datos de la aplicación. Según esta clasificación, ese tipo de archivos puede representar más del 70% del espacio total ocupado por WhatsApp en el teléfono.
Cómo hacer una limpieza profunda en Android e iOS
El procedimiento para acceder a este gestor es el mismo en ambos sistemas operativos, con pequeñas diferencias en la ruta de acceso inicial.
El primer paso es abrir WhatsApp y entrar a Ajustes: en iOS se encuentra directamente en la pestaña correspondiente, mientras que en Android es necesario tocar los tres puntos ubicados en la parte superior de la pantalla.
Dentro de Ajustes, hay que seleccionar “Almacenamiento y datos” y luego tocar la primera opción disponible, “Administrar almacenamiento”. Allí aparece una barra con el desglose exacto de cuánto ocupan los archivos de WhatsApp, cuánto ocupa la aplicación en sí y cuánto espacio libre queda disponible en el teléfono.
El siguiente paso es entrar a la sección “Reenviados muchas veces”. Dentro de ella se puede tocar “Seleccionar todos” para borrar de una vez todo el contenido duplicado, o elegir los archivos de manera individual.
Después de presionar el ícono de la papelera, es necesario marcar la casilla “Eliminar también los elementos recibidos” o “Borrar copias”, en caso de que aparezca, ya que ese paso es el que fuerza la limpieza efectiva del caché.
Tras completar ese proceso, conviene regresar al menú anterior y entrar a la sección “Más de 5 MB”. Allí es posible ordenar los archivos por criterios como “Más reciente” o “Más antiguo” y seleccionar los videos o documentos pesados que ya no se necesiten.
Como paso adicional, el panel incluye una lista inferior llamada “Chats”, donde los contactos y grupos aparecen ordenados según el peso total que ocupan en megabytes o gigabytes, y no según la cantidad de mensajes intercambiados. Entrar a los chats más pesados de esa lista permite borrar videos y audios específicos sin necesidad de eliminar el historial de texto de la conversación.

articles.title: Texas city demands $2M for public records on Flock usage
articles.text:
As bipartisan backlash against Flock grows, some cities are asking anti-surveillance advocates and media outlets to pay eye-popping fees—including charging tens of thousands or even millions—to get information about how police departments are using and potentially abusing AI-enabled camera systems that track every vehicle that passes them.
On Monday, the Texas Tribune reported that city officials in a Fort Worth suburb, North Richland Hills, asked one group to pay $2.3 million before it would fulfill a public records request for Flock data. To reach that high fee, officials claimed that searching “about a terabyte worth of communications about errors, misuse, and effectiveness of the Flock system” would take approximately 14 years of labor at a rate of $15 per hour.
Phil Mynona, who filed the request using a pseudonym on behalf of his group, the Texas Privacy Coalition, told the Tribune that the fee seemed “ludicrous” and designed to stifle his public records searches.
Mynona has sought similar records from more than 200 law enforcement agencies across the US, and he said it was impossible to predict how cities assessed fees for Flock records. Some cities provided more than 400,000 pages of documents for free, while others charged $5,000. Other groups, including a Houston news station called KPRC, have seen officials quote up to $121,000 for Flock records, the Tribune reported.
The high price tags may be hiding data that anti-surveillance groups note have triggered audits, arrests, and changes in how law enforcement uses cameras, including decisions to get rid of cameras. Many cops have been found using the cameras to stalk strangers and people in their personal lives, and so far, Flock has yet to introduce meaningful reforms to confront its stalker cop problem.
Texas is a perfect example of how increasing transparency about police use of Flock cameras works to protect the public from invasive searches that serve no lawful purpose. Last week, an ex-Texas cop, Zachary Anthony Klein, reportedly pled guilty to 100 felony counts of misuse of official information, which he agreed to do in exchange for the state not pursuing charges related to stalking several people. Klein’s Flock abuse—along with another cop’s—was outed after USA Today submitted a public records request that sparked a probe, then his arrest. Disturbed by the case, Texas Governor Greg Abbott quickly halted Flock funding and stopped issuing permits, the Tribune noted.

articles.title: Tencent scores 100,000 offshore AI chip deal with Oracle for $7 billion despite climbing prices
articles.text:
Tencent scores 100,000 offshore AI chip deal with Oracle for $7 billion despite climbing prices — per-hour costs estimated to be 43% under standard H100 rental rates
Neither company has said which chips Tencent is renting.
Oracle has reportedly made a deal with Tencent for a five-year lease at several Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, covering about 100,000 advanced AI chips unavailable in China. The deal is estimated to be worth about $7 billion, which would come out to about $1.60 per chip per hour over five years, with about 30% upfront, according to a report by the Financial Times (FT). The deal lands as compute rental prices continue to climb, per Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell on Tencent’s August 12 earnings call. Neither company has commented on the report, but such leases are legal under current U.S. rules, per the FT.
The estimated chip-hour price is around 43% less than the roughly $2.80 per GPU-hour for Nvidia’s H100 with a one-year contract, per research firm SemiAnalysis in August. It’s also about 48% lower than the $3.09 per GPU-hour for a three-year contract with Nvidia’s B200, per a 2025 filing by Japanese data center operator Datasection for an unnamed customer. Market trends have pricing running the other way, with the FT reporting longer terms and larger upfront payments for such leases. Tencent president Martin Lau said on the same call the company could sell its existing orders at “more than 30% profit” compared to what it “paid just a few months ago.”
No chips are named. The FT says that such leases could reach even Nvidia’s top processors, but that does not mean this deal involves Nvidia hardware. One-year H100 contracts on SemiAnalysis’s index were above the estimated rate at about $1.70 per GPU-hour even as of October 2025, with the B200 rate being even more expensive despite its longer, three-year term. Going by raw B200 server costs, which exclude buildings, power, networking, and financing, 100,000 B200s would cost $5.44 billion, or about 78% of the reported value, based on Datasection’s 2025 purchase of servers with 5,000 B200s for $272 million.
Without specifics on the hardware being rented, it is not possible to determine whether this is a bulk deal or if the leasing costs are closer to the actual hardware cost. The pricing on paper, however, better fits Hopper-class at volume. Hopper would include the H100 and H200 and, with H200 imports still limited, could meet the criterion of the chips in the deal not being available in China.
The Oracle data centers are located outside China, with Tencent merely renting time on them. Details including the countries involved, sites, and start date remain undisclosed. Oracle has two Singapore cloud regions, with a Malaysia one announced. The FT says the biggest clients of Southeast Asian data centers are ByteDance and Alibaba, with Chinese firms using the capacity especially for AI training, which domestic chips cannot yet do. Tencent previously inked a $1.2 billion-plus deal for Datasection Blackwell rentals in Japan and Australia, the FT reported in December 2025.
Some Oracle clients have prepaid for GPUs or brought their own hardware since its March call, and fiscal Q4, from March to May, added $67 billion of AI contracts, mostly of those two kinds, per its June call. June through August, per its quarterly filing, the company “received $11.4 billion of prepayments from customers that included a significant financing component.” Deferred revenue rose from $15.4 billion to $30.8 billion over the quarter. No customers were named, so this can’t be tied to Tencent. The company reported 97.9% GPU utilization during its September 10 earnings call, with renewals at a 20% average premium, which was mostly on GPUs four years or older.
Tencent prepaying about 30% makes sense given Oracle’s statements earlier this year. It’s a good deal for both parties. Oracle would improve its cash flow following a quarter of negative free cash flow, and Tencent Cloud’s May price raises, per Mitchell, could help recoup the cost of the rented chips.
The legal picture, given the friction between the United States and China over AI export controls, is thorny. The Remote Access Security Act, a bipartisan bill that passed the House 369–22 in January, would give the U.S. government the right to regulate remote cloud access to sensitive technology, which could cover the chips under the reported deal. The bill specifically targets cloud loopholes and applies to any foreign person rather than naming countries, to prevent adversaries from leveraging cloud networks to bypass U.S. export bans. The bill currently sits in the Senate Banking Committee.
Separately, Export Administration Regulations license requirements under the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) have covered shipments of advanced AI chips, including to China-headquartered companies abroad, since November 2023. Cloud rentals were left out, with the BIS only asking for comment on them. Renting remains one loophole around BIS guidance on restricted chips. Bloomberg reported that the BIS was reviewing offshore access with legal rentals included. The deal is also not barred by Tencent being on the Pentagon’s 1260H list of “Chinese military companies,” as this is not a sanction. No statement about the deal by any regulatory government official accompanied the report.
According to The Information, the Department of Commerce is drafting a rule to block Chinese firms from renting compute in third countries, such as Thailand and Singapore, which would align with the reported details of this deal. U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met late last month in Washington, covering AI and extending a trade truce for a further two months.
However, the deal is of a type that might face trouble from both the House-passed bill and Commerce’s reported rule. But the latter cannot be enforced under current law, an attorney at Baker McKenzie told The Information. At the summit, the two leaders agreed to set up a channel to handle AI-related incidents, but nothing was announced on chip controls. While the U.S. has cleared some firms, including Tencent, to buy Nvidia’s H200, China has let in only about 10,000 for Tencent so far, the FT reported in August. The next meeting between the two, at APEC in Shenzhen in November, may clarify the situation.
The reported deal comes weeks before Oracle’s Investor Day on Oct. 28 in Las Vegas, during its Oct. 25–28 Oracle AI World event at the Venetian. That would be a chance for the company to disclose details about the deal, such as announcing what hardware is to be leased. Given the hardware math, our assumption is that it involves older or non-Nvidia hardware rather than an action born of financial stress at Oracle. The month following Oracle’s event, Tencent is expected to report its Q3 results. These events could also reveal more concrete details about the arrangement.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: B.C. teen stranded on cliff after having AI plan his route
articles.text:
A B.C. teen found himself stranded on a cliff over the weekend after he followed a route plotted by AI.
As reported by local news outlet North Shore News, the unnamed 16-year-old had to be rescued after getting stuck on Crown Mountain on Saturday afternoon. According to search manager Paul Markey, the boy started a hiking trail from Grouse Mountain that went to Crown Mountain.
Following directions from AI, the boy began ascending Crown Mountain via a gully, a narrow ditch that’s formed by running water. However, the trail led the teen to a rock-climbing route with steep terrain, and it was there that he got stuck at the base of a cliff. Ultimately, Markey says the boy was able to be located and rescued by volunteers a few hours later after calling for help with his cell phone.
The article didn’t mention a specific AI platform, so it’s unclear which the boy used. Still, this points to the larger issue regarding the mistakes that AI can make, whether it’s misleading search results, unauthorized purchases or wrongful criminal charges. (That’s to say nothing of how it’s used for even more malicious ends like Elon Musk’s Grok creating sexual images of women and minors, or the steep environmental costs associated with AI data centres.)
Naturally, Markey advised people to not use AI to plan hiking routes.
“Be cautious when getting routes and information suggested through AI,” he told North Shore News. “You can’t just blindly follow what AI is proposing to you. You need to question the information and just see whether it makes sense or not.”
In place of AI platforms, Markey suggests using tools like Gaia GPS, CalTopo or AllTrails. He also said it’s important for hikers to bring other gear with them, which he did praise the boy for doing, including a cell phone battery pack, headlamp, hiking boots and a windproof jacket.
Ironically, this report comes just a few days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, one of the biggest AI-pilled tech executives, pushed back against fears that AI is making people dumber. According to him, it doesn’t matter if people forget basic skills like math due to AI use because they’ll simply pick up other skills in the process. But of course, examples like the B.C. teen hiker show the importance of being able to think for yourself, regardless of what AI might tell you.

Source: North Shore News

articles.title: En los años 90, unos investigadores descubrieron unas algas que reaccionaban increíblemente rápido a la luz. Hoy son el Nobel de Medicina
articles.text:
En el día de hoy se ha dado el pistoletazo de salida que inicia una de las semanas en el mundo científico y cultural más importantes de todo el año, como son los premios Nobel. Y como es tradicional, ha dado inicio con la lectura del veredicto del jurado en la disciplina de medicina y fisiología, que este año ha concedido el Nobel a Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann y Georg Nagel.
Hay razones. Detrás de un premio tan importante como un Nobel lógicamente debe haber unas razones de peso para concederlo, y en esta ocasión el hito que galardona es importante por todo lo que ha conllevado a posteriori. Y es que este trío de investigadores puso hace muchos años las bases sobre las que se fundamentan buena parte de las investigaciones actuales en el campo de la neurociencia, llegando hasta el punto de dar alas a la posibilidad de que una persona ciega pueda ver.
Nuestros límites. Durante gran parte de la historia de la neurociencia moderna, el enorme desafío no ha sido solo observar el cerebro, sino intervenir en él con la precisión suficiente para establecer relaciones de causa y efecto en el comportamiento. Ya en 1979, el científico Francis Crick teorizó que para descifrar el cerebro se necesitaría un método que permitiera encender y apagar tipos específicos de neuronas de forma ultrarrápida, sugiriendo que la señal ideal para lograrlo sería la luz.
Y esta idea que para el propio Crick era descabellada, se ha hecho realidad de la mano de una simple alga verde y que ha dado lugar a este premio Nobel.
La historia de este gran avance comienza como una casualidad fundamental sobre la fototaxia, que es el comportamiento que permite a las microalgas verdes con flagelos orientarse y nadar dinámicamente hacia una fuente de luz. Y aquí, a principios de los años 90, Peter Hegemann estudió las corrientes fotorreceptoras de la Chlamydomonas reinhardtii y descubrió que su reacción a la luz era extraordinariamente rápida, con una latencia de apenas microsegundos.
Esta velocidad sugirió a su equipo que el fotorreceptor y el canal iónico responsable de la corriente debían estar íntimamente unidos en una única proteína, descartando las lentas cascadas bioquímicas que se dan en la visión animal. Y a principios de los años 2000, su laboratorio logró identificar las secuencias genéticas responsables.
Su implantación. De estas algas que pueden ser insignificantes para el ojo humano, sacamos unas proteínas llamadas canalrrodopsinas y lo mejor es que contábamos con la información necesaria para que una neurona de ratón comenzara a sintetizarlas también en su superficie. Y eso es precisamente lo que hizo Karl Deisseroth en su laboratorio.
La optogenética. Deisseroth demostró que la iluminación con pulsos de luz azul podía desencadenar potenciales de acción neuronales precisos al milisegundo. Y para encapsular esta sinergia entre los actuadores ópticos y la expresión genética dirigida, en 2006 se acuñó formalmente el término "optogenética". Aunque hubo que esperar a la posterior integración de cables de fibra óptica para que los científicos lograran iluminar regiones profundas del cerebro de animales despiertos y en movimiento, permitiendo un control sin precedentes sobre funciones como el sueño, las interacciones sociales y la memoria.
En la actualidad. Como decíamos, lo importante aquí es la aplicación que puede tener este resultado científico y en cómo va a beneficiar a la sociedad. Y aquí lo vemos con una patología llamada retinitis pigmentosa, que es una enfermedad neurodegenerativa hereditaria que destruye progresivamente los fotorreceptores del ojo. De esta manera, la optogenética puede llegar para introducir una variante de la canalrodopsina sensible a la luz roja llamada Chrimson, directamente en las células viables sobre la retina.
Aquí el equipo del investigador Botond Roska aplicó recientemente esta terapia en un paciente ciego afectado por retinitis pigmentosa y, utilizando unas gafas especiales de ingeniería que proyectaban pulsos de luz hacia los ojos para activar estas células genéticamente modificadas, el paciente logró una recuperación parcial prolongada de su función visual. Por primera vez en mucho tiempo, esta persona fue capaz de percibir, localizar y distinguir objetos de alto contraste sobre una mesa, un cambio con beneficios reales para su vida diaria.
Imagen | Bernd Dittrich

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass perdería 9 videojuegos el 15 de octubre, incluido Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
articles.text:
Xbox Game Pass perdería nueve videojuegos el próximo jueves 15 de octubre de 2026, según reveló un listado compartido en Reddit. Entre las bajas destaca Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, ganador del premio GOTY 2025 y señalado como uno de los mejores lanzamientos de la última década.
El título de Sandfall Interactive llegó al catálogo de Microsoft en abril de 2025, por lo que habrá permanecido disponible para los suscriptores durante más de 17 meses antes de su salida.
La lista completa de bajas incluye, además del RPG francés, a The Casting of Frank Stone, Crime Scene Cleaner, Donut County, Evil West, Superball, Nova Roma, Pacific Drive y A Plague Tale: Requiem. La variedad de géneros entre estos nueve títulos (desde la acción hasta los simuladores pasando por el terror narrativo) deja en evidencia el alcance de la renovación que se aproxima en el servicio.
Qué juegos salen de Xbox Game Pass el 15 de octubre
La salida de Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 es, sin duda, la que generará mayor repercusión entre la comunidad de jugadores. Se trata de un videojuego de rol por turnos que se consolidó como una de las sorpresas más comentadas del año, al punto de hacerse con el galardón al mejor juego de 2025.
Su desaparición del catálogo obligará a quienes aún no lo hayan completado a decidir si lo adquieren de forma definitiva o se despiden de la aventura.
Junto a él, A Plague Tale: Requiem también dejará la suscripción. Esta entrega retoma la historia de los hermanos Amicia y Hugo en una narrativa que combina mecánicas de sigilo, resolución de acertijos y la presencia constante de plagas de ratas como amenaza ambiental. Su salida representa la pérdida de otro de los exponentes narrativos más sólidos del catálogo.
A esta despedida se suma Pacific Drive, un juego de supervivencia centrado en la reparación y mejora de un vehículo que funciona como herramienta principal para explorar una región marcada por fenómenos sobrenaturales. Su propuesta, que mezcla mecánica vehicular con elementos de terror ambiental, también abandonará Game Pass en la misma fecha.
Para los amantes de la acción más desenfrenada, Evil West pondrá fin a su etapa dentro de la suscripción. El título, centrado en el enfrentamiento contra vampiros, se caracteriza por un estilo de combate caótico que lo convirtió en una opción popular entre quienes buscan ritmo y adrenalina dentro del catálogo de Microsoft.
Otros títulos y juegos indie que dejarán el servicio
Más allá de los lanzamientos de mayor repercusión, la lista de bajas también contempla producciones de menor escala, pero con seguidores propios dentro de la comunidad. The Casting of Frank Stone es uno de ellos: un juego pensado para los aficionados a las aventuras de terror con un fuerte componente cinematográfico en su narrativa.
Entre las producciones independientes, Crime Scene Cleaner desaparecerá del catálogo. Se trata de un simulador centrado en la limpieza de escenas del crimen, un género que ha ganado terreno entre los jugadores que disfrutan de experiencias atípicas y minuciosas.
En la misma categoría de proyectos menores se encuentra Nova Roma, un título de construcción y gestión de ciudades que, pese a seguir en fase de acceso anticipado, también dejará de estar disponible.
Para quienes prefieren experiencias más breves, Donut County representa una de las bajas más sensibles dentro del segmento de los puzles. Su propuesta, pensada para completarse en pocas horas, lo convirtió en una recomendación habitual para quienes buscaban un juego accesible y entretenido dentro del catálogo.
El caso de Superball es distinto al resto. Al tratarse de un juego gratuito, su salida de Xbox Game Pass no implicará la pérdida de acceso al título en sí, sino únicamente de las ventajas y beneficios asociados a la suscripción, como posibles descuentos o contenido adicional vinculado al servicio.

articles.title: 7 Books that teach you why rich people think differently
articles.text:
7 Books that teach you why rich people think differently
Discover 6 powerful books that reveal how wealthy people think about money, habits, risk, and success differently from everyone else.
Most people assume that becoming rich is simply a matter of earning more money. Yet many people with high incomes struggle financially, while others quietly build substantial wealth over time. The difference often lies in how they think.
Wealthy people tend to view money, opportunities, risk, and time differently. They focus on building assets, making long-term decisions, and developing habits that compound over years rather than seeking quick rewards.
While no book can guarantee financial success, some offer valuable insights into the mindset and principles that have shaped generations of entrepreneurs, investors, and self-made millionaires.
Here are seven books that explain why rich people think differently and what the rest of us can learn from them.
1. Rich Dad Poor Dad by Robert Kiyosaki
Few books have influenced conversations about money as much as Rich Dad Poor Dad. Through the contrasting lessons of two father figures, Kiyosaki introduces readers to a different way of thinking about wealth.
The book challenges the traditional belief that a good job alone leads to financial freedom. Instead, it emphasises financial education, building assets, and making money work for you rather than constantly working for money.
One of its biggest lessons is that wealthy people focus on acquiring assets that generate income, while many others spend most of their earnings on liabilities.
2. The Psychology of Money by Morgan Housel
Many people know what they should do with money but still make poor financial decisions. Morgan Housel explores why. Rather than focusing on complex investment strategies, the book examines the role of behaviour, emotions, patience, and decision-making in wealth creation. It argues that financial success is often less about intelligence and more about habits and discipline.
The book shows that wealthy individuals understand the power of long-term thinking and compounding, while others often allow fear, ego, or impatience to dictate their choices.
3. Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill
First published in 1937, this classic remains one of the most influential books on success and wealth.
Hill studied the lives and habits of highly successful individuals and identified common principles such as persistence, goal-setting, belief, and focused action. The book argues that wealth creation begins with a clear purpose and a strong desire to achieve it.
While some ideas reflect the era in which it was written, its central message remains relevant: successful people often think differently long before they achieve different results.
4. The Intelligent Investor by Benjamin Graham
Widely regarded as one of the greatest investing books ever written, The Intelligent Investor teaches readers how to think rationally about money.
Graham encourages investors to focus on value, remain patient, and avoid emotional decisions driven by market excitement or panic.
The wealthy often understand that preserving capital and making thoughtful decisions are just as important as making money. This book explains why emotional discipline is a crucial part of long-term financial success.
5. The Richest Man in Babylon by George S. Clason
Written as a collection of parables set in ancient Babylon, this classic presents timeless principles of wealth creation.
Its lessons are remarkably simple: save a portion of every income, control spending, invest wisely, and allow money to grow over time.
The book demonstrates that many financial truths remain unchanged regardless of the era. Wealth often begins with small, consistent actions repeated for years.
6. How Rich People Think by Steve Siebold
After studying wealthy individuals for decades, Steve Siebold set out to understand what separates their thinking from that of the average person. The book contrasts common beliefs about money with the attitudes often found among self-made millionaires. It explores topics such as responsibility, opportunity, risk-taking, and personal growth.
Its central argument is that financial success is heavily influenced by mindset and that changing the way you think can change the way you approach opportunities and wealth.
Final thoughts
Rich people are not necessarily smarter than everyone else, but they often approach money with a different perspective. They focus on ownership rather than consumption, long-term growth rather than instant gratification, and opportunities rather than limitations.
These seven books offer different viewpoints on wealth creation, but they share a common message: financial success begins with how you think. Changing your mindset may not make you rich overnight, but it can help you make better decisions that compound over time.

articles.title: Como saber se a caixa ou o fone da JBL são originais • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como saber se a caixa ou o fone da JBL são originais
Um fone de ouvido JBL falsificado pode gerar riscos, como baterias instáveis, danos à audição por falhas de equalização e prejuízo financeiro sem garantia
A JBL conquistou o setor global de áudio com caixas de som e fones de ouvido conhecidos pela alta potência sonora, durabilidade e design marcante. Contudo, o enorme sucesso fez com que o mercado fosse inundado por réplicas e modelos piratas que não entregam a mesma fidelidade de som.
Para saber se a JBL é original, o consumidor deve analisar detalhes como o acabamento, o peso do dispositivo e a presença do número de série na embalagem. Identificar um produto falso evita prejuízos financeiros e garante a compra de um produto legítimo e com garantia de fábrica.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog apresenta 8 pontos que ajudam a descobrir uma JBL falsificada.
A embalagem, a construção, os softwares e a qualidade do som do fone ou caixa de som JBL trazem pistas se o produto é original ou uma cópia fabricada pelo mercado paralelo. Então, o Tecnoblog revela os detalhes a serem observados.
Para saber se a JBL é original, examine o acabamento da embalagem: caixas legítimas usam papelão rígido, alinhamento perfeito e impressão gráfica de altíssima definição. As réplicas costumam exibir material frágil, encaixes tortos e artes borradas com baixo contraste visual.
Também verifique o número de série, código de barras, a identificação do modelo e o selo de homologação da ANATEL. Se essas informações estiverem ausentes, adulteradas ou ilegíveis, o dispositivo certamente é pirata.
Compare o número de série gravado no dispositivo JBL com a sequência alfanumérica impressa na caixa externa do produto. Se houver qualquer divergência entre esses dados, o item foi adulterado ou montado fora dos padrões de fábrica.
A gravação do código também exige atenção: no dispositivo original, os caracteres têm tipografia nítida, alinhada e perfeitamente legível na superfície. Já um fone ou caixa de som JBL falsa traz sequências apagadas, cobertas por adesivos suspeitos ou falhas de impressão.
Você pode identificar uma JBL falsificada ao analisar o logotipo: no produto original, a marca é gravada ou embutida no material com alinhamento milimétrico. Enquanto isso, no pirata, ela fica torta, solta ou com cores desbotadas.
Fique atento aos detalhes do emblema, pois réplicas costumam trocar entalhes e relevos oficiais por adesivos simples de baixa qualidade. Texturas irregulares e a ausência do acabamento metálico característico confirmam a procedência duvidosa do aparelho.
Para saber se o fone JBL é original, observe a estrutura: modelos autênticos trazem plástico emborrachado premium, tecidos resistentes, botões firmes e encaixes simétricos. Do outro lado, as cópias entregam material frágil, peças folgadas, rebarbas ásperas e tinta descascada.
Também preste atenção aos componentes de vedação e conectores, que nas réplicas apresentam portas desalinhadas, tampas de borracha frouxas e pintura de baixa aderência. Qualquer divergência tátil nos botões ou na profundidade dos encaixes em relação às fotos oficiais entrega a falsificação.
Um fone ou caixa de som JBL falsa é visivelmente mais leve que a original por substituir transdutores pesados e baterias de alta densidade energética por componentes baratos. A diferença na massa do aparelho fica evidente ao comparar o produto físico com as especificações oficiais.
Essa folga no peso acontece porque piratas removem circuitos de proteção, blindagem e módulos acústicos densos para cortar custos. Qualquer discrepância na balança revela um hardware inferior e confirma a ausência das peças originais que garantem o som potente.
Um acessório da JBL falsificado entrega a pirataria logo de cara: cabos originais vêm bem embalados, trazem o logo impresso no conector e possuem blindagem espessa. As réplicas, no entanto, acompanham fios finos e conectores genéricos.
Fontes de alimentação e adaptadores originais ostentam selos de conformidade e gravações nítidas, sem riscos ou borrões. A falta dessas certificações no carregador, associada a um isolamento elétrico frágil, confirma que o conjunto é adulterado.
Outro meio de saber se a caixa JBL é original é conectando o aparelho no aplicativo oficial da marca: modelos legítimos são reconhecidos de imediato para atualização de firmware, enquanto réplicas são ignoradas pelo software.
No pareamento Bluetooth, o dispositivo deve exibir o nome comercial exato do modelo e parear via protocolo nativo sem emitir avisos sonoros genéricos. Se o aparelho surgir como um código estranho na busca sem fio, o hardware é pirata.
A qualidade de som de uma caixa de som ou fone JBL original destaca graves incorporados, médios limpos e alta fidelidade. Já as cópias entregam áudio abafado, ruídos de fundo e distorções em volumes altos.
Outro ponto fraco dos piratas é o processamento de áudio: por usarem codecs sem fio genéricos, sofrem com atrasos e perdas na resposta de frequência. Se o som degradar no volume máximo ou cortar com frequência, a falsificação fica evidente.
Sim, um produto JBL “Made in China” é original, pois o país abriga linhas oficiais de fabricação da marca para suprir a demanda global. O selo de origem chinesa, isoladamente, não indica pirataria.
Para tirar a prova real, confirme se a nomenclatura do aparelho consta no catálogo oficial da marca e analise o acabamento do hardware. Discrepâncias no número de série e falhas na montagem são evidências muito mais confiáveis do que a indicação do país de fabricação.
Para garantir que está comprando os melhores fones de ouvido JBL, é fundamental checar a reputação do vendedor e as especificações físicas do produto. Essa análise prévia evita réplicas e garante o suporte à garantia oficial da marca.
Os eletrônicos JBL originais são projetados pela Harman sob rigorosos padrões de engenharia, oferecendo construção em materiais de alta densidade. Eles apresentam integração com o ecossistema de software oficial, assinatura sonora equilibrada e garantia direta do fabricante.
Os modelos JBL falsificados são réplicas piratas que reproduzem o design da marca, mas empregam circuitos de baixa qualidade, componentes sem homologação regulatória. As baterias instáveis também comprometem o desempenho do hardware e a segurança do usuário.
Usar um fone de ouvido JBL falsificado expõe o usuário a graves riscos de segurança, além de causar frustração sonora e prejuízo financeiro. Sem controle de qualidade e certificações regulatórias, o dispositivo pirata compromete tanto o hardware quanto a saúde do consumidor.

articles.title: Rapidus Unveils "Rapidus CORE" Global Framework for Development and Mass Production of Semiconductors
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
Rapidus Unveils "Rapidus CORE" Global Framework for Development and Mass Production of Semiconductors
Rapidus Corporation today announced that it will establish the Rapidus Collaborative Open Rapid Ecosystem (CORE), a global ecosystem framework to support the development and mass production of cutting-edge semiconductors.
Today, semiconductor development requires more than just manufacturing technology; it is essential to integrate the entire semiconductor value chain—including research institutions, EDA, IP, design and manufacturing—to provide customers with a development and production infrastructure they can rely on. Further, amid a global shortage of cutting-edge semiconductor talent, it is crucial to build a design ecosystem that enables customers to begin development at an early stage by collaborating with design-related companies.As the first Rapidus CORE initiative, Rapidus is announcing the formation of Design Solution Associates, a group of design companies. Design Solution Associates will serve as a bridge between customers and Rapidus, providing each company's design resources and specialized expertise to support the rapid evolution of semiconductor development. This will enable Rapidus to strengthen its support system—from design through manufacturing—to meet customer needs both in Japan and overseas.
The 17 Design Solution Associates announced today are as follows, in alphabetical order: AION Silicon Limited; Cadence Design Systems, Inc.; Dai Nippon Printing Co., Ltd.; GreatAsic Technology Sdn. Bhd.; HCL Technologies Limited; Infinecs Systems Sdn. Bhd.; Infosys Limited; MavissDesign Co., Ltd.; MosChip Technologies Limited; NSW Inc.; Oppstar Technology Sdn Bhd; Quest Global Services Pte. Ltd.; SkyeChip Berhad; Synopsys, Inc.; TOPPAN Inc.; Toshiba Information Systems (Japan) Corporation and Wipro Limited.
Moving forward, Rapidus will expand its CORE offerings beyond design to include EDA, IP and other categories. By strengthening partnerships with companies in each of these categories, Rapidus will help accelerate the global ecosystem that supports the development and mass production of cutting-edge semiconductors.

articles.title: Windows 11 adopte enfin ce petit raccourci bien connu sur Linux et macOS
articles.text:
Microsoft teste une petite nouveauté dans l’Explorateur de fichiers de Windows 11. Le caractère « ~ » permettra bientôt d’accéder directement au dossier personnel de l’utilisateur, une convention familière aux habitués de macOS et Linux.
Un caractère, quelques frappes en moins. Dans la build 26340.9596 de Windows 11 26H2, actuellement distribuée dans le canal Experimental du programme Insider, Microsoft apprend à la barre d’adresse de l’Explorateur à reconnaître « ~ ». Un raccourci permettant d’accéder directement au répertoire personnel, vieux de plusieurs décennies dans l’univers Unix, dont profitent depuis longtemps les utilisateurs et utilisatrices de Linux comme de macOS.
Pourquoi faire compliqué quand un caractère suffit
Microsoft n’a rien inventé ici. Sur Linux comme sur macOS, « ~ » désigne depuis longtemps le répertoire personnel de l’utilisateur. Placé au début d’un chemin, il évite d’en saisir toute la première partie. ~/Downloads, par exemple, renvoie directement au dossier Téléchargements du compte courant. Adieu C:\Users\Nom\Downloads, donc.
Pour rappel, Windows disposait déjà d’autres moyens d’arriver au même résultat, à commencer par la variable %USERPROFILE%. Mais difficile de rivaliser avec un seul caractère (même si ~ ne tombe pas tout seul sous les doigts sur un clavier AZERTY), à plus forte raison quand le raccourci censé simplifier la saisie repose sur une syntaxe autrement plus cryptique.
À noter enfin que PowerShell reconnaît déjà ~ comme raccourci vers le répertoire personnel. Pour gagner la bataille du clavier, PowerToys permet aussi d’affecter le caractère à une touche que vous n’utilisez jamais. Celle de Copilot, par exemple.
Dans les systèmes de type Unix (Linux, macOS), « ~ » est un alias qui représente le répertoire personnel de l’utilisateur courant (le “home”). Quand il est placé au début d’un chemin (ex. ~/Downloads), le shell ou l’application remplace « ~ » par le chemin absolu réel du home. Cette substitution évite d’écrire une partie fixe et longue du chemin, tout en restant indépendante du nom de compte. En pratique, cela repose sur une règle de “tilde expansion” (expansion du tilde) appliquée avant la résolution du chemin par le système de fichiers.
« %USERPROFILE% » est une variable d’environnement Windows qui contient le chemin complet vers le profil de l’utilisateur (par ex. C:\Users\Nom). Elle est surtout utilisée dans des contextes qui interprètent les variables (Invite de commandes, scripts, certains champs système), et pas systématiquement dans toutes les interfaces. « ~ » est plutôt un alias de saisie, plus court, dont la prise en charge dépend de l’application (Explorateur, PowerShell, etc.). Les deux visent le même endroit, mais n’obéissent pas aux mêmes mécanismes d’interprétation.
PowerShell interprète la saisie comme une commande ou un chemin et applique ses propres règles d’expansion, dont « ~ » vers le dossier personnel. L’Explorateur de fichiers, lui, traite la barre d’adresse avec une logique différente, mélangeant chemins Win32, URL internes (shell:), et raccourcis spécifiques à Windows. Ajouter « ~ » à l’Explorateur implique donc d’intégrer cette règle au parseur de la barre d’adresse, pour qu’elle se transforme en chemin valide avant navigation. C’est une différence d’architecture : un shell de commande fait de l’interprétation de texte, l’Explorateur fait de la navigation “Shell Windows” avec ses propres conventions.

articles.title: Google benches open source bug bounty program following ‘significant rise’ in AI submissions
articles.text:
Google benches open source bug bounty program following ‘significant rise’ in AI submissions
Another bug bounty program choked to death on AI slop
- Google paused OSS bug bounty submissions after a surge of AI-generated, invalid reports
- AI boosts vulnerability discovery but often produces flawed, incomplete, or hallucinatory findings
- Rising AI-driven bounty spam has also overwhelmed curl maintainers and Linux security reviewers
Google has revealed it is pausing one of its bug bounty program and it’s all AI’s fault.
The company said its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program (OSS VRP) is being flooded with bogus and irrelevant submissions to the point where it was simply unmanageable.
As a result, the company is pausing accepting all submissions until the end of the year, taking the time to reassess the process and come up with new solutions.
Bug hunting in the age of AI
Generative Artificial Intelligence is supercharging defenders, discovering vulnerabilities at machine speed, making software better and more resilient against exploits and zero-day vulnerabilities.
A few frontier models, including the famed Mythos and GPT-5.6-Cyber, have allowed companies to discover a hundred times more vulnerabilities in less time than ever before.
The best example is Microsoft’s Patch Tuesday. In March 2026, the company addressed 79 flaws in its products, and in April (around the time it started using Mythos) - almost double (167). From that day on, the number of patched bugs grew significantly month-over-month: 200 in June, 400 in August, and 966 in September. In just half a year, Microsoft started fixing more than ten times as many flaws.
However, machines still cannot be trusted to discover and patch vulnerabilities entirely on their own. In early August, security researchers from 1Passwords Off-by-1 Labs set out to see just how good AI was at discovering and fixing flaws and found that half (49.3%) of the patches failed to fix at least one existing exploit path. A fifth (20.1%) fixed the original issue but changed application behavior, while 2.3% introduced new security issues. Funny enough, 2.2% failed to fix the vulnerability while also introducing additional exploit paths, as well.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Even among the patches that might be considered (26% of clean ones and 20.1% of those that changed app behavior), more than a third were fragile and not entirely addressing the underlying problem. 1Password concluded that missing context was the number one challenge, finding that when given proper background information, AI was able to produce significantly better results.
Despite not being able to provide their AI with wider context, many security researchers still use AI for vulnerability discovery. Simple prompts, very little analysis, and even less human oversight, results in “discoveries” that are incorrect, unsubstantiated, and sometimes outright hallucinated. As a result, Google is (temporarily) stepping away from bounty submissions:
“We are temporarily no longer accepting OSS VRP product vulnerability submissions. This does not impact OSS VRP supply chain reports, or any outstanding reports. As an alternative, we encourage you to find impact across our other VRP programs and submit there instead, or pursue the Patch Rewards Program,” Google said in a short tweet, published on October 1 2026.
“Why is this happening? This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid. We will continue to reformat and work on this aspect of the OSS VRP and commit to giving an update in Q1 2027.”
HackerOne and Linus Torvalds
Google is not the first company whose bug bounty program choked to death on AI slop. In late January 2026, the developers of curl, the open source command-line tool and software library, announced killing their HackerOne bug bounty program due to being flooded with fake problems and vulnerabilities.
In an advisory published on GitHub, it was said that the program is being sunsetted at the end of January, 2026.
“Up until the end of January 2026 there was a curl bug bounty. It is no more,” the document reads. “The curl project no longer offers any rewards for reported bugs or vulnerabilities. We also do not aid security researchers to get such rewards for curl problems from other sources either.”
A few months later, in May, lead maintainer of the Linux security mailing list, Linus Torvalds said it was “almost entirely unmanageable” due to researchers using AI to flood it with useless reports.
“The continued flood of AI reports has basically made the security list almost entirely unmanageable, with enormous duplication due to different people finding the same things with the same tools,” he said. “People spend all their time just forwarding things to the right people or saying "that was already fixed a week/month ago" and pointing to the public discussion”.
