articles.title: AI trust strengthens cyber resilience in the digital age - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
What to expect during the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit
AI trust increasingly determines whether enterprise AI scales. As organizations move beyond pilots and put models and agents into operational systems, the question is no longer whether AI performs well in isolation. Enterprises also have to determine whether the infrastructure, data and applications underneath it can withstand cyberattacks, data integrity failures and operational disruption.
That challenge is moving cyber resilience deeper into the enterprise infrastructure stack. Security controls, data protection and recovery can no longer be treated as separate disciplines when AI systems are drawing from sensitive corporate data, interacting with applications and taking actions with limited human intervention.
Those issues will be at the center of the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, with a Dell Technologies-led flagship program Oct. 27 followed by additional industry perspectives, including InfoScale and Infinidat Ltd., on Oct. 28. The broadcasts will reach North America, EMEA and APJ audiences Oct. 28–29. TheCUBE Research analysts Dave Vellante, Krista Case, Christophe Bertrand and Scott Hebner will examine how enterprises are rethinking architecture, security and operating models as AI increases both the value of corporate data and the speed at which attackers can target it. (* Disclosure below.)
“AI projects don’t fail first on capability; they fail first on trust,” Hebner said. “Until enterprises can verify and defend outcomes, autonomy stays trapped in low-stakes use cases. This is what this summit is all about.”
Bertrand positions cyber resiliency not as a supporting layer, but as the structural backbone of enterprise AI — where data governance, protection and infrastructure converge.
“There is no trusted AI in the enterprise without a cyber-resilient IT and data foundation,” he said. “And without trusted, compliant and governed data, AI credibility collapses before it ever scales.”
Dell puts cyber resilience into the AI infrastructure stack
Dell’s role in the summit reflects how closely AI infrastructure and cyber resilience have become intertwined.
AI factories introduce new attack surfaces across model inference, training data, identity, applications and the underlying infrastructure. Rather than treating those systems as another workload protected by existing controls, Dell has been pushing security deeper into the infrastructure itself.
“AI changes the whole game,” Steve Kenniston, senior cybersecurity evangelist for portfolio marketing at Dell, recently told theCUBE. “There’s the model inferencing. There’s the model training data. There are systems where people can do things like prompt injection. There’s identity management that needs to be thought about.”
That expanded attack surface is driving a security-by-design approach across the AI stack, including supply chain protections, infrastructure controls, identity and data protection.
“At Dell, we integrate security into everything that we do, right from the supply chain, through the chips, right to the device that gets delivered to you,” Kenniston added. “Where [it] breaks down in a system like this is where security falls between the cracks.”
Dell has also been broadening the role of its PowerProtect portfolio from conventional backup toward cyber resilience management. New capabilities announced this year include AI-assisted recovery guidance, enhanced anomaly detection across PowerStore snapshots and managed detection and response for PowerScale, which stores much of the unstructured data feeding enterprise AI systems.
At Dell Technologies World, Rob Emsley, director of cyber resilience product marketing at Dell, described the data itself as the constant across both traditional computing and the agentic era.
“At the end of the day, it’s the data layer that’s still the crown jewel,” Emsley told theCUBE. “Whether or not the data has been interacted [with] by a human or a digital agent, the data is still the data.”
That makes recovery an increasingly important part of the AI security equation. Dell’s strategy centers on three principles: secure, detect and recover. The company is also emphasizing isolated cyber recovery environments that preserve clean copies of essential data and applications outside potentially compromised production systems.
“We have over 2,700 customers that have deployed on-premises cyber recovery vaults,” Emsley said. “The name of the game is to put in that vault your minimal viable company. That’s the part of the infrastructure and the data and the applications that your company needs to get back online and survive from an outage.”
AI-driven attacks change the security architecture
Agentic AI adds another dimension to the threat model because autonomous systems can interact with applications, identities and data at machine speed. That shift is already changing how theCUBE Research views security architecture.
“We used to draw the stack, and security was a layer,” Vellante said recently on theCUBE Pod. “It’s not a layer anymore. It has to be something that’s orthogonal.”
The implication is that security must cut across infrastructure rather than sit alongside it. AI systems increase the number of identities, interactions and potential failure points, while attackers can increasingly use the same automation and reasoning technologies available to defenders.
Hebner further believes that scaling AI requires rethinking architecture itself, not just tooling: “The next frontier isn’t smarter agents. It’s agents whose decisions are audit-ready by design. Trust is the architecture,” he added.
Case made a related point following theCUBE’s recent coverage of Oracle’s AI cybersecurity event. Even highly mature security programs must operate under the assumption that prevention will eventually fail.
“What agentic has done is it really has solidified the fact that even very mature security programs, at some point, will likely fail,” Case said. “When it comes to cyber resilience and business resilience, the impact that this has had is that it’s really become a part of the security conversation.”
For theCUBE’s Bertrand, cyber resiliency is not a supporting function, but a gating condition: “There’s simply no trusted AI in the enterprise without a prerequisite cyber-resilient IT and data infrastructure,” he said. “Resiliency at the core is what enables autonomy at scale.”
Data integrity remains the foundation beneath enterprise AI systems. Congruity360 InfoGov Inc., for example, has emphasized the importance of eliminating redundant and outdated data before it feeds AI systems.
“We’re seeing the early adopters leverage our technology in the reduction of infrastructure costs,” said Mark Ward, chief operating officer of Congruity360. “By eliminating anywhere from 60% to 70% of the data, by eliminating rot, we’re able to reduce the amount of AI compute and AI storage required on the backend.”
That changes the measure of cybersecurity success. Preventing attacks remains essential, but enterprises increasingly must also know which applications and data are critical, determine whether those assets remain trustworthy and restore operations quickly when defenses are breached.
Operational resilience moves closer to real time
That same shift toward faster recovery and operational resilience is also evident in the strategies of InfoScale and Infinidat Ltd., a Lenovo company.
InfoScale is pushing the resilience conversation beyond restoring infrastructure and data after disruption toward maintaining a trusted operational state while an incident is unfolding. In a recent conversation with Case, InfoScale Director of Product Management Joseph D’Angelo said the traditional approach to resilience has been rooted largely in infrastructure failures, while cyberattacks and AI are expanding both the attack surface and the potential fallout.
“We know that that has changed,” D’Angelo said. “The attack surface is growing tremendously; the exposure, the fallout, all of that is increasing exponentially — so must then the response and … the way that you envision your cyber resiliency posture.”
That shift underpins InfoScale’s focus on autonomous operational resilience, which combines application awareness, continuous protection and automated response with the goal of keeping critical operations running rather than waiting for conventional recovery to begin. It also aligns closely with the summit’s broader question of how enterprises can protect the operational state of the business as AI increases the speed and complexity of cyber risk.
Infinidat is approaching the issue from the enterprise storage and data protection layer. In an interview with theCUBE’s Bertrand, Chief Marketing Officer Eric Herzog emphasized that AI systems are ultimately dependent on trusted data, making cyber protection of both primary and backup storage increasingly important.
“It’s all about the data,” Herzog said. “The core is the data, which is why you need next-generation data protection on your primary storage, which is what AI would use. You need next-generation data protection on your backup, as well.”
Infinidat’s InfiniSafe portfolio combines immutable snapshots, cyber detection and recovery capabilities designed to help organizations identify clean recovery points and avoid restoring compromised data. Herzog has also emphasized the importance of shrinking recovery times. During an earlier theCUBE Cyber Resiliency Summit interview, he pointed to a demonstration in which Infinidat recovered 2.5 petabytes of primary storage in four seconds.
“You need to have cybersecurity on primary storage and on backup storage,” Herzog said. “If you’re not including storage in your comprehensive cybersecurity strategy, that is a huge miss.”
Recovery becomes part of AI readiness
As AI moves deeper into production, cyber resilience is becoming part of the infrastructure decision itself. Enterprises need to know not only how systems are protected, but how quickly critical data, applications and operations can be restored when defenses fail.
That puts recovery architecture, trusted data and operational continuity alongside compute, storage and networking as core elements of AI readiness. The organizations best positioned to scale AI will be those that can maintain confidence in the data feeding their systems, isolate compromised environments and restore essential services without prolonged disruption.
Those priorities will frame much of the discussion at the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, where Dell, InfoScale, Infinidat and other industry leaders will examine how cyber resilience is being built into the infrastructure supporting production AI.
TheCUBE event livestream
Don’t miss theCUBE’s coverage of the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, with broadcasts Oct. 27-28 in NA and Oct. 28-29 in EMEA and APJ. Plus, you can watch theCUBE’s event coverage on-demand after the event.
How to watch theCUBE interviews
We offer you various ways to watch theCUBE’s coverage of the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, including theCUBE’s dedicated website and YouTube channel. You can also get all the coverage from this year’s events on SiliconANGLE.
TheCUBE podcasts
SiliconANGLE’s “theCUBE Pod” is available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube, which you can enjoy while on the go. During each podcast, SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier and Dave Vellante unpack the biggest trends in enterprise tech — from AI and cloud to regulation and workplace culture — with exclusive context and analysis.
SiliconANGLE also produces our weekly “Breaking Analysis” program, where Dave Vellante examines the top stories in enterprise tech, combining insights from theCUBE with spending data from Enterprise Technology Research, available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube.
Guests
During the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, theCUBE’s coverage will feature discussions with enterprise information and security leaders on the architecture, policies and operating models required to enhance AI trust and reliability. Stay tuned for our complete guest list.

articles.title: 32GB dethrones 16GB as top RAM capacity in gaming rigs despite memory shortage — AMD closes in on Intel with record 48.4% CPU share
articles.text:
32GB dethrones 16GB as top RAM capacity in gaming rigs despite memory shortage — AMD closes in on Intel with record 48.4% CPU share
Gamers are seemingly willing to invest in their gaming PC despite crushing RAM prices.
Despite being in the midst of an unprecedented memory chip shortage, it seems that gamers are still willing to invest in their gaming PCs to extract the best performance out of their favorite titles. The September 2026 Steam Survey results show that 42.22% of the surveyed units now have 32GB of system RAM — a 4.77% increase compared to the previous month — while 16GB configurations have shrunk by 3.38%, falling to just 37.82%.
We’ve also seen increases in “weird” memory configurations — 24GB has grown to 2.56%, increasing by 0.34%, while 48GB inched up to 1.46% after a 0.26% increase.
This comes as a surprise, as some manufacturers have reintroduced laptops with 8GB of RAM even as Microsoft called 16GB the new “practical starting point,” and recommended 32GB as the future-proof “no worries” configuration for gaming. It should be noted, though, that the company quietly erased this suggestion after it released 8GB base models for its Surface laptops a few months later.
It’s quite possible that memory capacities were always destined to increase for gamers, especially as titles become more demanding. Minecraft, which hasn’t updated its system requirements for 17 years and is known for being potato-PC-friendly, even increased its recommended memory to 16GB earlier this year, forcing players on older systems to switch to the Java Edition or play retro games instead. Because of that, the memory shortage may have merely postponed the inevitable reign of 32GB RAM on gaming PCs.
Another metric we’ve been following in the survey results is AMD’s slow but relentless march toward taking away Steam Survey market share from Intel. Team Red’s 48.37% market share across all platforms is the highest we’ve seen so far this year, with Team Blue now at just 51.63%. The May 2026 Steam Survey showed AMD at a little under 45% — at this pace, it’s possible that it will overtake Intel in just a matter of months.
If we break it down by operating system, 52.59% of Windows users are on Intel, while 47.41% use AMD. Intel may have an advantage here compared to the overall result, but it’s just a tiny margin, and the trend shows that AMD is gaining ground month after month. The difference between Intel and AMD is more glaring when it comes to Linux users, with an overwhelming 66.18% preferring Team Red over Team Blue’s 33.71%.
The Steam Survey is far from scientific and may not even reflect the broader movement of the overall PC market. But with Steam reporting a peak of more than 38 million concurrent players at the time of writing, the survey still offers a useful snapshot of what’s happening in the gaming PC market.

articles.title: Android Auto ne fonctionnera bientôt plus sur des millions de smartphones
articles.text:
Les possesseurs de smartphones Android fonctionnant sous Android 10 vont peut-être devoir changer d’appareil s’ils souhaitent pouvoir continuer de connecter celui-ci au système Android Auto embarqué dans leur véhicule.
Des utilisateurs ont rapporté sur Reddit avoir reçu une notification au moment de connecter leur smartphone à leur véhicule indiquant que leur « téléphone ne sera bientôt plus pris en charge » et que « Android Auto cessera bientôt de fonctionner sur [leur] téléphone ».
Android Auto bientôt accessible à partir d’Android 11 ?
L’affichage soudain de ces avertissements sur des appareils anciens semble indiquer que Google envisage de relever très prochainement la configuration minimale requise pour connecter un smartphone Android en filaire avec un système compatible Android Auto.
Jusqu’à présent, seule la connexion sans fil imposait l’utilisation d’un smartphone fonctionnant au moins sur Android 11 pour utiliser Android Auto, la connexion filaire nécessitant elle au minimum un appareil sous Android 9. Le fait que Google affiche cet avertissement sur des appareils fonctionnant sous Android 10 laisse supposer que la firme de Mountain View pourrait mettre la configuration minimale requise pour la connexion filaire à Android Auto au même niveau que la connexion sans fil.
Et cela ne serait pas une grande surprise. Car Google a déjà revu plusieurs fois la configuration minimale requise d’Android pour l’utilisation d’Android Auto. En 2022, Google mettait ainsi fin à la prise en charge d’Android Auto avec les appareils fonctionnant sous Android 8 Oreo. En 2024, l’entreprise opérait une nouvelle révision du système minimal requis, et demandait au moins un appareil sous Android 9 Pie.
Surtout, les développeurs de l’appli Open HeadUnit, qui permet de transformer un smartphone en récepteur Android Auto, avaient récemment remarqué des signes avant-coureurs d’une potentielle révision des conditions minimales requises pour l’utilisation d’Android Auto, certaines fonctionnalités de projection automatique ayant été désactivées sur les appareils sous Android 10 et inférieurs.
Des millions de smartphones potentiellement privés d’Android Auto
Si Google n’a pour l’heure pas confirmé directement cette nouvelle configuration minimale requise sur ses pages de support, la mise en place de celle-ci pourrait laisser quelques millions d’appareils sur le carreau. Des smartphones bloqués sous Android 10, comme les Samsung Galaxy S9 et Galaxy Note 9, ou encore le Sony Xperia XZ2, pourraient par exemple faire partie des appareils bientôt privés d’Android Auto.
Les utilisateurs concernés, s’ils souhaitent continuer de profiter d’Android Auto, n’auront donc pas d’autre choix que d’envisager l’achat d’un nouveau smartphone plus récent, à moins qu’une ROM alternative basée sur Android 11 et compatible avec leur appareil existe.

articles.title: Command-line tool quickly removes Apple Intelligence from macOS 27
articles.text:
A new tool is allowing Mac users the ability again to easily turn off Apple Intelligence with one click and free up to 12GB of storage.
Unlike with previous versions of macOS, macOS 27 Golden Gate doesn’t have a toggle for turning off Apple Intelligence. That makes disabling AI features that you may not want more difficult. It also means that the AI models necessary for running Apple Intelligence will take up space on your disk, even if you don’t use them or if you go through your settings to individually find and disable AI capabilities.
In response, a developer known as Om Lahore on GitHub last week created RemoveMacAI, a command-line tool that allows macOS 27 users to “turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27″ in a way that is “fully reversible,” per the GitHub page. They said that Apple’s Intelligence models take up “about 12GB,” but the models can actually take up over 30GB, The Verge noted.
RemoveMacAI “turns off Siri, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension, and all the summaries, then it deletes the models and stops macOS from downloading them again. Dictation still works because it’s a separate setting,” the developer said in a Reddit post first spotted by MacRumors.

articles.title: We attended Fortinet's Cybersecurity Summit in Calgary to learn about cyber resilience
articles.text:
Seventeen billion. That’s how many cyberattacks hit Canadians last year, making Canada the second-most targeted country in the world for ransomware, with nearly 400 Canadian organizations extorted. While cyberattacks aren’t new, they are growing in prevalence and sophistication, and reality is that many companies don’t have the knowledge or expertise to stay one step ahead of hackers and scammers.
These were among the challenges discussed at the Fortinet Cybersecurity Summit West 2026, marking the global conference series’ Western Canadian debut, which brought together customers, partners, and cybersecurity leaders to explore the ideas and technologies facing Western Canada’s cyber future.
The agenda tackled pressing themes like securing AI transformation, the rise of a new cybercrime economy, closing the cybersecurity skills gap, and AI-driven threats targeting the industrial systems that power Alberta’s economy. It was also an event that highlighted Fortinet’s investment in Canada and generated excitement for the new $30 million Cybersecurity Innovation Hub that recently opened its doors in Calgary.
“It’s not just a building; it’s a community hub,” Pedro Paixão, Fortinet’s Senior Vice President of Latin America and Canada Sales, tells MobileSyrup. “We want people to come in, test the technologies, simulate their environments, and make sure that security tomorrow is going to be better than what they have today.”
Cybersecurity in Western Canada
Alberta is a particularly attractive target for cybercrime, as its energy sector, agriculture, and public services represent the kind of high-value targets that sophisticated criminals are increasingly focused on. The consequences of a successful attack would be dire. Ask yourself, what would happen if that critical infrastructure were to become unavailable?
“It’s about protecting not just one institution or infrastructure, but providing resiliency to the whole economy and country that, without those things, can’t function,” Paixão explains.
The AI influence
Conference keynote speaker and Fortinet’s Vice President of Global Threat Intelligence Derek Manky described the influx as a “worldwide pandemic of cybercrime.” What used to be a lone hacker in a basement or an organized criminal enterprise has transformed into an AI-powered attack generation, capable of breaking into systems and creating playbooks for attacking at a faster pace.
It also doesn’t help that people are sending private documents, emails, and pictures to AI services just so they can write a better email to their boss, or generate an image of what they would’ve looked like in the 80s. Information that was once only leaked by bad actors and disgruntled employees is now offered up willingly. For public sector organizations, keeping sensitive data on Canadian soil is a top priority.
“Public sector customers hold a lot of data, and need to protect a lot of data, and that data needs to stay in Canada,” says Gordon Phillips, Regional Vice President, Western Canada Sales, at Fortinet. “Our Calgary office supports data sovereignty by adding to the multiple data centres and workplaces we already have.”
Fortinet by the numbers
Fortinet has been investing in Canada for 26 years, and now employs over 2,750 people across the country, with additional major campuses in Burnaby and Ottawa. As organizations across Western Canada modernize their operations, Fortinet’s expanded Calgary presence brings more expertise, technology, and resources closer to the customers navigating that shift.
The innovation hub was developed with the support of the Government of Alberta, Invest Alberta, and Calgary Economic Development – a reflection of how seriously Alberta’s institutions are taking cybersecurity.
So, how exactly is Fortinet closing the cybersecurity skills gap? At the foundation of everything it does is industry-recognized certification and training, which takes place in a 4,000-square-feet state-of-the-art facility that can handle teams of up to 30 people in the Calgary Innovation Hub alone. That capacity is expanded when including the Burnaby and Ottawa campuses. In 2022, Fortinet set a goal of training one million people within five years, and hit that goal six months early.
But education doesn’t stop with working professionals. Fortinet is developing the future of the workforce and empowering students of all ages to be tech-educated with cyber courses from kindergarten to university level.
As part of that commitment, Fortinet has also established a new annual scholarship with the University of Calgary, awarding $3,000 a year for five years to a student pursuing a degree in computer science or engineering.
“Our lives are online, so we can’t escape not touching a phone every day,” says Paixão. “The importance is starting with the people, then the institutions, then the companies. If we don’t invest at all levels, we’re basically leaving some of it behind.”
Looking ahead
It can all sound a bit frightening at the macro level, but when it comes to the future of cybersecurity, both Paixão and Phillips remain hopeful.
“We have wonderful ideas around the Calgary Innovation Hub,” says Phillips. “Training facilities will upskill talent, it’ll provide cybersecurity awareness, and the idea is to just reduce the number of threat vectors in any way we can.”
“The future in terms of cybersecurity as an industry has a lot of room to grow,” adds Paixão. “And the future here in Canada is the expansion of our footprint. We want to hire more talent and develop more talent, and those things are very exciting.”
Learn more about Fortinet’s impact in Canada.

articles.title: Creíamos que Fukushima estaba encerrada en un sarcófago como Chernóbil. La realidad es mucho más compleja
articles.text:
Aunque es habitual pensar que Fukushima tuvo la misma solución que Chernóbil y que todo se resolvió con un colosal sarcófago de hormigón, lo cierto es que la realidad es muy diferente y mucho más compleja. Y es que desde que ocurrió el terremoto que después desencadenó el gran tsunami, hace ya quince años, el interior de los reactores es un tema polémico que a día de hoy sigue despertando cierta controversia.
Lo que pasó. El 11 de marzo de 2011, Japón sufrió en sus costas orientales un terremoto de magnitud 9.0, como cuenta Business Insider. Esta sacudida tuvo como consecuencia un tsunami de olas de más de 10 metros que alcanzaron la central nuclear de Fukushima Daiichi, dando lugar a un incidente peligrosísimo. El agua inundó los equipos eléctricos y los generadores diésel de emergencia, provocando la pérdida de alimentación eléctrica necesaria para mantener la refrigeración. Como consecuencia, tres de los reactores que estaban en funcionamiento de la planta sufrieron fusiones del núcleo y se produjeron diversas explosiones de hidrógeno durante los tres días siguientes, provocando una fuga de materiales radiactivos y contaminación en la zona.
Las primeras mediciones detectaron niveles elevados de radiactividad en los alrededores de la central. El accidente acabó siendo clasificado como nivel 7 en la Escala Internacional de Sucesos Nucleares y Radiológicos (INES). Solo otro desastre nuclear ha alcanzado ese mismo nivel. Efectivamente: Chernóbil en 1986.
Preparados para el terremoto, no para el tsunami. Según la Asociación Mundial Nuclear, el terremoto, que duró unos 3 minutos, hizo que se apagaran automáticamente los once reactores de las cuatro centrales nucleares de la región afectada y ocho de ellos lograron parar en frío en cuatro días. Sin embargo, los tres de Fukushima Daiichi no lo consiguieron, ya que todo el recinto quedó inundado por el maremoto. La inundación dejó fuera de servicio prácticamente toda la alimentación eléctrica de emergencia; solo sobrevivió un generador diésel refrigerado por aire en la unidad 6.
A diferencia de la central de Prípiat, aquí no hay ningún sarcófago. En los meses posteriores al accidente de 1986, se levantó un sarcófago de emergencia con el objetivo de contener las emisiones radiactivas del infame Reactor 4. Posteriormente, en 2015, se instaló El Arca, una enorme estructura de confinamiento diseñada para limitar la dispersión de materiales radiactivos y facilitar el desmantelamiento del antiguo sarcófago. Sin embargo, en Fukushima, no existe una estructura de confinamiento equivalente que encapsule los tres reactores dañados.
La estrategia ha sido bastante diferente: mantenerlos refrigerados, controlar el agua contaminada y avanzar progresivamente hacia la retirada del combustible fundido. Lo que sí existe es una especie de complejo industrial donde los equipos de la central siguen interviniendo regularmente para vigilar los reactores, inyectar agua e intentar extraer el combustible.
Más de 150 m3 de agua al dia. Según Space Group, cada día se inyectan en los tres reactores dañados unos 150 metros cúbicos de agua para enfriar de forma continua los residuos de la fusión que siguen emitiendo calor incluso hoy, quince años después del accidente. Esta cantidad de agua equivale a más de sesenta bañeras llenas hasta rebosar y sirve para evitar que la temperatura aumente peligrosamente y se produzcan reacciones sin control.
Aunque se ha intentado, nunca se ha conseguido retirar el combustible fundido por completo, debido a las dificultades de acceso a estos reactores y a la intensa radiactividad que les rodea.
Una decisión polémica. Después de usarla para refrigerar los núcleos dañados, ¿qué pasa con esos 150 m3 de agua contaminada? Esta agua se somete a un proceso de tratamiento mediante el sistema ALPS, diseñado para eliminar la mayor parte de los radionúclidos. El tritio es la principal excepción, ya que no puede separarse del agua. Según France24, se hace en niveles considerados seguros, según los estándares nacionales e internacionales.
Desde agosto de 2023, Japón está liberando esta agua tratada y diluida en el océano. La decisión provocó la oposición de organizaciones ecologistas, parte de la comunidad pesquera y algunos gobiernos de la región. En 2021, varios expertos independientes de derechos humanos de la ONU también expresaron su preocupación por los posibles efectos sobre la salud y el medioambiente.

articles.title: La nueva herramienta de IA de McDonald’s evaluaría cuánto están dispuestos a pagar los clientes en cada establecimiento
articles.text:
McDonald’s estaría utilizando cada vez más inteligencia artificial para fijar los precios de su menú en Estados Unidos y en otros mercados globales. La estrategia busca aumentar las ganancias de la sede central, aunque implica riesgos de alejar a los clientes y atraer la atención de las autoridades antimonopolio.
Reuters revisó capturas de pantalla del motor de precios de la compañía tomadas en agosto de 2026 y entrevistó a nueve fuentes con conocimiento directo de la estrategia de la cadena de hamburguesas.
Cómo funciona el algoritmo que calcula la disposición a pagar de cada cliente
El sistema de fijación de precios de McDonald’s utiliza algoritmos de aprendizaje automático que analizan de forma continua datos de millones de transacciones diarias en los casi 14.000 restaurantes de la marca en Estados Unidos. Con esa información, genera lo que la compañía denomina “el precio óptimo” en cada establecimiento para cada producto del menú, desde las Big Macs hasta el café con descuento para personas mayores.
La herramienta evalúa cuánto están dispuestos a pagar los clientes de cada tienda en particular. Las capturas de pantalla de la interfaz que utilizan los franquiciados, revisadas por el medio citado, muestran mensajes como: “Su restaurante muestra una sensibilidad media al precio”, una valoración basada en parte en la “disposición de los clientes a pagar en su zona”.
La plataforma también incorpora información pública sobre precios obtenida de los menús en línea de restaurantes cercanos de la competencia, como Wendy’s y Burger King. Ambas cadenas afirman no utilizar inteligencia artificial en sus propias decisiones de precios.
Según tres franquiciados consultados por Reuters, este sistema ha ampliado las diferencias de precio que ya existían para un mismo producto entre restaurantes, incluso entre distintos barrios dentro de una misma zona.
Diferencias de precios entre locales de una misma cadena
Una comprobación de precios realizada por el medio citado en septiembre a través de la aplicación móvil de McDonald’s reveló disparidades entre establecimientos cercanos. Un restaurante de la compañía en Fresno, California, vende una Big Mac a 5,69 dólares, mientras que otro local de la misma marca, a tres kilómetros de distancia, cobra 6,89 dólares por el mismo sándwich, un 21% más.
No se pudo confirmar si esa diferencia de precio responde a las recomendaciones del sistema de inteligencia artificial o a otros factores ajenos al algoritmo.
La empresa sostiene que sus franquiciados tienen libertad para fijar sus propios precios. Sin embargo, cinco propietarios de restaurantes declararon a la agencia que la compañía los presionó para que utilizaran las herramientas de fijación de precios basadas en inteligencia artificial.
Un documento de franquicia de junio muestra que McDonald’s registra de forma detallada las desviaciones de los franquiciados respecto a las recomendaciones del sistema.
En enero de 2026, la compañía comenzó a exigir a sus franquiciados que “participaran de forma constructiva con el consultor y las herramientas de precios aprobados por McDonald’s” como parte de sus nuevos estándares comerciales, según una comunicación interna enviada a los franquiciados.
La respuesta de McDonald’s ante las críticas por sus precios
En un comunicado, McDonald’s afirmó que los costos y otros factores varían entre sus establecimientos, y que incluso restaurantes separados por pocos kilómetros pueden pertenecer a mercados distintos.
La compañía describió su portal de precios como “una herramienta, no una imposición, diseñada para ofrecer recomendaciones específicas para cada restaurante y ayudar a los franquiciados a brindar valor a los clientes y tomar decisiones comerciales informadas”.
En una reunión con inversores, la compañía en cuestión señaló que su sistema de precios resulta importante para una apuesta corporativa más amplia por la asequibilidad, y que los franquiciados ven la necesidad de ofrecer productos económicos en el menú para atraer a los consumidores de bajos ingresos.
La compañía no está sola en esta tendencia. Otras cadenas de comida rápida recurren a la inteligencia artificial para optimizar precios y operaciones, entre ellas Yum Brands, la mayor cadena de restaurantes del mundo por número de establecimientos y propietaria de KFC y Taco Bell.
El riesgo antimonopolio que enfrenta McDonald’s con sus franquiciados
A medida que el uso de la inteligencia artificial se generaliza en el sector, los tribunales y reguladores estadounidenses examinan si ciertas prácticas de fijación de precios algorítmicas pueden facilitar la coordinación ilegal entre competidores, categoría en la que a veces se incluye a los propios franquiciados de una misma marca.
McDonald’s advierte a quienes acceden a su portal de precios que podrían ser objeto de escrutinio relacionado con las prohibiciones antimonopolio, ya que los propietarios de sus restaurantes “pueden ser competidores” entre sí, según las capturas de pantalla de los términos legales del portal revisadas por Reuters en agosto.

articles.title: Windows 11 déraille : des jeux et applications plantent depuis la dernière mise à jour
articles.text:
Windows 11 a enchaîné deux livraisons en septembre : une mise à jour de prévisualisation le 22, puis la version 26H2 le 29, déployée progressivement depuis. Dans la foulée, Microsoft a confirmé le 2 octobre un problème connu : les programmes qui décodent le son AC-3, le format Dolby Digital, peuvent se fermer brutalement, au lancement ou en pleine lecture. Jeux, lecteurs multimédias et applications de productivité sont concernés, sur les trois moutures du système, 24H2, 25H2 et 26H2 fraîchement arrivée.
Un codec de l’ère du DVD au cœur de la panne
La panne remonte à la mise à jour KB5124010 du 22 septembre et suit depuis dans les livraisons suivantes : « certaines applications qui requièrent le décodage du son AC-3 (Dolby Digital) peuvent se fermer de façon inattendue ». Les victimes sont surtout des logiciels anciens, ceux qui s’appuient sur le décodeur intégré de Windows plutôt que sur le leur. L’AC-3, popularisé par le DVD, traîne encore dans d’innombrables bandes-son de jeux et de vidéos, et Microsoft annonçait déjà la fin de son support maison en mai 2024.
Lire aussi : Cette appli contourne les restrictions de Microsoft pour installer Windows 11 26H2 sur les très vieux PC
La fiche officielle du bug ne nomme aucun logiciel, ne propose aucun contournement et n’impose aucun blocage de déploiement. La seule promesse tient en une ligne : « une résolution dans une future mise à jour de Windows », sans date. Des joueurs rapportent par ailleurs, depuis la même mise à jour, des plantages sur des titres protégés par anti-triche, Battlefield 6 en tête. Ces incidents restent des signalements : Microsoft n’a confirmé aucun lien, et parmi ces plantages, seul le dossier AC-3 a droit à une fiche officielle.
Le 13 octobre, le bug peut devenir l’affaire de tous
KB5124010 est une mise à jour optionnelle, installée par celles et ceux qui vont la chercher dans Windows Update ou qui ont activé la réception des nouveautés en avance. Son contenu doit en revanche être intégré à la mise à jour obligatoire du 13 octobre, le traditionnel Patch Tuesday. Sans correctif d’ici là, le bug voyagera avec elle vers l’ensemble du parc Windows 11.
En août déjà, la mise à jour mensuelle faisait planter ARC Raiders et THE FINALS, la faute à des pilotes d’éclairage RGB. Deux mois, deux mises à jour, deux fournées de jeux cassés. Fin 2024, l’histoire avait pris une autre ampleur avec la 24H2 et les jeux Ubisoft, Assassin’s Creed en tête. Microsoft avait alors bloqué le déploiement sur les machines concernées pendant près de deux mois, le temps que l’éditeur corrige. Cette fois, aucun garde-fou de ce genre n’est en place.
En pratique, si vous n’avez ni installé de mise à jour optionnelle ni basculé sur la 26H2 ces dernières semaines, vous êtes tranquille jusqu’au 13. Si vous avez installé la préversion et qu’un programme se ferme à la lecture d’une vidéo, le coupable est tout trouvé, et il faudra patienter : ni réglage ni rustine au programme. Le jour du Patch Tuesday, un détour par les notes de version avant de cliquer ne sera pas du luxe.

articles.title: 7 Books that teach you how to think under pressure
articles.text:
7 Books that teach you how to think under pressure
Discover 7 insightful books that teach you how to stay calm, make better decisions, and think clearly when facing pressure and uncertainty.
Pressure is an unavoidable part of life. Whether it arrives as a looming deadline, a difficult decision, a personal setback, or an unexpected crisis, the ability to think clearly under stress often determines how well we respond.
While pressure can cloud judgment and trigger emotional reactions, it can also become an opportunity to develop resilience, focus, and confidence.
The good news is that clear thinking under pressure is not simply an inborn trait. It is a skill that can be learned and strengthened over time. Some of the best insights on decision-making, mental toughness, emotional control, and resilience can be found in books that explore how people navigate challenging situations.
Here are seven books that can help you stay calm, think clearly, and make better decisions when the stakes are high.
1. The Comfort Crisis by Michael Easter
Modern life often shields us from discomfort, but growth happens when we learn to face challenges. Easter explores how embracing controlled hardship can build resilience, confidence, and the ability to stay calm under pressure.
2. The Art of Clear Thinking by Hasard Lee
Written by a former U.S. Air Force fighter pilot, this book examines how people can make better decisions in high-stakes situations. Lee shares practical strategies for reducing panic, evaluating risks, and thinking clearly when every second counts.
3. Building a Second Brain by Tiago Forte
Pressure often comes from information overload. Forte's book teaches readers how to organise knowledge effectively so they can think more clearly, make decisions faster, and reduce mental stress during demanding situations.
4. The Scout Mindset by Julia Galef
Galef argues that the best thinkers approach problems with curiosity rather than defensiveness. The book teaches readers how to evaluate situations objectively, challenge assumptions, and make better decisions under pressure.
5. The Courage to Be Disliked by Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga
Based on the ideas of psychologist Alfred Adler, this book explores how people can stop seeking constant approval from others. It offers insights into handling criticism, pressure, and anxiety with greater confidence.
6. Peak Mind by Amishi P. Jha
Neuroscientist Amishi Jha explains how attention works and why stress can impair decision-making. The book provides research-backed techniques for improving focus and maintaining clarity during challenging moments.
7. The Extended Mind by Annie Murphy Paul
This book challenges the idea that thinking happens only inside our heads. Paul explores how our surroundings, relationships, and physical actions can help us solve problems and make better decisions when under pressure.
Final thoughts
Pressure has a way of revealing our habits, thought patterns, and emotional responses. While stressful situations cannot always be avoided, our ability to navigate them can improve through practice and learning.
These seven books approach the subject from different angles- psychology, philosophy, leadership, history, and personal development- but they share a common lesson: clear thinking under pressure comes from preparation, perspective, and resilience. The more we develop those qualities, the better equipped we become to handle life's most demanding moments.

articles.title: Aux États-Unis, bientôt plus de documents pour s'offrir une RTX 5090 que pour acheter une maison ?
articles.text:
Acheter une carte graphique était simple autrefois, c'est maintenant un parcours du combattant chez certains revendeurs, surtout pour certains modèles de chez NVIDIA. Alors, pour les Américains, outre le budget, est-il plus facile d'acheter une RTX 5090 ou un ranch dans le Texas ?
Les restrictions sur les cartes graphiques se font de plus en plus nombreuses au fil des mois et de la crise de la RAM. Les composants électroniques et semi-conducteurs globalement, subissent de fortes pressions en raison des demandes massives pour les serveurs d'intelligence artificielle. Mais un revendeur exige des demandes pour le moins étonnantes.
Plusieurs revendeurs, pour l'instant qu'aux États-Unis
C'est Micro Center, un revendeur américain, qui demande à ses clients de signer un formulaire d'engagement avant d'acheter une NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. Un client ayant acheté une station de travail PowerSpec AI90 dans le magasin de Tustin en Californie, a été contraint de remplir une déclaration spécifique.
Alors, qu'est-ce que ce document ? Il demande déjà les coordonnées, à savoir le nom complet de l'acheteur, l'adresse personnelle ou professionnelle le cas échéant, une pièce d'identité officielle, mais également un numéro de téléphone et une adresse mail.
L'acheteur doit préciser le lieu d'installation du produit et son usage prévu. Le formulaire contient également une clause bien spécifique, laquelle exprime clairement :
« Aucune exportation - sans exception. Micro Center ne vendra pas ce produit à un acheteur qui aurait l'intention de l'exporter, de le réexporter, de le revendre, de le transférer ou de le faire quitter les États-Unis, quelle qu'en soit la destination. »
En d'autres mots, la carte est vendue sur le territoire américain, et elle y reste ad vitam æternam. Le revendeur n'a pas expliqué les raisons de cette demande assez spéciale, mais on peut imaginer qu'avec la crise des composants actuelle, les quantités sont limitées.
D'autres revendeurs également sur le coup
Si sur les réseaux sociaux, d'autres clients affirment ne pas avoir eu ce type de demande lors de leurs précédents achats, un autre revendeur, Central Computers, aurait imposé un formulaire encore plus long lors de la vente de cartes graphiques.
En cause, on peut surtout trouver les exportations vers la Chine. En effet, les cartes offrant les performances d'une RTX 4090 ou des performances supérieures sont interdites à l'exportation vers la Chine depuis novembre 2023.
- Des performances démesurées
- La qualité d'image du modèle Transformer
- La multi-frame generation
Récemment, les autorités américaines ont intensifié leur vigilance envers les tentatives de contrebande et d'exportations de produits vers la Chine. Ce, depuis que trois employés de Supermicro sont soupçonnés d'avoir illégalement exporté pour 2,5 milliards de dollars de matériel NVIDIA.
L'efficacité réelle de ce formulaire reste toutefois à démontrer. Il ne contient pas de numéro de série du GPU vendu et aucun contrôle à domicile ne semble possible. La mesure pourrait en revanche dissuader les reventes entre particuliers.

articles.title: Flagged by the Machine: How Google Ads Suspended an Open-Source macOS Term as Malicious
articles.text:
Automated verification pipelines inside major distribution platforms continue to create operational bottlenecks for systems utility developers. Przemyslaw Alexander Kaminski, the creator of RACE, an open-source native macOS terminal multiplexer written in Rust, recently detailed the automated suspension of his ad distribution account following an ad campaign launch. Despite distributed release binaries passing native operating system notarization and independent antimalware inspections, security policy crawlers flagged the developer account under compromised site and malicious binary designations. The incident highlights the disconnect between developer tools utilising advanced POSIX process orchestration and automated safety heuristics.
RACE differs from conventional grid-based terminal multiplexers such as tmux by implementing an infinite canvas architecture where shell surfaces can be arbitrarily positioned, resized, and grouped. Architecturally, the multiplexer detaches command execution from window layout lifecycles, guaranteeing that child interactive shells persist across desktop application restarts or UI crashes. Under macOS, this requires managing pseudoterminal pairs and background worker processes through either an internal PTY host daemon or an external dtach backend.
Generate with Gemini based on information provided in the original blog post
Automated security scanners evaluate binary safety and web endpoints by analysing file signatures, static strings, and dynamic process execution patterns. In typical desktop application spaces, an executable that persistently forks orphaned background workers capable of receiving arbitrary command-line input shares behavioural signatures with persistent backdoors and remote access trojans.
When Kaminski provisioned campaigns pointing to the product documentation domain and binary downloads, the campaign platform flagged the destination infrastructure for malicious software violations. A manual verification sweep by the author revealed clean reports across third-party malware analyzers as well as the Google's own diagnostics tools. Google Search Console and the Google Safe Browsing verification service reported zero compromised assets across the domain root and download infrastructure.
// Diagnostic payload submitted during automated appeal review
{
  "target_binary": "RACE.dmg",
  "notarization_status": "Apple Notarized Developer ID",
  "google_safe_browsing": "CLEAN",
  "search_console_security": "NO_ISSUES_DETECTED",
  "virustotal_positives": 0,
  "process_lifecycle": "documented_pty_multiplexing"
}
Attempts to remediate the suspension uncovered circular dependencies inside the platform's automated enforcement loop. Submitting diagnostic reports via standard appeal interfaces resulted in deterministic rejections without disclosing the specific binary hash, rule match, or network artefact triggering the policy flag. Seeking account support was blocked by prerequisites that the underlying security suspension must be resolved first.
To isolate whether runtime daemon persistence caused the flag, the developer modified the lifecycle teardown routines in version 1.0.39, introducing explicit user prompts and process cleanup hooks to terminate orphaned multiplexing threads upon parent deletion. A later edit to the post underlines that the policy suspension was ultimately rescinded only after community escalation surfaced the operational deadlock to engineering teams:
Through the apparent magic of Hacker News, my Google Ads account has been reinstated. Still no explanation of what triggered the suspension, but thank you to everyone who helped make it visible (and/or fixed).
The case illustrates the systemic tension between security automation and non-standard systems programming. As platform operators rely increasingly on black-box behavioural models to inspect software ecosystems, developers building legitimate native utilities that manage processes, manipulate memory maps, or hook low-level kernel abstractions face growing friction across distribution and commercial infrastructure. Engineering teams distributing developer-focused binaries must anticipate false positives by documenting process topologies and isolating persistent worker agents from primary UI binaries. Kaminski stated in his article that he will continue his fight on all possible paths, even in the EU Court.

articles.title: Controlling the brain with light earns a physiology Nobel
articles.text:
Over decades of research, scientists have built up a partial picture of what specialized cells within the brain and spinal cord do. By studying how the brain develops, they could identify genes that were active in different populations of neurons and where in the brain those neurons resided. In some cases, these genes could then be used to genetically delete the neurons, allowing us to get some indication of what they might be doing, building on the information we’ve obtained from studies of brains with damaged regions.
But this approach has its limits. The brain is flexible enough to potentially adapt to the loss of some cells, and their loss early in development may alter the development of any neurons they would have normally formed connections with. It would be far more informative to activate and shut down the neurons in an otherwise intact brain.
Today’s Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine rewards three people—Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel—who developed our ability to do precisely that. Starting from studies of single-celled algae that are attracted to light, these and many other researchers built an entire field of study that we now call optogenetics: using light to alter the behavior of nerve cells marked by the activity of individual genes.
From algae to human cells
Nerve impulses are generated by proteins called ion channels, which sit in the membrane and allow charged atoms to cross it. The nervous system uses a population of ion channels that are only active under specific circumstances, like when they sense a neurotransmitter or experience voltage changes. It’s this fine level of control that allows specialized nerve cells to send impulses only under specific circumstances, keeping the brain from descending into a haze of electrical noise.
So if we want to find out what any of the multitudes of specialized nerve cells might be doing, the easiest way is to hijack this system: force the cell to send ion-based impulses when we tell it to, and see how the animal’s behavior changes.
The Nobel Committee notes that this idea was obvious enough that people tried several methods of doing so before developing optogenetics. But it turns out “the easiest way” did not mean “easy,” and most of these methods didn’t end up widely used because they involved some combination of needing to insert multiple genes, supplying the nerve cells with some very specific chemicals, or using lasers at an intensity that physically damaged the cells.
The ultimate solution, it turned out, was lurking in a single-celled algae called Chlamydomonas. The organism’s single cell is remarkably complicated, having two flagella that help it move around, and an eye spot that detects the light it moves toward. People had been studying the organism for quite some time as a model for basic biological processes.
This is where Hegemann, then working at Berlin’s Humboldt University, entered the picture. He and his coworkers managed to hook an electrode up to a Chlamydomonas and showed that exposing it to a flash of light resulted in a very rapid influx of ions, suggesting the light was triggering an ion channel to open. As other scientists started scanning the messenger RNAs made by Chlamydomonas, Hegemann spotted a couple of genes that were similar to a light-activated ion pump found in an archaeal species.
Suspecting these might be responsible for the ion fluxes in Chlamydomonas, Hegemann used RNA interference to block their activity. This did limit the flow of ions in response to light, clearly implicating these genes in the organism’s light sensing.
At that point, Hegemann started an extended collaboration with Nagel, then at the University of Würzburg, an expert in ion fluxes. They showed that one of the two genes was selective for only letting protons (which you can think of as a hydrogen ion) into the cell, while the other would allow a broad range of positively charged ions through. They were also sensitive to somewhat different wavelengths of light. The proteins also used a chemical relative of Vitamin A to sense light, just as the receptors in our eyes do. Collectively, this class of proteins is now termed “channelrhodopsins.”
Nagel was instrumental in broadening the use of channelrhodopsins, showing that the genes that encode these proteins could work everywhere from developing frog embryos to cultured human cells. He went on to show that, when active in the neurons of a small worm called C. elegans, exposing the worms to light could cause them to alter their behavior.
Lighting up the brain
Deisseroth and his coworkers at Stanford then played key roles in developing this into a broadly useful technology. They showed that the channelrhodopsins work in neurons, and the ion fluxes they trigger are transmitted as nerve impulses. They also found more members of the channelrhodopsin family, some of which are sensitive to different wavelengths of light. A version that allows negatively charged chlorine ions into the cell was also discovered, allowing researchers to selectively shut down nerve cells.
At the same time, Deisseroth and his team worked on the engineering side of the problem, developing compact light sources and small, flexible fiber optics that allowed the system to act in the brains of animals that were free to move about and behave relatively normally.
The result has been nothing short of a revolution in our ability to understand what different populations of nerve cells are doing. If we know a gene is active in a small population of nerve cells, then we can use the mouse version of that gene to activate channelrhodopsin there and start testing how light changes the behavior of the resulting mice.
We’ve described work that relies on optogenetics a dozen times or more. And the Nobel Committee cites its use in everything from understanding how memories are stored to figuring out what signals wake mice from sleep. In one amazing set of experiments they note, a research group took an area of the brain known to be needed for maternal care and showed it contained specialized cells that performed one of a long list of functions, like triggering mothers to search for their pups, or governing physical interactions with them.
Channelrhodopsins have even been used to restore limited light sensing in a patient with a form of blindness in which their rod and cone cells die off.
One of the clearest signs of how significant this development is has been the widespread adoption of optogenetics. While the three people being honored made key contributions to its development, they have only made a relatively small contribution to its use. Instead, the studies we see that rely on optogenetics are largely done by other people who recognized its utility and refined and extended it.
The award is also very timely for the US, where the current administration has been pushing for cutbacks in fundamental research and shifting funding to its priorities in applied fields like AI and quantum computing. It’s hard to imagine a more fundamental scientific question than “how does this bit of pond scum move to ensure it gets enough light for photosynthesis?” And it’s definitely the sort of question that gets asked without any sense that the answers would ultimately have practical applications.
But science’s story, again and again, has been one where seemingly trivial research has revolutionized entire fields of study and ultimately had implications for human health and technology. The Nobel Prize Committee, in honoring a clear breakthrough, has inadvertently provided us with a reminder of that story.
John is Ars Technica's science editor. He has a Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry from Columbia University, and a Ph.D. in Molecular and Cell Biology from the University of California, Berkeley. When physically separated from his keyboard, he tends to seek out a bicycle, or a scenic location for communing with his hiking boots.

articles.title: WhatsApp vai barrar o login em celulares com sistema desatualizado • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
WhatsApp vai barrar o login em celulares com sistema desatualizado
Medida da Meta impede acesso à conta até que o usuário atualize o Android ou iOS do aparelho.
O WhatsApp vai bloquear o login em celulares com versões desatualizadas do Android e do iOS. A medida é aplicada pelos servidores da Meta e impede o acesso à conta até que o sistema operacional seja atualizado.
A mudança impede que o usuário entre na conta até a atualização do sistema. O bloqueio foi identificado pelo site especializado WABetaInfo e tem sido liberado gradualmente para contas selecionadas.
Ao tentar acessar o WhatsApp em um aparelho considerado incompatível, o usuário recebe o aviso “Atualize o software do seu telefone para entrar novamente”. A mensagem, que não pode ser ignorada, orienta a verificar as configurações do aparelho e instalar uma atualização disponível.
O WhatsApp já impõe restrições a celulares mais antigos: atualmente, o aplicativo só pode ser baixado nas lojas oficiais em aparelhos com versões superiores ao Android 6.0 ou ao iOS 15.1. O novo bloqueio, porém, é diferente por ocorrer no login e já está sendo liberado gradualmente para usuários. A empresa ainda não informou quais versões do sistema operacional serão afetadas.
De acordo com o site, a medida busca garantir que o app seja executado em um ambiente com mecanismos de segurança atualizados. A criptografia de ponta a ponta, por exemplo, não impede que um celular comprometido vaze informações que aparecem na tela ou que são armazenadas no aparelho.
No aviso, o WhatsApp menciona que versões antigas podem colocar o celular em risco de ataques por malware. Se um invasor conseguir comprometer o próprio sistema do celular, poderá ter acesso a informações antes ou depois de elas serem protegidas pela criptografia do aplicativo.
No que diz respeito à segurança no app, a empresa tem lançado outras ferramentas mirando especialmente a aplicação de golpes através do mensageiro. Em agosto, o WhatsApp trouxe recursos como novas opções de chave de acesso e a expansão do sistema de verificação em duas etapas, com possibilidade de definir um código alfanumérico. A Meta também investe em inteligência artificial para identificar mensagens fraudulentas e alertar as possíveis vítimas.

articles.title: Namespace raises $42M to build out developer-focused compute cloud - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Namespace raises $42M to build out developer-focused compute cloud
Zurich-founded developer infrastructure startup Namespace Labs Inc. today announced it raised $42 million in Series B, led by Scale Venture Partners, to give developers powerful compute infrastructure to speed up software engineering work.
NEA, 20VC, Essence, Burst Capital and Susa Ventures also joined the round. The round comes just seven months after the company’s Series A, led by NEA, bringing total funding to $65 million.
Founded in 2022 by former Google engineer Hugo Santos, Namespace delivers a specialized compute stack for developers that runs artificial intelligence agents, developer tools, continuous integration, container builds, testing and more at lightning speeds. This lets software engineers move faster through the software lifecycle because the underlying compute can keep up with demand.
As AI agents become more pervasive in coding, the coding lifecycle has gotten tighter. Even as DevOps and continuous delivery and integration cycles shorten the time from feature to deployment, testing cycles have squeezed the way that software is delivered, sometimes down to the smallest feature request – often developers work on micro-versions where multiple tiny changes are wrapped up daily or weekly and then pushed into production.
The 2025 DORA Report, run by Google LLC’s Cloud division, found that 16.2% of respondents deployed on demand, 6.5% deployed between hourly and daily, and 21.9% deployed between daily and weekly.
This is generating constant labor and an appetite for compute that can handle the speed needed to build, validate, test and deploy while maintaining quality. Generic cloud virtual machines may handle the durability question, but they’re not generally built with developer tools in mind; they must be configured and constantly monitored and they are often sold with enterprise scale in mind, not developer needs.
To handle the role and purpose of development, Namespace purpose-built its compute cloud for ephemeral storage, running with high-speed networking and cache support.
Additionally, the company is investing in Mac architecture. An increasing number of applications are built for MacOS and Apple Inc. hardware and run on iPhone and MacBook. Many of today’s infrastructure providers skip Mac, which means that most developers building for iOS or macOS have to go to specialized providers.
The company said the new funding will help it expand its data centers, including its fleet of Mac hardware. The company supports multiple OS versions, including Sonoma, Sequoia, Tahoe, and Golden Gate, and can handle up to 12 virtual central processing units and 56 gigabytes of memory.
Namespace currently supports build and test environments across Mac, Windows and Linux.

articles.title: Cohere rolls out Enterprise AI platform North 2
articles.text:
Cohere has released a new version of its North AI system that lets users deploy rival agents without compromising security, while keeping cost and complexity down.
According to the company, North 2 can now set up AI agents to manage more complex, multi-step processes independently. North 2 also offers reusable agents people can call on, shared knowledge assets an entire organization can draw on, and the ability to retain content from previous sessions to improve automations over time. North also offers a drag-and-drop visual workflow builder, real-time performance monitoring, and integrations with tools already in use.
Security
On security, Cohere says North Admin, a feature that lets users see how their AI is used, also lets teams enforce guardrails at the individual agent level to safeguard data and prevent leaks.
The platform also offers tools to monitor service performance and add detailed logs, autonomy policies designed to take only authorized actions, and ongoing security testing, including red-teaming exercises and third-party vulnerability scanning.
One company currently using North is Bell Cyber, which partnered with the company to bring “government-grade” security to its agentic AI usage.
Interestingly, Cohere also noted that North 2 is “model-agnostic,” so clients can use Cohere’s model or swap to models from other companies to suit their needs. Believe it or not, Cohere actually expects this, as Paul Teyssier, the company’s vice-president of product for AI, told The Logic that the company anticipates clients will keep using its tech for most of their regular AI applications, but could choose alternatives for experimentation and niche tasks (such as if another model outperforms Cohere’s models).

'An impressive camera that delivers amazing video quality and beautiful slow-motion scenes': DJI's Osmo Pocket 3 with built-in three-axis stabilization is reduced in price for a limited time
The rotating OLED screen makes switching between horizontal and vertical video easy
DJI's Osmo Pocket 3 is one of the top action cams we've ever tested - and easily one of the most popular for creators. This is a 4K handheld camera is small enough to carry almost anywhere, designed to give creators a more dedicated video setup without the bulk of conventional camera equipment.
• Best for: Travelers, vloggers, creators, and anyone who wants stabilized 4K video without carrying a full-size camera and separate gimbal.

ActiveTrack 6.0, 10-bit color, and a rotating 2-inch OLED touchscreen add plenty of creative flexibility.
Today's best DJI Osmo Pocket 3 deal
The DJI Osmo Pocket 3 features a 1-inch CMOS sensor, 4K/120fps recording, three-axis mechanical stabilization, a rotating 2-inch OLED touchscreen, ActiveTrack 6.0, 10-bit color, stereo audio, and microSD storage.
Why we recommend it

The Pocket 3's combination of size, sensor, and mechanical stabilization makes it particularly appealing for travel, vlogging, and shooting while moving. The 1-inch CMOS sensor can record 4K footage at up to 120fps, while D-Log M and 10-bit color give you more flexibility when color grading footage afterwards.

At $395 rather than $439, you're saving $44, which works out to a cut of 10%. This is one of the lowest prices we've seen for the Osmo Pocket 3, although it has previously been down to around $378 elsewhere.
For more shopping options, take a look at our roundup of the best action cameras, and our advice on which DJI cameras to buy.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the DJI Osmo Pocket 3 camera if...
You shoot travel videos, vlogs, family events, or other footage while moving and want something more purpose-built than a smartphone without resorting to a full-size camera setup.
❌ Skip the DJI Osmo Pocket 3 camera if...
Still photography is your main priority, or you simply need an inexpensive camera for occasional video. Much of the Pocket 3's appeal comes from features such as the gimbal, ActiveTrack, and high-frame-rate 4K recording.

articles.title: Modder brings original Xbox emulation to jailbroken PS5 — XPSemu plays Halo 2 and Forza as PS5 emulators outnumber its 15 exclusives
articles.text:
Modder brings original Xbox emulation to jailbroken PS5 — XPSemu plays Halo 2 and Forza as PS5 emulators outnumber its 15 exclusives
Developer claims Halo 2 runs at 60fps.
Popular Xbox emulator Xemu has just been ported to jailbroken Sony PlayStation 5 consoles. Reddit user u/Yzenxam posted a video of their PS5 running the emulator with three games installed: Forza Motorsport, Halo 2, and Crash Bandicoot. The port, playfully named XPSemu, is on their GitHub page: ZiZc3.
The modder has stated that XPSemu is Xemu and is nothing different; all they did was allow it to be opened on the PS5 as an application. Xemu uses QEMU’s TCG JIT to translate the Xbox CPU to the PS5 CPU in realtime, allowing for fast performance compared to interpretation-based translation.
Xemu has its own translation for the Xbox’ NV2A GPU and uses a Vulkan renderer to work with modern GPUs; thanks to the modder behind PS5_Vulkan, Xemu can talk to the PS5’s AMD GPU through the open-source RADV Vulkan driver — allowing the porter to run Xemu as a native PS5 application.
ZiZc3 also added their own touches as explained in their GitHub repository:
"On top of the port, XPSemu adds its own controller-friendly dashboard, per-game settings, cover art, play time, game patches, a performance overlay, a per-game log and a set of CPU optimizations made for the PS5's Zen 2 processor."
While QEMU's TCG JIT is relatively fast, it still leaves plenty to be desired. ZiZc3 explains that the emulated Xbox CPU is the bottleneck, loaded at 85-97% while the PS5 GPU remains mostly idle. As a consequence, the resolution multiplier up to 3-4x barely affects performance, and upscaling with FSR does not add performance.
The developer further explains that the PS5's Zen 2 cores are slower per core than a fast PC, and CPU-heavy games suffer from this. In terms of performance, ZiZc3 has provided a table of their experience and performance of the games on XPSemu:
| XPSemu performance as stated by developer |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Halo 2 | ✅ Good | 30 FPS stock. With the Halo 2 60 FPS patch: 51-60 FPS in the opening, 36-50 in gameplay.. | 
| Forza Motorsport | ⚠️ In-game | 30 FPS (its cap) in menus and intro, 15-21 FPS while racing. | 
| Fable: The Lost Chapters | ⚠️ In-game | 22-30 FPS in many areas (30 is its cap), 10-20 FPS in heavy areas. | 
| Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex | ✅ Great | Runs smoothly. | 
As of writing, there are fewer than 15 fully PS5-exclusive games, while the number of emulators the PS5 can run is increasing by the week. On X, users BrinoTk and Mihawk9_9 (the same person behind PS5_Vulkan) announced their Xbox 360 and PS5 Proton projects on the same day, with the Xbox 360 emulator already available for testing.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The PS5 already has emulators for PS1-3, with PS4 emulation technically built in. Non-PlayStation emulators besides the XPSemu include the Nintendo Switch, Wii U, 3DS, and of course the myriad of emulators available on RetroArch as well. On the other side of the coin, the PS5 itself has also been emulated on PC and the Xbox Series X — at this point, the lines are blurring faster than owners know what to do with their jailbroken PS5.

Éblouis par une Tesla la nuit ? Cette nouvelle mise à jour change la donne
articles.text:
Avec la mise à jour 2026.38, Tesla ajuste désormais en temps réel l'inclinaison des feux de croisement de certaines Model 3 et Cybertruck, en réponse aux critiques sur l'éblouissement. Mais seuls quelques chanceux peuvent en profiter.
Les phares Tesla traînent une réputation encombrante, celle de l'éblouissement qu'ils provoquent, qui suscite régulièrement des plaintes. Le sujet a même pris un tour réglementaire cet été, avec le rappel de plus de 20 000 voitures aux États-Unis. Avec la mise à jour 2026.38, qui date d'il y a quelques jours à peine, le constructeur répond sans convoquer personne à l'atelier. Certaines Model 3 et certains Cybertruck reçoivent un système qui incline physiquement les projecteurs pour garder les feux de croisement pointés vers la route. L'intention est louable, mais le déploiement reste confidentiel, et rien ne dit encore que cette correction suffira à solder le dossier. Certains Français ont pu en profiter.
Des phares Tesla qui corrigent leur regard en temps réel
C'est Teslarati qui a mis la nouveauté en lumière, en relayant un message publié sur X par le compte Frunk To Trunk. La fonction accompagne la version 2026.38 du logiciel de bord, diffusée à distance depuis le 30 septembre, à la manière d'une mise à jour tout ce qu'il y a de plus classique. Son nom, Dynamic Headlight Leveling, pourrait littéralement se traduit par « nivellement dynamique des phares ». En gros, ici, la voiture ajuste elle-même l'inclinaison de ses feux de croisement, sans aucune pièce à changer. Le but est de mieux éclairer la route pour le conducteur, sans aveugler ceux qui arrivent en face ni ceux qui roulent devant.
Pour bien comprendre, pensez à une lampe torche. Il suffit de lever légèrement le poignet pour que le faisceau quitte le sol et file droit dans les yeux de la personne d'en face. Une voiture connaît le même phénomène dès que son avant se relève, par exemple lors d'une forte accélération, quand le poids bascule vers l'arrière, dans une côte raide ou avec un coffre lourdement chargé. Le logiciel commande alors des moteurs internes, qui abaissent les projecteurs d'autant, en temps réel. Le conducteur n'a rien à régler, car tout se fait automatiquement.
Attention à ne pas confondre avec les feux matriciels, dont les Model 3 et Model Y profitent depuis début 2024. Eux s'occupent des feux de route, les « pleins phares ». Leur faisceau est découpé en une multitude de segments LED, que la voiture peut allumer ou éteindre un par un. Quand un véhicule se présente, seuls les segments qui le viseraient s'éteignent, ce qui crée une bulle d'ombre autour de lui sans plonger le reste de la route dans le noir. Le nivellement dynamique, lui, ne touche pas à la forme du faisceau des feux de croisement. Il se contente en effet de le relever ou de l'abaisser. Ce sont deux outils distincts, qui se complètent.
Une mise à jour Tesla encore très discrète sur nos routes
Le déploiement de cette mise à jour intervient dans un contexte assez particulier pour le constructeur auto d'Elon Musk. Le 4 août 2026, Tesla a dû rappeler 20 349 véhicules aux États-Unis (18 735 Model Y et 1 614 Model 3 de première génération), dont les feux de croisement envoient trop de lumière vers le haut. La NHTSA, l'agence fédérale chargée de la sécurité routière, avait refusé de classer ce défaut comme sans conséquence. Tesla indiquait alors que sa solution était encore en développement.
Cette mise à jour règle-t-elle pour autant le problème ? Frandroid invite à la prudence. Le nivellement change la direction du faisceau, mais pas la façon dont la lumière s'y répartit, c'est-à-dire que si un phare envoie trop de lumière dans sa partie haute, l'abaisser ne suffira pas forcément à tout corriger. Surtout, la fonction a besoin de moteurs de réglage, et toutes les voitures n'en sont pas équipées. Teslarati parle d'ailleurs d'une atténuation possible pour les modèles qui disposent de ce matériel, pas d'une réparation en bonne et due forme.
Encore faut-il évidemment recevoir la mise à jour. Les premiers servis sont des Model 3 et des Cybertruck aux États-Unis et aux Émirats arabes unis, sans lien évident avec une version matérielle précise. En France, comme nous avons pu le constater, tout le monde ne peut y prétendre. Au 1er octobre, moins de 1 % de la flotte avait installé la 2026.38, selon les données de TeslaFi et Tessie citées par Tesla Oracle.

articles.title: TVS Automobile Solutions raises Rs 425 Cr from UAE investor to expand myTVS brand
articles.text:
TVS Automobile Solutions raises Rs 425 Cr from UAE investor to expand myTVS brand
The funding will be used to expand the conpany's myTVS auto aftermarket brand in the Middle East and North Africa markets.
TVS Automobile Solutions, which owns the omnichannel automotive aftermarket brand myTVS, has raised Rs 425 crore in a Series D round of funding led by CE-Invests, the investment arm of UAE-based Crescent Enterprises.
TVS Automobile Solutions is part of the $3 billion TVS Mobility Group. Prior to this funding round, myTVS had raised around Rs 690 crore, comprising Rs 203 crore from Lingotto (Exor) in 2022 and Rs 487 Cr from Castrol in 2023.
According to a statement, the latest funding will support myTVS' overseas expansion with initial focus on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) markets, where both the companies see potential to adapt and scale its technology and capabilities for mobility and fleet businesses.
For CE-Invests, this partnership provides an opportunity to leverage myTVS' technology platform and capabilities in the automotive aftermarket in the Middle East. For myTVS, CE-Invests brings deep regional market understanding and business networks that can support the identification and development of new opportunities across MENA.
The statement noted that myTVS has developed an integrated automotive aftermarket platform that combines digital capabilities with a physical service network for OEMs and EV manufacturers to access a broad range of vehicle service and maintenance solutions.
R Dinesh, Director, TVS Automobile Solutions said, “This investment is a further proof that this technology-led platform is capable of delivering a similar experience in other markets. This will further enable the company to scale up its operations in India and the MENA region and continue to maintain its profitable growth.”
According to the statement, myTVS has achieved EBITDA breakeven in FY26 and expects its business to grow 25–35% in the near term. The company is accelerating investments in AI and technology to support this growth, strengthen the scalability of its platform, and build the capabilities required for its next phase of expansion.
Badr Jafar, CEO of Crescent Enterprises said, “When India’s scale, talent and innovation connect with the UAE’s capital, infrastructure and regional reach, each market becomes a platform for the other’s growth. That reciprocal model creates value far beyond either country and reflects principles that have long shaped Crescent Enterprises’ investment and partnership strategy.”
Edited by Swetha Kannan
