articles.title: La voiture électrique bat un record en Europe : comment la hausse des carburants et les modèles pas chers ont fait exploser la demande — Frandroid
articles.text:
On entend souvent dire que les ventes de voitures électriques ne progressent pas assez vite. Il est vrai que certains automobilistes ont encore quelques réticences. C’est particulièrement le cas sur le prix et l’autonomie. Cependant, les choses se passent tout de même plutôt bien pour le marché européen.
C’est ce que montre le rapport publié ce lundi 5 octobre par l’ONG Transport & Environment (T&E), qui milite pour des transports plus propres. Selon ses calculs, les ventes de voitures électriques ont battu un record dans l’Union européenne entre janvier et août 2026.
Au total, 1,64 million de voitures électriques ont été vendues sur cette période, soit 45 % de plus que sur les huit premiers mois de 2025. Dans les ventes de voitures neuves, leur part de marché atteint 22 % sur les huit premiers mois de l’année, six points de plus qu’à la même période en 2025. Sur les routes, l’électrique reste pourtant très minoritaire, avec seulement 3 % du parc automobile de l’UE en 2025, selon T&E.
En août, cette part a même grimpé à 28 % dans l’UE. À titre de comparaison, la part de marché des voitures électriques atteignait 38 % en France et 32 % en Allemagne en août, selon T&E. Elle est même montée à 42 % en France en septembre.
D’ailleurs, selon l’ONG, la France et l’Allemagne tirent la croissance. À elles deux, elles ont pesé environ la moitié des ventes de voitures électriques de l’UE au premier semestre 2026. Au deuxième trimestre 2026, pour la première fois, les ventes d’électriques ont dépassé celles des modèles essence (hors hybrides) sur un trimestre complet.
La flambée des carburants pousse aussi vers l’électrique. Selon T&E, au 14 septembre 2026, une voiture électrique rechargée à domicile coûtait 50 % de moins à l’usage qu’un modèle essence ou diesel, le gazole ayant pris 38 % depuis le début de la guerre en Iran.
    Pour aller plus loin
Prix en baisse, carburant en hausse : rouler en voiture électrique coûte 33 % de moins qu’une thermique en Europe
            
Un choix de plus en plus vaste
Ce succès s’explique en partie par une offre plus large. On compte désormais plus de 150 modèles électriques disponibles dans l’UE, dont près de 40 lancés au premier semestre. Au total, une soixantaine est attendue sur l’ensemble de l’année 2026.
On pourrait penser que les constructeurs chinois sont désormais majoritaires. Ce n’est pas le cas : les marques européennes représentent près de 60 % des modèles électriques disponibles, contre 21 % pour les marques chinoises. Ces dernières accélèrent toutefois, avec 11 nouveaux modèles au premier semestre, contre 16 pour les européennes. Côté ventes, sept des dix électriques les plus vendues dans l’UE sont signées par des constructeurs européens.
Parmi ces nouveautés, les modèles abordables sont de plus en plus nombreux. D’ici à la fin de l’année 2026, 16 modèles à moins de 25 000 euros seront disponibles, deux fois plus qu’en 2025. Quatre d’entre eux passeront sous les 20 000 euros. D’ici à 2028, une dizaine de voitures électriques devraient être proposées à 20 000 euros ou moins, dont la Renault Twingo, la Volkswagen ID.Up et des modèles Dacia. En parallèle, le groupe Stellantis prépare une famille de petites électriques (E-Car) autour de 15 000 euros, dont une renaissance de la Citroën 2CV.
    Pour aller plus loin
La Citroën 2CV électrique à 15 000 € arrive : voici les premières images du concept présenté à Paris
            
L’offre bon marché reste toutefois en retrait face au thermique. Au premier semestre 2026, T&E recense 24 voitures électriques à moins de 30 000 euros, quand les modèles thermiques sont près de trois fois plus nombreux à ces prix (et 4,4 fois plus entre 20 000 et 25 000 euros).
L’ONG estime que l’écart sera en grande partie comblé d’ici à 2028 sur la tranche des 20 000 à 25 000 euros, à condition que l’offre thermique ne bouge pas. Les ventes de modèles électriques à moins de 25 000 euros devraient, elles, être multipliées par sept en 2026 par rapport à 2024.
Environ 60 % des modèles abordables attendus d’ici à 2028 devraient être produits dans l’Union européenne. Ces modèles peuvent aussi être rentables. Selon T&E, Renault dégage une marge plus élevée sur ses plus petites électriques, comme les R5 et R4, que sur les plus grandes, comme la Mégane ou le Scénic E-Tech.
L’ONG demande toutefois à l’Europe de ne pas assouplir ses objectifs de CO₂ pour les voitures neuves, en cours de renégociation. Sinon, la part de marché stagnerait à 22 % en 2030 au lieu d’atteindre les 47 % estimés.
Ces projections visent la proposition de l’eurodéputé italien Massimiliano Salini (PPE), rapporteur du texte sur les normes CO₂ des voitures au Parlement européen. Elle prévoit notamment d’étaler l’objectif 2030 sur cinq ans et d’accorder une exemption aux voitures roulant aux biocarburants. Les 47 % correspondent, eux, à la proposition de la Commission européenne. Le Parlement et les États membres doivent voter cet automne. À mi-parcours de la période 2025-2027, les constructeurs ont déjà comblé 75 % de l’écart avec leur objectif de CO₂, et la moitié du marché est déjà en règle, selon T&E.

articles.title: Cloudflare Introduces CLI for AI Agents, Sunsetting Wrangler
articles.text:
Cloudflare recently launched the open beta of cf, a new open-source, agent-focused command-line interface for interacting with Cloudflare services through a unified CLI. Written in TypeScript, it provides structured output and command discovery to make Cloudflare’s APIs easier for both developers and AI agents.
The hyperscaler argues that introducing a new CLI avoids conflicts with LLMs’ learned behavior around Wrangler, allowing cf to adopt agent-focused design changes without the compatibility constraints of an established tool. Matt Taylor, senior product manager at Cloudflare, and Samuel Macleod, senior systems engineer at Cloudflare, explain why a new CLI was needed:
Wrangler was hand-built with each product team contributing and taking their own approach to their command developer experience. Enforcing patterns across teams was virtually impossible, even across our ~280 command paths. We had inconsistent terminology across d1 info, hyperdrive get, workflows describe as each team came up with their own practices at different times.
Released under either the Apache License 2.0 or MIT license, the cf CLI is designed for agent-driven development, with command discovery, JSON output optimized for both humans and agents, and a new TypeScript-based cloudflare.config.ts configuration format. It also makes Vite the default development environment, providing a consistent local development experience and plugin support.
Using Cloudflare’s OpenAPI schemas as the source, cf can cover more than 3000 API operations, compared with roughly 280 functions built into Wrangler. Taylor and Macleod add:
We wanted to both standardize what we had and make a massive expansion, all at once. Forge — Cloudflare’s new unified API generation pipeline — enabled us to do this, building on the idea of generating our CLI commands directly from the API schema that powers our API documentation and SDK generation.
In a popular Hacker News thread, community reaction has focused in particular on the choice of TypeScript for a CLI, with discussion around startup time, portability, and dependency management. User slowin comments:
I don't understand why this is written in TypeScript. This is a great example of how agents can write code (I'm sure they wrote `cf`), yet having fundamental computer science knowledge is still critical. Do not force your users to manage the dependencies of your CLI. Do write your CLI in a compiled language.
Cloudflare argues instead that TypeScript makes configuration easier for both humans and agents by providing type safety and LSP support, enabling agents to understand and modify configurations more accurately. The authors contrast this with TOML and JSONC, where schema information is less accessible to agents, and say programmatic configuration can also reduce configuration duplication. Ashish Ganda notes on LinkedIn:
Cloudflare's new cf CLI outputs JSON by default. Not a table. You have to ask for the table (...) Tables are for eyes. JSON is for parsers.
Cloudflare makes JSON the default output format, allowing agents to filter and transform the output into the format required by human users while avoiding the table output used by default in Wrangler. The company plans to deprecate Wrangler after the cf open beta ends, release a final major Wrangler version directing users to cf, and provide 18 months of maintenance support to allow migration.

articles.title: AMD EPYC "Verano" CPUs to Use New SB1 Socket, Dynatron Cooler Listing Suggests
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
AMD EPYC "Verano" CPUs to Use New SB1 Socket, Dynatron Cooler Listing Suggests
AMD's upcoming EPYC "Verano" processors will apparently use a new socket called SB1. The name comes from server cooler maker Dynatron, which now states on its website that its cooling solutions support "AMD EPYC Verano on Socket SB1." Dynatron also has a product page up for a 4U active cooler listed as "SB1-4U-ACTIVE (TBD)," so the final product name is still pending. The "B" in SB1 could point to a BGA package soldered to the board, although that is a guess based on the name and nothing official. The listing doesn't help much either. Maximum power is marked as TBD, and the 128.05 x 106.6 x 130.7 mm dimensions are identical to Dynatron's J26 cooler for SP7, so the specs could simply be placeholders for now.
Verano is the codename for the EPYC 9006 LP, a Zen 6 part that AMD announced alongside the rest of its 6th Gen EPYC lineup. It tops out at 72 cores with boost clocks of up to 5 GHz, and it runs on 24 channels of LPDDR5X memory through replaceable SOCAMM2 modules. AMD is aiming it at AI racks as a host processor for GPU clusters, with a launch planned for the second half of 2027. The regular "Venice" chips use different sockets, namely SP7 for up to 256 cores and SP8 for up to 128. For "Verano," AMD itself hasn't revealed the socket name yet.

articles.title: Russian drones strike Ukraine’s data centers by exploiting air defense gaps
articles.text:
A surge in Russian jet-powered drone strikes on Ukrainian data centers has increasingly disrupted mobile phone and Internet services for thousands of people. Now Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and other government officials are warning of the need for more air defense capabilities, as such telecommunication outages could threaten Ukraine’s digital economy and undermine the country’s ongoing resistance to Russia’s invasion.
The Russian attacks on Ukrainian telecommunication infrastructure have focused on Ukraine’s capital of Kyiv since September 23, according to the nonprofit Reporters Without Borders. Ukraine’s digital transformation ministry reported that 100,000 households in the Kyiv region were temporarily experiencing Internet outages from those initial strikes—and Russia has only intensified its strike campaign against major Ukrainian data centers and mobile phone networks in recent weeks.
“Russian attacks on Ukraine’s telecommunication infrastructure are not new, with strikes and shelling previously damaging fiber optic lines, cell towers, and facilities belonging to mobile network companies,” said Tetiana Gaviuk, analyst for Europe at ACLED, in a post on October 1. “However, the recent concentrated attacks on Kyiv’s data centers and telecom networks stand out because multiple providers and facilities were hit within days, indicating Russia’s increased pressure on Ukraine’s digital infrastructure.”
Such repeated attacks could undermine the telecommunication networks that support Ukraine’s banks, payment systems, and public services, according to warnings from officials and industry figures, as reported by The Guardian.
Russia’s strike campaign
Russia has launched mass missile and drone attacks on Ukraine’s power grid infrastructure, railroad stations, shipping ports, and even residential apartment buildings since the first year of its full-scale invasion in 2022. But such long-range strikes have become even more damaging this year, as they have exhausted Ukraine’s supply of missile interceptors—and Russia has also upgraded many of its one-way attack drones to become faster jet-powered drones that are more difficult to shoot down.
For example, Zelenskyy stated on October 4 that Ukrainian air defenses currently intercept more than 85 percent of conventional Shahed-type drones originally developed by Iran and supplied to Russia. But such interception rates fall to just 50 or 60 percent when dealing with newer and faster jet-powered Shahed drones.

articles.title: Nvidia and CoreWeave rethink agentic AI infrastructure - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia and CoreWeave tackle the CPU bottleneck in agentic AI infrastructure
Agentic AI infrastructure must support the work between a model’s decisions as agents move from answering questions to executing tasks.
Central processing units handle much of that execution, while graphics processing units power model reasoning. Those complementary roles shape Nvidia Corp.’s planned Vera CPU deployment with CoreWeave Inc., according to Hannah Coutand (pictured, right), director of product marketing, Vera CPU, at Nvidia.
“The reason why Vera is so important is because we recognize that extreme co-design means that we look across the AI factory and we want to make sure we solve for any inefficient bottlenecks,” she said. “We recognized the CPU was becoming one of them. We didn’t set out to say, ‘Let’s go and build CPUs.’ We set out to solve this bottleneck.”
Coutand and Harsh Banwait (left), senior director of product at CoreWeave, spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and John Furrier at the Fully Connected event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed CPU requirements, sandbox performance and infrastructure security. (* Disclosure below.)
Agentic AI infrastructure puts CPU performance under pressure
As training and inference become increasingly intertwined, infrastructure must accommodate both model computation and the environments where agents act. Tool calls, application programming interface calls and SQL queries increase the execution work handled by CPUs, Coutand explained.
“I think the volume certainly plays a role,” she said. “That’s why having a CPU that handles those types of calls extremely well, with fast, beefy cores, high memory bandwidth and low latency, it handles both operating in this new world … and serves as a great foundation for simply agentic use cases [and] reinforcement learning.”
CoreWeave announced plans to offer standalone Vera CPU capacity alongside its existing infrastructure. Its Sandboxes offering provides isolated environments where agents can execute tasks during reinforcement learning and inference, Banwait explained.
“Quite recently, we also tested that with Vera CPUs, and we were proud to share that we saw about a 3x improvement in performance in terms of Sandbox startup times,” he said. “For us, it’s a very important combination of getting the performance that we need from the silicon and getting our customers the experience that they expect from a product.”
Coordinating security and performance across the AI factory
Security also shapes agentic AI infrastructure. Nvidia’s Open Agent Safety Platform combines OpenShell runtime controls with Nvidia Sentry running on BlueField-4 data processing units to provide an independent layer of monitoring and enforcement.
“They’re all in a single Vera Rubin tray, which includes Vera CPU as well as the DPU; that’s all included in the same hardware infrastructure,” Coutand said. “So, Open Agent Safety Platform, the secure runtime, which is OpenShell, runs on the Vera CPU in that tray, and DOCA Sentry runs on the DPU part.”
Operating that infrastructure requires attention to power, cooling and automation. Networking, CPUs and storage also figure in CoreWeave’s engineering priorities, Banwait explained.
“All of that needs to be able to keep up,” he said. “We’re going to continue to focus on wherever the bottleneck is so that when the entire system is kind of advancing, it’s doing that in one cohesive way. Otherwise, the weakest link in the chain kind of holds it all back.”

articles.title: ChatGPT começa a testar anúncios com imagens • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ChatGPT começa a testar anúncios com imagens
Novo formato será testado de início durante a geração de imagens; OpenAI afirma que publicidade continuará separada das respostas.
A OpenAI vai começar a testar anúncios com imagens dentro do ChatGPT. O novo formato visual será exibido inicialmente durante a geração de imagens e poderá mostrar produtos, inspirações de uso e experiências relacionadas aos serviços anunciados. Segundo a empresa, os testes começam neste mês nos Estados Unidos.
Os anúncios serão identificados e ficarão separados do conteúdo gerado pelo ChatGPT. A empresa afirma ainda que as propagandas não influenciam as respostas do chatbot.
A novidade amplia um programa de publicidade que já chegou ao Brasil para usuários das contas gratuitas e do plano Go. Até agora, as peças publicitárias exibidas no ChatGPT utilizavam formatos mais simples, com texto, nome da empresa, logotipo e um link para o produto ou serviço. O novo modelo acrescenta imagens.
O movimento faz parte de uma expansão de publicidade na plataforma. Em agosto, foi revelado que a OpenAI também testava anúncios capazes de levar o usuário a uma conversa com uma IA criada por uma empresa anunciante.
Além do novo formato, a companhia anunciou mais ferramentas para que as marcas consigam acompanhar resultados de campanhas no ChatGPT. Entre as métricas disponíveis estão cliques, conversões e testes para estimar se um projeto de publicidade realmente provocou novas vendas.
A OpenAI afirma que parceiros responsáveis pela avaliação de segurança de marcas não terão acesso às conversas privadas dos usuários. Segundo a empresa, suas políticas também impedem a exibição de publicidade em contextos considerados sensíveis.
Essa separação entre publicidade e respostas é um dos princípios adotados pela companhia desde o início dos testes. Quando a publicidade começou a aparecer no ChatGPT, a OpenAI afirmou que anunciantes não teriam influência sobre o conteúdo produzido pela IA.
A expansão dos anúncios acontece enquanto a OpenAI transforma o ChatGPT em uma plataforma cada vez mais ligada à descoberta e compra de produtos. A empresa já testou uma experiência de compras que apresenta preços, avaliações e links para lojas diretamente nas conversas. Posteriormente, também passou a permitir compras dentro do próprio chatbot em alguns mercados.
Segundo a OpenAI, as propagandas ajudam a ampliar o acesso gratuito ao serviço e representam uma fonte de receita complementar às assinaturas. Por enquanto, não há previsão de quando os anúncios com imagens serão disponibilizados no Brasil ou em outros países.

articles.title: Amazon ends secret data center pacts and pledges $1 billion to host towns — AWS promises 30,000 home efficiency retrofits amid 100 proposed bans
articles.text:
Amazon ends secret data center pacts and pledges $1 billion to host towns — AWS promises 30,000 home efficiency retrofits amid 100 proposed bans
It will also invest more than $1 billion over five years in communities hosting its facilities.
Amazon will no longer require nondisclosure agreements (NDA) with government agencies involved in its data center projects and will adhere to its new Data Center Commitment program designed to address mounting opposition to AI infrastructure, it disclosed on Friday in a blog post. The company also unveiled plans to invest more than $1 billion over five years in communities hosting its facilities. The announcements come as more than 100 data center moratoriums are being considered across the U.S., so AWS wants to make data centers more attractive to locals.
No NDAs
Amazon's decision to no longer require NDAs from government officials working with it is part of the company's newly announced Data Center Commitment program aimed at making data center building more transparent and somewhat less unpleasant to people living nearby. Among other things, the company vows to hold community open houses, disclose information about projects as early as possible, and listen to local concerns as development proceeds. Amazon also vows annual disclosure of its energy consumption and efficiency, water consumption and efficiency, and the proportion of electricity supplied by carbon-free sources.
Speaking of power usage efficiency (PUE), Amazon reports a global PUE of 1.14 for 2025, compared with an industry average of 1.25 and 1.63 for on-premises enterprise data centers. It also says its facilities were 7x more water-efficient than the industry average and that it had reached 75% of its goal to become water-positive by 2030.
Many concerns
Also, new sites will use backup generators compliant with EPA Tier 4 emissions standards. While Amazon emphasizes that new sites will use backup generators meeting EPA Tier 4 emissions standards, the commitment is somewhat ambiguous in general, as the specification limits vary by engine power and generator classes, whereas Amazon does not specify the generator classes it intends to deploy.
The company says an average U.S. data center consumes around 170,000 gallons of water per day, whereas an average Amazon facility uses less than 13,000 gallons, equivalent to 42 U.S. households. However, Amazon does not distinguish between the water consumption of a typical AWS data center designed for general-purpose cloud workloads and newly built AI data centers packed with power-hungry AI accelerators, which certainly have substantially different cooling requirements.
In general, Amazon is trying to counter concerns about the resource requirements of data centers, although some of its comparisons remain rather ambiguous.
When it comes to energy efficiency, the new Built Together initiative will add more than $1 billion to Amazon’s existing community spending. The company expects to provide more than 300,000 students with access to free community-college education over five years. It currently operates three Modular Training Centers, has six more under development, and plans another 16. Each facility can train roughly 2,000–4,000 people annually, with Amazon targeting as many as 100,000 trained workers per year by the end of 2028.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Amazon also plans energy-efficiency upgrades for more than 300 schools and community buildings and 30,000 homes, targeting energy-bill reductions of 20%–40% and savings of approximately $700 per household annually. Separately, more than 65 contracted water projects are expected to return over 8 billion gallons annually, more than twice the water Amazon says its data centers consumed in 2025.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Google limits free and AI Plus access to some Gemini models
articles.text:
Google will soon add limits to which Gemini models free and AI Plus members are able to access.
As spotted by 9to5Google, the tech giant has updated its support page to mention these new limitations. Starting Oct. 9, free Gemini users will only be able to use Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, while AI Plus subscribers will be limited to Flash-Lite and Flash (newer models like Pro not included).
Naturally, those who pay for the more premium Gemini AI Pro or Ultra subscriptions won’t have these restrictions. Additionally, Google says Gemini users will be able to choose between low, medium and high-effort options for models.
Unfortunately for people on the cheaper AI Plus plan, these changes mean reduced access to some Gemini features, though the distinctions remain muddy thanks to Google’s use of meaningless terms. For example, the company’s feature breakdown notes that AI Plus subscribers get “more” access to capable models, while AI Pro and AI Ultra get “higher” and “highest” access, respectively.
Check out the Google support doc for a full breakdown of all the changes.

articles.title: Kepler Targets 2027 for Energy-Saving HBM Alternative- EE Times
articles.text:
Kepler Computing, founded in 2018, aims to start production of memories that address HBM and SRAM “bottlenecks” in AI chips by next year, company executives told EE Times. The company is ready to work with industry partners to enter large-scale manufacturing, according to Intel Capital, an investor in Kepler.
The company, which has partnered with GlobalFoundries for production, has built its own fab to ramp up its proprietary 3D and ferroelectric memory technology. The company believes a small Kepler fablet beside a customer’s legacy fab can help leapfrog to leading nodes by multiple generations at one tenth of the investment compared to a new advanced node.
Kepler said it expects to make AI chips with partners such as GlobalFoundries without depending on EUV to reach advanced nodes.
“We look just like Micron, or SK Hynix, or Samsung,” Kepler CEO Debo Olaosebikan told EE Times. “Customers just buy a memory module from us, and then they integrate it with their chip.”
AI models are straining conventional memory architectures. Those stresses appear in rising DRAM and HBM design and manufacturing costs, higher energy use and heat dissipation, and diminishing scalability options. AI data centers are also stressing power grids. Most of the energy consumed in an AI facility is spent in data fetches between GPUs and HBM.
Monolithic stacking
Olaosebikan said the company has achieved monolithic stacking of devices within a chip that avoids thermal problems.
“That’s why we can avoid EUV,” he said. “I can take the old big transistor but just use fewer of them and put things on top of that transistor.”
The transistor on the bottom could be made with EUV.
“We’re okay with that,” Olaosebikan said. “Whatever the base node is, we’re not pushing the requirement that you must shrink that transistor. We are going to amortize the use of that transistor with new devices that we stack on.”
“We increase the memory density by a factor of two to three, and it is actually compatible into CMOS,” Kepler CTO Sasi Manipatruni told EE Times.
The company has reached a stage where it is ready to work with industry partners, Intel Capital managing director Srini Ananth told EE Times.
Manufacturing ready
“They already have partners with some of the top leaders in the industry, in the ecosystem, and the time is now for them to take this into larger scale manufacturability,” Ananth said. “It opens the door to a new scale of high-performance computing architectures; you’re not constrained any longer by two-dimensional scaling.”
SRAM scaling ended years ago around 5 nm, hindering the move to advanced nodes.
“If you can use a backend of line process to get densities that are much higher than what the boundary node supports, you are advancing Moore’s Law,” Ananth said. He called Kepler’s five co-founders a unique team with expertise across physics, material science, and chip architecture. Three of the five co-founders were formerly with Intel.
“I was, I think, the first engineer they hired to go find the next transistor,” said Manipatruni, who worked at Intel on next-generation logic. “Kepler came organically out of that effort when we figured out what is the specific architectural problem and the materials problem that we needed to be addressing. Our architecture addresses the interconnect problem for memory and increases the memory capacity and bandwidth much beyond the HBM roadmap and is not really bound by HBM physics.”
Two memories
Kepler has developed two memories that blur the lines between HBM and SRAM, Olaosebikan said.
“For practical purposes, we can think of one of the memories as an HBM replacement, and the other one can be thought of as an SRAM replacement,” he added. “Our memories are always going to be much larger capacity than you can get with SRAM, at least 10×. There will be 5× to 10× more bandwidth per watt than HBM.”
The company declined to go into detail on its ferroelectric memory.
“We think that if our foreign adversaries know what the material is and know that it allows them to circumvent EUV, they would be all over it,” Manipatruni said. “So, we are being very careful with the materials specifications. Over the past seven years or so, we went through thousands of iterations of discovering the ferroelectric; the composition, the gradients, the electrodes, the whole shebang it takes to discover that class of materials.”
Kepler’s HBM replacement will rely on 3D packaging technology the company has developed.
“When people do 3D integration, they are worried about thermals,” Kepler co-founder Rajeev Dokania said. “Our 3D architecture works around that. There’s negligible thermal overhead relative to the traditional way of doing it. That brings in a tremendous amount of bandwidth at a very low energy cost.”
The company said all its production capacity for 2027 is allocated. Kepler declined to name customers and partners outside of GlobalFoundries, saying only that they are in AI data centers as well as manufacturing. Over the longer term, Kepler also plans to develop logic chips.

Compact, sans fil et connecté, le SwitchBot Battery Circulator Fan veut trouver sa place parmi les ventilateurs d’appoint de l’été. Nous l’avons soumis à nos mesures pour voir ce qu’il a dans le souffle.

Le SwitchBot Battery Circulator Fan n'est pas le ventilateur le plus tape à l'œil du marché, mais c'est précisément ce qui fait son intérêt. Le niveau sonore reste contenu, même à pleine puissance, et la consommation électrique est presque négligeable. La veilleuse intégrée ajoute une petite touche pratique. Reste que ce format de table impose quelques compromis. Ainsi, il faudra parfois lui trouver un support pour souffler à la bonne hauteur et la présence de pales réclame un entretien régulier. Les fonctions connectées avancées nécessitent également un hub SwitchBot. Rien de rédhibitoire, mais de quoi rappeler que ce ventilateur se destine avant tout à un usage de proximité et nomade. Dans ce rôle, il est convaincant et suffisamment efficace pour apporter un vrai gain de confort pendant l'été.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: JobRunr 9, OpenXava 8, Quarkus, LangChain4j, JNoSQL, Introducing Lathe
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for September 28th, 2026, features news highlighting: the GA releases of JobRunr 9.0 and OpenXava 8.0; point releases for Quarkus, Micronaut, LangChain4j, Eclipse JNoSQL; ADK for Java and ADK for Kotlin; and introducing Lathe, a new Java language server.
OpenJDK
JEP 544, Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation, has been elevated from Proposed to Target to Targeted for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to improve application startup and warmup time such that it is instantly available with optimized native code when the HotSpot JVM starts. This enables applications to achieve peak performance more quickly and to sustain peak performance.
JDK 28
Build 18 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was made available this past week featuring updates from Build 17 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
Jakarta EE
In his weekly Hashtag Jakarta EE blog, Ivar Grimstad, Jakarta EE Developer Advocate at the Eclipse Foundation, provided an update on Jakarta EE 12, writing:
For Jakarta EE 12, the vote for including Jakarta Authorization in Jakarta EE Web Profile is ongoing. It makes perfect sense to group it together with the other security specifications there. On request from the steering committee, the timeline for Jakarta EE 12 was discussed and firmed up in the platform call this week. The timeline for Jakarta EE 12 will look like this:
- December 1 - Jakarta EE 12 Core Profile
- March 31 - Jakarta EE 12 Web Profile
- May 15 - Jakarta EE 12 Platform
One specification I, personally, really want to see included in Jakarta EE 12 Web Profile is Jakarta NoSQL. Simplifying and standardizing access to NoSQL datastores is a great feature when integrating artificial intelligence in enterprise applications. Particularly, support for vector databases for RAG is something that will be very useful. If you agree with me, or have an opinion about including Jakarta NoSQL in Jakarta EE 12, please do let us know on the mailing list or in the platform calls. The voice of the community matters!
Eclipse JNoSQL, the compatible implementation of Jakarta NoSQL was recently elevated from an incubating project to an Eclipse Enterprise for Java (EE4J) project. It has been an Eclipse project since 2017 and has been included in Eclipse GlassFish since Jakarta EE 11 as part of support for Jakarta Data.
JobRunr
The release of JobRunr 9.0.0 delivers notable changes such as: a new Chart tab in the History section of the dashboard that shows the life of a job, in Gantt chart format, with a row per state and a row per durable step; support for Micronaut 5 and Quarkus 3.40; and the addition of a warning when a serialized job is too large that will trigger an unwrap of the StepExecutionException. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes and this version 9 launch webinar. InfoQ will follow up with a more detailed news story.
OpenXava
The release of OpenXava 8.0.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: OpenXava built on Spring Boot; support for some Jakarta EE 11 specifications; and a more modern look-and-feel. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Quarkus
The release of Quarkus 3.34.0 provides bug fixes and notable changes such as: improvements to the AeshLauncher interface that hardens the signal protocol and timeout diagnostics; and an elimination of an unnecessary warning from the ResteasyReactiveJacksonProcessor class when an endpoint returns void. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes for version 3.40.1 and version 3.40.0.
Micronaut
The Micronaut Foundation has released versions 5.2.1 and 5.2.0 of the Micronaut Framework (announced here and here, respectively) based on Micronaut Core 5.2.11 and 5.2.8. Along with bug fixes and updates to many of the Micronaut ecosystem modules, new features include: experimental support for Micronaut for Python, for processing of Python source code at compile time; and a new Micronaut Jakarta EL module that serves as an implementation of the Jakarta Expression Language specification. More details on these releases may be found in the release notes for version 5.2.1 and version 5.2.0.
LangChain4j
The formal release (along with the thirty-first beta release) of LangChain4j 1.21.0 delivers bug fixes, dependency upgrades and introduces new, experimental decision models. This includes a new API consisting of the DecisionModel interface, and DecisionServices, RoutingChatModel and DecisionRouterPlanner classes. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes and tutorials for Decision Models and Decision Services.
Eclipse JNoSQL
The release of Eclipse JNoSQL 1.19.0 ships with new features such as: support for ScyllaDB; database drivers updated for Neo4J 6.3.0, InfluxDB 1.11.1, DynamoDB 2.55.7, and MongoDB 5.13.0; and improved lifecycle logging that include the Oracle NoSQL and Jakarta Persistence extensions. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Google Agent Development Kit
The release of ADK for Java 1.11.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements and new features such as: a new rewindBeforeInvocationId() method, added to the EventActions class, for rewind compatibility with ADK for Kotlin; and new thread-safe methods, immutableEvents(), addEvent(), and addEvents(), added to the Session class, to replace the now deprecated events() method. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Similarly, the release of ADK for Kotlin 1.3.0 delivers bug fixes and new features such as: a new @ExperimentalLiveApi annotation that marks a live bidirectional streaming API; and a change from null to an empty string in the initialization of the author attribute in the Event class. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Lathe
Alexey Gavrilov, Senior Software Engineer at Telenor Linx, has introduced a new Java language server, Lathe, an implementation of the Language Server Protocol (LSP). Lathe eliminates the difficulties with traditional project import and classpath or module-path configuration. It works in any editor compatible with LSP and its model comes from a Maven build such that everything remains synchronized. Lathe ships with a Neovim client and an MCP server for AI coding agents. The latest release, available this past week, is version 0.1.14.

articles.title: Votre pilote graphique pose problème ? Grâce à cet outil, vous repartez sur une installation propre !
articles.text:
Changer de carte graphique ou simplement mettre à jour son pilote peut parfois réserver de mauvaises surprises. Installation qui échoue, bugs d’affichage ou conflit avec une ancienne version, plusieurs problèmes peuvent apparaître. Display Driver Uninstaller permet alors de supprimer en profondeur les composants et résidus de l'ancien pilote afin de repartir sur une installation propre.
Il ne s’agit toutefois pas d’un outil à utiliser à chaque mise à jour. Display Driver Uninstaller intervient surtout lorsque quelque chose s’est mal passé, lorsqu'une désinstallation classique ne suffit pas ou lors d'un changement de fabricant de GPU. L'utilitaire supprime les principaux éléments associés au pilote graphique afin d’éviter qu’une ancienne installation ne vienne perturber la suivante.
Avec Display Driver Uninstaller, il faut commencer par sélectionner le fabricant du pilote graphique que l’on souhaite supprimer. NVIDIA, AMD et Intel sont pris en charge, tout comme certains GPU Qualcomm et Lisuan dans les versions récentes du logiciel. Il reste ensuite à choisir le type de nettoyage souhaité.
Le logiciel peut supprimer les fichiers, dossiers, entrées de la base de registre et autres composants liés à l'installation du pilote. Le nettoyage n'est toutefois pas nécessairement absolu : DDU peut volontairement conserver certains éléments OEM ou composants spécifiques lorsque leur suppression risque de perturber le fonctionnement de la machine.
Le cas typique est celui d’un changement de fabricant de carte graphique, par exemple lors d'un passage d'AMD à NVIDIA ou inversement. Display Driver Uninstaller permet alors de supprimer les pilotes de l'ancien GPU avant d'installer ceux du nouveau matériel. L'outil peut également être utile lorsqu'une mise à jour provoque des dysfonctionnements ou qu'une nouvelle installation refuse de fonctionner correctement.
En revanche, remplacer une carte graphique par un autre modèle utilisant le même environnement de pilotes ne nécessite pas systématiquement DDU si tout fonctionne normalement.
Display Driver Uninstaller permet également d'empêcher temporairement Windows Update d'installer automatiquement un pilote graphique pendant l'opération. Le développeur recommande par ailleurs de couper la connexion Internet ou de bloquer Windows Update jusqu'à l'installation du nouveau pilote afin d'éviter que Windows n'intervienne entre les deux opérations.
- Nettoyage approfondi des anciens pilotes
- Plusieurs fabricants de GPU supportés
- Options de nettoyage personnalisables
Une opération à préparer en amont plutôt qu’un bouton à cliquer
Il est recommandé d'utiliser Display Driver Uninstaller en mode sans échec, même si le nettoyage reste possible depuis une session Windows classique. Le développeur conseille également de créer un point de restauration ou une sauvegarde avant de commencer.
Sur un PC utilisant BitLocker, mieux vaut également vérifier que la clé de récupération est disponible avant de redémarrer en mode sans échec, certaines configurations pouvant la réclamer au démarrage.
Une fois l'ancien pilote retiré, Windows peut temporairement utiliser son pilote d'affichage générique. Ce comportement est normal : il suffit ensuite d'installer manuellement le pilote correspondant à la nouvelle carte graphique.
Avec un tel fonctionnement, Display Driver Uninstaller n’est donc pas destiné à être utilisé comme un simple logiciel de nettoyage. Il s'agit avant tout d'un utilitaire de dépannage. Son utilisation peut notamment supprimer certains réglages, profils de couleurs ou paramètres personnalisés associés au pilote graphique.
Pour un changement de fabricant de carte graphique, une installation qui tourne mal ou des problèmes qui persistent après une mise à jour, Display Driver Uninstaller peut ainsi permettre de repartir sur une installation propre avant de réinstaller le pilote.
En revanche, si le pilote fonctionne normalement et qu'une mise à jour classique s'installe sans difficulté, il n'est généralement pas nécessaire de passer par DDU. L'outil prend surtout son intérêt lorsque les méthodes habituelles de mise à jour ou de désinstallation ne suffisent plus.

articles.title: Le retour du monospace ? Renault va dévoiler l’E-Space Concept au Mondial de Paris - Numerama
articles.text:
Après plusieurs éditions marquées par de grosses têtes d’affiche, le stand Renault du hall 6 devrait surtout attirer notre curiosité avec plusieurs concepts. À quelques jours de l’ouverture du Mondial de l’Automobile de Paris (le 12 octobre 2026), Renault donne un premier aperçu d’un tout nouveau concept-car baptisé E-Space Concept.
Aux côtés des concepts Renault 8 Gordini et Renault 4 JP4x4, cette étude de style entend réinterpréter l’héritage de la première génération de l’Espace lancée en 1984, mais cette fois sans abuser du design néo-rétro.
Un gabarit de 4,70 mètres, une nouvelle signature lumineuse mais le même esprit
Derrière sa robe rouge et son losange lumineux flottant au milieu d’un jeu de pixels, l’E-Space Concept pose des jalons plutôt concrets. Avec ses 4,70 mètres de long, il reprend exactement le gabarit de l’Espace E-Tech actuel (désormais positionné comme un SUV), mais réagencé de fond en comble. L’allure du concept est une ode au monospace, mais Renault ne dit pas encore s’il ira jusqu’à le produire.
Même si Renault écrit que ce concept est « la vision réinventée par Renault du voyage et de la mobilité familiale à l’ère électrique », rien n’indique que ce concept soit 100 % électrique. Il pourrait être l’un des modèles à prolongateur d’autonomie (EREV) dont François Provost, le patron du groupe, a évoqué l’idée lors de la présentation du plan stratégique futuREady, le 10 mars 2026.
Sur le plan du style, l’élément le plus notable est la face avant, qui teste de nouvelles approches avec un imposant bandeau lumineux en « U » et en pixels. Le reste sera dévoilé le lundi 12 octobre, lors de la présentation complète sur le stand de la marque au Mondial de Paris.
Du R-Space Lab à l’E-Space : l’obsession assumée du monovolume
Cette annonce n’arrive pas de nulle part. Elle prolonge directement la trajectoire initiée à l’hiver lors de la présentation de la nouvelle stratégie du groupe (futuREady), où le losange avait surpris tout le monde avec le R-Space Lab. Ce véhicule-laboratoire de 4,50 mètres explorait déjà la modularité intérieure (sièges coulissants, triptyque vitré, boîte à gants déployable) avec une silhouette monovolume très éloignée des stéréotypes actuels.
Avec l’E-Space Concept, Renault pousse le curseur un cran plus haut en appliquant cette réflexion aux grands gabarits familiaux. L’intention est claire : prouver que l’ère électrique permet de libérer de l’espace à bord et de redonner du sens aux véhicules familiaux sans être contraint de copier les codes massifs des SUV. Alors, est-ce que les constructeurs français (Renault comme Citroën, qui a aussi un projet du genre) vont réussir à réintroduire avec succès des monospaces dans leur gamme ?

articles.title: Uniden releases its first video walkie talkie that works without wi-fi or a mobile network - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Uniden has released its first video walkie-talkie that allows for two-way video chats without wi-fi, a network or any apps.
The KVWT01 Uniden Adventure Series Video Walkie Talkie adds live video functionality to the traditional walkie-talkie form factor and all without a smartphone or wi-fi.
It has been designed for use at home or outdoors and offers has real-time two-way video with clear voice communications at a range of up to 400m in open space.
The KVWT01 has been designed with simplicity in mind and only requires a one button push-to-talk function to initiate communication.
And the device comes ready to use out of the box with no setup or connectivity required.
Also onboard are other playful features, including three voice effects and four screen viewing modes, so you can switch between self-view, remote view, and picture-in-picture.
The walkie-talkies are lightweight and have a built-in rechargeable battery, USB-C charging and adjustable volume so it’s perfect for your backyard adventures and indoor play as well as a handy addition to a camping trip and family outing.
“Walkie-Talkies have always been a simple way for kids to explore, play and stay connected, and our new Kids Video Walkie Talkie brings that familiar experience into a more interactive format,” says Brad Hales, Head of Marketing, Oceania at Uniden.
“By adding live video without relying on Wi-Fi, a mobile network or an app, we’ve created a product that gives kids more ways to play while keeping the experience incredibly simple for parents.
“We’re seeing technology become an increasingly natural part of how kids play, but it doesn’t mean it needs to be complicated.
“It is designed to offer the fun and immediacy of video communication while remaining completely standalone, no accounts, downloads or connectivity setup required.
“It’s a fresh take on a familiar category that brings together technology play and adventure in one easy-to-use product.”
The Uniden KVWT01 comes in a two-unit set and includes two USB-C charging cables and two lanyards.
The Uniden Adventure Series video walkie-talkie is available now and is priced at $69.
Customers can also purchase a 3-pack for $104.95, a 4-pack for $131.20 and a 5-pack for $157.45.

articles.title: Fin du retour en 30 jours sur Amazon : quels produits sont directement touchés ?
articles.text:
Longtemps perçue comme un geste fort pour rassurer les acheteurs, cette période de 30 jours pour retourner ses produits disparaît progressivement pour certains articles vendus sur Amazon. En modifiant ses politiques de retour pour les vendeurs, le géant du e-commerce passe à un délai de 14 jours pour les retours, selon les catégories de produits.
De plus en plus de produits n’ont plus que 14 jours pour être retournés
Ce changement, qui est effectif en Allemagne depuis 2024, s’est déroulé en deux temps. Depuis le 17 juillet 2026, vous n’avez plus que 14 jours pour formuler une demande de renvoi sur les appareils photo, l’informatique, l’électronique, les produits sans fil, la fourniture de bureau, la musique, les DVD et les jeux vidéo. Une fois que vous avez fait votre demande, vous avez 14 jours supplémentaires pour expédier le colis. Depuis le 1er août, les livres, les logiciels, les jouets, l’outillage, le bricolage, les articles de cuisine, l’automobile, les soins personnels, le home cinéma et le gros électroménager subissent le même traitement.
Comme vous pouvez le voir ci-dessus, la politique de retour a changé, aussi bien pour les produits vendus par Amazon que par des vendeurs tiers. En revanche, ceux qui expédient les produits eux-mêmes (sans passer par les entrepôts d’Amazon) gardent la possibilité d’ajuster manuellement ces paramètres dans leur espace de gestion pour proposer des conditions plus larges, obligeant dans ce cas les clients à passer par la messagerie pour organiser le renvoi d’un produit.
Les catégories de produits qui restent à 30 jours
Tout le catalogue n’est pas logé à la même enseigne et certains univers comme les vêtements, les chaussures, les montres, la bagagerie, le mobilier, le sport, le jardin, la beauté, la puériculture, les produits animaliers et la joaillerie gardent leur garantie de 30 jours. Les produits estampillés Amazon, comme les liseuses Kindle et les boîtiers Fire TV, échappent également à ce coup de rabot.
À lire : Amazon lance ses nouveaux Kindle et fait grimper les prix
On vous invite à regarder avec attention la politique de retour de chaque produit dans la mesure où un ordinateur portable ou un smartphone peut avoir un délai de 14 jours, alors qu’une montre connectée pour sport peut conserver le délai de 30 jours, selon la catégorie à laquelle elle est rattachée.

articles.title: "Los precios son una vergüenza": Ibai ha encontrado la forma perfecta de mojarse y no mojarse sobre la crisis de vivienda
articles.text:
Dice el refranero que en la mesa no debe hablarse ni de política ni de religión. Si quieres evitarte peleas, mejor dejar el fútbol al margen también. En la España de 2026 hay otro tema tan o más controvertido: la vivienda. Desde hace casi dos años el CIS nos recuerda de forma periódica que la crisis residencial es el asunto que más quita el sueño a los españoles, lo que explica que en los últimos días su conversación haya experimentado un in crescendo que ha pasado del desahucio de Maricarmen a los acampados en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid, los decretos exprés fallutos y finalmente, este lunes, una convocatoria de adelanto electoral.
No hay forma fácil de abordar el debate sobre la vivienda en España, aunque Ibai Llanos, uno de los grandes streamers del país, ha dado con la cuadratura del círculo: la forma de mojarse y no mojarse al mismo tiempo sobre el tema.
La vivienda (otra vez). En 1992 James Carvielle, estratega de la campaña de Bill Clinton, hizo fortuna con una de las frases más famosas de la política estadounidense reciente: "Es la economía, estúpido". Con ella Carvielle quiso centrar el foco de debate en el tema que, en su opinión, podía inclinar la balanza electoral a favor de los demócratas, más allá de la política exterior, marcada por el fin de la Guerra Fría y la Guerra del Golfo: el bolsillo de los votantes.
En 2026 esa frase podría repetirse tal cual, pero cambiando "economía" por "vivienda", el tema que el CIS lleva 22 meses identificando como uno de los asuntos que más preocupa a los españoles. La escalada de precios y los problemas para acceder al mercado han alentado varias manifestaciones en los últimos años, un amago de revolución (la de "las llaves") y otro de huelga de inquilinos. Ha sido sin embargo el desahucio de una anciana del Retiro lo que ha prendido la mecha, resucitando el fantasma del 15-M y agitando el debate parlamentario hasta derivar en un adelanto electoral.
ibai no se calla y habla claro sobre el tema de la vivienda en españa 👏👏👏 https://t.co/tUeSoANuCo
— ana.ツ (@bdttrp) October 4, 2026
Sumándose a la discusión. Con ese telón de fondo, el fin de semana el debate sobre la vivienda sumó una nueva voz: la de Ibai Llanos, 17 millones de seguidores en X, 28,5 en TikTok y 16,5 en Instagram. Durante una retransmisión, el streamer, seguido tanto en España como en otros países de habla hispana, decidió hacer un resumen valorativo del 'caso Maricarmen' y la situación de la vivienda en España. De entrada es importante porque no todos los influencers deciden meterse en el barro político, un terreno en el que es fácil resbalar, polarizar opiniones y ganarse enemistades.
Entre los creadores que lo hacen tampoco es habitual encontrar el tono de Ibai, quizás el único streamer masivo de España que, sin tener contenido explícitamente político, aborda con frecuencia asuntos de actualidad y temas de corte social. Destaca su puntería para captar la conversación del momento y sobre todo su tono políticamente correcto, alejado de la pronunciada ideologización de otros streamers. Su tono es moderado. Le darían 'like' los padres de cualquier chaval. Y el equipo de marketing de cualquier corporación.
¿Y qué ha dicho? Eso es lo interesante. En un tema espinoso, Ibai ha dado con una peculiar cuadratura del círculo: la forma de abordar el asunto mojándose y sin mojarse al mismo tiempo. En menos de tres minutos expone el problema con un punto valorativo, pero sin ir más allá ni entrar en causas o atribución de responsabilidad. Se queja, pero sin apuntar a nadie, con un discurso por y para sintonizar con el mayor espectro de opiniones posible. Una forma de abordar “temas políticos” de forma “política”, sin levantar ampollas.
Agustin51 le dice a Ibai que ya no es rojo por no haber ido a las manifestaciones de Sol por la vivienda. "A ver, aunque no vayas a manifestarte, puedes estar a favor de que el precio de la vivienda en España es una vergüenza. Yo no invierto en vivienda. Yo invierto en ser muy bueno en mi trabajo y ganar dinero de otra manera."
— Terreno Viral (@terrenoviral) October 4, 2026
"Da mucha pena". Tras recordar que "el tema de la vivienda" lleva "muchos años siendo vergonzoso en España", Ibai aborda el caso concreto de Maricarmen, la anciana expulsada de la casa en la que llevaba 71 años viviendo de alquiler por una sociedad inmobiliaria. "Da mucha pena. Es una señora de 87 años que sale en silla de ruedas y, joder, al final un desahucio así dices: ‘te impacta’. Pero el problema no es solo ese", arranca el streamer, que pasa a quejarse de las dificultades de los jóvenes para acceder a la vivienda.
UN VISTAZO A...
"Nosotros vivimos en un país donde yo tenía en la LVP compañeros que tienen 30 años, que han estudiado, que tienen una carrera terminada, que tienen un máster, que trabajan, y que es imposible plantearse el comprarse una casa. ¿Cómo es posible que una persona con 30 años, habiendo terminado una carrera, un master, trabajando, viva en Madrid en un piso acompañado por dos italianos que no conoce de nada, porque lo único para lo que le llega es para alquilar una habitación y sea imposible pensar en comprase una casa?"
"Un sueño es un Ferrari". "Coño, un sueño es tener un Ferrari, tener un Lamborghini, ser CEO de una empresa, montarte un restaurante, ganar una estrella Michelin, ser futbolista… Eso es un sueño", continúa Ibai, que sigue exponiendo el que, en su opinión es el meollo del problema: la vivienda elevada a la categoría de sueño inalcanzable.
"Pero es que ahora es tan imposible para mucha gente comprarse una casa que el sueño para mucha gente es poder hacerlo. Luego que por qué los jóvenes no tienen hijos. ¿Cómo vas a tener hijos? Si tienes 32 años, compartes piso con dos personas que no conoces de una mierda, cobras una mierda en tu curro y los precios de los alquileres y de las casas son una vergüenza. ¿Cómo vas a tener una familia con treinta y pico años? Me acuerdo cuando trabajaba en la LVP que tenía compañeros de treinta años y decían 'cómo me voy a comprarme una casa, bastante que pago el alquiler'".
@carric0che participaré en la próxima velada contra todos los especuladores de la vivienda
— Ibai (@IbaiLlanos) May 11, 2026
"Yo no invierto en vivienda". No es la única declaración de Ibai sobre el tema. Ni la única que bordea la misma línea, políticamente correcta y sobre todo estratégica, válida para conectar con la mayor audiencia posible. Durante otra intervención, el streamer vasco volvía sobre el asunto: "Aunque no vayas a manifestarte puedes estar a favor de que el precio de la vivienda en España es una puta vergüenza. Yo no invierto en vivienda, lo siento. Yo invierto en que soy muy bueno en mi trabajo y gano dinero de otra manera".
En mayo ya había abordado el mismo tema con un tono similar al responder a un tuit viral de un usuario que se quejaba de los precios que se estaba encontrando en Idealista con un mensaje que no tardó en sumar varios millones de visualizaciones y cientos de comentarios: "Participaré en la próxima velada contra todos los especuladores de la vivienda". Mismo tono, misma forma de abordar el problema.
¿Es el único? No. Ibai no es el único streamer que se ha pronunciado públicamente sobre el desahucio de Maricarmen. Hace poco lo hizo también el Xokas, aunque con un tono mucho más rotundo y adoptando un tono claramente crítico y polarizador. Su perfil es distinto. El discurso también.
"Le han dado un montón de oportunidades para vivir en otros sitios, pero no. Ella quiere vivir en el centro de Madrid por 500 euros. Yo también quiero vivir en el centro de Madrid por 500. ¿Por qué tiene más valor una señora que mi hijo de 25 años que también ha hecho una carrera, un máster y que quiere vivir en Madrid? ¿Por qué él se tiene que ir a vivir a la puta periferia, coger dos metros y tardar 40 minutos en llegar al trabajo? ¿La vivienda será igual para todos, no?"

articles.title: Flipkart picks up minority stake in B2B travel startup TravClan
articles.text:
Flipkart picks up minority stake in B2B travel startup TravClan
Flipkart has invested in TravClan to strengthen international holiday offerings across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel, while expanding access to global suppliers and destination support.
Ecommerce marketplace Flipkart has picked up a minority stake in global B2B travel tech startup TravClan. The move is designed to upgrade international holiday packages and expand supply on both Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel.
TravClan said it plans to use the new capital to scale its platform, deepen its global supply relationships, and expand its engineering, business development, and operational teams.
Through the deal, Flipkart taps into TravClan's network of direct global suppliers and on-ground teams. TravClan currently powers outbound travel for over 15,000 travel agents, helping them build customised itineraries, book hotels, and handle activities with 24/7 destination support. Integrating these operations allows Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel to offer Indian travelers more curated international trips with reliable support throughout their journey.
"Investing in TravClan strengthens our ability to offer international holiday packages while deepening our travel capabilities. Travellers today are looking for more than a flight or hotel booking. They want a holiday that is curated around their interests and supported throughout the journey. TravClan’s supplier network and destination capabilities will help us build that experience across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel,” said Nishant Verman, SVP, Corporate Development and Partnerships, Flipkart.
"India is becoming one of the largest outbound travel markets in the world, with travellers taking their first international trips driving a significant part of this growth. The opportunity lies in making these trips more affordable while maintaining reliable service levels. By contracting directly with suppliers and operating our own ground teams, we are able to offer competitive prices and deliver a consistent experience," said Arun Bagaria, Co-founder and CEO, TravClan.
"This partnership with Flipkart allows us to take affordable travel products to millions of Indians as they embark on their international journeys," he added.

Juan Rey, senior VP and general manager of Calibre and CTO of Siemens EDA, shares his perspective on building trust in artificial intelligence for engineering. In this AI Summit interview, Rey explores how AI is changing semiconductor design and what it will take for engineering organizations to confidently embrace autonomous AI.
The opportunity goes beyond simply applying greater intelligence to engineering problems. Trusted AI requires a combination of AI intelligence, deep domain expertise, and deterministic verification.
AI can help engineers analyze complex problems, accelerate workflows, and reach results faster. But intelligence alone is not enough. Domain expertise provides the engineering knowledge and context needed to understand the problem, guide AI toward meaningful solutions, and determine whether an answer makes sense. For critical engineering decisions, verification remains essential. Trusted, deterministic solutions provide a certification layer that verifies outcomes and gives engineering teams greater confidence.
As AI becomes more autonomous, manufacturers, design teams, and electronic design automation (EDA) companies will play important roles in creating the technologies, processes, and verification frameworks needed to establish that trust. At the center of this transformation remains the engineer. AI can augment engineering expertise, automate complex tasks, and dramatically improve productivity, but the engineer retains ultimate responsibility for engineering decisions.

Presente para crianças: Nintendo Switch OLED alcança o menor preço de 2026
Bundle do Nintendo Switch OLED com Super Mario Wonder e 3 meses de Nintendo Switch Online fica mais acessível com pagamento via Pix
O Nintendo Switch OLED entrou em oferta por R$ 1.831,08 no Pix com o cupom NINTENDO na Amazon. O bundle do console da Nintendo com o jogo Super Mario Wonder, lançado por R$ 2.699, fica 32% mais barato faltando poucos dias para o Dia das Crianças.
O Nintendo Switch OLED adota uma tela OLED de 7 polegadas com resolução HD (720p) e taxa de atualização de 60 Hz no Modo Portátil, reproduzindo cores mais vivas que a versão padrão. O videogame traz uma dock para ser conectada à TV, promovendo jogos em telas maiores com resolução Full HD.
O console é equipado com o chip customizado Nvidia Tegra X1 e 4 GB de RAM, conseguindo executar jogos com gráficos 3D. Os 64 GB de armazenamento interno podem ser um pouco limitados, mas é possível expandir a memória usando cartões microSD de até 2 TB.

O bundle do console da Nintendo inclui uma versão digital do jogo Super Mario Wonder. Nele, os jogadores controlam o Mario e outros personagens da franquia em uma aventura pelo inédito Reino Flor.
Outro “mimo” do pacote é o voucher de três meses do Nintendo Switch Online, assinatura que permite aos jogadores participar de partidas online em diferentes títulos. Além disso, ele libera o acesso a uma ampla biblioteca de jogos retro de consoles antigos, como o Game Boy e Super Nintendo.

articles.title: Chinese NAND Maker YMTC Reportedly Expects Memory Shortage to Last Another Three Years
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
Chinese NAND Maker YMTC Reportedly Expects Memory Shortage to Last Another Three Years
Chinese NAND flash maker YMTC apparently expects the global memory shortage to last another three years. The claim comes from a profile of the company published by The Wire China, in which a YMTC employee, speaking anonymously, shared the outlook. The same employee said YMTC has raised prices for its chips and shifted capacity toward higher-margin products. The excerpt was shared on X by @jukan05, who read it as a NAND forecast, although the employee's wording covers memory in general. Three more years would put the end of the shortage somewhere around late 2029. This is one unnamed employee's words, of course, and not public guidance from YMTC.
That 2029 prediction is well past TrendForce's estimate, which has NAND flash supply loosening in the second half of 2027 as new capacity comes online. It sits closer to Micron's view, with CEO Sanjay Mehrotra saying last week that supply will be much tighter in 2027 and 2028. The shift in capacity matters too, especially for regular PC builders. Counterpoint Research ranked YMTC fourth in NAND bit shipments in Q2 with a 14% share, yet only fifth in revenue, since its product mix leans toward consumer applications. Moving capacity to higher-margin chips could leave less for consumer SSDs, even as YMTC works to double its wafer output with new fabs. Nevertheless, readers planning a storage upgrade shouldn't count on prices dropping anytime soon.
Sources:

articles.title: Asus Googlebook 14 first thoughts: Great hardware, meh software
articles.text:
Asus has launched its Googlebook 14 laptop in Canada, available now starting at $1,799.
The new laptop is one of several Googlebook devices, which run the poorly named GooglebookOS, a strange amalgamation of Android and ChromeOS boasting a bunch of ‘smart’ Gemini features.
I’ve got my hands on one of Asus’ Googlebook 14 laptops and will be testing it for a full review, but my initial impressions are mixed.
Great hardware from Asus
Let’s start with the good: the hardware looks and feels excellent. Asus made a really great laptop here. It features a ‘nano ceramic’ magnesium-aluminum chassis that feels really cool; it reminds me a bit of the OnePlus sandstone material with a bit of texture while not being overly grippy. The Googlebook 14 is also impressively thin and weighs in at 0.99kg (2.18lb).
Asus equipped the Googlebook 14 with a 14-inch, 3K 120Hz OLED touchscreen and a six-speaker audio setup. It also has a six-sensor haptic touchpad that works well in my initial testing. Powering it all are Intel Core Ultra 5 or 7 Series 3 chips, up to 16GB of RAM, and up to a 512GB SSD.
While there’s plenty of power under the hood and the hardware is quite premium, the laptop isn’t perfect. I haven’t spent a ton of time using it yet — pretty much just long enough to set up the laptop and poke around GooglebookOS — but so far, I don’t love what I’m seeing on the software side.
The app problem
Everything looks and feels like ChromeOS, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing (I actually really like how ChromeOS looks!). Frankly, it’s expected, given Google basically ripped the desktop and windowing features out of ChromeOS and layered them on top of Android for GooglebookOS.
However, when I attempted to install some apps that I need for work, things started going off the rails. For one, I’d rather not use Chrome (crazy, I know!) and my browser of choice is Firefox because of some features and extensions that are only available on it, like Container Tabs.
While I could install the Android version of Firefox without issue, what I really want is the desktop version. Theoretically, I should be able to, since there’s a Linux version of Firefox, but so far every attempt I’ve made to install it has failed. There might be something that I’m missing here — it’s my first time using GooglebookOS after all — so here’s hoping I can figure it out.
Similarly, the only version of Photoshop available is the Android version. Unfortunately, Adobe doesn’t make a Linux version of Photoshop, so I’ll need to see if the mobile version can handle my needs.
Headline features have issues
Third-party apps aside, I also attempted to use some of the new connected and smart Gemini features, to mixed success. The much hyped app mirroring feature barely functions. Most of the apps I tested had text rendering issues that made them impossible to use. However, most of the Google apps I tried looked fine, so it might just be that developers will need to add support for the feature. Regardless, there was a noticeable amount of latency that made using the feature unappealing.
The ability to wiggle your cursor to summon Gemini does work, once you jump through the hoops required to turn it on. But I’ll need to spend more time with it to judge its usefulness. For the moment, the only thing I’ve used it for was highlighting a button in GooglebookOS that I wasn’t familiar with and asking Gemini what it was, only for the AI to make up an answer that was very obviously wrong.
All this is to say, I have very mixed feelings about GooglebookOS. I’m sure a lot of this is just getting used to a new operating system, and likely some teething issues for Google as well. I expect GooglebookOS will improve, especially since being Android at the core means Google can develop for both mobile and desktop simultaneously, which could yield some cool interactions down the line.
At the same time, I expected staple features like app mirroring to work a lot better out of the box. If these unique capabilities don’t work well, there’s not much to entice customers away from macOS or Windows. Especially since, at least in the desktop app space, Googlebooks are starting well behind the competition.
At least it looks like Google will let users unlock the bootloader, which means if GooglebookOS doesn’t cut it for you, you can run something else on it instead.
Where to buy in Canada
If you like to take a risk on a whole new product line like this, the Asus Googlebook 14 is available now directly from Asus as well as from Amazon, Best Buy, Canada Computers, Costco, and Staples.
Plus, there are a number of launch incentives available to take advantage of if you do pick one up, including:
- Best Buy: choose between Pixel Buds 2a ($180 value) or $280 off Google Pixel 9a with purchase (until Oct. 31).
- Asus store: get a one-year warranty extension, an Asus backpack, and an Asus Marshmallow mouse (combined $170 value) with purchase (until Dec. 31).
- Get a $150 gift card/promo code with purchase at Staples and Amazon (until Dec. 31).
- Get a $165 gift card with purchase at Costco.
- Get a Logitech MX Master 4 mouse ($160 value) with purchase at Canada Computers.
Stay tuned to MobileSyrup for a full review of the Googlebook 14 and GooglebookOS in general. And if you’ve got any questions about Googlebooks, drop ’em below, and I’ll answer them.

articles.title: Akka Tests Spec-Driven AI Delivery Across 65 Open Source Projects
articles.text:
Akka used 65 open source projects to test a spec driven workflow for AI assisted software porting, measuring specification structure, context, model and effort selection, automated validation, token consumption, and runtime performance. The initial tranche took 99.3 hours and consumed 9.41 billion tokens, with Akka reporting a lines of code or performance improvement in 57 of the 65 ports.
The experiment used two tranches. Akka analyzed all 65 projects, generating specifications and implementing up to 10% of each project's surface area, then selected 10 for complete implementation based on system characteristics and measurable results. The delivery harness cycled through discovery, specification, porting, benchmarking, and improvement. Discovery analyzed code, models, schemas, and runtime behavior, while Claude with Akka Specify handled implementation, testing, and review. A common benchmark runner compared tests, code size, and latency.
Akka delivery harness workflow(Source: Akka Blog Post)
Akka found that structured specifications with claims, evidence, and typed behavior improved first-pass implementations, while gaps in context files remained around cross-component decisions. Follow-up areas include interface enumeration, test ingestion, provenance tracking, differential testing, and adversarial testing.GitHub Spec Kit similarly structures coding agent workflows around specification, planning, tasks, implementation, and convergence. In Akka's experiment, Sonnet averaged 61 minutes per port versus 120 minutes for Opus, while Opus used about 40% fewer tokens. Higher effort settings increased consumption without consistently improving efficiency.
The finding prompted discussion among engineers following the research. Aaditya, commenting on a LinkedIn post by Tyler Jewell, CEO of Akka, wrote
Smaller model's behavior matched modernization work he had observed, where the small model follows the spec while a larger model may improvise.
Aaditya also questioned
Whether reductions in lines of code resulted primarily from dead code removal or from differences in the target language.
Rick Bryce, Head of Marketing at Avahi, raised a related point in the same discussion and suggested that constraints could influence the result. The comments add questions around whether model capability, specification constraints, or both account for differences in porting efficiency.
Cheaper model giving the tighter port is the finding worth chasing
Akka model and effort efficiency chart (Source: Akka Blog Post)
Validation used the original unit and integration tests alongside auditors checking serialization, security, error handling, PII, idempotency, and architectural boundaries. Akka added guardrails as failures exposed new issues, while reporting that additional exit conditions increased porting costs. Performance varied by project: applications, frameworks, and libraries generally improved, while infrastructure and tooling showed median degradation. Akka reported a 143,333 times improvement for Dify, but noted that the compared workloads differed, while Netflix Metaflow was approximately 100 times slower.

articles.title: Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest razed — trees were removed before a mandatory environmental impact assessment, say reports
articles.text:
Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest razed — trees were removed before a mandatory environmental impact assessment, say reports
300 hectares of Finland's forest gobbled up by data center development.
Google’s latest data center construction project in Finland is being investigated after the company representing the search giant allegedly cleared over 300 hectares of forest. The reported issue is that Google’s local operator, Tuike Finland, cleared the 420 football fields' worth of trees without obtaining a mandatory environmental impact assessment beforehand, says AFP.
Google sees Finland as an attractive European data center host country due to a number of favorable factors. The source notes that it is a country with a cool climate, plus stable and cheap energy supplies (mostly nuclear, wind and hydro). Moreover, Finland sees data centers as a solution to address some current woes such as slow economic growth and record-high unemployment levels.
This new development near Muhos, a small town with fewer than 9,000 residents, isn’t the first for Google in Finland. It already has a facility up and running in Hamina, in the south, but hopes to expand in Muhos, Kajaani, and Vaala, in the north. Overall, it is a massive expansion project, and part of a 13-billion-euro ($15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years. Finland’s potential data center appeal has also made it a location of choice for Microsoft and TikTok.
While the local mayor looks forward to the massive investment, growth of business, and general economic boom for the region, residents are waking up to the experience of others where data centers have sprung up. Concerns about impacts on the environment, energy supply stability, and energy prices are simmering under the surface.
Google seems to have trampled on some of these concerns already, with these reports of trees already felled and excavators clearing the ground before government agency approval. Not a good start.
"In our view, operations at this construction site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project is in compliance with the law," Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the board of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, told AFP at the edge of the freshly deforested area near Muhos. Even some nature preservation areas have been logged, reckons the chair. Halmeenpaa was responsible for filing the suspension request with the conservation agency.
Google denies prematurely devastating the forest. It told AFP that tree felling had been "in compliance with Forestry Act requirements." Moreover, its Finland comms manager said, in a contrasting statement to that of Halmeenpaa, that Google has been ensuring "high-value nature zones within the sites have been protected during forestry works."
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
We haven’t seen any other reports indicating that preparation and construction work has ceased at the new data center development site near Muhos. So it seems like Google will plow ahead, hoping or knowing that the political and/or business will is sufficiently strong to ensure it won’t have to undo any of the actions it has already completed.
