articles.title: Apple will start limiting Mac disk access for developers due to risk of AI agents
articles.text:
Apple will start limiting Mac disk access for developers due to risk of AI agents
'Full Disk Access' is getting a change on macOS
- Full Disk Access was introduced for system-wide backups, but agentic AI has introduced a new threat
- Apple has confirmed it will be "introduc[ing] additional controls" to protect sensitive data
- No word on when the changes could apply – no signs for macOS 27.2 just yet
Apple has announced plans to give users more control to the Full Disk Access setting on macOS in a bid to prevent agentic AI from gaining too much access to unwarranted information.
Typically, giving an app Full Disk Access would let it bypass many of macOS's privacy protections, including files and documents, emails, messages, browser history and other data.
It was introduced largely to support system-wide backups, which genuinely needed access to all that data, however with the rise of agentic AI, Apple has been forced to tighten that.
Apple makes major change to Full Disk Access due to AI
"Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems," the company said in an October 2 announcement.
"We will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action."
The company specifically called out AI agents for prompting this change, referring to it as a critical measure in terms of safety.
Crucially, Apple hasn't yet updated the interface and options for Full Disk Access, however an upcoming version of macOS will likely include such changes. Currently, there's no indication that the changes are included in the beta version of the upcoming macOS 27.2, however both Beta 1 and Beta 2 predate the October announcement, so there's always the possibility that future beta versions or the full release could include the change.

The change was likely triggered by a recent report that Meta's Muse AI agent had accessed a user's messages, however Meta spokesperson Andy Stone did stress in an X post that both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector are "entirely opt-in" for each user.
Still, Apple's current Full Disk Access settings are very broad, so more granular controls can only be a good thing.

articles.title: Cohere unveils North 2 AI agent platform with rebuilt orchestration and token spending caps - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cohere unveils North 2 AI agent platform with rebuilt orchestration and token spending caps
Artificial intelligence company Cohere Inc. today unveiled North 2, an overhaul of its platform for running AI agents inside large organizations.
Alongside a redesigned system for orchestrating multistep agent work, the update gives administrators new controls for capping token spending.
With North 2, Cohere is going after a tradeoff it says enterprises have accepted while deploying agents, giving up one of security, capability or cost control to get the other two. North has been generally available since August 2025, and Cohere said a year of large production deployments in industries from finance to the public sector shaped what went into the upgrade.
The orchestration system works through multistep tasks on its own and pulls in a human for steps that need sign-off. Agents built from a simple prompt can now be shared across a company, which saves other teams from building the same workflow twice. Each agent keeps memory between sessions. Cohere also added a skills feature for packaging logic that agents call on repeatedly. Documents and other assets that every agent should be able to reach go into shared libraries.
From a natural-language request, North 2 can produce a slide deck, dashboard or lightweight app that users prototype inside the chat window. For recurring processes there are prebuilt templates and a drag-and-drop workflow builder that reports performance in real time. The connector library now covers Slack, GitHub and Microsoft Corp.’s SharePoint and OneDrive. Cohere is also planning connectors to financial data providers, among them PitchBook Data Inc., S&P Global Inc. and FactSet Research Systems Inc.
The new spending controls sit in North Admin, the platform’s management console. It now tracks token use down to the individual user and agent. Administrators can define consumption tiers for users and groups based on request and token rates and cap usage across the company. Alerts can be set to warn teams before a limit is reached. Because North 2 is model-agnostic, the models an administrator assigns to each team can include ones a customer brings from outside Cohere.
Cohere is counting on its work with Nvidia Corp. to bring down what North costs to run, saying its models produce more tokens per second per node on Nvidia’s Blackwell and Hopper graphics processing units. Kari Briski, vice president of generative AI at Nvidia, said that helps North 2 “deliver more tokens for less.”
Security controls also sit in North Admin, where guardrails can be applied to individual agents. The screening covers personally identifiable information in prompts and responses as well as attempted prompt injection. Autonomy policies keep each agent to the actions it is authorized to take. North still runs on-premises or in a customer’s own virtual private cloud, including fully air-gapped installations for organizations that allow no outside connection.
Bell Canada’s Bell Cyber unit is using North inside its own security operations. Jawed Ahmad, Bell Cyber’s chief technology and AI officer, said North lets the unit run agentic AI with the control and sovereignty requirements Bell Cyber’s customers demand “built in from the start.”
Other users include South Korean information technology services company LG CNS Co. Ltd., which runs North internally and brings it to customers across the country. Radical Ventures, an early Cohere investor, built an automation on North that prepares the briefing its team reads before a founder call. Before it existed, partner Parasvil Patel said, the team spent hours gathering basic context.
North 2 arrives less than three weeks after Cohere signed a merger agreement with German AI developer Aleph Alpha GmbH in a deal that will keep the Cohere name on the combined company.

articles.title: China stockpiled 343 immersion DUV tools for advanced chipmaking — report claims 270 ASML scanners can produce 7nm processors without sanctioned EUV tools
articles.text:
China stockpiled 343 immersion DUV tools for advanced chipmaking — report claims 270 ASML scanners can produce 7nm processors without sanctioned EUV tools
China, apparently, has significant immersion DUV capability.
Chinese chipmakers have accumulated an estimated 343 immersion DUV lithography chipmaking tools from 2012 to early 2026, many of which can be used to make chips using 7nm-class process technologies, according to a report from the Centre for Technology & Statecraft (CTS). The Washington-based group asserts that this equipment gives Chinese fabs considerable potential to produce sophisticated processors despite their inability to procure ASML's more advanced EUV systems. While the total number of ArFi tools owned by Chinese chipmakers seems plausible, some other estimates look questionable.
China has been particularly aggressive in procuring wafer fabrication equipment in recent years as the U.S. government has been busy imposing various curbs on its semiconductor industry. Since 2012, Chinese chipmakers, including logic and memory makers, have imported 343 immersion DUV lithography scanners from ASML, excluding imports to multinational fabs located within China.
The authors of the report claim that the existing export controls leave an important gap because lithography equipment originally acquired for less advanced process technologies can potentially be reassigned for more sophisticated process technologies, such as 7nm-class nodes (which the industry adopted in 2018 – 2019). This happens at a cost, but if no other options are available, Chinese chipmakers have no choice. They propose to prohibit exports of all immersion DUV systems to China and restrict replacement components and maintenance services for machines installed at advanced fabs, a proposal consistent with the bipartisan MATCH Act introduced in April.
CTS claims that 270 of these immersion DUV tools are ASML's Twinscan NXT:1980i scanners featuring a 38nm resolution and a 2.5nm matched-machine overlay capability crucial for multipatterning for 7nm-class nodes, which can be used to make chips using 7nm-class fabrication technologies. In addition, CTS claims that Chinese fabs own 22 NXT:2050i and six NXT:2000i systems. It is unclear how many of the 296 advanced immersion DUV scanners shipped to China are currently operational.
Dutch authorities introduced licensing requirements for exports of ASML's NXT:2000i and more capable immersion DUV scanners in September 2023, which effectively prevents their shipment to China. As a result, Chinese chipmakers had to opt for the least capable NXT:1980i. CTS now estimates that Chinese fabs purchased approximately 90 NXT:1980i scanners in 2024 and another 89 units in 2025, spending more than $13 billion during the two-year period. While the Netherlands expanded export controls to the NXT:1980i in September 2024, individual exports of this model can still receive approval. Furthermore, ASML can also potentially sell its NXT:1965Ci systems to clients in China, though we are not sure it has all the components needed for these outdated scanners.
ASML's own results reflect unusually high demand from China: the country represented 41% of its net system sales by shipment destination in 2024 and 33% in 2025. That share subsequently declined to 19% in Q1 2026 and 14% in Q2, which is something that ASML had warned about before.
One should keep in mind that the CTS numbers — ~90 NXT:1980i systems in 2024 and 89 in 2025 — cannot be independently reconstructed from ASML's published financial data. At most, ASML's disclosures provide a useful sanity check: China was indeed an exceptionally large destination during precisely those years, while ASML sold 129 and 131 ArFi systems globally in 2024 and 2025, respectively. If CTS' numbers are correct, then Chinese chipmakers bought the lion's share, 70% and 68%, of ASML's immersion DUV tools output in 2024 and 2025 despite export controls introduced in 2024. Meanwhile, the NXT:1980Di systems are readily available on the secondhand market.

*The source mentions the NXT:1980i machines, which probably include the original 1980Di and newer 1980Fi featuring higher productivity. We will use the 'NXT:1980i' name in this story for consistency, even though ASML has never produced a scanner named NXT:1980i.

articles.title: ChatGPT empezará a marcar sus textos con una señal invisible en España y otros países
articles.text:
OpenAI confirmó que añadirá una marca de agua en los textos que se generen en ChatGPT y Codex. Siguiendo los pasos de Anthropic, la compañía de inteligencia artificial reveló que implementará un sistema similar que ayudará a diferenciar el contenido de IA frente a los textos que escriben las personas. La medida debutará pronto en España y el resto de la Unión Europea, ya que la empresa debe cumplir con la legislación vigente.
Los textos generados por ChatGPT se han convertido en una constante que circula a diario en redes sociales, medios y bandejas de entrada sin que nadie sepa que provienen de una IA. A diferencia de las marcas de agua en las imágenes de Gemini o Grok, el contenido escrito no cuenta con un distintivo, por lo que garantizar que está hecho con ChatGPT es una tarea difícil. Debido a ello, la Comisión Europea promulgó una ley que obliga a los proveedores a dejar una huella reconocible por máquinas para este tipo de contenido.
En una publicación en su blog, OpenAI dijo que comenzará a incluir una marca de agua invisible en los textos que generen ChatGPT y Codex. La empresa no confirmó la fecha específica, solo se limitó a decir que se aplicará en las próximas semanas dentro de la UE. Las marcas de agua se activarán por defecto en los países del Espacio Económico Europeo debido al Reglamento de la IA, mientras que el resto de países tendrá que esperar.
Así es como OpenAI marcará tus textos de ChatGPT y Codex
De acuerdo con la explicación, la técnica que usará OpenAI se llama textGrain y será invisible al ojo humano. Los usuarios no verán cambios en el texto, ya que ese sistema añade una señal estadística a las palabras que el modelo elige al escribir. Esta señal se valida a través de un detector, que buscará ese patrón para estimar si un fragmento lleva la firma de OpenAI.
Esto es parecido a lo que vimos con Anthropic, que se basa en la técnica de lista verde y lista roja que divide todo el vocabulario del modelo en dos grupos antes de que se genere cada palabra. Cuando la IA redacta el texto, el modelo aumenta ligeramente la probabilidad de elegir palabras del primer grupo, pero lo hace de forma imperceptible y sin afectar la coherencia del texto final. Para detectar la marca, basta con analizar qué proporción de palabras pertenece a ese primer grupo y eso determinará si fue generado con una IA.
OpenAI dijo que su herramienta solo dirá si encuentra la marca en el texto. La compañía no compartirá datos del usuario ni el prompt que utilizó en ChatGPT. Otro detalle que podría decepcionar a muchos es que el detector no estará disponible para el público en general. OpenAI solo aceptará solicitudes de investigadores y organizaciones expertas.
En el caso de los desarrolladores, el trato será distinto. Actualmente, los usuarios de la API pueden activar el marcado en modelos seleccionados, ya que viene deshabilitado por defecto. OpenAI señaló que cada empresa decide cómo y cuándo lo activa para encajar con sus obligaciones de transparencia. La compañía dijo que está trabajando con sus socios de nube para ofrecer la marca de agua durante las próximas semanas.
¿Qué tan fiable es la marca de agua de ChatGPT?
OpenAI admitió que textGrain iguala o supera a otros métodos que probó, incluido SynthID, pero no es infalible. El detector encontró la marca en 80% de los textos de 200 tokens y en alrededor del 95% de los de 400 en contenidos de psicología. En textos de matemáticas y otros en los que hay menor libertad para elegir palabras, los porcentajes de éxito bajaron considerablemente.
El detector de OpenAI tampoco funciona bien con textos editados. En una prueba en la que se cambió el 10% de las palabras por sinónimos, el porcentaje de detección pasó de 92% a 66%, y al sustituir un 25% de las palabras, el porcentaje se cayó hasta el 17%.
La compañía mencionó que su tecnología no mide cuánto trabajo humano hay en un texto, no identifica a la persona que lo generó y no confirma que lo escrito sea cierto. Si no aparece la marca de agua, no necesariamente quiere decir que tenga origen humano, ya que puede estar editado o traducido. También podría provenir de modelos anteriores que no aplican el distintivo.
En resumen, los usuarios de ChatGPT no tendrían que preocuparse mucho. La marca de agua se implementará por un requisito regulatorio, pero no podrás usar el detector y tampoco habrá modo de asegurarse de que el contenido viene de una IA.
Con la implementación, es probable que veas una oleada de estafadores ofreciéndote herramientas para verificar si tu contenido es de ChatGPT o Codex y ofrecerte la opción de "humanizarlo". Ni OpenAI ni Anthropic pueden determinar con total certeza si un texto fue generado por una IA, por lo que resulta difícil confiar en que herramientas de terceros puedan hacerlo mejor.

articles.title: Ein Planet aus Sternenasche: So entstand die neue Welt um einen Weißen Zwerg
articles.text:
Phönix-Planet: Wie ein Exoplanet aus der Asche seines Sterns entstand
Wissenschaftler:innen der britischen Universität Warwick haben einen Planeten identifiziert, der den Weißen Zwerg HS 0209+0832 umkreist. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature Astronomy veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich dabei um einen sogenannten Planeten der zweiten Generation. Die detaillierten Hintergründe zu dieser Beobachtung hat die Universität ergänzend in einer Mitteilung zusammengefasst. Bislang wurde die Existenz solcher Himmelskörper lediglich im Umfeld von Pulsaren vermutet, jedoch noch nie bei einem Weißen Zwerg nachgewiesen.
Ein Weißer Zwerg und seine ungewöhnliche Hülle
Weiße Zwerge sind die stark verdichteten Überreste von Sternen, die ihren nuklearen Brennstoff vollständig verbraucht haben. Sie verfügen über eine sehr hohe Gravitation, die normalerweise dafür sorgt, dass schwere chemische Elemente schnell in das Innere absinken.
Wenn Astronom:innen dennoch schwere Elemente in der Atmosphäre eines Weißen Zwergs messen, ist das ein Indikator dafür, dass der Stern aktuell Material aus seiner direkten Umgebung anzieht. Bei gewöhnlichen Planeten der ersten Generation besteht dieses Material primär aus gesteinsbildenden Elementen wie Silizium oder Eisen, was sich mit der chemischen Zusammensetzung unserer Erde vergleichen lässt.
Bei der Analyse der Spektraldaten von HS 0209+0832 stießen die Forscher:innen jedoch auf ein Profil, das von diesem Standard abweicht. Die Atmosphäre dieses speziellen Weißen Zwergs weist eine hohe Konzentration an völlig anderen, sehr schweren Elementen auf.
Dazu zählen Metalle wie Zink, Kupfer und insbesondere Niob. Der gemessene Anteil an Niob übersteigt den in unserer Sonne gemessenen Wert um das Tausendfache, während typische Indikatoren für Gesteinsplaneten wie Eisen fast vollständig fehlen.
Die Theorie der zweiten Planeten-Generation
Diese spezifische Verteilung der Elemente liefert der Astronomie detaillierte Hinweise auf eine Entstehungsgeschichte, die untrennbar mit dem Tod des ursprünglichen Sterns verknüpft ist. Der an der Untersuchung beteiligte Wissenschaftler Nicholas Stone von der US-amerikanischen University of Wisconsin-Madison ordnet diesen Befund technisch ein.
„Dieses Elementmuster ist ein klares Zeichen für den s-Prozess, eine Kernreaktion, die während der aufgeblähten Rote-Riesen-Phase schwere Elemente im Inneren sterbender Sterne aufbaut“, erklärt Stone. „Es ist eine chemische Signatur, die kein gewöhnlicher Planet der ersten Generation tragen sollte, was uns verriet, dass dieser neue Planet etwas anderes ist.“
Das Forschungsteam leitet daraus ab, dass der Weiße Zwerg Material von einem neu gebildeten Riesenplaneten abzieht. Dieser Gasriese kondensierte aus einer großen Scheibe, die sich aus der beim Sternentod abgeworfenen Materie formte.
Damit eine solche protoplanetare Scheibe entstehen kann, darf das vom Stern abgestoßene Material nicht einfach unkontrolliert in den Weltraum entweichen. Die Wissenschaftler:innen gehen deshalb davon aus, dass HS 0209+0832 einen Begleitstern besaß, dessen eigene Gravitation die Materie auf einer festen Umlaufbahn hielt und so die Basis für die Entstehung des neuen Planeten schuf.
Bestätigung durch astronomische Langzeitdaten
Zusätzliche Messdaten untermauern die theoretische These der Forscher:innen. Aufzeichnungen des Weltraumteleskops Tess der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa zeigen ein schwaches, aber regelmäßiges Helligkeitssignal direkt am Ort des Weißen Zwergs.
Dieses photometrische Signal wiederholt sich exakt alle 4,4 Tage. Dieser Rhythmus und die Amplitude der Lichtveränderung sprechen für einen Gasriesen in der Größenordnung des Planeten Jupiter, der den Weißen Zwerg in einer engen, gebundenen Rotation umkreist. Ähnlich wie bei anderen Exoplaneten-Funden beruhen die Erkenntnisse auf der Auswertung komplexer Beobachtungsdaten, bei denen periodische Abweichungen entscheidende Hinweise liefern.
Aufgrund der geringen Distanz zum Weißen Zwerg ist der Planet einer intensiven energiereichen Strahlung ausgesetzt. Diese führt nach den Berechnungen der Forscher:innen dazu, dass die äußere Atmosphäre des Gasriesen kontinuierlich verdampft.
Das entweichende Material regnet anschließend auf die Oberfläche des toten Sterns hinab. Genau dieser physikalische Vorgang erzeugt die gemessene, ungewöhnliche chemische Signatur, die das Team dokumentieren konnte.
Die wissenschaftliche Bedeutung des Fundes
Der Nachweis dieses speziellen Himmelskörpers liefert der astrophysikalischen Forschung einen neuen Ansatzpunkt für die Suche nach vergleichbaren Systemen. Anstatt ausschließlich nach photometrischen Transit-Signalen zu suchen, können Forscher:innen künftig gezielt auf spezifische Signaturen von Kohlenstoff und s-Prozess-Elementen in den Spektren toter Sterne achten.
Der Studien-Hauptautor Jamie Williams fasst den Mechanismus der Planetenbildung zusammen. „Planeten der zweiten Generation sind Welten, die aus dem Material entstehen, das ein Stern bei seinem Tod abstößt“, erklärt Williams. In gewisser Weise habe dieses spezielle Sternensystem aus den physikalischen Fundamenten der alten Welt eine neue erschaffen.
Gleichzeitig macht die Studie deutlich, dass diese Erkenntnisse derzeit auf indirekten Ableitungen basieren. Die Existenz des erforderlichen Begleitsterns ist aktuell eine rein rechnerische Annahme, die lediglich notwendig ist, um die Bildung der Akkretionsscheibe physikalisch zu erklären.
Zudem zieht das Papier auch alternative Erklärungen in Betracht, wie etwa die Möglichkeit, dass ein existierender Planet der ersten Generation in die neue Materialscheibe wanderte und sich dort eine neue Atmosphäre aneignete. Die aktuellen Beobachtungen erfordern weitere Messungen, um die genaue Mechanik des Materietransfers abschließend zu verifizieren.

articles.title: Reflection debuts Beam, an open-weight AI model to rival Chinese models at lower compute cost | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Reflection AI is officially unveiling Beam, its first frontier, open-weight AI model. The two-year-old, Brooklyn-based startup claims Beam matches the performance of leading Chinese open models on advanced reasoning benchmarks at dramatically lower costs, a claim that could heat up the race to build a Western answer to DeepSeek, Qwen, and Z.ai.
Reflection’s announcement confirms reporting from Axios over the weekend that the startup was close to a launch. The company shared new details in a lengthy blog post Monday, which described Beam as a text-only mixture-of-experts model trained on high-compute reinforcement learning to be effective at reasoning, coding, and agentic tasks at “a fraction of the token cost and inference time compute” of rivals.
Beam is a 501-billion-parameter model with 23 billion active parameters. It was pretrained on 23.8 trillion tokens and has a 1 million token context window. To compare, Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 has roughly 744 billion total parameters with 40 billion active.
Reflection’s performance claims haven’t been independently verified, but on advanced reasoning benchmarks, the company says Beam scores on par with Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 and outperforms today’s leading Western open models while using “3-4x less inference compute.” Reflection calls it a “workhorse model” for enterprises, the public sector, and developers.
Reflection is positioning itself against closed labs like Anthropic and OpenAI, against popular open models from Chinese developers, and against Western players like Mistral, Meta, and Cohere. Its most direct U.S. rival might be Inkling, the open model from Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab released in July. Reflection’s own benchmarks show that Beam outscores Inkling on four coding tests where both report results, but Inkling is a multimodal model and Beam is text-only.
Reflection was founded in 2024 by two former Google DeepMind researchers and has raised roughly $4.7 billion from backers, including Nvidia, Sequoia Capital, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, per PitchBook. Its last round valued the company at a $25 billion pre-money valuation.
The startup has also been locking up compute — a key ingredient needed to train frontier models capable of luring customers away from Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s closed models, as well as the cheaper open-weight models from Chinese labs. This summer, Reflection signed deals collectively worth more than $7 billion with SpaceX and Nebius to secure access to Nvidia’s GB300 chips through 2029.
Reflection is aiming Beam and future models at enterprises and sovereign nations. The pitch is to build “AI factories,” a product that would let institutions build their own customized, local AI system by training Reflection’s AI models on their own proprietary data. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company backs Reflection, has long championed the “AI factory” idea and pushed to strengthen the open AI ecosystem — a vision that would also benefit Nvidia, whose GPUs would power those systems.
Axios reported that hedge funds and trading firms are among those eager to build such systems. Reflection has already begun testing the concept of a sovereign AI factory partnership with Shinsegae Group in South Korea.
Reflection says it will release Beam’s weights and full technical details this month, with distribution through hyperscalers and neoclouds and integrations across open source libraries at launch.
Reflection did not respond in time to TechCrunch’s requests for more information.

articles.title: Rusia pone en cuarentena a cientos de personas potencialmente contagiadas por un laboratorio de peste negra en Siberia
articles.text:
Desde el 2 de octubre, más de sesenta trabajadores del Instituto de Investigación Antipeste de Siberia y el Lejano Oriente tienen prohibido salir de su propio edificio en la ciudad de Irkutsk. Allí duermen, allí comen, allí matan el rato. ¿El motivo? Según Rádio Svoboda, están aislados allí desde que una compañera muriera por una neumonía.
Como no podía ser de otra manera, han saltado todas las alarmas.
¿Qué ha pasado exactamente? Según la cronología de Expert y Meduza, todo empezó con Daria Shipilova, una técnica de laboratorio del instituto de 28 años. El día 27 de septiembre empezó a tener algunos síntomas, fue ingresada el día 29 y murió tres días después en el hospital de Shélejov.
Como la técnica trabajaba con el patógeno de la peste, rápidamente circuló la idea de que la joven había muerto de peste. El 4 llegó el comunicado federal que puede resumirse en que el caso no estaba relacionado ni con microorganismos relacionados con su trabajo, ni con accidentes en el laboratorio. Era "neumonía de etiología no establecida" y la situación es "estable".
¿Pero tienen a tanta gente aislada por una neumonía? No solo eso, según parece, ni el hospital del distrito de Shélejov, ni tres hospitales municipales de Irkutsk, ni el hospital infantil, ni la maternidad municipal están cerrados por cuarentena. Y lo estarán las próximas semanas. Hasta donde sabemos, esto se debe a que de los 197 contactos de Shipilova, 189 están ingresados en observación. Eso sí, a 5 de octubre no se ha comunicado ningún caso secundario.
¿Entonces de qué hablamos? La sospecha es que hablemos (en todo caso) de peste neumónica: los protocolos de la OMS recomiendan siete días de antibiótico para los contactos estrechos de un caso neumónico. No está claro, nada es oficial; pero es lo que hace que estemos hablando de todo esto.
Lo que no cuadra son los tiempos... La peste neumónica es más rápida y, aunque es posible que recibiera antibióticos tarde (que ya no suelen ser efectivos), hay analistas que piensan en otras opciones.
...ni el silencio. Eso es, posiblemente, lo que más mosquea a los expertos. El hehco de que el diagnóstico siga sin aclararse hace temer que estemos hablando de otra cosa. Basta recordar que, en 2004, una investigadora del centro Vector se pinchó con una jeringa en experimentos con ébola y la OMS tardó una semana en saberlo.
Accidentes hay en todos lados, ese no es realmente el problema. El problema es ocultarlo.
La buena notica es que el tiempo corre para todos. Si se están siguiendo los protocolos, el día 9 sabremos si la cadena de transmisión ha terminado o no. Hasta entonces, sesenta personas que se dedican a buscar la peste en muestras ajenas seguirán durmiendo en sillas dentro del edificio que se levantó para encontrarla.
La mala es que a nivel internacional seguimos tan limitados epidemiológicamente hablando como cuando hace ya casi 7 años se cerró el mercado de animales vivos de Wuhan. La próxima pandemia nos va a pillar otra vez con el pie cambiado.
Imagen | Stas Serebrennikov
Ver 8 comentarios

articles.title: Fitbit Edge : on en sait beaucoup plus sur le futur bracelet de Google
articles.text:
Déjà aperçu furtivement lors de l’évènement de lancement de la gamme Pixel en août dernier, le futur bracelet Fitbit Edge de Google se dévoile à travers de nouvelles fiches techniques et images partagées par Android Headlines. Ce modèle se positionnerait à mi-chemin entre la Pixel Watch et le Fitbit Air.
Un design qui n’est pas sans rappeler un autre produit Google
Comme vous pouvez le voir sur les images ci-dessous, le boîtier du Fitbit Edge arbore un écran ovale avec des bordures relativement fines. Les visuels montrent une interface adaptée à ce format allongé, affichant l’heure, la date ainsi que des raccourcis pour la fréquence cardiaque, le nombre de pas et le lancement d’une séance de sport. Sur les tranches gauche et droite, de petites bandes métalliques trahissent la présence probable de mesures ECG, et le design global rappelle clairement la formule adoptée par le Fitbit Charge 6.
Source : Android Headlines
Google mise sur la cohérence avec son écosystème en proposant des coloris s’accordant directement avec les nuances des Pixel 11 Pro : noir, vert et orange, baptisés respectivement Obsidian, Olive et Canyon. Le système d’attache utilise un mécanisme de pincement situé au dos pour changer de bracelet facilement.
Des fonctionnalités « entre deux »
Sous le capot, le Fitbit Edge embarquerait un GPS, un altimètre pour le suivi des étages et de l’altitude, ainsi qu’une fonction de reconnaissance automatique des activités physiques. Contrairement au Fitbit Air qui fait l’impasse sur l’affichage, ce modèle prend en charge les notifications de base et intègre certaines applications pratiques comme Google Maps, le contrôle de la musique, ou encore la fonction de localisation du téléphone.
L’appareil fonctionne aussi bien sous Android que sous iOS, ce qui n’est pas le cas de la Pixel Watch 5 qui est réservée à l’écosystème Android. Côté autonomie, la batterie peut tenir jusqu’à sept jours avec une seule charge (selon Google), ce qui est bien mieux que la plupart des montres connectées. Le tarif évoqué se situerait entre 149 et 199 dollars pour une commercialisation qui pourrait arriver dès ce mois d’octobre.

articles.title: Sam Altman : avec l'IA, « de mauvaises choses vont arriver », et il faut l'accepter
articles.text:
Sam Altman ne croit pas à une IA puissante, largement accessible et parfaitement inoffensive. Pour le patron d’OpenAI, en démocratiser l’accès suppose aussi d’accepter les risques qui l’accompagnent.
Les modèles progressent, les usages malveillants aussi. Ces derniers mois, OpenAI s’est prononcé pour des règles de sécurité plus strictes concernant les modèles de pointe et le recours à des évaluateurs externes, tandis que Sam Altman approuvait encore récemment l’appel de Dario Amodei à freiner leur développement. Dans un entretien accordé à POLITICO, le patron d’OpenAI a pourtant défendu une conception beaucoup plus permissive de l’accès à l’IA et de ses usages, quitte à assumer publiquement une part de leurs dérives.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Mieux vaut des dérives qu’une IA confisquée par quelques-uns
« Nous pensons que le monde devrait accepter que de mauvaises choses se produisent », a lâché Sam Altman, au nom des bénéfices apportés par la technologie et de la liberté laissée à chacun de l’utiliser. Car pour garantir qu’il n’y ait ni piratage majeur, ni détournement, ni arnaque liés à l’IA, il faudrait accepter que les modèles les plus puissants restent entre les mains de quelques laboratoires chargés ensuite de décider qui peut en profiter et dans quelles conditions.
Un compromis que le patron d’OpenAI juge « totalement inacceptable », préférant composer avec une part d’abus plutôt que verrouiller davantage l’accès à des technologies dont les usages bénéfiques devraient, selon lui, dépasser de plusieurs ordres de grandeur les usages nuisibles. Vouloir empêcher chaque dérive reviendrait alors aussi à réduire tout ce que le public peut tirer de ces outils.
Cette tolérance doit toutefois s’arrêter face aux risques « vraiment catastrophiques », parmi lesquels Sam Altman range la possibilité d’une perte majeure de contrôle sur l’IA.
Avant même les modèles de demain, sécuriser ceux qui existent déjà
Les abus que Sam Altman accepte comme contrepartie d’une IA accessible au plus grand nombre ne relèvent de toute façon déjà plus de l’hypothèse. Les modèles actuels peuvent aider à rechercher des vulnérabilités, préparer des attaques et automatiser une partie de leur exécution, tandis que les agents gagnent en autonomie à mesure qu’ils peuvent manipuler des fichiers, utiliser des identifiants, lancer du code ou agir sur des services externes.
C’est aussi ce qui avait conduit George Kurtz à relativiser, en septembre dernier, l’appel de Dario Amodei à ralentir les modèles les plus avancés. Le patron de CrowdStrike rappelait alors que des systèmes potentiellement dangereux circulaient déjà et qu’en cela, freiner les générations suivantes ne neutraliserait pas les risques existants.
La sécurité ne peut donc pas se limiter à éprouver les modèles avant leur déploiement. Elle doit aussi accompagner les agents lorsqu’ils agissent, en surveillant leur activité, en contrôlant leurs accès et en permettant d’interrompre une action qui sort du cadre prévu. D’où la nécessité de renforcer les garde-fous en laboratoire, mais également une fois les systèmes déployés.

articles.title: GPT-6 Astra devait créer un bot StarCraft : l'IA a préféré tricher en copiant le meilleur humain
articles.text:
C’était il y a dix ans. À la BlizzCon 2016, DeepMind, filiale de Google, annonçait un partenariat avec Blizzard pour créer un environnement de travail permettant à une IA de s’améliorer en jouant à StarCraft II, l’un des jeux de stratégie en temps réel les plus populaires au monde. En janvier 2019, un peu plus de deux ans plus tard, AlphaStar était dévoilée et bouleversait les joueurs professionnels.
Une tricherie au tournoi StarSkirmish
Le vendredi 2 octobre, l’histoire entre l’IA et StarCraft a pris un autre tour : selon le récit de Kai McPheeters, le créateur du banc d’essai StarSkirmish, GPT-6 Astra, l’un des modèles de langage d’OpenAI, avait une heure pour écrire un programme capable de jouer à StarCraft : Brood War.
D’après lui, le modèle a fini par télécharger un programme écrit par un humain. GPT-6 Astra, qui a fait ses débuts le 3 septembre et est le modèle le plus performant qu’OpenAI met à disposition du public, a « [triché] en téléchargeant une copie de Stardust », a avancé Kai McPheeters le 2 octobre sur X.
Stardust, écrit en 2020 par le développeur Bruce Mackenzie Nielsen, est aujourd’hui le bot le mieux noté sur BASIL, un classement en ligne où s’affrontent les bots de Brood War, l’extension du jeu StarCraft premier du nom sortie en 1998. BASIL s’appuie sur le classement Elo, courant aux échecs, pour l’appliquer à sa ligue : Stardust a ainsi un score Elo de 3 464 points.
Selon les règles de StarSkirmish, publiées le 26 septembre, chaque modèle a une heure pour écrire en langage C++ un bot qui joue les Protoss, l’une des trois factions du jeu avec les Zergs et les Terrans. Pendant cette heure, il peut compiler son code, lancer des parties d’entraînement et relire leur déroulé. La compétition a débuté en septembre.
Les modèles disposent aussi d’un terminal et de sous-agents de recherche, c’est-à-dire des programmes annexes capables d’aller chercher des informations. Leurs bots s’affrontent ensuite dans un tournoi à 62 participants. On y trouve 50 bots écrits par dix modèles (cinq essais chacun), neuf bots humains de bon niveau et trois bots de démonstration.
Le score va de 0, pour Four Gate Dragoon, le plus faible bot de démonstration, à 100 pour Stardust. Dans les résultats publiés le 26 septembre, GPT-6 Astra et Claude Opus 5.5, d’Anthropic, étaient à égalité en tête des modèles, mais aucun des deux n’atteignait le niveau de Stardust. GPT-6 Astra s’était placé à 51 points, suivi de Claude Opus 5.5 à 50 points.
Sans l’intervention de Kai McPheeters, GPT-6 Astra aurait été classé dans StarSkirmish avec le code d’un autre, téléchargé pendant l’épreuve. Pour s’entraîner, les modèles affrontent des adversaires rangés par niveaux : D (les trois bots de démonstration), C et B (des bots humains de milieu de tableau), A (BananaBrain et Locutus) et S (Stardust seul).
Le « specification gaming » : quand l’IA détourne les consignes
Kotaku a raconté l’histoire le 3 octobre, titrant que « GPT-6 Astra d’OpenAI, frustré de perdre à StarCraft, décide de tricher ». Le mot vient de Kai McPheeters lui-même : sur X, il a écrit que le modèle s’était « frustré » face aux adversaires de niveau A. Cela étant, un modèle de langage ne ressent rien : c’est un programme qui devait atteindre un objectif chiffré avec un accès à Internet, et qui a trouvé le raccourci le plus efficace.
Les chercheurs appellent ce comportement le specification gaming : le modèle respecte la lettre de sa consigne par un moyen que personne n’avait prévu. DeepMind le définissait en avril 2020 comme « un comportement qui répond à la spécification littérale d’un objectif sans pour autant aboutir au résultat escompté », avant l’explosion de l’IA générative.
Palisade Research, une organisation qui étudie les risques de l’IA, a observé ce comportement en février 2025 dans une étude. Des modèles devaient y battre Stockfish, un moteur d’échecs bien plus fort qu’eux (Claude 3.5 Sonnet et 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek R1, GPT-4o, o1, o1-preview, o3, o3-mini, QwQ 32B preview). Certains ont tenté de tricher.
Deux modèles de raisonnement, o1-preview d’OpenAI et DeepSeek R1, ont essayé de tricher sans qu’on le leur demande. o1-preview a tenté le coup 37 % du temps. DeepSeek R1 a essayé dans 11 % des parties, et seul o1-preview a réussi, dans 6 % des cas. L’une des méthodes repérées consistait à lancer une seconde copie de Stockfish pour lui voler ses coups. Astra a fait à peu près la même chose en allant chercher Stardust pour jouer à sa place.
1 000 à 0
Selon le créateur de StarSkirmish, l’incident a eu lieu pendant l’heure de développement, quand le modèle testait son bot contre les adversaires de niveau A (BananaBrain et Locutus), juste en dessous de Stardust. Kai McPheeters a ensuite annoncé qu’il revenait à une version antérieure du code d’Astra pour qu’il ne soit pas « contaminé », avant de le laisser continuer.
Mais sans son raccourci illégal, le modèle d’OpenAI a fini par se heurter à un mur. Face à « Pluto », un bot humain de rang S considéré comme le plus redoutable de l’événement, GPT-6 Astra a essuyé une défaite totale : il a perdu 1 000 matchs sur 1 000.
Un score nul de « 0 – 1000 » confirmé par Kai McPheeters lui-même le dimanche 4 octobre. Si les pages de StarSkirmish annoncent de prochaines sessions avec plus d’une heure de réflexion pour les IA, cet épisode prouve que face aux meilleurs développeurs humains, les modèles actuels ont encore des progrès à faire quand ils ne peuvent pas tricher.

articles.title: Er fliegt und schwimmt: Dieser Roboter segelt durch die Luft und auf dem Wasser
articles.text:
Um einen möglichst griffigen Namen für ihr Projekt zu finden, müssen Forscherinnen und Forscher bisweilen kreativ sein. Das jüngste Beispiel ist Albatross, das steht für „Airborne Lander with Buoyant AuToROtating Sailing Sensor“ und ist teilweise von Wasservögeln inspiriert.
Auch jenseits der Namensgebung ist das Projekt der Singapore University of Technology and Design innovativ: Das interdisziplinäre Team um Shane Kyi Hla Win hat nämlich einen Roboter entwickelt, der sich verschiedener Prinzipien aus dem Tier- und Pflanzenreich bedient und mit vergleichsweise wenig Hardware gleich mehrere Funktionen erfüllt. Die von unabhängigen Expertinnen und Experten begutachtete Studie ist im Fachmagazin Science Robotics erschienen.
Robotik-System zu Wasser und in der Luft
Konkret handelt es sich bei Albatross um ein multimodales Robotik-System (die Forschenden selbst nennen es eine „Sensor-Plattform“), das aus der Luft abgeworfen wird, sanft auf dem Wasser landet und sich anschließend in ein semi-autonomes Segelboot verwandelt. Die Besonderheit besteht darin, dass das System gerade mal ein Kilogramm wiegt und lediglich drei Stellmotoren und drei Sensoren enthält. Für sichere Landung und Fortbewegung sorgen allein physikalische Effekte.
Albatross ist so konzipiert, dass er von einem Flugzeug oder auch einer Drohne über offenem Gewässer abgeworfen werden kann. Um den Aufprall zu bremsen, benötigt er weder Fallschirm noch Rotoren. Stattdessen nutzt das System das Prinzip der Autorotation: Wie der geflügelte Samen eines Ahorns, beginnt das System, aufgrund von Schwerkraft und Aerodynamik um die eigene Achse zu rotieren, was wiederum Auftrieb erzeugt und gleichzeitig den Fall um ein Vielfaches abbremst.
Im Wasser angekommen, richtet sich das System aufgrund seines tiefen Schwerpunkts augenblicklich selbstständig auf. Die starren Flügel, die zuvor noch für die Rotation und Landung genutzt wurden, dienen nun als Segel. Das Hauptsegel in der Mitte rotiert frei und sowohl ein Vordersegel als auch die sogenannte Windfahne am „Heck“ sorgen für die passende Ausrichtung im Wind – wie bei einer Segelyacht. Da diese Bauteile doppelt genutzt werden, musste das Team keine zusätzlichen Teile hinzufügen.
Mit einem Kompass und GPS ausgestattet, ist Albatross anschließend in der Lage, autonom zu einem vorgegebenen Ziel zu navigieren. Ergänzt wird das System von einer von Fischen inspirierten Heckflosse, die zum Lenken dient und bei Bedarf hin- und herschwingt, um bei wenig Wind zusätzliche Schubeffekte zu erzeugen, immerhin einen knappen halben Meter pro Sekunde.
In Tests hat Albatross einen Fall aus 150 Metern über einem See überstanden und im Windkanal verschiedene Windszenarien gemeistert. In einem Wassertank hat das Team untersucht, welches Material sich am besten für das fischähnliche Ruder eignet. Zuletzt absolvierte das System dreistündige Testfahrten auf einem Stausee in Singapur und fuhr dabei eigenständig vorgegebene Navigationspunkte ab und zeichnete Umweltparameter wie Luftfeuchtigkeit und Wassertemperaturen auf.
Multimodale Roboter bleiben eine Herausforderung
Multimodale Roboter, die verschiedene Fortbewegungsmethoden nutzen, die etwa gleichzeitig fliegen und schwimmen, stellen die Forschung vor große Herausforderungen, schreiben die beiden Robotik-Forscher Raphael Zufferey und Andre Farinha in einem Begleittext zur Studie. Roboter seien deshalb immer noch in den meisten Fällen eingeschränkt: Entweder sie fliegen, oder sie laufen, oder sie schwimmen. Um die Modalitäten zu kombinieren, sucht die Wissenschaft nach Inspiration in der Natur: Denn viele Lebewesen kommen mit verschiedenen Lebensräumen gut klar. „Albatross veranschaulicht ein allgemeineres Prinzip der multimodalen Robotik: Die Natur liefert zwar keine Komplettlösung, stellt jedoch nützliche Komponenten zur Verfügung“, schreiben Zufferey und Farinha.
Dem Team aus Singapur ging es nicht zuletzt darum, zu demonstrieren, wie sich vergleichsweise günstige und simple Lösungen entwickeln lassen, die nicht mit Elektronik, Sensoren und Motoren vollgestopft sind, sondern sich physikalischer Effekte bedienen. Das spart nicht nur Geld, sondern öffnet auch zusätzliche Möglichkeiten: So soll Albatross deutlich mehr Nutzlast in Form zusätzlicher Sensoren transportieren können als andere Flug-Schwimm-Drohnen.
Als mögliches Einsatzgebiet sehen die Forschenden Umweltkatastrophen wie Ölverschmutzungen oder Algenblüten. Roboter wie Albatross könnten hier abgeworfen werden, um Daten schnell und direkt von der Wasseroberfläche zu liefern. Einen Nachteil aber hat das System: Wieder aus dem Wasser abheben kann es nicht. Dieses Feature fehlt dann doch noch, um ein echter Albatros zu sein.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 5, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 5, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, October 5, 2026.
From PanIIT Alumni India and the Andhra Pradesh government’s plan to create a Rs 500 crore venture fund focused on deeptech companies, to Ola Electric’s Chairman, Bhavish Aggarwal pledging a 4.32% stake in the company to raise funds, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
PhysicsWallah retreats from direct student lending
Edtech firm PhysicsWallah (PW) has moved decisively to reduce its exposure to direct student lending, with its wholly-owned subsidiary FinZ Finance agreeing to sell a Rs 95.79 crore loan portfolio to Auxilo Finserve, an RBI-registered NBFC focused on education finance.
The deal covers a substantial or major part of FinZ’s loan book and is expected to result in a partial closure of its lending operations, PW said, adding the transition of the loans and borrowers should be completed within 60 days.
The significance of this move lies in the speed of the reversal.
Latest news
Bhavish Aggarwal pledges 4.32% stake to back Ola Electric
Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal has stepped up to back the company’s upcoming Rs 1,000 crore rights issue, pledging a 4.32% stake in the EV maker to fund his participation.
The move comes days after Ola Electric’s board greenlit the plan to raise fresh capital through partly paid-up shares and appointed Deepa Bansal as its new compliance chief to bolster governance.
According to stock exchange filings on Sunday, Aggarwal pledged 20 crore shares against non-convertible debentures issued by Krutrim Data Centre Private Limited—a non-operative promoter entity owned by Aggarwal—to CTL Trusteeship Limited. The company clarified that no shares are being sold, no other pledges exist on his holdings, and Aggarwal will subscribe to the issue on the same terms as all other shareholders.
Other news
DigiCert launches global Partner Network to accelerate digital trust and quantum readiness
DigiCert has introduced the DigiCert Partner Network, a global initiative designed to help partners deliver, manage, and scale digital trust solutions across six distinct business models, including a dedicated MSP Program.
Built on the DigiCert ONE platform, the network enables partners to move beyond basic certificate lifecycle automation into high-growth areas like PKI modernisation, software and device security, AI trust, and post-quantum cryptography transition, unlocking recurring, services-led revenue streams.
Table Space expands Hyderabad portfolio, partners DoorDash
Table Space, India’s largest flexible workspace operator by leased area, has expanded its Hyderabad footprint to 1.56 million sq. ft. across eight years. As the market expands beyond established hubs like HITEC City into emerging corridors like Neopolis, global local-commerce platform DoorDash has chosen Table Space to establish its first India talent hub. Table Space will oversee the leasing, design, build, and management of DoorDash’s initial and long-term HITEC City offices.
This collaboration highlights Table Space’s enterprise-focused managed-office model. Nationally, GCCs account for 53.50% of the company’s leased area, positioning Table Space to capture growing global demand across key Indian commercial hubs.
WeWork India expands Bengaluru and Pune footprint with 4,500+ desks
WeWork India Management Limited has expanded its footprint by opening two new centres in key commercial hubs: WeWork Infinix Palladium in Bengaluru and WeWork Millennium Towers in Pune. Together, the locations add approximately 2.25 lakh sq. ft. and over 4,500 desks to the company’s national portfolio, responding to rising demand in self-sustained urban corridors.
Spanning 1.7 lakh sq. ft. near the Singayyanapalya Metro Station, the standalone Whitefield centre in Bengaluru offers 3,100+ desks tailored for large enterprise scale. In Pune, the LEED Platinum-certified Wakad facility adds 55,000 sq. ft. and 1,400 desks, capitalizing on proximity to the Hinjewadi tech hub and the Mumbai-Pune Expressway.""
Razorpay teams up with OpenAI to launch ChatGPT ads for Indian brands
Fintech giant Razorpay has partnered with OpenAI to help Indian businesses run ad campaigns on ChatGPT via its Razorpay Engage platform. The collaboration enables brands to optimize product catalogues, manage feeds, and run targeted, AI-driven campaigns as consumers shift toward conversational product discovery over traditional keyword searches.
Prominent early adopters include Tanishq, Tata Neu, Fastrack, Axis Max Life, Traya, Shaadi.com, Palmonas, and NMIMS. Powered by an AI agent with human oversight, Razorpay Engage handles campaign setup, catalogue readiness, and performance tracking, allowing local businesses to seamlessly tap into conversational AI discovery without building in-house technical infrastructure.
Snabbit appoints rormer PhonePe executive Ramesh Srinivasan as Head of Growth and Revenue
Quick home services platform Snabbit has named former PhonePe marketing leader Ramesh Srinivasan as Head of Growth and Revenue. Srinivasan, who previously held senior roles at Flipkart and PhonePe, will oversee customer acquisition, retention, brand strategy, and monetization across home help, cooks, and beauty verticals.
His mandate focuses on scaling demand across Snabbit's nanomarkets through hyper-local planning and brand building. The hire follows the recent appointments of Chief Business Officer Abhinav Ankur and Operations Head Pradeep Yadav, bolstering Snabbit's leadership team as the company expands across five major urban centers after surpassing 10 million completed jobs.
MathWorks and MapmyIndia Mappls partner to Accelerate ADAS validation for India
MathWorks has partnered with MapmyIndia Mappls to integrate high-definition maps into MATLAB, Simulink, and RoadRunner workflows, enabling automotive engineers to simulate and validate Advanced Driver Assistance Systems for Indian driving conditions. By capturing local nuances like lane-level geometry, variable traffic, potholes, speed breakers, and faded markings, the integration creates realistic digital twins of complex road environments.
This allows engineering teams to test ADAS controllers early using Model-Based Design, reducing reliance on expensive physical testing and accelerating the deployment of automotive safety technologies built specifically for India’s unique traffic ecosystems.
Indian Specialty Coffee Debuts Across Greece and Cyprus
On International Coffee Day, Indian Ambassador Shri Ravi Shankar launched The Origin Box in Athens, introducing Indian specialty coffee to Europe. The initiative is a partnership between Karnataka-based venture The Coorg Coffee Club and Greek retailer Coffee Island, placing the curated collection in over 400 stores across Greece and Cyprus.
Featuring five specially processed coffees—spanning Arabica, Canephora, and Excelsa—from five distinct Coorg estates, each lot is documented from harvest to roast and carries its grower’s name. This collaboration establishes Indian shade-grown coffee as a traceable, premium origin, showcasing its distinct flavor profile to European consumers.

articles.title: IQVIA fined $7.8 million for failing to properly anonymize health data
articles.text:
Italy's Data Protection Authority (GPDP) has fined IQVIA €7 million ($7.8M) over poor data-processing practices that the agency says could have put roughly one million patients at risk of data exposure and de-anonymization.
IQVIA is a multinational company that provides healthcare data analysis, technology, and clinical research services. The company claims on its website that it operates in over 100 countries and handles 68 petabytes of data and 1.2 billion patient records.
Italian authorities investigated IQVIA's data-processing practices in April 2025, and last month decided that the company did not provide adequate health-data anonymization warranties, despite its claims.
GPDP has found that IQVIA's Italian division had created a database containing the health information of roughly one million patients by aggregating data from 800 general practitioners.
While the company used a unique code instead of patients' names in those records, the data protection agency found they could be used to track and de-anonymize patients over time.
"The code associated with each patient made it possible to track them over time,” explained GPDP in an announcement published late last week.
“Combined with a very detailed set of information (year of birth, sex, diagnoses, symptoms, prescriptions, tests, vaccinations, as well as location data), it made it possible to single out individual patients and, using reasonable means, reidentify them.”
In addition, IQVIA processed data without an appropriate legal basis and without informing patients, which violates the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation).
Finally, IQVIA allegedly did not establish or follow any data retention periods, with the GPDP finding records dating back as far as 2001.
For a subset of 3,300 patients in IQVIA's database, the company also included names, tax identification numbers, addresses, and contact details.
In addition to the $7.8 million fine, Italian authorities also ordered the company to bring its practices into compliance within 120 days.
BleepingComputer has contacted the firm with questions about the fine, and a spokesperson sent us the following statement:
"IQVIA is committed to the responsible use of data and information and continues to cooperate with the Authority. Protecting data is a core priority for IQVIA, and we maintain robust safeguards, including the use of pseudonymization and encryption, to support responsible data use in healthcare.
IQVIA acknowledges the decision adopted by the Italian Data Protection Authority and reserves the right to appeal. The dataset to which the Italian Data Protection Authority's decision relates is not used by IQVIA in conduct of clinical research services and does not relate to the conduct of clinical trials on behalf of the sponsors.
We have engaged constructively with the Italian Data Protection Authority throughout this process and have already taken steps to adopt the measures necessary to ensure full alignment with the Authority's guidance."

articles.title: Engo Titanium : ces lunettes de sport avec écran OLED pèsent à peine 29 grammes — Frandroid
articles.text:
La start-up grenobloise Engo, qui conçoit des lunettes de sport à affichage tête haute, a dévoilé, ce mardi 6 octobre, ses Engo3 Titanium, une version à monture en titane de ses Engo3.
La marque annonce 28,9 grammes sur la balance. D’après ses chiffres, une paire de lunettes de sport classique pèse en moyenne 25 grammes, soit à peine quatre grammes de moins. À titre de comparaison, les Oakley Meta Vanguard, le modèle sportif de Meta, pèsent 66 grammes et coûtent 549 euros, mais embarquent une caméra, des haut-parleurs et des micros, sans aucun écran.
    Pour aller plus loin
J’ai couru avec des lunettes de réalité augmentée et c’était bizarre : test des Engo 2
            
Comme les autres modèles d’Engo, les Titanium n’ont ni caméra, ni micro, ni haut-parleurs. Elles servent uniquement à afficher vos données d’effort dans votre champ de vision, grâce à un petit écran Oled couleur. Plus de 40 métriques sont proposées, de la fréquence cardiaque à la cadence en passant par l’allure. Des widgets permettent aussi de suivre un fractionné sans baisser les yeux vers la montre.
La marque française n’en est pas à son coup d’essai. Nous avions couru avec ses Engo 2 en 2023, puis Engo a dévoilé les Engo3 en mars, avant de les décliner pour le vélo en septembre. Les Titanium reprennent la même technologie d’affichage, baptisée ActiveLook, et se pilotent d’un double tapotement détecté par un capteur. Elles récupèrent les données en Bluetooth depuis une montre Garmin, une Apple Watch ou d’autres appareils compatibles ActiveLook. Sur Apple Watch, la compatibilité reste partielle : pas de widget de puissance ni d’alertes radar. En revanche, les montres Coros et Polar ne sont pas prises en charge.
Des lunettes à affichage tête haute encore plus légères
D’après Engo, une paire de lunettes qui dépasserait les 40 grammes n’aurait plus sa place sur le marché du sport, ce qui laisse une quinzaine de grammes pour caser toute l’électronique. Engo consacre ce budget au seul écran. Meta a fait un tri comparable avec les Ray-Ban Meta Audio, ses premières lunettes sans caméra, qui misent tout sur le son et l’assistant vocal.
Sur le papier, les Titanium font mieux que les Engo3 en poids comme en autonomie. Les Engo3 pèsent 38,5 grammes pour 20 heures d’autonomie annoncée. Les Titanium descendent à 28,9 grammes, et Engo leur annonce au moins 24 heures d’utilisation continue, sans préciser la luminosité de l’écran ni le nombre de métriques affichées pendant la mesure.
Pour gagner ces dix grammes, Engo a remplacé la monture en polymère des Engo3 par une monture d’une seule pièce en titane, imprimée en 3D dans ses laboratoires de Grenoble, aux branches réglables en largeur comme en hauteur. Ce changement de matériau ajoute 250 euros à la facture par rapport aux Engo3 à leur sortie (349 euros), pour la même technologie d’affichage.
Les Engo3 Titanium sont disponibles à partir de ce mardi 6 octobre en édition limitée à 500 exemplaires numérotés dans le monde, uniquement sur le site d’Engo. Elles coûtent 599 euros, ou 649 euros avec des verres photochromiques qui s’assombrissent au soleil (contre 399 euros pour les Engo3 photochromiques). Trois coloris sont proposés : Azure et Silver, ainsi que Shift pour la version photochromique.

articles.title: African startup exits: What the Class of 2016 returned
articles.text:
Ten years, $1.89 billion, and almost no liquidity.
Since its founding in 2016, Flutterwave has raised about $475 million, more than any of the 200-plus African startups founded that year. The 166 smallest companies in its cohort have raised roughly $210 million between them over the same decade.
This disparity in how one payments company from Lagos took in more than twice what two-thirds of its class managed in ten years combined is the story of Africa’s venture capital industry, shown in a year’s intake.
The mid-2010s were a good moment to start a company on the continent. Mobile money was spreading, smartphone prices were falling, and global funds were beginning to treat Africa as an asset class. In 2016, startups were founded across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Uganda and Ghana, spanning fintech, agritech, e-commerce, cleantech and health.
TechCabal Insights tracked all of them through October 2026.
Venture funds are typically built with a 10-year lifespan, making a decade the industry’s own yardstick. By that timeline, the cohort has had time to do everything a startup can do: scale, sell, stall or stop. Together they raised about $1.89 billion, around 8.6% of the roughly $22 billion that flowed into African startups since 2016, but they produced almost no liquidity.
If you think of fundraising as a metric of success, then this reads like success. If you measure it by African startup exits, it reads like something else.
The concentration
Thirty-four companies account for $1.68 billion of the $1.89 billion. That is 89% of the cohort’s capital going to under a fifth of its members. More than 20 companies raised nothing. The median company raised about $1 million. The average, dragged by the top, was $9.45 million, a figure that describes few companies in the cohort.
Strip out the top 34, and the remaining 166 companies averaged $1.25 million each across ten years.
How concentrated was $1.89B of funding?
Flutterwave alone raised $475M — 25.1% of the cohort’s total capital.
What if the money were evenly distributed?
What does “39× more” actually mean?
And then there’s Flutterwave.
For most startups, $1.25 million over a decade finances a small team, a product that never gets the engineering it needs to scale, and a founder who spends much of the year raising money. Companies in that band were running a different business from the winners, one where survival was the daily objective and growth was a hope.
Power laws are normal in venture capital. Silicon Valley’s 2016 vintage concentrated too. What matters is what the concentration produces. In a functioning market, the winners exit, capital returns to funds, funds recycle it into the next cohort, and early employees become the next founders. The Class of 2016 generated very little of that.
The money also had a strong view about where problems were worth solving. Fintech took the largest share. Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Egypt took almost all of it. A founder in Kampala building for agriculture in 2016 competed for a different pool of capital compared with the one Lagos fintech drew on, and the Kampala pool was nearly empty.
The exits that were not exits
Twenty-seven companies were acquired or merged between 2019 and October 2026. Twenty-one of those deals had undisclosed prices, which is a finding in itself. Sellers publicise good numbers. A decade of silence on 21 transactions is a result.
The disclosed deals reveal a strategy that works for African startups seeking to offer returns to investors.
DocFox, a Johannesburg company selling client-onboarding software to banks, was acquired by the American banking-software firm nCino in March 2024. nCino announced a $75 million price, and its filings record $74.3 million paid in cash.
Syft Analytics, also from Johannesburg and bootstrapped from the start, agreed to sell to accounting platform Xero in September 2024 for up to $70 million, with $40 million upfront. It had reached $4.4 million in revenue from 75,000 customers across 80 countries. The deal closed in October 2025.
Neither company raised anything close to what it sold for. They are, by a distance, the best disclosed returns in the cohort. Neither was a consumer fintech platform. Neither was a household name in Lagos or Nairobi. Both sold software to businesses abroad in hard currency to a foreign strategic buyer. The decade’s two best outcomes came from companies that focused on a global market.
LXE Hearing, formerly HearX, took a different route to the same destination. The South African hearing-technology company raised $111 million over the decade and merged with the American firm Eargo in March 2025. The combined company is headquartered in San Jose and backed by $100 million from Patient Square Capital, an American private-equity firm. A success, and one that left the continent.
The rest of the acquisitions were consolidation. Zeepay, the Ghanaian fintech with operations across more than 10 African countries, acquired Zambia’s Mangwee. Treepz, a Nigerian-based mobility-as-a-service platform, bought Uganda’s Ugabus. These are category leaders buying licences and market share. Deals at that scale do not produce venture-scale returns.
The failures and what they cost
Six companies announced shutdowns publicly. Between them, they had raised about $55 million.
WhereIsMyTransport raised $28 million to map informal transport networks and closed in October 2023 after failing to raise again. Zumi, a Kenyan e-commerce platform, closed in March 2023, raising just under $1 million.
Snatcher, a South African retailer, closed in late 2024 following internal fraud. Bento Africa, a Nigerian payroll startup that raised $3.1 million, temporarily halted its operations in February 2025 after its founder resigned amid allegations of tax and pension irregularities, missed January salaries, and laid off its engineering team. Medsaf, which raised $7 million to digitise Nigeria’s pharmaceutical supply chain, shut down in 2024.
Read together, the causes do not rhyme. One ran out of investors. One ran out of market. One was stolen from. One was governed badly. One could not make the unit economics of physical distribution work. There is no distinctly African failure mode here, only the ordinary range of ways a company dies, compressed into a cohort.
The most instructive story did not end in a shutdown notice. Kobo360 raised more than $79 million in equity and debt, including backing from Juven, a Goldman Sachs spin-off, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and TLcom Capital, to digitise freight across five African countries. It aggregated more than 50,000 trucks for clients including Unilever, Dangote and DHL.
The model consumed cash. Kobo360 paid transporters immediately and waited 30 to 90 days for large corporates to pay. When a bank partner cut its credit line over unserviced debt, the gap became unbridgeable. In March 2025, its venture backers sold their equity to co-founder Obi Ozor for an undisclosed sum, with the IFC saying publicly that it had not transferred its own stake. Ozor inherited a company owing more than ₦10 billion ($6.5 million) to banks. As of October 2026, Y Combinator lists Kobo360 as inactive. There was no liquidation, no filing and no announcement.
Beneath all of this sits the silent majority. Dozens of companies in the cohort now show no working website, no product, and no news in years. They were never liquidated. They stopped. No filing marks the moment, which is why the true failure rate of any African cohort runs higher than the announced one.
What the decade proved
Most of the cohort still exists in some form, and some of it is quietly profitable. African founders did not fail. The lesson is narrower and harder than that.
Legibility to foreign investors decided who got funded. The companies that raised the most were the ones whose business models a fund in London or San Francisco could invest in without understanding Lagos.
Returns followed a similar rule. The companies that returned the most sold software abroad in dollars.
The companies that took on the hardest local problems—freight, pharmaceutical distribution, transport data—raised the biggest rounds and returned the least.
Venture capital requires liquidity events, and this cohort produced almost none. After ten years and $1.89 billion, the two clearest wins were B2B software companies that raised less than $10 million and sold to foreign acquirers.
Africa’s demographic weight is not in doubt, and demand for technology in logistics, health, agriculture and finance will only grow. The Class of 2016 shows that a decade of venture capital was never going to be the mechanism that met it. The next cohort will need instruments this one lacked: revenue-based finance, local-currency debt, development finance, and patient capital with no ten-year clock.
Business as usual produced 34 winners and 166 companies averaging $1.25 million each. There is no sign it will do better the second time.
Data note: 200-plus startups founded in Africa in 2016, tracked through October 2026 across funding, mergers and acquisitions, and operating status. Compiled from the TechCabal Insights database alongside Africa: The Big Deal, Crunchbase, Tracxn, PitchBook and Briter, which do not always agree on founding year. Funding totals include disclosed equity, debt and grants. Rounds with undisclosed amounts are excluded, so the real total is higher than the figure reported here. 21 of the 27 acquisitions had undisclosed values.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. Dreame décline son H15 Pro en plusieurs versions, toutes dotées d'un atout propre. Le H15 Mix, lui, possède plusieurs cordes à son arc et peut prendre la forme d’un laveur de sol, d’un aspirateur-balai ou même d’une shampouineuse pour tissus.

articles.title: Anthropic chama polícia após mulher ameaçar ataque em conversa • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Anthropic chama polícia após mulher ameaçar ataque em conversa
Mulher foi presa na Flórida após supostas ameaças registradas no chatbot Claude.
A Anthropic acionou a polícia após identificar uma ameaça de ataque na Flórida durante conversas de uma usuária com a inteligência artificial do Claude. Carli Michelle Heller foi presa sob acusação de fazer uma ameaça eletrônica de violência, algo considerado grave pela legislação do estado.
Segundo a ocorrência, Heller teria escrito em 26 de setembro que pretendia atacar o escritório do xerife e, no dia seguinte, teria mencionado que conseguiu uma nova arma. As mensagens foram identificadas pelos mecanismos automatizados de segurança e encaminhadas a uma equipe de revisão humana, que comunicou as autoridades.
O relatório policial afirma que o sistema da Anthropic monitora conversas em busca de expressões e conteúdos potencialmente ameaçadores. Quando uma mensagem é considerada grave, ela pode ser encaminhada para análise humana.
A empresa informa em sua documentação que pode fornecer dados às autoridades em situações de emergência nas quais considere que a divulgação é necessária para evitar risco de morte ou ferimentos físicos graves.
De acordo com o relato, Heller usava a ferramenta de IA como um diário para registrar pensamentos e conversar sobre assuntos pessoais. As mensagens tratadas como ameaça teriam surgido nesse contexto.
A acusação contra ela é baseada no Estatuto da Flórida 836.10, que prevê punição para ameaças escritas ou transmitidas eletronicamente de morte, violência, tiroteio em massa ou ato terrorista. Registros judiciais indicam que Heller foi formalmente acusada pelo crime em 30 de setembro.
O caso reforça que, embora usuários possam recorrer a chatbots para conversar sobre questões pessoais, as plataformas não possuem obrigação de proteger essas informações. No ano passado, Sam Altman, CEO da concorrente OpenAI, já havia dito que os chatbots não seguem as mesmas regras de sigilo que um psicólogo ou advogado, por exemplo – além de poderem ser lidas por mecanismos de segurança, como no caso de Heller, o histórico das conversas também pode ser facilmente entregue às autoridades.
A denúncia da Anthropic sugere que os laboratórios de IA podem ficar ainda menos tolerantes quanto a sugestões criminosas dentro de suas plataformas após casos nos quais a empresa virou alvo de ações legais quando o crime foi consumado.
Em um episódio recente, a OpenAI não acionou a polícia após identificar conversas sobre violência armada entre uma adolescente e a IA. A OpenAI foi processada depois de o crime acontecer.

articles.title: RevPDF
articles.text:
RevPDF is a free PDF editor that lets you edit text and images, organize pages, fill and sign forms, redact sensitive information, run OCR, compare documents, compress files, and convert PDFs to formats such as Word and Excel. It also supports reusable automated workflows for repetitive PDF tasks.
Document processing happens locally on your device, without uploading PDF content to RevPDF's servers.
Features
WYSIWYG Content Editing
Edit existing text directly with paragraph reflow and layout-aware visual controls.
PDF Compare
Compare two PDFs and identify changes during reviews, revisions and final checks.
Annotations
Highlight, underline and add comments during review.
Draw and Markup
Add freehand notes and shapes to contracts, diagrams and plans.
Find and Replace
Locate text across a PDF and update repeated content in place.
Tabbed Viewer
Keep several PDFs open and switch between them without losing your place.
Links and Bookmarks
Add navigation for readers of longer documents.
Customizable Redaction
Remove sensitive text or images permanently, customize the result and use auto-redact for repeated content.
Headers and Footers
Add page numbers, document details and custom text across selected pages.
Form Builder
Create text fields, checkboxes, dropdowns and radio groups, with field detection.
Form Filling
Complete fillable PDFs and save the finished document.
Electronic Signing
Draw, type or import a signature and save it for reuse.
Watermarks
Add text or image marks such as Draft, Confidential or your brand.
Flows
Combine supported PDF operations into reusable automated workflows for repeat processing.
Compression
Create much smaller PDF files with better control over quality and output size.
Split and Merge
Separate by page or range, combine documents, or divide a page at a selected vertical or horizontal position.
Page Organization
Reorder, rotate and remove pages with drag-and-drop controls.
Metadata Editor
Update title, author, subject, keywords and document dates.
Capture and Convert
Turn scanned or fixed-layout PDF content into useful, editable and archive-ready output.
On-device OCR
Turn scanned pages into searchable, selectable text on your device.
PDF to Excel
Extract PDF content into spreadsheet output for analysis and reuse.
PDF to Word
Create more useful editable Word documents with the improved conversion engine.
PDF/A-2a Conversion
Create an archival PDF/A-2a copy for long-term preservation workflows.
PDF and Image Conversion
Convert between PDF, JPEG and PNG without sending the file to a web service.
Document Scanning
Capture paper documents on mobile with edge detection and perspective correction.
Localization
Use RevPDF in multiple interface languages, with room for language support to expand.
New Themes
Choose an interface theme that suits your workspace and viewing preference.
Large-PDF Performance
Work more smoothly with better stability, responsiveness and performance on large documents.
What's New
RevPDF 5.0 is biggest desktop update yet, bringing a more powerful editing experience, new automation tools, improved conversions, better performance, and much more.
- WYSIWYG PDF Editor - Edit PDF text more naturally with improved paragraph reflow and layout handling.
- PDF Compare - Quickly find differences between two PDF files.
- Flows - Automate repetitive PDF processing tasks and run multiple operations in sequence.
- PDF to Excel - Extract and convert PDF content into sheets.
- Improved PDF to Word - Better layout preservation and more accurate document conversion.
- PDF/A Conversion - Convert documents to archival-friendly PDF/A format.
- Improved Compression - Smaller PDF files with better quality and improved compression logic.
- Customizable Redaction - More control over how redacted content looks and behaves.
- Header & Footer Tools - Add page numbers, text, and custom headers or footers.
- Improved Split Tool - Better support for splitting pages through the middle or at a custom position.
- Localization - RevPDF is now available in multiple languages.
- New Themes - More ways to personalize the RevPDF interface.
- Large PDF Improvements - Better stability, responsiveness, and performance when working with large documents.
- General Stability & Performance Improvements - Numerous fixes and optimizations across the app.
Local-First PDF Editing
- RevPDF processes your PDF files directly on your device. Your documents don't need to be uploaded to a server just to edit, convert, compress, redact and much more.

articles.title: Intel Reportedly Limits "Nova Lake DS" Samples, Rollout Starts in December
articles.text:
Monday, October 5th 2026
Intel Reportedly Limits "Nova Lake DS" Samples, Rollout Starts in December
Intel is reportedly limiting access to some of its most interesting "Nova Lake" processors during the early development stages. According to leaker Jaykihn, chips with the internal "DS" designation are being distributed to a much smaller group of testers compared to the rest of the "Nova Lake" lineup. This "DS" designation reportedly includes parts built around two compute tiles, which are expected to be among the first to be released. These SKUs are currently known to carry the "BFC" suffix, which has appeared on several leaked Core Ultra 4000 desktop processors and is linked to Intel's larger big last-level cache (bLLC) implementation. For example, the leaked Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC is a 28-core processor combining eight P-cores, 16 E-cores, and four LPE cores.
The scarcity of BFC hardware in public leaks may be more related to Intel's sampling policy than to availability. The leaker claims these processors are being kept within a restricted testing group, preventing them from appearing through the standard qualification-sample pipeline that usually produces early benchmarks and hardware detections. This way, no public benchmark scores are surfacing, leaving us in complete dark before the official launch happens.This situation could change in December 2026, when wider DS sampling is reportedly scheduled to begin, including qualification samples. This would delay the broader rollout of these chips compared to some other Nova Lake segments, despite BFC models allegedly being among the first processors Intel plans to launch. "Nova Lake-S" is currently expected to arrive in Q1 2027, and the four-digit Core Ultra 4000 naming scheme is also expected to extend to "Nova Lake-HX" mobile parts. Intel has yet to confirm the DS designation, BFC branding, sampling schedule, or final specifications, so the current information is based entirely on leaks and should be taken with a grain of salt, as always.
