articles.title: New forensic evidence supports Egyptian "retainer sacrifice"
articles.text:
Egyptologists have long debated whether the earliest pharaohs of the First Dynasty were buried with various servants and officials to serve them in the afterlife—a form of human sacrifice. But there is very little archaeological evidence available, given that many of the earliest Egyptian tombs were plundered and/or hastily excavated. A new paper published in the journal Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology reassesses a collection of skulls excavated from tombs in the 1920s and concludes that over one-third show evidence of blunt force trauma. This suggests that they may have been victims of so-called “retainer sacrifice.”
Author Roselyn Campbell is a bioarchaeologist at Purdue University who has long been fascinated with the history of human sacrifice. “I’m interested in how we as human beings decide which types of violence are okay and which are not, and how we even define violence,” Campbell told Ars. “It’s very context-specific. We have to be careful not to extend our own ideas about what violence is and how it’s used into other cultures. With Egypt, we have such a long history of European and colonial archeology; they came in with very specific ideas about what this culture was. You really have to make an effort to contextualize the legacy data we have.”
Naturally she found the debate over whether ancient Egyptians practiced retainer sacrifice pertinent to her interests. “People tend to fall into one of two camps,” said Campbell. “Either retainer sacrifice definitely happened, end of discussion, or it definitely didn’t happen, end of discussion. But nobody’s actually looked at the bones in a very long time.” Forensic science has advanced considerably over the last century, so re-analysis could be useful. Complicating matters is the fact that older sets of remains are often incomplete and/or modified for preservation, destroying vital forensic information in the process.
Cold case files
As a case study, Campbell turned to a collection of human remains first excavated by famed British archaeologist Flinders Petrie in the 1920s, from the Abydos site in southern Egypt. Abydos is the site of a royal necropolis where many of the early pharaohs were buried, along with many ancient temples. (It’s also the home of what may be the world’s oldest brewery.) This particular set of remains—46 crania stored at Cambridge University—came from the Umm el-Qaab cemetery, which contains subsidiary burials presumed to be retainers of deceased First Dynasty rulers. Petrie noted several grave markers with names and official titles, mostly lower- to mid-level officials and artisans.

articles.title: Aspire 13.6 Adds Persistent Dashboard Telemetry and First-Party Java and Rust Hosting
articles.text:
Last week, Microsoft released Aspire 13.6. The release adds persistent telemetry and run history to the dashboard, along with docked terminals and database REPLs, first-party hosting for Java and Rust, and two Azure preview integrations. It also brings coordinated .NET project builds, portable volume paths, new CLI and Visual Studio Code workflows, and several breaking changes.
The dashboard now stores resource snapshots and telemetry in a SQLite database. When started by an AppHost, it uses run persistence by default and keeps up to ten runs per application. Completed runs are read-only. As stated in the release notes, the database has no encryption or authorization layer, and Aspire does not set Windows ACLs on the data directory.
Default limits for console logs, structured logs, and traces rise to 100,000 each. Also, the dashboard now ships as a Native AOT executable and moves to Fluent UI Blazor v5.
(Run persistence by default, Source: Official Microsoft documentation)
Furthermore, AppHosts can now open their own terminals in a dashboard dock through the experimental TerminalService API. A new WithRepl option on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, SQL Server, Redis, and Valkey resources opens the client bundled in the container. According to the release, these REPLs use the resource's real credentials and are not read-only, so they stay disabled unless a developer opts in.
Four hosting integrations arrive as prerelease packages. Aspire.Hosting.Java supports executable JARs, Maven and Gradle wrappers, Spring Boot, and Quarkus. Aspire.Hosting.Rust models Cargo applications through AddRustApp.
var builder = DistributedApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.AddRustApp("api", "../rust-api")
    .WithHttpEndpoint(env: "PORT")
    .WithExternalHttpEndpoints();
builder.Build().Run();
Both build on work from the Aspire Community Toolkit, as described in the release notes. Azure Connector Namespace and Azure Container Apps Sandboxes are also added, with a note that both need preview access in the Azure subscription.
As reported, AddDotnetProject now places compatible projects into shared restore and build groups, which avoids repeated restores. Volume mounts on projects and executables accept a new env argument, so an application reads one environment variable for its data path locally and after deployment.
TypeScript AppHosts load appsettings.json from their own directory, and Deno 2 or later can run the TypeScript AppHost.
The CLI adds a --launch-profile option to aspire run and aspire start. According to the source, agent setup in aspire new and aspire init now leaves the Aspire MCP server unselected, which makes MCP opt-in. The Visual Studio Code extension lets coding agents start and stop AppHosts, and adds deploy and publish actions to the Aspire pane.
Among the breaking changes, MongoDB resources now use TLS during local runs when a certificate is available, which replaces the earlier plaintext default. The Cosmos DB emulator defaults to the Linux-based vNext image and, as stated, existing classic emulator data does not carry over.
Azure Front Door origin names change on upgrade, and connection names with hyphens get a portable environment-variable alias that some deployment targets emit on their own.
Other changes in this release are Azure Container Apps Express environments, Microsoft Foundry Toolboxes, MongoDB replica sets, Blazor WebAssembly debugging, and the removal of the GitHub Models integration.
For interested readers, the full What's New in Aspire 13.6 page, including the complete inventory, migration notes, and breaking changes, is available on the Aspire documentation site.

articles.title: Dutch eyewear company is the first retailer to pull Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses from over 400 stores due to ‘questions being raised’ about the technology
articles.text:
Dutch eyewear giant becomes first retailer to halt Meta Ray-ban sales — Hans Anders pulls smart glasses from 400 stores due to ‘questions being raised’ about the tech
Putting the 'ban' in 'Ray-Ban'
- Eyewear retailer Hans Anders has stopped sales of Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses
- The decision comes amid growing concerns over the public use of the tech
- Dutch consumer rights group Consumentenbond has said it will take Meta to court if it fails to comply with the law
The clampdown on privacy-threatening ‘pervert glasses’ continues, with Dutch eyewear retailer Hans Anders pulling the Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses from its online and high street stores in Belgium and the Netherlands indefinitely.
Hans Anders is part of the nexeye retail group, which operates over 400 stores across those two countries alone. When combined with its stores across Germany, Austria, and Sweden, it has 776 stores in total, although the Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses aren’t sold in the latter three regions.
The use of smart glasses has sparked a heated debate about whether these devices belong in public spaces, with concerns raised about general safety and privacy. Speaking with Reuters, a spokesperson for Hans Anders detailed the company’s decision to make the bold move, sharing the following:
"This decision follows the ongoing public and political debate surrounding smart glasses and the questions being raised about the conditions under which this technology can be used”.
One of the biggest areas of concern is women's privacy. According to a report from the NL Times, Meta's smart glasses have been used to capture footage of 'hundreds, maybe thousands' of Dutch women without their consent over the past few months. The outlet says the footage has been shared on messaging apps such as Telegram, as well as other harmful online sites.
The move follows a recent warning issued by the Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP), which said that photos and video footage of identifiable individuals taken using smart glasses can’t be shared without the individual's permission — though this is something that's clearly difficult to control in public spaces.
That’s not the only organization that’s decided to take an active stance against Meta. Earlier this week Consumentenbond, a consumer rights group, declared it will take Meta to court if the tech giant doesn’t amend its smart glasses to comply with privacy laws. That said, Meta says it’s always developing its smart glasses:
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"Every pair with a camera has a bright light on the front that blinks when you take a photo or video — it can't be turned off, and the camera is disabled if someone covers or tampers with it," a Meta spokesperson said. Despite this indicator, there’s nothing in place to stop users from covering the light to stop others from knowing if they’re being filmed.
As far as retailers go, Hans Anders is one of the first to enact a public protest against smart glasses, joining the fight to protect the privacy and wellbeing of consumers. The Netherlands’ combat against these devices is only just beginning — and other nations have expressed similar concerns.
The UK is also taking similar measures to ensure public spaces are free from the looming threat of smart glasses. Popular pub chain Wetherspoons has banned the use of smart glasses in its pubs across the country, while the UK Cinema Association says movie theaters could also introduce similar smart glasses restrictions to prevent piracy, and even stop users from livestreaming movies to social media platforms .

articles.title: Instinct brings its AI agent to group chats, even for friends without an account | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Instinct, the AI agent now valued at $10 billion as of its latest funding round, is expanding into group chats. The startup announced on Monday that users will be able to add the agent to chats with friends, which could be helpful in certain scenarios like travel planning, snagging event tickets, running fantasy leagues, organizing carpools, or managing who’s bringing what to Thanksgiving.
Notably, the group chats with the AI agent will work even if a user’s friends haven’t joined Instinct, the company said.
With the launch, Instinct moves ahead in its battle with top competitors in the space, like Meta’s Muse. The latter doesn’t yet offer the group chat functionality, though Meta’s older app, Meta AI, can be added to group chats on WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, and Facebook.
Instinct and Muse have been running neck and neck recently, with both of them adding the ability to make phone calls over the past couple of weeks, as their agents try to win more of the consumer AI market. Last week, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Dots, personal AI agents that can also be used in ChatGPT Spaces, collaborative workspaces where the Dots and humans work together.
On X, Instinct founder Noah Shinn explained how Instinct handles users’ privacy and security in group chats. He said a user’s personal Instinct agent will ask permission before connecting with the group’s Instinct agent, and that users can also choose which groups they trust and can remove that trust at any time.
Shinn also said the group’s Instinct is siloed from the users’ personal accounts, which it cannot access. The personal agent will always ask the user’s permission before sharing information or taking any action.
If new members join the group chat, any pending replies from a user’s personal Instinct agent are held before those are shared with the group, too.
“Making plans with friends usually turns into a frustrating back-and-forth over times and places. With Instinct in the group, you can explore options together, agree on a plan and get it done, all in one thread,” Shinn wrote.
The feature is rolling out initially to Instinct’s early access users but will expand to all users “soon.” To gain access to the new feature (or other recent additions), users can ask their Instinct agent to put them on the list to try it out.

articles.title: Promevo launches Insights to track Gemini Enterprise adoption and AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Promevo launches Insights to track Gemini Enterprise adoption and AI agents
Google Cloud partner Promevo LLC today launched Insights by Promevo, a platform for tracking adoption of Google LLC’s Gemini Enterprise and the artificial intelligence agents employees build with it, as well as spending across the rest of a customer’s Google Cloud environment.
Insights by Promevo goes after what the company calls a visibility gap in enterprise AI adoption. Google introduced Gemini Enterprise a year ago, and its no-code workbench lets staff across a business create agents of their own. According to Promevo, the native Google Cloud and Google Workspace consoles keep license and agent data on separate systems, and their history covers a rolling 28-day window. Insights pulls it all into one place with a longer record.
For Gemini Enterprise licenses, the platform separates seats that have been activated and are in use from those sitting idle, and it puts a figure on how much of the idle spending could be reclaimed. Every agent employees have built goes into an inventory that also shows what each one can access. Promevo said the software does this without reading or storing the content of prompts and responses.
Outside Gemini Enterprise, information technology and finance teams can break down cloud spending by project and service, while an asset map of the organization’s environment updates continuously. Identity and access management data is gathered across projects, and the platform flags overpermissioned users. Where Gemini Enterprise agents touch Google Cloud resources, Promevo said customers can trace a license to the agent using it and on to the cloud resources that agent draws on.
The product was built around the biggest questions enterprises have about AI, according to Promevo Chief Executive Karthik Kripapuri. One is whether agents are staying “within proper boundaries.” Kripapuri said the company is “already seeing customer organizations with thousands of agents” and expects that kind of scale to become common.
Promevo, based in Covington, Kentucky, has been in business for 25 years and says it serves more than 4,000 organizations. Alongside consulting work that includes a structured Gemini Enterprise adoption program and custom agent development, the company sells gPanel for Google Workspace administration. Enterprises that build their own agents can also list them on Google Cloud Marketplace through a Promevo program.
Insights by Promevo is available now for Google Workspace and Gemini Enterprise customers, with more of the platform due to roll out over the coming weeks.

articles.title: Amazon warns $68 billion in blocked data centers threatens US AI lead — AWS CEO decries 100 proposed bans, pledges $1B community fund
articles.text:
Amazon warns $68 billion in blocked data centers threatens US AI lead — AWS CEO decries 100 proposed bans, pledges $1B community fund
Various countries intentionally seeding misinformation in the U.S. about data centers to trick us into slowing down - AWS CEO
Amazon has issued grave warnings to communities opposing data centers, stating that their actions could cause irreversible damage to the U.S. economy and national security. In a lengthy 3000-word post earlier today, October 2, CEO of Amazon Web Services (AWS), Matt Garman detailed the many benefits of Artificial Intelligence, comparing the technology’s impact on the economy to those of modern transportation systems and the Internet, before attempting to debunk “myths” around data centers and calling on local communities to be more receptive to build-outs as a matter of national urgency. The post also details Amazon's plans to do more for data center host communities through its “Built Together” community investment frameworks.
After outlining AI’s impact and the need for data center buildouts, Garman explained why it was imperative for the U.S. to lead the AI race. “The countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it in the short and long run. The choices we make today will determine that outcome, and a lapse in our nation’s focus or resolve could put us behind, and potentially irreparably so,” he wrote, presenting urgent buildouts as a key factor in leading that race.
Next, Garman addressed growing anti-data center movements that have reportedly blocked data center projects worth $68 billion in the second quarter of 2026 alone, warning that if the 100 data center moratoriums being considered across the country should go through, “the US could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations.” He also pointed out that unlike transportation infrastructure, the comparably critical data center buildout is not funded by taxpayer money, but by private firms.
The post dismissed many of the concerns about the buildouts as myths, then proceeded to attempt to debunk them. Garman said that, contrary to popular belief, “Data centers actually use very little water relative to other industries,” a position many hyperscalers have repeated. Amazon earlier claimed that its data centers consume only 0.075% of the water Americans use to water their lawns and gardens.
Garman also claims the narrative that data centers are driving up energy bills is “misleading and convenient scapegoating.” He argues that AI is simply precipitating an expansion of power infrastructure that was always bound to happen. “Once we collectively build out this new capacity, again funded by the private sector, it should lead to flat or lower rates in the future for residents living in communities with these expanded grids,” he said. On the other hand, contradictory reports claim that AI data centers trigger a "massive irreversible" 76% electricity price spike. The U.S. House also recently passed a bill that directed regulators to consider making AI data centers pay for grid upgrades to minimize the impact on residents. The bill was eventually rejected in the Senate, with opponents saying it was "toothless" and didn't do enough to protect residents.
Speaking on pollution, Garman says that data centers emitting huge amounts of pollution with their large backup diesel generators is a myth. He claims that while data centers have rarely used backup power in case of a power outage, this is only necessary because many industries depend on the facilities. This claim doesn’t exactly address growing concerns of pollution from gas turbines powering off-grid data centers. Elon Musk recently came under fire for using unlicensed gas turbines at the Colossus data center.
Lastly, Garman said claims that communities do not benefit from data centers are false, citing “considerable tax revenue, positive economic impact, large numbers of good jobs, and education programs” as some of the benefits to the communities where data centers are built. Microsoft pledged to invest $1 billion in local infrastructure improvements in its Hyperion data center community and had reportedly awarded $1.6 billion in contracts to local businesses since construction began, in addition to paying teacher bonuses. As benefits specifically on Amazon’s part, Garman listed an estimated $3 billion in taxes to St. Joseph County, Indiana, over time; more than $1 billion already contributed to communities across the U.S.; thousands of jobs created in building and running the data centers; and education programs with over 10,000 educators and learners enrolled.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The company says it plans to do more. Through its “Built Together” initiative, Amazon says it will “add more than $1 billion over the next five years to what we’re already doing — with communities in the driver’s seat to determine what’s most useful for them across education, job training, energy affordability, water and energy preservation, and local priorities.”
Garman insists that data centers can’t be separated from the revolutionary impact of AI. U.S. President Donald Trump appears to agree, at least on the “revolutionary impact” aspect, and has repeatedly expressed a desire to maintain a lead over China. On the other hand, data center critics claim that responsible implementation of the build-outs, and not AI itself, is the bone of contention.
Like several industry leaders and hyperscalers, Garman insists that many of the issues were being blown out of proportion, and implied that much of the anti-data center sentiment could be traced to nefarious foreign influence. “With any change, there will be important questions raised, but there will also be misinformation and outright lies, and in the age of social media and 24/7 news, myths take hold faster than ever before. In fact, this buildout is so important geopolitically that there are widespread reports of various countries intentionally seeding misinformation in the U.S. about data centers to trick us into slowing down,” he said.

articles.title: El ingenioso truco que usa ‘Gears of War: E-Day’ para funcionar mejor en Xbox Series S
articles.text:
Gears of War: E-Day está a pocas horas de su lanzamiento oficial, pautado para mañana, martes 6 de octubre. El nuevo juego de The Coalition, que ha logrado muy buenas críticas tanto de la prensa especializada como de quienes tuvieron acceso temprano, aspira a ser uno de los grandes bombazos de 2026. Y sus responsables han revelado un curioso truco del que echaron mano para lograr que funcione de la mejor forma posible en la Xbox Series S.
Desde el estudio le revelaron a Digital Foundry una muy ingeniosa solución para lidiar con las limitaciones de hardware que tiene la Xbox Series S en comparación con la Series X, su hermana mayor. Puntualmente, para afrontar la disponibilidad de una menor cantidad de memoria RAM. Tengamos en cuenta que el modelo de entrada tiene 10 GB, mientras que la variante mayor cuenta con 16 GB.
Al ser Gears of War: E-Day un juego que presenta escenarios opulentos y muy densos, en The Coalition tuvieron que ponerse creativos para evitar que la experiencia gráfica y jugable se degradara (en demasía al menos) en la Xbox Series S. Para ello, desarrollaron un sistema que utiliza una porción del almacenamiento interno de la consola como si fuese RAM.
Kate Rayner, directora técnica de la compañía, explicó que la tecnología en cuestión les permite generar alrededor de 1 GB de "RAM" a partir de "un par de GB" de almacenamiento SSD. Claro que esto es bastante más complejo que simplemente asignar una porción del espacio interno para convertirlo en memoria del sistema.
Gears of War: E-Day usa parte del SSD de la Xbox Series S como memoria RAM
Según The Coalition, han desarrollado un método que detecta cuáles son los datos de uso más frecuente al jugar Gears of War: E-Day. Así, pueden determinar cuáles deben utilizar la RAM real y cuáles de acceso menos habitual pueden residir en la memoria generada a partir del SSD. El estudio ha logrado que la transferencia de esa información desde el disco de estado sólido hacia la RAM sea lo suficientemente veloz como para que los jugadores no noten nada extraño al accederla.
De esta manera, Gears of War: E-Day se puede ejecutar en la Xbox Series S con una calidad de gráficos y de jugabilidad muy buena. The Coalition incluso ha logrado que el título corra a una tasa regular de 60 fotogramas por segundo. Aunque eso no se ha conseguido solamente al transformar parte del almacenamiento en memoria de sistema. Desde la compañía reconocen que han tenido que eliminar los reflejos de Lumen, una característica de iluminación de Unreal Engine 5.
Si bien Rayner menciona que depender en exceso de esta característica puede afectar negativamente el desempeño de un juego, también puede ayudar a simplificar la adaptación al hardware de la Xbox Series S. Recordemos que Microsoft exige que todos los juegos que se lanzan en Series X también tienen que estar disponibles en su hermana menor. Esto ha llevado a retrasos en el debut de ciertos juegos y a la eliminación de características importantes.
Pero el trabajo realizado en Gears of War: E-Day podría abrir el camino a nuevas soluciones. De acuerdo con The Coalition, otros estudios ya están interesados en conocer más sobre esta técnica para aplicarla sobre sus propios desarrollos.

articles.title: 12 African companies from AT50 take part in Egyptian Exchange event - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Twelve companies represented in the AT50 Index (Africa Tech 50) took part in the AT50 Cairo Market Open at the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) on September 22, bringing together founders, regulators, institutional investors, banks and capital markets leaders from Egypt and across Africa.
The Cairo event marked AT50’s third major exchange engagement following its global launch at the London Stock Exchange in January 2026, and its first African exchange activation at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in July.
The 12 AT50 companies represented in Cairo included nine Egyptian companies – MNT-Halan, Nawy, Paymob, Bosta, MaxAB, Vezeeta, MoneyFellows, Breadfast and Yodawy – alongside Chari from Morocco, and Flutterwave and Paga from Nigeria.
“Fintech stands as one of the most critical drivers poised to fundamentally reshape the capital markets landscape in the coming period. As companies scale and mature, their engagement with capital markets must not be deferred until the decision to go public is finalised; rather, this connection should be forged much earlier. Exchanges play a pivotal role in cultivating that familiarity and bridging ties between innovators, investors, and the broader financial ecosystem. Hosting the AT50 Index Market Open in Cairo presents an exceptional opportunity to deepen this vision and anchor institutional partnerships both in Egypt and across the continent,” said Omar Radwan, chairman of the Egyptian Exchange.

articles.title: Denmark population registry data breach affects 8.8 million people
articles.text:
Denmark's Central Population Register (CPR) is warning of a data breach that exposed the personal information of approximately 8.8 million registered individuals.
This includes people who live in the country, individuals who have moved abroad, and also deceased people.
The CPR is the country's national civil registry, containing personal information on residents, including names, addresses, dates of birth, marital status, and unique CPR identification numbers.
According to a CPR announcement published earlier today, threat actors misused a private Danish company's legitimate access to the registry system to obtain names, addresses, CPR numbers, and other information relating to registered members.
A separate announcement by the Danish Data Protection Agency says that the attack involved some form of brute-forcing to enumerate valid CPR numbers, and then extract the related data from each entry.
The CPR system currently holds data for 11 million registered citizens, so the incident impacted a large portion (80%) of that, but not everyone.
The security incident occurred in September 2026, but CPR administration became aware of the breach on October 2 and determined the size of the impact over the weekend.
The private company's access to the registry has now been blocked, and police have launched an investigation, which is currently underway.
"This is an extremely serious incident, which is why I have also informed Parliament’s Business and Digitalization Committee," stated Minister for Research, Education and Digitalization Christina Egelund.
"Together with all relevant authorities, we are working to establish the full extent of the incident."
Egelund said additional security measures have been implemented to prevent similar incidents on the CPR system, and urged citizens to stay on high alert for unsolicited communications.
A dedicated "cyber hotline" has been set up for potentially affected individuals,, and help and guidance are also available online at sikkerdigital.dk.
"In light of the incident, everyone is reminded never to disclose passwords or other confidential information in response to telephone calls, emails, or similar communications," the announcement warned.
"This also applies even if the recipient appears to know your name, address, and CPR number."
BleepingComputer has contacted the agency to learn more about the incident, including how the private company was compromised, but we have not received a response as of publication.

Prime Day – La barre de son Sonos Beam (Gen 2) à 379,00 € (-21%)
La barre de son Sonos Beam (Gen 2) passe sous les 400 € chez Amazon Prime soit une baisse d'environ 21% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Pour le renouvellement de son excellente barre de son compacte Beam, Sonos joue la carte de la sécurité. Mais si l'apparence de la Beam Gen 2 n'a connu quasiment aucune modification, cela ne l'empêche pas de proposer quelques alléchantes nouveautés.

Points forts
- Restitution sonore chaleureuse, mais équilibrée.

- Excellente précision des médiums et aigus, sonorité claire et ouverte.
- Spatialisation virtuelle horizontale ample et enveloppante.
- L'écosystème audio connecté Sonos, complet et mature comme aucun autre.

articles.title: Nouveau Siri : la douche froide que les utilisateurs d’iPhone redoutaient tant
articles.text:
Les utilisateurs européens du flambant neuf iPhone 18 Pro devront encore s’armer de patience. Alors que la firme de Cupertino déploie progressivement Siri AI, son nouvel assistant dopé à l’intelligence artificielle à travers le globe, le Vieux Continent reste une nouvelle fois sur le banc de touche. En cause : le bras de fer réglementaire permanent entre la marque à la pomme et Bruxelles autour du Digital Markets Act (DMA).
Apple justifie officiellement ce blocage par les exigences d’interopérabilité imposées par le texte européen, affirmant qu’elles mettraient en péril la sécurité et la confidentialité des données privées de ses clients. Mais derrière cette prudence technique affichée se cache un calcul stratégique bien plus agressif.
Une attente de plus de 5 mois est possible
Interrogé sur le calendrier d’une sortie sur notre territoire, le journaliste de Bloomberg Mark Gurman, très bien informé en la matière, affirme :
« Ne vous attendez pas à ce que Siri AI arrive de sitôt dans l’Union européenne. Apple se sert de l’absence de l’IA Siri sur iOS dans la région pour faire pression sur la Commission européenne, dans l’espoir que les clients frustrés s’opposent à l’approche réglementaire de l’UE. L’IA Siri en elle-même n’est pas suffisamment convaincante pour susciter un tel élan, mais ce retard frustre clairement les utilisateurs européens — à en juger par le flot constant de messages que je reçois à ce sujet. Le meilleur précédent est celui d’Apple Intelligence. Ces fonctionnalités ont été lancées ailleurs en octobre 2024, mais ne sont arrivées dans l’UE qu’à la fin du mois de mars 2025, soit un décalage d’environ cinq mois. Je considérerais un retard similaire pour Siri AI comme le meilleur scénario possible cette fois-ci — et je ne serais pas surpris que les utilisateurs européens doivent attendre bien plus longtemps encore. »
En répétant la méthode déjà employée lors des premiers pas d’Apple Intelligence, l’entreprise espère probablement transformer le mécontentement de ses clients en levier politique face aux régulateurs. Pour se faire l’avocat du diable, ajoutons qu’il est vrai qu’Apple a mis en place des procédés de protection des données très avancées qui rendent l’interopérabilité plus compliquée à mettre en place. Mais si la firme à la pomme a fini par y parvenir concernant l’App Store, il n’y pas vraiment de raison pour un tel blocage sur d’autres sujets.
De son côté, la Commission européenne refuse pour l’instant d’assouplir ses exigences de concurrence. Résultat le bras de fer s’installe dans la durée, laissant les possesseurs d’iPhone en Europe privés du nouveau Siri pour un bon moment. On peut également citer les nouveautés de watchOS, pour la plupart matinées d’IA, qui devront prendre quelques mois avant d’être déployées. Un sujet qui commence à devenir une habitude chez la firme à la pomme depuis le lancement d’Apple Intelligence.

articles.title: Cybersecurity startup Hadrian raises €35.68 million to scale its agentic AI offensive security platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Hadrian, a London-Amsterdam-based agentic AI offensive security platform, today announced a €35.68 million ($40 million) funding round to fund expansion across EMEA and the U.S. and deepen investment in its engineering and research teams.
The round was co-led by Forgepoint Capital International and SmartFin, with participation from existing investors HV Capital, Motive Partners, Picus Capital and Oetker Ventures. The backing brings the company’s total funding to nearly €58 million ($65 million).
Rogier Fischer, CEO of Hadrian, said, “Everyone can see that AI is changing the threat landscape. It might also hold the answer, but most people are focused on automating the wrong bits. We have been working with LLMs since before they went mainstream, and we know that AI can work much faster than any human offensive security team. So we built a platform that emulates hackers’ attack paths, helping our customers to understand their key risks and prioritise their security resources appropriately.”
Founded in 2021 in Amsterdam by Fischer, Olivier Beg and Maurice Clin, Hadrian offers an offensive security platform that helps enterprise security teams identify, verify and close security gaps before attackers can exploit them.
The company says its agentic engine delivers always-on discovery, validation, and mobilisation of an organisation’s most critical cyber risks. It adapts to each organisation’s environment to probe, discover and validate the risks attackers can actually exploit. Coupled with a proprietary predictive discovery agent, Hadrian autonomously verifies remediation, delivering an end-to-end solution.
The cybersecurity startup highlighted how AI has upended the offensive security landscape and cited recent reports of AI agents escaping test environments and hacking company systems without human direction. It also referenced Anthropic’s disclosure that criminals and state-linked groups had used its models to automate entire attack chains and write zero-day exploits.
According to the company, while attackers now move at machine speed, many security teams are years behind and still run manual pentests. It also noted that the volume of irrelevant signals distracts teams, making it difficult to determine which exposures are exploitable.
Hadrian argues there is a real market need for a solution that can identify genuine threats and cut through the noise. It claims to let businesses see security through a hacker’s eyes, map the digital footprint, discover risks, and prioritise remediation so security teams can harden their external attack surfaces.
It states that humans set the mission and make the decisions that matter, while AI does the work in between, providing the coverage, repetition and speed that no team can sustain around the clock.
To achieve this, Hadrian combines continuous exposure management and agentic penetration testing in one platform and claims to be the only vendor offering this approach. Its product Atlas continuously maps an organisation’s external attack surface and uses purpose-built AI agents to validate which exposures are actually exploitable. Nora, its other product, provides agentic pentesting on demand at a human pentest level and beyond.
Together, the company reports that these products deliver 10x greater visibility into critical exposures, 80% faster time to resolution, and 5x ROI compared to manual pentesting.
Damien Henault, Managing Director and Partner at Forgepoint Capital International, said, “There are too many vulnerabilities and noise out there for teams to manage, so they need tools that can help them see clearly and think like AI-armed hackers. Hadrian’s AI native always-on solution delivers both depth and breadth and helps its customers to focus on genuine issues and risks, and the companies using its platform are testament to both its innovative approach and the strength of its team, both aspects which make them a natural choice for us to back.”
Hadrian works with companies in the US and Europe, including Fortune 500 leaders and industry disruptors such as McKesson, NBCUniversal, Francisco Partners, Total Energies, Amadeus, Leroy Merlin, and Damen Shipyard.

articles.title: Quand les bornes de recharge ultra-rapides de BYD sont détournées en balançoires par des enfants
articles.text:
Les bornes de recharge les plus puissantes de BYD ont trouvé un usage que le constructeur n’avait pas prévu. Une vidéo tournée le 2 octobre à Nanning, dans la région autonome du Guangxi, montre deux jeunes enfants accrochés aux pistolets d’une station Megawatt Flash Charging du géant automobile chinois. Ils se balancent, les pieds dans le vide, pendant que des adultes filment. La séquence a fait le tour des réseaux sociaux chinois pendant les congés de la fête nationale, rapporte CarNewsChina ce lundi 5 octobre.
Dans une réponse relayée par le site chinois IT Home, le service client de BYD a rappelé dimanche 4 octobre qu’il est strictement interdit de jouer avec les équipements de recharge. Le constructeur a envoyé des techniciens inspecter la station et promet de renforcer la surveillance et les contrôles sur place.
Pour mémoire, BYD a présenté une première version de ces bornes en mars 2025. Elles délivrent jusqu’à 1 000 kW de puissance et permettent de passer de 10 à 70 % de batterie en cinq minutes avec les modèles compatibles. Depuis le début de leur déploiement au mois de février.
Une forme de borne parfaite… pour jouer
Pour faire passer une telle puissance, ces câbles refroidis par liquide sont imposants, lourds et difficiles à manipuler. BYD a donc suspendu l’ensemble à un rail en forme de T installé en hauteur, avec un enrouleur à ressort. Le rail porte le poids du câble, alors que le pistolet reste à hauteur de poitrine afin que rien ne traîne dans la boue ou les flaques. C’est là tout le problème : un pistolet de 3 à 5 kilos pendu à un rail devient un pendule dès qu’un enfant s’y accroche.
Le risque d’électrocution immédiate reste naturellement limité. Les normes imposent que les contacteurs de la borne restent ouverts tant que le pistolet est rangé. La haute tension n’arrive qu’une fois le connecteur branché et verrouillé sur la prise d’une voiture, après une série de vérifications d’isolement entre la borne et le véhicule.
Finalement, le danger est surtout mécanique. Les enrouleurs, les passe-câbles et les renforts à la base du connecteur sont dimensionnés pour les gestes d’un conducteur qui branche sa voiture, pas pour des balancements répétés.
Sous leur gaine, ces câbles contiennent des conducteurs en cuivre, des fils de communication et des canaux de liquide de refroidissement. Plier et tirer le câble encore et encore peut abîmer ces éléments, ou le fil de terre, par l’intérieur, sans laisser de trace visible à l’extérieur. Le conducteur suivant brancherait alors sa voiture avec un câble endommagé, traversé par des courants très élevés.
Il ne faudrait pas que ce genre de comportement devienne une pratique courante, car BYD vise 20 000 stations Flash Charging en Chine d’ici la fin de l’année 2026. Ça en ferait des bornes à surveiller. À l’international, ces bornes ultra-rapides seront progressivement déployées, notamment en Europe où l’on devrait en compter 3 000 à l’horizon 2027.

articles.title: L’Echo Dot Max à moitié prix : Amazon baisse le prix de son enceinte connectée à 64,99€ pour les Jours Flash Prime
articles.text:
L’enceinte connectée Echo Dot Max permet d’écouter de la musique, mais aussi d’utiliser l’assistant vocal Alexa à tout moment. Amazon la propose à 64,99 € au lieu de 129,99 € pour les membres de son programme Prime.
Pas besoin d’attendre les Jours Flash Prime pour vous équiper d’une enceinte connectée Amazon à petit prix. La preuve : l’Echo Dot Max est disponible pour 64,99 € dès aujourd’hui chez le cybermarchand. Cela correspond à une réduction de 50 % par rapport à son tarif habituel, mais, pour bénéficier de cette offre, il est indispensable d’être client Prime. Cette enceinte intègre deux haut-parleurs et un hub domotique dans un format compact.
L’Echo Dot Max passe à 64,99 € au lieu de 129,99 € chez Amazon, soit 50 % d’économie.
Pour profiter des Jours Flash Prime n’oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d’un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c’est donc le bon moment pour tester.
Pourquoi choisir l’Echo Dot Max ?
- Pour sa partie audio : un tweeter et un woofer assurent la diffusion musicale, avec une adaptation automatique à l’acoustique de la pièce.
- Pour ses commandes vocales : Alexa répond à des centaines de demandes vocales différentes.
- Pour son hub intégré : la prise en charge de Zigbee, Matter et Thread facilite la connexion des équipements domotiques compatibles.
Une enceinte connectée qui réagit à vos demandes
L’un des principaux intérêts de l’Echo Dot Max est de vous permettre d’écouter de la musique via Spotify, Deezer, Apple Music ou Amazon Music. Mais ce n’est pas le seul : ses capteurs de présence et de température peuvent aussi déclencher des routines, comme l’allumage d’un luminaire connecté quand quelqu’un entre dans la pièce. Notre test de l’Echo Dot Max salue, par ailleurs, la bonne réactivité de l’enceinte aux requêtes vocales.
Son achat vous donne également accès à Alexa+ gratuitement pendant l’accès anticipé. Celui-ci restera gratuit par la suite pour les adhérents Prime, mais coûtera 22,99 € par mois pour les non-membres.
Un modèle plus complet qu’une Echo Dot classique
L’Echo Dot Max est certes plus cher que l’Echo Dot classique, mais il apporte des fonctionnalités supplémentaires, comme la présence d’un hub domotique et d’une conception audio à deux haut-parleurs. Cependant, il ne vaut pas une enceinte 100 % dédiée à l’écoute musicale : notre test relève une saturation lorsqu’on cherche à pousser le volume.
✅ Les points forts
- Hub connecté Zigbee, Matter et Thread.
- Adaptation automatique du son à la pièce.
- Bouton pour désactiver les microphones.
❌ Les limites
- Équilibre sonore perfectible à haut volume.
- Fonctionne uniquement sur secteur.
Disponible à 64,99 €, l’Echo Dot Max est vendu et expédié par Amazon.
À ce prix, l’Echo Dot Max présente un vrai intérêt pour compléter une installation autour d’Alexa, et même pour en débuter une. Si vous désirez vous équiper d’un assistant vocal, c’est un choix adapté.
Cependant, les amateurs éclairés d’écoute musicale doivent bien garder en tête que cette enceinte possède des limites en matière d’équilibre sonore. Un modèle plus spécialisé leur conviendra sans doute davantage.

articles.title: Whatsapp greift durch: Login-Sperre für Smartphones mit altem Betriebssystem
articles.text:
Warum Whatsapp auf veralteten Handys bald nicht mehr startet
Facebook-Mutter Meta greift beim Messenger-Dienst Whatsapp zu einer restriktiven Maßnahme, um die Integrität der Nutzerdaten zu wahren. Wie der auf Vorabversionen spezialisierte Blog WABetaInfo berichtet, rollt der Dienst aktuell ein serverseitiges Update an erste Nutzer:innen aus, das den Login auf mobilen Endgeräten mit stark veralteten Betriebssystemen physisch blockieren kann.
Nutzer:innen, die versuchen, sich auf einem unzureichend gepatchten Smartphone anzumelden, erhalten anstelle des regulären Posteingangs einen ganzflächigen Sperrbildschirm. Dieser Dialog fordert sie auf, in den Systemeinstellungen des Geräts nach einem Update für das Betriebssystem zu suchen und dieses vor der weiteren Nutzung der App zu installieren.
Sicherheit des Betriebssystems als Bedingung
Ein Überspringen dieser Aufforderung ist laut den Erkenntnissen der Forenbeobachter nicht vorgesehen. Der Messenger verweigert den Zugang konsequent, bis das betroffene Smartphone über die offiziellen Systemeinstellungen auf einen aktuellen Stand gebracht wurde.
Hintergrund dieser Entscheidung ist die grundlegende Sicherheitsarchitektur mobiler Applikationen, die vollständig auf die Isolationsmechanismen des jeweiligen Betriebssystems vertrauen. Angreifer nutzen bekannte Schwachstellen in ungepatchten Systemen, um Schadsoftware zu installieren, die Daten ausliest, noch bevor die Ende-zu-Ende-Verschlüsselung des Messengers überhaupt aktiv werden kann.
Serverseitiges Update greift sofort
Das bedeutet, dass die beschriebene Sperre nicht auf eine akute Schwachstelle in der Anwendung selbst zurückzuführen ist. Vielmehr macht das Unternehmen mit diesem Schritt deutlich, dass die Datensicherheit der eigenen Software maßgeblich von den Abwehrmechanismen des zugrundeliegenden Betriebssystems abhängt.
Der Eingriff erfolgt als serverseitiges Update und setzt keine vorherige Aktualisierung der App über die jeweiligen App-Stores voraus. Die Server des Unternehmens würden demnach beim Verbindungsaufbau die Systemdaten des anfragenden Smartphones prüfen und könnten dann die Authentifizierung bei veralteten Versionen künftig schlichtweg ablehnen.
Offene Fragen für ältere Hardware
Daraus kann sich natürlich ein Problem für Besitzer:innen älterer Hardware ergeben. Es bleibt abzuwarten, wie sich der Dienst bei Geräten verhält, deren Hersteller den Software-Support bereits vollständig eingestellt haben und die hardwareseitig keine Aktualisierungen mehr verarbeiten können.
Bereits im Spätsommer hatte Whatsapp den grundlegenden Support für sehr alte Systemversionen eingestellt und als Minimum Android 6 oder iOS 12 definiert. Die nun beobachtete Loginsperre würde diese formellen Richtlinien technisch direkt auf dem Endgerät durchsetzen und so die weitere Nutzung effektiv verhindern.
Schrittweise Einführung der Sperren
Whatsapp testet den neuen Sperrmechanismus derzeit in Wellen für Konten unter den Betriebssystemen von Apple und Google. Welche exakten Versionierungsnummern der Betriebssysteme den beschriebenen Sperrbildschirm bei einem Anmeldeversuch im Detail auslösen, hat der Anbieter bislang nicht in einer offiziellen Dokumentation zusammengefasst.
Die serverseitige Sperre reiht sich in eine erweiterte Sicherheitsstrategie des Anbieters ein, die den Schutz vor Kontoübernahmen fokussiert. Dazu gehören neben dem Zwang zu aktuellen Betriebssystemen auch Warnungen vor inoffiziellen Web-Clients sowie eine lokale Betrugserkennung, die potenziell gefährliche Nachrichten analysiert.
Parallel zur Durchsetzung aktueller Systemsoftware implementiert die Plattform zunehmend den sogenannten Passkey-Support, der klassische Passwörter durch biometrische Merkmale oder lokale Geräte-PINs ersetzt. Durch diese Kombination lagert der Messenger die Verantwortung für die Gerätesicherheit an die Plattformbetreiber aus, was ungepatchte Altgeräte unweigerlich vom Netzwerk trennen würde.

articles.title: Surprise : voici le Renault E-Space Concept, un concept de monospace électrique pour ringardiser les SUV — Frandroid
articles.text:
Plus on se rapproche de l’ouverture du Mondial de l’Auto, plus les annonces se font nombreuses. Aujourd’hui, Renault présente les nouveautés de son stand, et il y a une surprise.
Car oui, aux côtés de la Renault 8 Gordini Concept et de la nouvelle gamme électrique, trônera le Renault E-Space Concept, un hommage appuyé à l’Espace, le roi des monospaces.
Encore très peu d’infos
À vrai dire, il s’agit ici d’une annonce plutôt que d’une révélation, puisque Renault reste encore très avare en informations avant la présentation complète du concept prévue le 12 octobre 2026 (date d’ouverture du Mondial).
Nous aurons donc cette unique photo et quelques bribes d’informations. Loin des 4,25 m de long du premier Espace, cet E-Space prend ses aises avec 4,70 m de long, mais l’esprit du « profil TGV » demeure avec ce museau en pointe et dans le prolongement du pare-brise en trois parties.
Quant au soin apporté aux passagers, Renault se contentera d’évoquer « un habitacle généreux, technologique et accueillant »… et c’est à peu près tout. Pour découvrir l’intérieur et le reste des détails, il faudra donc encore attendre quelques jours, histoire de voir si cet E-Space mérite son slogan de « voiture à vivre ».
La question de la motorisation demeure en suspens. Sera-t-il 100 % électrique ou pourrait-il accueillir un petit prolongateur d’autonomie, comme l’a annoncé Renault dans sa dernière conférence stratégique, pour booster l’autonomie jusqu’à 1 400 km ?
Un stand bien rempli
Aux côtés de cet E-Space Concept et de la R8 Gordini Concept, Renault présentera donc sa gamme hybride et électrique, incluant notamment les évolutions techniques de la Renault 5 E-Tech et du Scénic électrique, sans oublier le restylage de la Mégane.
Il y aura également une petite surprise : l’apparition d’un toit vitré sur la Twingo E-Tech, baptisé « Twingobay ». Certes, le toit en toile de la Twingo 1 n’a pas été retenu, mais il permettra d’ajouter pas mal de luminosité dans l’habitacle pour 550 euros supplémentaires.

articles.title: JSE wants to turn 10 SMEs into investor-ready businesses
articles.text:
The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), Africa’s largest stock exchange, has teamed up with the Technology Innovation Agency (TIA), a government agency that supports technology commercialisation, to help 10 South African tech SMEs become investment-ready and connect with new markets and sources of capital.
The 16-week pilot gives the companies access to capital-market expertise, investor networks and commercial opportunities, as the JSE tests whether it can play a bigger role earlier in the startup funding pipeline.
Launched on September 30, the programme will support SMEs in the health, agriculture and fintech sectors with investment readiness, market access and connections to potential sources of capital.
The 10 companies were selected based on their existing products or services, operating maturity and commercial potential, according to a statement. Participants will receive support on investment readiness and pitch development, while gaining access to JSE networks through a market access day and sector-specific engagements.
At the end of the programme, the JSE and TIA aim to produce SMEs with funding-ready pitch packs, market linkages and a pipeline of potential capital engagements. Some participants could also become eligible for AltX screening, the JSE’s process for assessing companies for potential listing on its alternative market for smaller and growing businesses.
That does not mean the companies will be listed or funded as a result of the programme. Instead, the initiative is designed to move them closer to the point where they can engage investors and potentially access formal capital markets.
For TIA, the partnership addresses a persistent problem in South Africa’s innovation ecosystem: getting technologies that have been developed locally into the market.
“One of the key challenges in the innovation value chain is ensuring that new technologies and innovations are commercialised and access the markets,” said Patrick Krappie, executive for innovation enabling at TIA, in a statement.
He said the partnership between TIA and JSE Rise, the local bourse’s SME investment-readiness programme, aligns with the agency’s role as a “connector and facilitator” for the commercialisation of locally developed innovations. The agency wants the programme to support businesses addressing national priorities while helping them move from developing technologies to finding markets, customers and capital.
The JSE said the initiative expands its SME Rise, the JSE’s SME growth support programme, into technology sectors it considers important to economic growth. SMEs account for 91% of formal businesses, provide 60% of jobs and contribute up to 34% of GDP, according to Deputy Finance Minister Ashor Sarupen.
“We are pleased to expand our suite of SME Rise development solutions to support sectors that are critical to driving economic growth,” said Vuyo Lee, chief marketing and corporate affairs officer at the JSE.
Through the partnership, Lee said the JSE is seeking to equip South African technology SMEs with the capabilities and opportunities to compete regionally and globally. The move also gives the exchange an earlier role in the lifecycle of high-growth businesses.
Traditionally, capital markets sit further down the growth journey, after a company has developed a product, found customers, built revenue and established the governance and financial systems investors require. Optasia, a global fintech platform that provides mobile financial services, listed on the JSE’s Main Board in November 2025 at an implied market capitalisation of R23.5 billion ($1.4 billion). Technology group 4Sight also moved from AltX to the JSE Main Board in January 2025.
The JSE and TIA are now testing whether bringing some of that capital-market preparation forward can improve the chances of innovative businesses reaching that stage.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Apps de Android podem falhar em Googlebooks com chip Intel • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apps de Android podem falhar em Googlebooks com chip Intel
Google admite que alguns aplicativos de Android podem ter instabilidades em Googlebooks com chip Intel, mas afirma que já trabalha na solução.
Os primeiros Googlebooks foram anunciados em setembro. A maioria dos modelos desta primeira leva é equipada com processadores Intel. E todos podem executar aplicativos desenvolvidos originalmente para Android. Ou deveriam executar: o Google reconheceu que alguns dos apps podem não rodar satisfatoriamente nessas máquinas.
Provavelmente, o que chama a atenção nos Googlebooks na primeira olhada são os seus recursos de hardware. A nova categoria de laptops é focada na execução local de aplicações de IA, razão pela qual seus requisitos mínimos incluem 16 GB de RAM de alto desempenho e um processador complementado com uma NPU de 45 TOPS ou mais.
Mas o Googlebook OS, o sistema operacional da categoria, também atrai os olhares. Em poucas palavras, essa é uma solução que combina recursos do ChromeOS com tecnologias do Android. É por isso que aplicativos para esta última plataforma podem ser executados em um Googlebook.
Outro detalhe notável é que a categoria foi preparada para funcionar tanto com chips x86 quanto com unidades com arquitetura Arm. Por conta disso, três dos primeiros modelos do Googlebook contam com chip Intel Core Ultra 5 (x86). Outros dois vieram com o Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite (Arm).
Hoje, a maioria dos aplicativos para Android é desenvolvida com foco em chips Arm. Apesar disso, Googlebooks com chip Intel podem rodar esses aplicativos porque, quando um deles tem apenas código compilado para Arm, o Googlebook OS aciona uma camada de tradução que o converte para instruções de x86.
O problema é que, em alguns casos, essa dinâmica pode necessitar de ajustes, como o próprio Google admitiu ao Android Authority:
A grande maioria dos aplicativos Android funciona perfeitamente em Googlebooks com processadores Intel e Qualcomm, logo após a instalação.
Como muitos aplicativos Android foram originalmente projetados para chips Arm, alguns apps ou jogos mais complexos precisam de ajustes por parte dos desenvolvedores para funcionarem da melhor forma em plataformas baseadas em Intel.
Estamos trabalhando em conjunto com desenvolvedores de aplicativos, a Intel e a Qualcomm para otimizar continuamente o desempenho e expandir a compatibilidade em todo o portfólio.
Google
Não é bem assim. Até o momento, não há problemas de incompatibilidade em larga escala com apps para Android. Além disso, o próprio Google enfatizou que trabalha com desenvolvedores e companhias parceiras para tratar desse problema.
Levemos em conta também que o Google criou uma seção na App Store que lista aplicativos otimizados para Googlebooks, o que significa que esses apps devem apresentar pouco ou nenhum problema de compatibilidade.
O que essa história toda talvez queira nos dizer é que, como a categoria acabou de chegar ao mercado, ainda não é o momento de comprar um Googlebook. Até para quem é entusiasta de tecnologia, talvez seja o caso de esperar o que as primeiras análises independentes dirão sobre essas máquinas.
Os primeiros Googlebooks aparecem na lista a seguir, com preços para os Estados Unidos. Vale destacar que ainda não há informação sobre lançamento oficial desses notebooks no Brasil.

articles.title: RTX 5090 modder claims to have solved melting power connectors with auxiliary 8-pin board
articles.text:
Something to look forward to: A hardware modder has shared a promising fix for Nvidia's RTX 5090, a GPU with a documented history of power-related issues. Best yet, the workaround is said to be "relatively affordable" and would even come with a warranty.
Over on Reddit, user DallasGrave outlined the approach taken when developing the mod. In short, the fix utilizes a pickup PCB soldered to the contacts of the original 12VHPWR header that feeds an auxiliary dual eight-pin board. This effectively spreads the load across three sets of cables, which significantly reduces power draw and temperature.
According to the user, the modded card was tested at full load for 48 hours (at 550W), and cable temps never climbed above 40 degrees Celsius. Even the joints stayed nice and cool, we're told.
Tom's Hardware notes that the user, DallasGrave, appears to be affiliated with Grave PC, a company that specializes in CPU / GPU cooling and compact system design. In the Reddit thread, DallasGrave said they are working on a "relatively affordable" service to convert existing cards – complete with warranty. In another reply, the user says they are a PNY partner and that eventually, customers will be able to buy a PNY card with a similar mod directly from them – again, with a full warranty.
Asked about specifics of the mod, DallasGrave said they could have replaced the header with a higher current model but that does not fix the cable. "12VHPWR is simply rated too high," he said, adding that it never should have been approved beyond 350-ish watts.
This is not the first attempt we've seen to address the issue of melting connectors, but it does appear to be one of the cleanest solutions yet. Over the summer, YouTube channel TecLab shared a fix that involved connecting power wires directly to the GPU's PCB. It seemed to work, but it wasn't all that aesthetically pleasing. DallasGrave said their solution would be more of a universal option that could work across multiple GPU brands.
Image credit: DallasGrave

Plan Tasks, Resources, and Deadlines in One Place With Microsoft Project 2024 for $49.97

Define tasks and dependencies, and Project can calculate start and finish dates based on how those tasks relate to one another. Multiple timeline views also make it easier to get a visual overview of complex project schedules.Gantt chart task-path highlighting shows how individual tasks relate to one another. What-if scenarios allow project managers to test different assignments before committing resources. Baselines preserve the original plan so actual progress can be measured against initial schedules.
Microsoft Project also includes built-in reports such as Burndown and Resource Overview. These reports help communicate schedule, workload, and progress information to executives, clients, and other stakeholders.
Timesheets record hours spent on project and non-project work. That information can support payroll, invoicing, and internal resource management. The application can also synchronize with Project Online and Project Server.
Microsoft Teams for Business integration allows users to check a team member's online presence and begin chats or calls from a project plan. Teams for Business must be licensed separately.
The licensing terms are specific: The lifetime license covers one PC and connects to that device rather than a Microsoft account. Buyers should select the installation computer carefully.
Lifetime access to Microsoft Project Professional 2024 is available for $49.97 through October 4.

articles.title: Google Narrows Open Source Bug Bounty Amid Wave of Invalid Automated Reports
articles.text:
Google has temporarily closed its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) to product vulnerability submissions, saying a growing number of automated reports, most of them invalid, prompted the move.
The pause was announced on X on October 1.
“This pause is due to a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid,” Google said.
Only product vulnerabilities are covered by the pause. According to Google, it has no impact on the program’s supply chain reports or on any pending reports.
“This change does not affect product vulnerabilities submitted before October 1, 2026,” the company noted in an update on the program’s page.
Some product vulnerability reports may still be eligible elsewhere. “For some Google Cloud repos impacting Google Cloud products we may still accept reports covering product vulnerabilities through the Cloud VRP,” Google said.
Google wants bug hunters to look for impact in its other vulnerability reward programs and submit their findings there. Researchers can also turn to its Patch Rewards Program, which offers rewards for proactively improving the security of open source projects.
“We will continue to reformat and work on this aspect of the OSS VRP and commit to giving an update in Q1 2027,” Google said.
[ Read: Will AI Kill the Bug Bounty Industry? ]
Introduced in 2022, the OSS VRP pays researchers for vulnerabilities found in Google’s open source projects.
The OSS VRP pause follows changes Google made in May to its Chrome and Android reward programs, in response to the growing use of AI tools for vulnerability discovery.
Standard Chrome payouts were reduced, as the company began favoring concise reports that provide concrete proof a bug exists. For Android, Google said it would prioritize vulnerability types that are harder for AI tools to find, and the top reward for a zero-click Pixel Titan M exploit with persistence went from $1 million to $1.5 million.
In March, the Internet Bug Bounty (IBB) program run by HackerOne paused new submissions, saying the speed and volume of AI-assisted vulnerability discoveries had outpaced the open source community’s ability to deliver fixes.

articles.title: Cloudflare Fixes Cross-Tenant Data Exposure in Containers
articles.text:
Cloudflare recently disclosed a cross-tenant data exposure vulnerability in Containers, the platform that also underpins Cloudflare Sandboxes. A customer on a Workers Paid account could recover residual disk blocks left behind by other customers' containers on the same host. Cloudflare has remediated it and says it found no evidence of malicious exploitation. The failure was not in the virtual machine boundary but in the storage allocator beneath it.
Oren Yomtov, a security researcher at Accomplish, reported the issue on September 4 through Cloudflare's bug bounty program.
Each Cloudflare container runs inside a Firecracker virtual machine with a writable root disk, provisioned through Linux device mapper thin provisioning. The affected pools used a 64 KiB thin-block size and were configured with skip_block_zeroing, which tells dm-thin not to clear newly allocated blocks before exposing them.
That combination created the gap. Writing a single 4 KiB block into an unmapped region caused dm-thin to allocate a 64 KiB physical block from a pool shared across customer accounts. The write replaced only its own portion, leaving up to 60 KiB that could still hold whatever the previous container had written there. A raw read of the disk could then return bytes the new container never wrote.
The researchers used ext4 directory block checksums to tell their own blocks apart from everyone else's. Across six production placements, all 5,614 testable directory blocks came from elsewhere, with 2,700 distinct foreign directory inodes identified. Residual material appeared on 18 of 24 placements and 20 of 22 underlying nodes across four continents. Recovered block types included directory structures, database pages, and structurally complete SQLite databases.
Cloudflare is precise about the limits. An attacker could not choose a victim, a workload or a host, could not read an actively attached disk, and had no guarantee that residual data would be present at all. Exposure depended on where Cloudflare placed the workload and which released blocks dm-thin happened to reassign. The researchers did not demonstrate modification of another customer's data or any impact on availability.
Reaction among security practitioners on LinkedIn has focused on where the isolation broke rather than on the platform. Peter Ward, a senior cloud security engineer at Visa, described the pattern as a recurring one:
That is tenant isolation broken at the storage layer, not an app bug.
He argued that ephemeral disk and shared host warrant explicit zero-on-allocate or wipe-on-release checks in the control plane rather than network isolation alone, and offered a test teams can apply to any container or serverless platform: ask whether every reused volume path zeroes on allocate, and treat residual data on shared storage as a first-class isolation control.
Sherin Shahanas, a technology leader working in cloud and cybersecurity, made the point that the root cause is rarely verified:
"Isolated" is usually an architectural claim, not something independently tested at the storage layer.
His question for teams running shared infrastructure of any kind, whether containers, virtual machines or a shared virtualization cluster, was whether they know or merely assume that deallocated blocks are zeroed before reuse.
That question has arrived at a useful moment. The disclosure landed within days of two adjacent launches: Microsoft made Azure Container Apps Sandboxes generally available, describing each workload as running inside a hardware-isolated microVM boundary, and Google published benchmarks for GKE Pod snapshots, which checkpoint memory and disk through gVisor and store the result in Cloud Storage. Both vendors are selling isolation for agent workloads that execute untrusted code. Cloudflare's disclosure is a reminder that the guarantee spans every layer beneath the one named in the announcement, including the block allocator.
If these reactions are representative, the lesson practitioners are drawing is about verification rather than vendor choice. The Firecracker boundary held. What leaked sat below it, in a performance option that skipped zeroing on block reuse.
Cloudflare's response was fast, and the timeline shows why the fix alone was insufficient. The report arrived at 15:26 UTC on September 4. Cloudflare opened an incident at 18:45, merged a runtime fix at 21:27, merged changes for new and live pools at 22:03, and began rolling out at 23:15 the same day. The rollout completed on September 7.
Removing skip_block_zeroing restored default behavior for newly allocated blocks, but it did not sanitize blocks already mapped into existing thin devices, whether in running container disks or in each host's cache of prepared snapshots for OCI image layers. A new container could inherit those mappings without allocating the blocks again. Cloudflare therefore retired all running container disks, drained hosts during off-peak hours, restarted the virtual machines and cleared each host's image cache. That cleanup completed on September 19.
On detection, Cloudflare says it built signatures from the characteristic pattern of a small write followed by a larger read, applied them to retained historical disk-I/O telemetry, and found only activity attributable to the researchers and to its own engineers conducting authorized validation.
The researchers confirmed that their proof of concept stopped working after the change, and that recovered data under their control was securely deleted following submission. Cloudflare awarded the bounty on September 14.

articles.title: Equs launches a personal AI platform with private storage to give users greater control over data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Equs launches a personal AI platform with private storage to give users greater control over data
Equs Inc., a startup developing a trust layer for artificial intelligence data, today announced the launch of Equs X, a personal AI that lets customers retain control of their information.
Equs X pairs a personal AI with private data storage the user manages. The company said the AI model reads nothing unless the user allows it, file by file, and access is controlled by a toggle. The AI keeps what it learns in private storage rather than on the model provider’s servers.
“Most AIs now on the market require you to trade data ownership for speed and usability,” said Chief Executive Sandy Carter. “To Equs, that trade is unwarranted and most likely, short-lived.”
Carter added that customers want personal AI assistants, but they want assistants that help them without breaching their privacy. Too often, AI models are trained on user data; they are used to display advertisements, inform the company that runs the model about the customer or can leak sensitive information.
Because Equs X reads from the customer’s own storage, rather than copying it into a separate profile, revoking access ends access immediately. When access is denied, it’s not a deletion request to a provider that has already taken the data.
Headlines about users whose AI chats were exposed to the world are not hard to find. In August 2025, Google indexed nearly 300,000 Grok conversations, with Forbes counting more than 370,000 – users who pressed “share” created a link that also made chat searchable. Obsidian Security revealed in the same month that a researcher discovered over 143,000 Claude, Copilot and ChatGPT conversations publicly accessible on archive.org – the nonprofit digital archive of websites.
“Private data store means you are entrusting your data to an organization without relinquishing ownership and control of the data to them,” said Carter. “Trust stems from that company not being in the business of using your data.”
Equs X provides a Personal Data Store that delivers a unified data layer owned entirely by the customer, including a granular data switch that allows per-data-point access. This means that a user can choose exactly which documents or details the platform can access and when and retain the ability to revoke that permission.
Users also receive a daily brief, which assembles scheduled tasks and relevant updates sourced strictly from the user’s personal data store.
“What stood out in the Equs X beta was how much control I had over my own AI context: what information I bring in, what the AI can see, and when it gets access,” said Brian Silverman, founder of The Business of AI Roadmap. “As personal AI becomes more useful, that kind of control matters more, not less.”
Although the company’s platform is a consumer product, Equs also built what it calls the Equs Developer Toolkit. It includes a stack for issuing, holding and verifying digital credentials. People, organizations and the AI agents working on their behalf can interact with it. It supports industry-standard protocols and credentials.
Users can join a waitlist for the Equs X platform, opening later this month, which will be free for the first 90 days, but the developer toolkit is invite-only in private beta mode and is currently accepting applications.
