articles.title: Blue Origin reveals 65-foot solar tower designed to power future bases on the Moon
articles.text:
First look: Blue Origin is developing a solar power system designed for use on the Moon, where keeping equipment supplied with electricity will be one of the biggest practical challenges. The tower is still at an early stage of development, and Blue Origin has not said when it could fly to the Moon.
The proposed system reflects the growing focus on the infrastructure needed for future surface operations. Launch vehicles and landers may get equipment to the surface. Systems such as the Power Tower would help keep it running once it arrives.
Blue Origin calls the system the Power Tower. It is a 20-meter-tall (65 foot) solar array that deploys vertically after landing and is designed to generate more than 10 kilowatts of electricity. The company said it is intended for Moon Base operations at the lunar south pole, the region NASA is targeting for its Artemis program.
Blue Origin released an animation showing the system landing on the lunar surface and extending from its base. A central mast rises first, followed by arms that unfold and lower the solar panels into place.
The design addresses a problem that will shape nearly every aspect of lunar operations: power is difficult to generate and distribute on the Moon. The lunar south pole is especially challenging. Parts of the region receive sunlight at low angles, while craters, ridges and other terrain can leave nearby areas in shadow. Conditions can change over short distances.
A vertical array can place solar panels above some of those surface-level obstacles. It could also reduce the amount of ground a power system occupies. That matters when a landing site must accommodate vehicles, science equipment, communications hardware and, eventually, habitats and rovers.
Blue Origin said the Power Tower's modular architecture will deliver power beyond the lander to the assets that need it most. That capability would be important for any permanent or semi-permanent lunar operation. Surface systems will need electricity for communications, thermal control, scientific instruments, computing equipment and mobility systems. A tower generating 10 kilowatts would not by itself run a large lunar settlement, but it could support smaller operations or serve as one part of a larger power network.
The Power Tower appears to be based on earlier work by Honeybee Robotics, a Blue Origin subsidiary. Honeybee developed the Lunar Array Mast and Power System, known as LAMPS, which was deployed during testing at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston in 2024.
 – Blue Origin (@blueorigin) September 25, 2026
Honeybee Robotics has also worked with NASA through the agency's Vertical Solar Array Technology project. That effort has examined solar arrays that can operate effectively in the lunar environment, particularly in areas where conventional ground-mounted panels may be blocked by terrain or exposed to unfavorable sun angles.
Blue Origin's announcement also ties the tower to NASA's Moon Base plans, which run through 2029. Under the agency's present timeline, the base would be operating by 2032.

articles.title: Developers are secretly hoping OpenAI fails to ship this month
articles.text:
Developers are secretly hoping OpenAI fails to ship this month
OpenAI’s 28-day Codex shipping sprint has its first result, which means subscribers hoping for a free usage reset will have to wait at least another day.
Thibault Sottiaux, engineering lead for Codex at OpenAI, said on Day 1 that the company had made GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol about 50% faster by default. Speeding things up is the first move in an unusually steep challenge Sottiaux set for his team on Sunday, when he promised to ship a “clear improvement” relevant to most Codex and ChatGPT Work users every day for the next 28 days or ship a full usage reset instead.
“Let the improvements begin,” the Sottiaux wrote.
Faster GPT-6 Astra and Sol
Sottiaux put a more concrete number on the change in a follow-up post, saying the two models can now generate approximately 50 tokens per second, up from about 30. Taken literally, that’s closer to a two-thirds jump than 50%, although both figures appear to be rough estimates rather than benchmark results.
The speedup isn’t limited to OpenAI’s own products, since subscribers using Sign in with ChatGPT also get it through OpenCode, Pi, Amp and Devin.
The timing carries some irony. Two days before the challenge began, Sottiaux apologized for a slow start with GPT-6.1 Sol, blaming a major load spike in the model’s first two days, and announced a global reset for paid ChatGPT accounts to make up for it, so the sprint’s first official ship turned out to be a speed improvement to that same model.
The first ship also gives an early sense of what OpenAI is willing to count. Just before announcing the challenge, Sottiaux said the team was “locking in” on simplification, greater efficiency that translates into more usage, “groundbreaking features,” and new models, adding that “feedback is clear that you all want things to get simpler.”
Just before announcing the challenge, Sottiaux said the team was “locking in” on simplification, greater efficiency that translates into more usage, “groundbreaking features,” and new models, adding that “feedback is clear that you all want things to get simpler.”
Codex resets as currency
Usage works as a currency for Sottiaux’s bet because OpenAI has spent months teaching subscribers to watch for resets. When he reset Codex rate limits for all paid plans in April, Sottiaux opened the announcement by joking that resets shouldn’t be handed out for fun because they cost money, before conceding that the vibes were good.
In July, after the launch that folded Codex into the ChatGPT desktop app introduced regressions in some multi-agent workflows, he reset usage twice in a single day, and he marked Codex and ChatGPT Work passing 8 million active users with yet another. He and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman later handed out a banked reset live on stage at DevDay on September 29.
Resets are common enough now that unofficial services track them, with one putting up a 28-day scoreboard within hours of Sottiaux’s announcement, and developers quickly worked out the obvious gamble.
One joked that Sottiaux had turned Codex usage into gambling, suggesting subscribers burn through their allowance each day and hope OpenAI misses a ship. Others would rather have higher limits in the first place. One Plus subscriber said the five-hour cap already dictates when they can work, while Mark Kretschmann, software engineer at ASYS Group, treated Sottiaux’s pledge as 28 Codex resets in 28 days.
That frustration over limits lands at an awkward time, since OpenAI said last week that starting October 30, near the end of the 28-day window, it will cut the Codex and ChatGPT Work allowance on its $200 Pro plan from 20 times the Plus allowance to 10 times.
That frustration over limits lands at an awkward time, since OpenAI said last week that starting October 30, near the end of the 28-day window, it will cut the Codex and ChatGPT Work allowance on its $200 Pro plan from 20 times the Plus allowance to 10 times. The company paired that change with a new $500 plan offering 25 times the Plus allowance and an Ultrafast tier for GPT-6 Astra that promises up to eight times the standard speed in Codex.
Not everyone is rooting for the reset button. The pseudonymous X account Token Gremlin argued that 28 smaller improvements won’t count for much unless OpenAI ships a model that can beat Claude Opus 5.5. That’s a high bar, but an understandable one, given that Opus 5.5 is already pulling developers its way. T3 Code creator Theo Browne said on October 3 that Anthropic’s newest Opus model had become the first to break 50% of traffic in T3 Code, with “literally half of all prompts” going to Opus.
Who judges Codex improvements
The 28-day challenge is not set in OpenAI terms, just in Sottiaux’s posts. Even the dates are unofficial, with one tracker putting the run from October 5 through November 1 and noting that it’s making its own call on the timeline. Sottiaux hasn’t said which subscription tiers would get a reset either, or what exactly a “full reset” would restore, confusion that OpenAI has caused before.
After the April reset for “ALL paid plans,” one Plus user filed a GitHub issue saying their weekly limit stayed on its normal cycle while Codex offered no way to tell whether the special reset had applied at all. According to the issue, OpenAI Support later clarified that the reset did not cover every quota type for every user.
“Full reset” still leaves plenty unanswered. Codex has shorter rolling windows alongside weekly limits, and those are very different things to get back when you’ve run out of usage.

articles.title: This startup is issuing AI-generated acne prescriptions
articles.text:
People in Utah can now use AI to get a prescription for acne treatment. On Monday, healthcare startup Nolla Health announced that users in the state can scan their faces using its app, allowing its AI system to analyze acne severity and autonomously write a prescription, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.
This startup is issuing AI-generated acne prescriptions
Utah has signed off on letting Nolla Health’s AI system scan a user’s face and issue a prescription directly.
The service is launching as a pilot program with gradually loosening physician oversight. Two physicians will approve each AI-generated prescription before they’re issued for the first 100 patients, but will start reviewing them only after they’re prescribed for up to 500 patients. “After that, physicians review a sample of at least 10% of prescriptions every month, plus every case involving an escalation or side effect,” Nolla Health says.
Several other healthcare companies are experimenting with AI-generated prescriptions in Utah, which started allowing AI systems to renew certain medications earlier this year. But Nolla Health says it’s the first in the country to issue initial prescriptions, rather than renewals. “The pilot is designed to complement, not replace, physicians,” Nolla Health writes in its press release. “By handling routine, low-acuity cases, Nolla Derm frees dermatologists to focus on complex, high-risk patients.”
The program will cost $4.99 / month, and only applies to Utah residents who are 18 years of age or older and have mild-to-moderate acne. Nolla Health says it will direct users to a physician if its AI system cannot “confidently select a treatment.” The startup’s AI can currently prescribe eight different skin treatments, according to Bloomberg.

articles.title: Infrastructure modernization with NetApp ONTAP native in OCI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
NetApp puts ONTAP inside Oracle’s cloud, betting native beats bolted-on
Infrastructure modernization often stalls at the storage layer, where moving mission-critical applications to the cloud can mean redesigning them from scratch. Now, AI is raising the stakes as enterprises push decades-old data estates into production AI.
NetApp Inc. and Oracle Corp. are tackling that problem with an inbound, fully managed storage service that runs NetApp’s ONTAP data management software natively inside Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The co-engineered offering is built to behave like any other OCI service rather than a third-party add-on, according to Pravjit Tiwana (pictured, left), senior vice president and general manager of cloud storage and services at NetApp.
“As far as our partnership, this is a co-engineered and co-developed product of ours,” Tiwana said. “It’s not like we have taken it and bolted it in OCI, but both [Oracle] and our organizations have worked very closely to have a deep integration into [the] control plane, data plane, as well as to the OCI’s native billing infrastructure, to provisioning, to console, to API.”
Tiwana and Konstantinos Papamiltiadis (right), senior vice president of partnerships at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, a division of Oracle, spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Christophe Bertrand at NetApp INSIGHT, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed native ONTAP integration in OCI, migration for existing NetApp workloads and plans to bring AI closer to enterprise data. (* Disclosure below.)
Native integration as a path to infrastructure modernization
Oracle has long built its own storage products, but customers wanted a way to bring mission-critical deployments from their data centers into the cloud. Many already run ONTAP on-premises, so matching that experience was a design priority, Papamiltiadis explained.
“When I’m going into the OCI console, I have the option to use the ONTAP as a native service,” Papamiltiadis said. “For me, the most important thing that we managed to build is, from an operational perspective, we bring everything under one single interface that provides simplicity and consistency.”
The native approach also matters for migration, where many cloud projects get bogged down. The two companies plan to co-sell the service, drawing on NetApp’s experience with other hyperscalers, according to Tiwana.
“The one important thing is nobody wants to redo the application redesign and all,” Tiwana said. “If you have applications or systems running on-prem, you bring it to OCI with ONTAP, you don’t have to do anything. It works as seamlessly as it was working on-prem.”
AI adds another layer to infrastructure modernization. NetApp’s decades of work on data protection, compliance and lineage let it prepare enterprise data for agentic workflows and inferencing, not just store it, Tiwana explained.
“Both the companies do plan to work together to bring Oracle’s great AI efforts into our ONTAP so customers don’t have to move data somewhere else,” Tiwana said. “They can run the AI right where the data lives.”

articles.title: Five numbers showing GTCO’s growing payments business
articles.text:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Segun Agbaje, the group chief executive officer of Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO), one of Nigeria’s largest financial services groups, told analysts in 2020 that the group was coming for the payments space. Six years later, GTCO’s numbers show that payments have become a business in their own right—one that makes money, brings in customers, and serves merchants.
Through Habari Pay Ltd, GTCO’s payments business, the group has built a payments infrastructure business across switching and processing. Through GTWorld and Pay-with-Transfer, it is processing increasingly large volumes of customer transactions.
On the surface, GTCO’s first half of 2026 numbers were not particularly impressive. Gross earnings increased by 3.25%, profit after tax declined by 7.76%, while its cost-to-income ratio remained low at 31.50%.
But underneath this is a bank pushing more of its customers’ financial activity online and increasingly sitting between customers, merchants, banks, and payment rails.
When fintechs entered the market, they won customers by making payments faster and more reliable, while building large merchant networks around Point of Sale (PoS) terminals. That helped reshape Nigeria’s payments landscape, with the country processing more than ₦1.2 quadrillion ($902.19 billion) worth of transactions in 2025, according to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).
GTCO’s H1 2026 numbers show that banks are now investing heavily in the same infrastructure and customer behaviour.
Here are five numbers that show where GTCO’s payments strategy is heading.
GTCO is moving closer to the transaction
1. ₦7.81 billion ($5.87 million): Payments is a profit engine
HabariPay, GTCO’s payments business, remains small relative to its banking franchise, but it is growing much faster. It is the most profitable bank-led fintech in the country.
In H1 2026, HabariPay generated ₦7.81 billion ($5.87 million) in profit after tax, almost double the ₦4.02 billion ($3.02 million) recorded in H1 2025. Its operating income increased 87.16% year-on-year to ₦9.44 billion ($7.09 million), while payment value processed through its switching and processing business increased by 136.5%.
HabariPay launched in June 2022 to target SMEs and retailers, offering PoS, USSD, web gateways, virtual accounts, and switching services through Squad.
In H1 2026, it reported payment value across switching, airtime vending and international payments for Habari.
“Strong transaction growth across switching, airtime vending and international payments reflects deepening ecosystem adoption, broader customer use cases and increasing cross-border activity,” GTCO said.
Habari’s switching and processing value has grown by 662.04% to ₦74.72 trillion ($56.17 billion) since H1 2024. As of the nine months ending September 2025, Access Holdings’ Hydrogen reported a translation value of ₦60.4 trillion ($45.41 billion).
GTCO is building a payments infrastructure giant.
HabariPay is extracting high returns on its assets while scaling transaction volumes exponentially. Interact with the financial data below.
How efficiently is HabariPay capturing value?
How fast is the infrastructure scaling since 2024?
In 2025, Habari told TechCabal that its switching and processing licence allows it to power Point-of-Sale terminals, a new line of business for it.
Airtime vending, the sale of mobile airtime through digital payment channels, is up 88.69%. This growth coincides with the temporary suspension of telecom companies from offering airtime and data credit advances in H1, a disruption that hit telco-led fintech businesses. MTN Nigeria’s fintech revenue, for example, fell by 72.4% during the period.
International payments rose by 3,890.67% over the same period. International payments have benefited from the stabilisation of the foreign exchange market, which has allowed banks to raise limits on international transactions. The bank raised international transaction limits from $6,000 to $20,000 quarterly in H1 2026.
In August, GTCO increased its quarterly international payments limit to $40,000, which should translate into higher volumes by year-end.
GTCO’s payments business spans multiple transaction channels, generating revenue from merchant payments, switching, transfers, airtime, international payments, and other services. GTCO earns small fees on the transaction its processes, with revenue accumulating as payment volumes grow.
“Revenue growth was supported by rising transaction activity, broader merchant and consumer adoption and expanding value-added services, while scalable infrastructure and disciplined execution continued to support strong PBT growth,” GTCO said.
HabariPay’s cost-to-income ratio stood at 17.3%, while return on average assets and equity rose to 75.3% and 78.2%, respectively, from 44.8% and 49.6% in H1 2024.
GTCO never really built HabariPay as another branded consumer fintech competing for downloads, but focused on making it a payments infrastructure business attached to a large banking group.
2. ₦26.70 trillion ($20.07 billion): GTWorld is becoming more than a banking app
GTWorld, GTCO’s personal banking app, crossed three million active users in October 2025 and is growing at a month-on-month rate of 12%. In H1 2026, it processed 337.4 million transactions, up 15.82% year-on-year, while transaction value increased by 22.1%.
E-business income, which captures revenue from the group’s digital banking channels, grew by 47.36% during the period.
GTWorld is becoming more than a banking app.
GTCO is turning its primary mobile application into a group-wide distribution layer across banking, pensions, and investments.
How fast is GTWorld processing transactions?
(+15.82% YoY)
(Growing 12% MoM)
How does GTWorld serve the entire holding company?
For GTCO, the growth of GTWorld gives the group a growing digital distribution channel through which it can move more banking services online while increasing the volume of transactions it processes. In that sense, GTWorld is becoming an important bridge between GTCO’s banking business and its broader payments ambitions.
GTCO noted that it is elevating GTWorld into a fully fledged financial services app with “the go-live of Account Opening and Linking, Subscription, and Redemption for GTFunds Managers. This milestone made Banking, Pensions, and Investments seamlessly accessible within a single integrated App.”
Customers can now access banking, pensions, and investments through the same digital interface. Instead of building separate digital journeys for each business inside the group, GTCO is using one customer interface to distribute banking, payments, and investment products.
The app is therefore becoming less of a digital version of a bank branch and more of a distribution layer across the group.
3. ₦1.11 trillion ($834.52 million): Pay-with-Transfer is changing how GTCO’s customers pay
GTCO’s Pay-with-Transfer feature recorded one of the fastest rates of growth in its payments business.
Between H1 2025 and H1 2026, transaction value increased from ₦70.05 billion ($52.67 million) to ₦1.11 trillion ($834.52 million), while volume increased by 1,587.39%.
“Pay-with-Transfer values continued to increase, reflecting strong user adoption driven by speed and convenience, positioning it among the fastest-growing payment methods,” the bank said.
The growth is happening as some older payment channels decline. Card usage dropped by 13.31%, while USSD transactions declined by 15.29%.
GTCO’s payment rails are being rewritten.
As instant transfers become the default way to move money, traditional channels like Cards and USSD are seeing volume declines.
How are GTCO customers making payments?
“Card payments remain important, although customer activity is increasingly shifting towards alternatives such as Pay-with-Transfer,” the bank said.
Cards have historically been one of the most visible pieces of Nigeria’s digital payments infrastructure, but instant transfers are increasingly becoming reliable for everyday transactions.
In 2025, Moniepoint said transfers accounted for 39% of payments for informal businesses it surveyed, compared with 51% for cash and 9% for cards.
For GTCO, Pay-with-Transfer growth means it is capturing more of its customers’ payment journey through its channels.
4. ₦1.50trillion: GTCO is serious about its PoS business
At the end of 2025, GTCO committed to deploying 200,000 PoS terminals nationwide and increasing the value of transactions processed through its terminals tenfold in 2026.
H1 numbers show that it is making significant progress.
PoS transaction volume increased 299% year-on-year to 50.3 million transactions in H1 2026, while transaction value increased 369% to ₦1.50 trillion ($1.13 billion).
“Increased merchant adoption and higher transaction activity drove strong growth in POS volumes,” GTCO said.
GTCO is serious about its PoS business.
After processing ₦1.50 trillion ($1.13B) in H1 2026, GTCO is aggressively expanding to reach its ₦1 trillion monthly processing target.
How far is GTCO from its ₦1T monthly PoS ambition?
Select metric to see GTCO’s exact PoS performance:
How GTCO is attacking Nigeria’s PoS market:
The lender did not disclose how many terminals it has deployed, but the growth in transaction volume and value points to an expanding merchant network.
GTCO’s target is much larger. Its 2026 PoS plan targets ₦1 trillion ($751.82 million) in monthly total payment value by deepening its reach among SMEs, corporates, fintech platforms, and institutions through embedded finance products and closer integration with the GTCO ecosystem.
At its current H1 average of roughly ₦250 billion ($187.96 million) per month, the business is processing about a quarter of that target, showing both the scale of GTCO’s ambition and the amount of growth still required to reach it.
PoS terminals are one of Nigeria’s most important financial distribution channels, serving millions of small businesses. PoS transactions amounted to ₦59.3 trillion ($44.58 billion) in Q1 2026.
As of March 2025, there were more than 5.90 million active PoS terminals in Nigeria, with fintechs still holding a significant position in the market. Moniepoint says it has more than one million active terminals processing over ₦10 trillion ($7.52 billion) in transactions every month. OPay says more than one million businesses depend on its merchant services.
Nigeria’s banks are now pursuing this payment channel more aggressively. GTCO has removed processing fees on all its PoS terminals, making merchant acquisition a strategic priority rather than simply a source of transaction revenue.
5. ₦31.09 billion ($23.37 million): Technology spending is slowing
After years of increasing technology investment, GTCO’s technology-related expenses declined by 17.66% year-on-year in H1 2026.
It is the lender’s lowest half-year technology-related expense since H1 2023, when it spent ₦17.02 billion ($12.79 million).
Between H1 2021 and H1 2025, GTCO’s technology spending increased more than fivefold. In 2024 alone, technology spending increased by 48.4% to ₦88 billion ($66.16 million). The H1 2026 decline could mean a shift in its tech investments.
GTCO is done building. Now it is extracting value.
Tap the bars to trace the bank’s technological and service-related expenses over four years, revealing the shift from aggressive infrastructure expansion to high-margin extraction.
Technology and service-related expenses fell to exactly ₦31,096,407,000 in H1 2026[cite: 199]. This marks GTCO’s lowest half-year tech expense since 2023, signaling that the core payment rails are built and the bank is now capturing revenue at scale.
After years of building digital infrastructure, GTCO may now be moving from expanding its technology stack to extracting more value from the infrastructure it has already built, with the numbers suggesting that the infrastructure is being used at greater scale.
When Agbaje outlined GTCO’s payment ambitions in 2020, he pointed to Paystack as a company operating in the space the group wanted to enter. In 2024, Paystack said businesses sent and received more than ₦1 trillion ($751.82 million) through its platform in July alone. Updated figures are not available, but that year the payments company said 66% of transactions on its platform were happening through bank transfers.
GTCO’s payment platform is still some distance from the scale of Nigeria’s biggest fintechs. OPay processed $358 billion in gross transaction value in 2025 and recorded $72.47 million in net profit. Moniepoint processed ₦412 trillion ($309.75 billion) in transaction value.
But the numbers suggest that Agbaje’s 2020 payments ambition is no longer just a strategy on paper. GTCO is increasingly building a payments business around its banking franchise’s infrastructure, customers, and transaction flows—and the gap between that ambition and its current business is beginning to narrow.
Note: exchange rate used: ₦1,330.11/$

articles.title: Menschlicher Linksdrall: Studie enträtselt unsere Fortbewegung
articles.text:
Studie zur Fortbewegung: Menschen laufen von Natur aus gegen den Uhrzeigersinn
Wissenschaftler:innen der spanischen Universität Navarra und der japanischen Universität Tokio haben ein bisher unbemerktes Verhaltensmuster in der menschlichen Fortbewegung nachgewiesen. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature Communications veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, besitzen Menschen einen statistisch signifikanten Drang, beim freien Gehen gegen den Uhrzeigersinn zu laufen.
Bislang ging die Forschung zu Fußgängerströmen davon aus, dass dieses kollektive Linksabbiegen durch die soziale Interaktion in einer Menschenmenge entsteht, um Zusammenstöße zu vermeiden. Die neuen Daten zeigen jedoch, dass dieser sogenannte Lokomotions-Bias bereits im einzelnen Individuum verankert ist und durch die Gruppe lediglich verstärkt sichtbar wird.
Studie in Japan und Spanien schließt kulturelle Prägung aus
Für die Untersuchung führten die Forscher:innen um den Wissenschaftler Iñaki Echeverría-Huarte fünf verschiedene Experimente mit Erwachsenen, Teenagern und Vorschulkindern durch. Dabei spazierten die Testpersonen sowohl isoliert voneinander in leeren Räumen als auch in größeren Gruppen auf einem freien Schulhof.
Um kulturelle Unterschiede bei Ausweichmanövern zu überprüfen, fanden die Versuche absichtlich in verschiedenen Ländern statt. In Europa weichen Fußgänger:innen bei frontalem Kontakt meist nach rechts aus, während dies in Japan überwiegend nach links geschieht.
Das Ergebnis blieb über alle Versuchsanordnungen und Länder hinweg konstant und zeigte eine messbare Asymmetrie hin zu einer Linksdrehung. Wie ZME Science unterstreicht, traten diese Kreiselbewegungen besonders bei fünfjährigen Kindern stark auf, was darauf hindeutet, dass erlernte kulturelle Regeln nur eine untergeordnete Rolle spielen.
Zusätzlich führten die Verantwortlichen eine Umfrage zu sozialen Normen durch, um zu prüfen, ob Menschen unbewusst einer unausgesprochenen Regel folgen. Die Befragten gaben dabei mehrheitlich an, sie würden von anderen Personen eher eine Bewegung im Uhrzeigersinn erwarten.
Anatomische Faktoren beim menschlichen Linksdrall ausgeschlossen
Das Team untersuchte im Anschluss, ob anatomische Eigenschaften für die asymmetrische Fortbewegung verantwortlich sein könnten. Sie testeten Personen mit unterschiedlicher Händigkeit, der Dominanz eines bestimmten Fußes sowie unterschiedlicher Augendominanz.
Auch Geschlechterunterschiede oder das absichtliche Verdecken des rechten Auges durch eine Augenklappe zeigten keine signifikanten Abweichungen vom dokumentierten Linksdrall. Die Forscher:innen konnten damit nachweisen, dass die Bewegungstendenz unabhängig von diesen biologischen Merkmalen existiert.
Relevanz des Lokomotions-Bias für Architektur und Stadtplanung
Die Erkenntnisse aus der Untersuchung bieten konkrete Anhaltspunkte für die künftige Gestaltung öffentlicher Räume und Gebäude. Stadtplaner:innen und Architekt:innen können das Wissen über den natürlichen Linksdrall nutzen, um Laufwege in Flughäfen, Museen oder Einkaufszentren effizienter zu strukturieren.
Wenn Räume künftig asymmetrisch konzipiert werden, könnte dies den Verkehrsfluss unterstützen und Staus in dichten Menschenmengen reduzieren. Digitale Simulationen von Fußgängerströmen, die zur Planung von Notausgängen dienen, lassen sich durch die Integration dieses individuellen Faktors genauer steuern.
Die neurologische Ursache für das Phänomen bleibt zum aktuellen Zeitpunkt ungeklärt. Der an der Untersuchung beteiligte Wissenschaftler Claudio Feliciani vermutet, dass winzige Asymmetrien im Gleichgewichtssinn des Innenohrs eine Rolle spielen könnten. Die starke Voreingenommenheit, die bei Menschen nachgewiesen wurde, deute laut Feliciani auf eine Asymmetrie auf biomechanischer Ebene hin.
Bemerkenswert ist in diesem Zusammenhang ein Blick in die Historie des Sports, bei dem Laufbahnen in der Leichtathletik traditionell gegen den Uhrzeigersinn angelegt sind. Bis weitere Studien den genauen Mechanismus entschlüsseln, bleibt das Wissen um den menschlichen Linksdrall eine statistisch belegte Eigenheit unserer Fortbewegung.

articles.title: Namespace secures €37 million to scale coding, build and test infrastructure across Mac, Windows and Linux | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Zurich-based Namespace, a developer platform that offers fast coding, build, and test environments across Mac, Windows, and Linux, today announced its €37 million ($42 million) Series B to accelerate product development and expand its data centers
The round, closed only seven months after their Series A funding, was led by Scale Venture Partners, with participation from 20VC, NEA, Essence, Burst Capital, and angel investors including Olivier Pomel (CEO of Datadog) – bringing the total raised to €58 million ($65 million). The expansion comes as demand surges, with Namespace’s total revenue growing 8x over the past 12 months.
“I started Namespace because I believe developers deserve better. At Google, I saw how much great tools & infrastructure changes the way developers work. Outside of a handful of companies, that still doesn’t exist,” says Hugo Santos, Founder and CEO of Namespace. “My vision is to make that experience the default for every fast moving company. We’re starting where developers and their agents spend the entire day: coding and CI.”
Namespace’s Series B comes amid continued investment in European developer tooling and infrastructure in 2026.
EU-Startups has covered approximately €160 million in funding across ten comparable or adjacent companies this year, including €61.5 million for Belfast-based software supply-chain platform Cloudsmith, €31 million for Cambridge-based software engineering company Undo, €21 million for Paris-based orchestration platform Kestra, and €4 million for Helsinki-based AI-native CI/CD startup Avrea.
Switzerland has also contributed to this activity, with Zurich-based Rapidata raising €7.2 million for AI development infrastructure and Pfäffikon-based AI Infrastructure Capital AG launching with around €16 million for compute capacity.
“The use of agents in software development challenges the tradeoff assumptions made by prior generations of tooling,” adds Javier Redondo, Partner at Scale Venture Partners. “Namespace is the platform that can meet the demand for speed and scalability, while delivering the same reliability and security that engineers have grown accustomed to.”
Founded in 2022, Namespace offers fast coding, build, and test environments across Mac, Windows, and Linux. The company was founded by former Google Principal Engineer Hugo Santos.
While hyperscalers like AWS and GCP optimise for production workloads, Namespace says they optimises for coding, build, and test environments. It designs and deploys its own server racks worldwide, then builds their suite of products on that engineering foundation.
Namespace is already working with over 1000 organisations including SpaceXAI, Ramp, Framer, ElevenLabs, Vanta, Bilt. and Sierra.
“Namespace is the best dev infrastructure tool I’ve used in years. We run everything from our CI to Oz, our cloud agent platform, on Namespace, and I could not recommend it enough,” says Aloke Desai, Head of Product Engineering, Warp
According to the company, some of the most important interactions today happen on an iPhone or a Macbook. Yet almost every infrastructure provider skips Mac, which means a developer’s agent, trying to build an iOS or macOS app for the App Store, has nowhere to build or test it. Coding agents need a Mac at any scale with all the required iOS and macOS developer tooling. This has led to a demand for Namespace’s Mac environments.
With the new funding, Namespace will expand its data centre locations, including its fleet of Mac hardware, and open offices in San Francisco and New York City.

articles.title: El mayor repositorio científico del mundo ha colapsado tras recibir 40.000 pre-prints este septiembre. Antes de la IA no pasaba de 15.000
articles.text:
Cuatro páginas. Cincuenta subsecciones. Algunas, sin una sola línea de texto. Cuando a principios de 2026, la revista Science se preguntó qué estaba pasándole a arXiv, una de las piezas claves de la ciencia actual, Ralph Wijers puso ese como ejemplo de lo que no paraba de llegar gracias a la IA.
Puede parecer una tontería, ese ejemplo se rechaza con un vistazo. Pero Wijers, astrónomo de la Universidad de Ámsterdam fallecido este verano, era uno de los responsables editoriales de la plataforma; es decir, sabía de lo que hablaba. El problema es que hay que echar ese vistazo.
En septiembre de 2026, de hecho, hubo que echar 40.363 vistazos.
Un segundo... ¿qué es exactamente arXiv? Es el mayor repositorio de preprints del mundo. El lugar donde físicos, matemáticos e informáticos cuelgan sus trabajos antes de que sean revisados por pares y publicados en una revista. Se fundó en 1991 y, hasta ahora, ha sido la verdadera puerta de entrada de casi toda la física nueva.
Tiene sentido: a medida que los procesos de publicación se burocratizaban, arXiv se convertía en una forma rápida de mostrar en qué estabas trabajando, compartir información y coordinarse. No revisa los artículos en profundidad, solo hace una moderación para evitar que el repositorio se convirtiera en un vertedero.
¿Y qué ha pasado? Que la facilidad con la que se pueden enviar pre-prints hoy por hoy gracias a la IA ha terminado por dejarlos fuera de juego. Para dimensionar la situación basta con entender que esos 40.363 envíos nuevo en septiembre, son unos 1.300 envíos al día. Y de moderarlos se encargan un grupo de entre 150 y 300 voluntarios.
Tras 35 años de un trabajo fecundísimo para la ciencia, arXiv se veía superada.
¿Y qué han hecho? Por lo pronto, han puesto un límite personal. Cada 'submitter' solo puede enviar dos artículos al mes y nadie puede tener más de tres pendientes de revisión a la vez. Aún así, el proceso no será rápido. Hay mucho que moderar.
Esto reduce mucho la eficacia de arXiv, es verdad. Hay investigadores que se plantean si tiene sentido esperar meses a que su pre-print se cuelgue en el repositorio.
Pero, claro, las cifras son tremendas. Desde noviembre de 2022 (cuando se lanzó CHatGPT) han entrado en la plataforma más de un millón de artículos. Esto es, un tercio de todo el archivo. Solo en 2026, de enero a septiembre, se han sumado 270.685 envíos. Un 30% más que en el mismo periodo de 2025.
Son quizás las cifras más elocuentes para señalar que el cuello de botella de la ciencia ha cambiado de lugar. Buena parte de la arquitectura mundial del desarrollo científico estaba articulada sobre la base de que escribir artículos era costoso. Ahora, en cambio, es gratis.
Y, sin embargo, no podemos decir que sean problemas nuevos. Estos problemas preexistían (los artículos crecían, los revisores escaseaban, nadie era capaz de estar al día): lo único es que está haciendo la IA es mostrar las costuras de forma mucho más evidente
¿Y ahora qué? Esa es la gran pregunta. Los expertos saben desde hace tiempo que el sistema científico tiene que reinventarse completamente, pero es algo rematadamente difícil de hacer: no hay estructuras centrales, no hay gobernanza posible; y sí enormes intereses.
Sería divertido, supongo; si no nos jugáramos tanto en ello.

articles.title: Why finance teams need to think in systems
articles.text:
Why finance teams need to think in systems
As financial workflows become more connected, finance teams are taking a greater role in designing processes that reduce manual work, improve visibility, and scale with the business.
Finance has always had a role beyond recording transactions. It is involved in planning, controls, treasury, risk, and decision-making. What is changing is the extent to which finance teams are also involved in the systems through which financial activity takes place.
A customer's payment information can now move through a website or app, a payment system, an invoicing platform, a bank account, and an accounting system before it appears in a financial report. If those systems do not communicate, someone has to fill the gaps: checking transactions, moving data, downloading reports, and matching records manually.
As businesses grow, it becomes harder to manage.
Finance teams are becoming more involved in how these processes are designed. They are looking at where data comes from, where it needs to go, which steps can be automated, and how different systems should work together.
Finance remains responsible for financial control, visibility, and decision-making. But fulfilling that responsibility increasingly requires an understanding of the systems behind the numbers.
From recording transactions to designing workflows
Consider a typical payment. A customer pays an invoice online. The payment needs to be recorded, the invoice updated, the money sent to the right bank account, and the transaction eventually reconciled with the accounting records.
When each step sits in a different system, finance teams can end up doing much of this work manually.
The same applies as businesses add subscriptions, recurring payments, payment links, marketplaces, or physical locations. Finance may also have to manage refunds, disputes, settlements, payouts, and multiple banking relationships.
So payments are becoming part of a wider financial workflow, not a series of individual transactions.
Technology can take some of the repetitive work out of this process. More importantly, it lets finance teams look at the workflow as a whole. Can a successful payment automatically update an invoice? Can payment information move into accounting without being entered again? Can a failed transaction trigger the next step without someone having to monitor it?
These are questions about how financial processes should work, and technology can help make them happen.
Finance starts thinking in systems
Accounting and financial controls remain at the centre of the function, but finance professionals also need to be comfortable with data, digital systems, and the way information moves between them.
A 2025 Wolters Kluwer survey of 100 senior finance executives in India found that 74% ranked digital transformation as a top priority, while 66% prioritized workflow automation. The survey also identified fragmented systems and data silos as challenges for finance teams.
Finance professionals do not need to become software developers. But they do need to understand what a system can do, where a process is breaking down, and what should happen when two systems need to exchange information.
As routine work becomes more automated, finance teams can spend more time on analysis, planning, problem-solving, and working with other parts of the business. That also brings them closer to decisions about how processes are built, how different systems connect, and where technology can improve them.
Connecting financial systems
An API allows different software applications to exchange information and interact with each other. For finance teams, this means that payment information related to payments does not have to stop at the payment platform. Transaction information can move into systems handling invoices, accounting, orders, or customer records.
For example, once a customer completes a payment, that transaction information can pass to another application, which can update the relevant financial record or trigger the next step in the workflow.
Zoho Payments provides REST-based APIs that allow businesses to incorporate payment functionality into their applications. It also supports webhooks, which can send real-time notifications when events such as successful or failed payments, refunds, and payouts take place.
For finance, the value is in what these connections let the business do. Payment collection, invoicing, and reconciliation can become one workflow, instead of separate activities that require moving information between systems.
Building finance operations that can scale
A process that works when a business handles a few dozen transactions can become a bottleneck as the number of customers, invoices, payment methods, and bank transactions grows. More manual work also creates more opportunities for errors and mismatches.
Connected systems can help businesses handle more volume without increasing manual work at the same rate. They can reduce the need to move information between systems manually, limit mismatches, and give finance teams better visibility into financial activity.
Zoho Payments is one example of this connected approach.When used with Zoho Books, payment information can flow into the accounting workflow, helping businesses record collections, track settlements, and reconcile transactions. For businesses with more specific requirements, APIs provide another way to connect payment functionality with existing applications and workflows.
The aim is to make payments, invoices, and reconciliation work together rather than treating them as separate tasks. This can give finance teams more control over how financial information moves through the business, while reducing the amount of manual intervention as transaction volumes grow. The finance team will still close the books, manage cash, and oversee reporting. But it is also likely to have a greater role in deciding which systems connect, which tasks should be automated, and how financial data moves from one part of the business to another.
Finance isn’t becoming IT. But understanding the numbers increasingly means understanding the systems that move them.

articles.title: EUA: Nova York declara estado de emergência por surto de sarampo
articles.text:
O Estado de Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, declarou situação de emergência por desastre nesta segunda-feira (5) diante do avanço de um surto de sarampo.
A medida, anunciada pela governadora Kathy Hochul, amplia a resposta das autoridades de saúde em comunidades rurais e permite a participação de mais profissionais na vacinação e no diagnóstico da doença.
A decisão ocorre após Nova York registrar 108 casos de sarampo em 2026 até 3 de outubro. Desse total, sete foram identificados na cidade de Nova York e 101 em outras regiões do Estado.
O número ganhou força principalmente nos últimos meses: 92 casos foram registrados desde 15 de julho, distribuídos por 18 condados com baixa cobertura vacinal. Mais de mil doses da vacina tríplice viral, que protege contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola (SCR), já foram aplicadas em áreas rurais desde então.
O que muda com a emergência
- A ordem executiva assinada por Hochul amplia o grupo de profissionais autorizados a atuar na resposta ao surto;
- Entre as medidas está a autorização para que enfermeiros registrados solicitem exames de casos suspeitos de sarampo. Farmacêuticos também poderão vacinar crianças a partir dos dois anos de idade;
- A determinação ainda exige que todas as aplicações da vacina contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola sejam registradas nos sistemas de imunização do Estado ou da cidade de Nova York em até 72 horas;
- A exigência de registro não elimina, porém, a necessidade de consentimento para a vacinação: a aplicação da vacina continua dependendo da autorização do paciente ou de um responsável legal;
- A situação de emergência entrou em vigor na segunda-feira e permanecerá válida até 4 de novembro. Segundo Hochul, a medida busca fortalecer os esforços para conter a doença.
Leia mais:
- Brasil entra em alerta máximo por surtos de sarampo na América
- Entrevista: Brasil entra em alerta máximo por surtos de sarampo na América
- Ebola, sarampo… doenças podem se espalhar na Copa do Mundo?
Surto também avança na Pensilvânia
O cenário em Nova York é agravado pela situação do estado vizinho da Pensilvânia, que enfrenta surto ainda maior.
Até 2 de outubro, a Pensilvânia contabilizava 977 casos e cinco mortes, principalmente em condados rurais próximos à fronteira com Nova York. Na segunda-feira, autoridades de saúde informaram que o número já havia ultrapassado mil casos.
Com isso, a Pensilvânia passou a registrar o maior surto estadual de sarampo nos Estados Unidos em mais de três décadas.
O avanço da doença não está restrito aos dois estados. Os Estados Unidos registraram quase 3,9 mil casos de sarampo em 2026, segundo dados dos Centros de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC), fazendo deste o pior ano para a doença no país desde 1991.
Por que o sarampo preocupa?
O sarampo é uma doença respiratória altamente contagiosa. Dados do Departamento de Saúde de Nova York indicam que o vírus pode ser transmitido pelo ar por meio de tosse ou espirro e que pessoas infectadas podem transmitir a doença antes mesmo do surgimento das manchas características.
Os sintomas costumam começar com febre alta, tosse, coriza e olhos vermelhos e lacrimejantes. Alguns dias depois, surge uma erupção cutânea que normalmente começa no rosto e se espalha pelo corpo.
A doença também pode provocar complicações graves, incluindo pneumonia, hospitalização, inflamação do cérebro e morte. A principal forma de prevenção é a vacinação com a tríplice viral.
O Departamento de Saúde de Nova York havia lançado em setembro um painel específico para acompanhar os casos de sarampo no Estado, após identificar aumento das infecções em diferentes regiões rurais. Na ocasião, eram 57 casos confirmados no Estado até 12 de setembro; o total chegou a 108 até 3 de outubro.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Pésimas noticias para millones de móviles antiguos: Android Auto los dejará sin soporte muy pronto
articles.text:
Si usas Android Auto a diario, pero tienes un móvil con algunos años de antigüedad, te traemos malas noticias. Usuarios reportan que la plataforma para conectar el smartphone con el coche está comenzando a mostrar avisos de que pronto se quedarán sin soporte. ¿El factor en común? Todos los impactados usando Android 10.
Según recoge Android Authority, múltiples publicaciones en Reddit revelan que Android Auto está mostrando alertas de que próximamente ya no funcionará en su móvil. El software indica simplemente la eliminación del soporte, sin brindar detalles más específicos en tal sentido.
Uno de los afectados indicó que estaba usando un Samsung Galaxy Note 9, mientras que otro comentó que su dispositivo era un Sony Xperia XZ2 Compact. El punto en común entre los modelos es que ejecutan Android 10, la última versión soportada de manera oficial por los equipos en cuestión.
Por lo pronto, Google no ha anunciado ningún tipo de cambio en los requisitos de software mínimos para la ejecución de Android Auto. Aunque es bastante común que la compañía los actualice cada cierta cantidad de años para elevar el listón y no tener que seguir ofreciendo compatibilidad con versiones de Android ya obsoletas. En octubre del año pasado, por ejemplo, puso punto y final al soporte de Android Auto en móviles con Android 8.
Android Auto estaría a punto de eliminar el soporte para Android 10
El citado reporte indica que la web de Google todavía muestra Android 9 como la versión más antigua que todavía soporta Android Auto. No obstante, no sería raro que la historia cambie muy pronto y que se vuelva obligatorio disponer de Android 11 o superior para poder utilizar el móvil conectado al coche.
Si efectivamente Google deja de soportar Android 10 en Android Auto, la medida seguramente impacte en millones de dispositivos activos a nivel mundial. Es cierto que estamos hablando de un software viejo y que ejecutar versiones tan antiguas conlleva enormes riesgos de seguridad. Sin embargo, los usuarios impactados por la situación también tienen su justificación: los móviles aún funcionan como corresponde y cumplen con lo que necesitan a diario con total suficiencia.
Para aquellos que se vean afectados por la quita de soporte a Android 10 en Android Auto, hay algunas opciones para considerar. La primera (y la más lógica) es actualizar su móvil a un modelo más moderno. Esto no solo les garantizará el acceso a la aplicación, sino también a un entorno más avanzado y seguro.
La segunda es un poco más complicada si no tienen conocimientos técnicos, pues implica extender la vida útil de su móvil con la ROM de algún fork de Android. Uno de los más conocidos y probados es LineageOS, que brinda soporte para apps de Google como Android Auto.
Por lo pronto, los usuarios de Android 10 que están recibiendo las alertas de quita de soporte de Android Auto mencionan que la plataforma todavía funciona con normalidad. No obstante, es imposible saber por cuánto tiempo más.

articles.title: HackerRank's AI interviewer offers a glimpse into what job interviews could become | TechCrunch
articles.text:
What happens when AI moves from helping job candidates to evaluating them? HackerRank, a platform used by companies to assess and hire developers, is offering a glimpse at what that future of job interviews could look like with Chakra, an AI agent that conducts interviews, observes candidates as they work, and evaluates not just their answers but also how they got there.
After around six months in beta, HackerRank is making Chakra generally available to its customers on Monday. The startup says the AI interviewer has already conducted more than 500,000 interviews during testing, with companies including Snowflake, Snorkel, and Capgemini among those that tried it, while HackerRank also tested the product internally.
AI has been a staple in job interviews for some time, with companies using voice agents and other automated tools to screen candidates and make the hiring process more efficient. Job seekers, meanwhile, have increasingly gained their own AI tools to help them navigate interviews, sometimes without employers knowing.
With Chakra, HackerRank is betting AI can change not only how interviews are conducted, but also what employers can measure. Beyond whether someone arrives at the right answer, the startup wants to assess harder-to-capture signals such as critical thinking and judgment, as well as what it calls “AI fluency” — how well a candidate frames a problem for AI, judges its output, and steers it toward a solution.
“The previous modality of evaluation was evaluating the output,” HackerRank co-founder and CEO Vivek Ravisankar said in an interview. “Now, because of AI, anybody can produce an artifact.” The question for employers, he said, becomes whether they can understand the thinking and judgment that went into producing it.
In practice, a Chakra interview is designed to look more like doing the job than taking a traditional coding test. A candidate gets a task involving a real-world code repository, and they work through it in a canvas that includes an AI assistant. As the candidate works, Chakra can use the context of what they are doing to ask follow-up questions, such as why they chose one approach over another, or how their solution would change if a new constraint were introduced.
Ravisankar told TechCrunch that Chakra is changing the basic structure of the hiring process itself. What previously involved three separate rounds, comprising a recruiter screen, take-home assessment, and follow-up interview with an engineer, is now combined into a single Chakra interview, he said.
Giving candidates access to AI during an interview might seem to make it easier to cheat. However, HackerRank says it found the opposite. Suspicious-activity flags, Ravisankar said, were 70% to 80% lower in Chakra interviews than in comparable traditional HackerRank assessments, though the rate varied depending on factors such as geography and seniority.
Ravisankar told TechCrunch that giving candidates access to AI reduces the incentive to secretly use outside tools that can feed them answers during an interview.
Launched at TechCrunch Disrupt in 2012, HackerRank built its business around coding challenges, eventually helping companies assess and hire developers based on their technical skills. The Y Combinator-backed startup now has more than 3,000 business customers, including Amazon, Nvidia, Clay, and Replit, and a community of over 30 million developers worldwide.
Chakra represents a bet against the kind of technical assessment business HackerRank spent years building. Its traditional product largely tested whether developers could solve coding problems correctly. Nonetheless, Ravisankar believes AI has made HackerRank’s earlier model less useful to measure engineering ability.
Ravisankar compared the transition internally to Apple moving from the iPod to the iPhone, as the old product still has value, but the new one represents where the startup believes the market is headed. “Chakra is going to be the headline,” he said. “It’s going to be the way that we’re going to move forward.”
However, giving AI a deeper role in evaluating candidates raises a different set of questions, particularly around how much of a hiring decision companies should delegate to an algorithm. Ravisankar told TechCrunch that Chakra is designed to score candidates rather than make the final hiring decision, which remains with humans.
AI, he said, can handle more structured parts of an interview by consistently applying criteria set by an employer, while human interviewers can spend more time determining whether they actually want to work with a candidate and answering questions about the company, team, and role.
“AI is way less biased than humans, if you tune it properly,” Ravisankar said, arguing that an AI system can be instructed to follow the same rubric for every candidate rather than being influenced by factors such as a candidate’s background or education.
Applying the same criteria consistently, however, does not necessarily make an AI system free of bias. Automated hiring tools can inherit or amplify biases from the data, models, and criteria used to build them, prompting regulators to scrutinize their use in employment decisions.
The use of AI in hiring is already drawing regulatory scrutiny. New York City, for instance, requires employers using certain automated employment decision tools to subject them to an independent bias audit and provide notice to candidates before using them. Ravisankar acknowledged that hiring is a regulated area and said complying with such requirements is part of what HackerRank has had to build for.

articles.text:
Home
                        
TECHNICAL PAPERS
								October 5th, 2026 - 
								By: Technical Paper Link
								
							
Researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz published a technical paper titled “Design Space Exploration of Backside Clock Meshes for 2 nm GAAFET BSPDN Technology.”
Abstract Excerpt: “Clock meshes are used in high-performance VLSI designs to minimize skew and tolerate on-chip variation, but they spend scarce routing resources on premium metal layers. Backside power delivery creates a new option: it adds thick, low-resistance metal layers on the back of the wafer, and the power grid does not consume all of them. Flip-flops remain on the frontside; a backside mesh therefore cannot drive them directly, and every connection passes through a through-silicon via. We present the first design-space exploration of backside clock meshes, implemented in OpenROAD on GT2N, a 2 nm nanosheet technology.”

articles.title: OpenAI : le responsable de la sécurité démissionne et tire la sonnette d'alarme à son tour
articles.text:
Ce n’est pas anodin. David Robinson, qui rédigeait les rapports de sécurité d’OpenAI, quitte l’entreprise dans un contexte extrêmement tendu. Selon lui, l’IA doit désormais être gérée avec la même rigueur qu’une centrale nucléaire.
Après trois ans et demi chez OpenAI, où il a accompagné le lancement de 12 modèles, David Robinson a décidé de quitter le navire, révèle Business Insider. Un départ qui résonne forcément avec celui de Jacob Coxon, chercheur chez Anthropic, il y a quelques jours. Il assurait alors que les entreprises d’IA « parient avec nos vies ». Johannes Heidecke, ancien responsable de la sécurité chez OpenAI, a également abandonné son poste plus tôt cette année.
Une approche à revoir
« Les entreprises qui construisent cette technologie ne sont pas du tout assez prudentes », écrit Robinson dans un essai publié dans The Atlantic. Selon lui, OpenAI « court d’un lancement à l’autre » sans atteindre le niveau de soin nécessaire.
Il cible particulièrement la méthode maison de « déploiement itératif ». Celle-ci consiste à lancer un produit, repérer les problèmes puis renforcer les garde-fous. Cette approche « garantit, par nature, des échecs périodiques », avance-t-il, et leur ampleur grandit à mesure que les systèmes gagnent en puissance. Elle découle d’un « optimisme sans entrave » sur la capacité à régler les problèmes au fur et à mesure, dénonce-t-il.
Or, l’actualité exige « une humilité qui n’est pas naturelle chez ceux qui ont réussi grâce à leur extrême confiance en eux », poursuit l’expert, avant de trancher : « le temps des essais et des erreurs est révolu ». David Robinson cite évidemment l’attaque de Hugging Face par un des agents d’OpenAI : « Un environnement où de telles choses peuvent arriver n'est pas un endroit où faire grandir des esprits artificiels qui pourraient être plus intelligents que nous et ne pas faire ce que nous voulons », écrit-il.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code
Les mesures à mettre en place selon l’expert
L’ancien dirigeant suggère que les entreprises d’IA devraient fonctionner « comme des centrales nucléaires ou des aéroports très fréquentés, avec des couches de redondance et une planification minutieuse », afin qu’une erreur humaine, « occasionnelle et inévitable », n’ouvre pas la porte à la catastrophe. Il appelle aussi à créer une « nouvelle science » pour s’assurer que ces systèmes restent contrôlables, car les mesures actuelles de leur alignement sur les valeurs humaines sont « grossières ».
OpenAI, elle, assure prendre le sujet au sérieux. « Nous veillons à ce que nos modèles ne deviennent pas plus capables que ce que nous pouvons gérer et sécuriser, et nous suspendons l’entraînement ou retenons des modèles quand il faut ralentir », a rappelé un porte-parole. Mais le constat est implacable et visiblement, ils sont plusieurs en interne à penser que ces efforts arrivent bien trop tard.
Car actuellement, OpenAI et Anthropic passent en revue des dizaines de milliers d’incidents de sécurité impliquant leur technologie.

articles.title: Windows 11 was released five years ago today — Microsoft promises latest update is 'predictable and low-disruption'
articles.text:
Windows 11 was released five years ago today — Microsoft promises latest update is 'predictable and low-disruption'
If it feels like longer than five years, probably due to the suffering.
Windows 11 was released five years ago, on October 5, 2021. It feels like it's been around longer, as Microsoft’s latest OS has generated numerous headlines, mostly concerning the pain it put users through. We’ve all aged with it. Things might be settling down, at last, though, as the 26H2 update started to roll out just a few days ago, and it is not promising a revolution, simply a “predictable and low-disruption” update.
After the crowd-pleasing Windows 10’s return to form, it was all too predictable that Windows 11 would misstep in some unexpected way, or actually in several ways. Microsoft is pretty creative with its misreading of the market. At release, the biggest issue with the new OS was that it sought to force lots of capable hardware into retirement. This issue churned for months, with folks wrangling system files to bypass minimum system requirements, and Microsoft seemingly shifting the goalposts around at the same time.
Another early controversy was Microsoft continuing to push users into setting up Windows using an online Microsoft account, and cutting off avenues of avoidance. Again, communities had to fight the OS to make it work the way they wanted, often with a simple local account. This struggle continues to this day. Microsoft paints the requirement as good for users, providing OneDrive backups, syncing across devices, and providing extra recovery and security features. However, forced online accounts are also a commercial vehicle for selling digital goods and services.
Things had settled down in Windows land by 2024, but Microsoft spoiled the broth again with the introduction of the Copilot+ PC era. In some ways, it showed some foresight in sensing that AI was going to be big. Nevertheless, this was another clear misstep, with gaffes/scares like the AI-centerpiece Windows Recall app.
Copilot+ PC’s failure was confirmed by Microsoft and its OEM partners when they quietly killed off all Copilot+ PC branding earlier this year. For now, built-in AI is being de-emphasized, and Microsoft is looking at a cross-platform agentic model.
A change of direction
This year has also seen Microsoft publicly realize that people need Windows 11 as a foundation for their productivity tasks and gaming fun. The OS isn’t the destination. Thus, in spring, execs promised to clean up and optimize Windows 11 for its basic everyday use. Going forward, Microsoft has dangled the carrot of faster built-in apps, lower memory/resource use, and other foundational OS optimizations.
Windows 11 26H2 was released to consumers last week. As a battle-scarred Windows veteran, I’ve not clicked the update button yet on any of my machines, but there are reasons to be optimistic that it doesn’t deliver new nightmares. Version 26H2 is being distributed with the promise to deliver a “predictable and low-disruption” update. Boring is good.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Despite the aforementioned controversies, as well as the usual collection of silly/scary bugs that needed ironing out, people are still using Windows 11. It is widely adopted and dominates the PC landscape. MacOS and Linux have made inroads in terms of users, but Windows still looks mostly unassailable on roughly 76% of all desktop/laptop computers. Among Windows versions, it holds nearly 72% of the market, with Windows 10 rapidly declining and dipping under 28% at the most recent count.

Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Cameroonian startup lensX launches Alibaba-style marketplace for African businesses - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Cameroonian startup lensX has launched an Alibaba-style online marketplace connecting businesses, vendors and customers across Africa, with augmented reality (AR) shopping on its longer-term roadmap.
lensX Inc has brought two web-based products to market – lensX Marketplace is aimed at customers, while lensX Vendors lets businesses list and sell their products online.
“In commerce, many African businesses still rely heavily on social media and informal channels to reach customers, creating a need for more structured digital marketplace infrastructure,” founder Ikomi Henry told Disrupt Africa. “Our approach is to build Africa-first technology platforms addressing these gaps.”
Founder-funded to date, lensX is now looking to build strategic partnerships and explore external investment to accelerate development and expansion.
“We are currently focused on building customer and vendor adoption, increasing marketplace inventory and improving the platform based on early market feedback,” Henry said.
The startup plans to make money through marketplace transaction fees, vendor services, subscriptions, featured listings, advertising and promotions, though it is not yet reporting significant revenue. Though it is launching in Cameroon, it has plans to expand into other African markets and eventually internationally. Its roadmap also includes AI-powered product discovery alongside AR shopping, with the goal of being among the first African marketplaces to bring augmented reality into the shopping experience.
Henry said getting to launch had not been easy, with challenges including regulatory and compliance requirements, integrating multiple third-party providers, and accessing infrastructure.
“Many infrastructure providers primarily serve larger established companies, meaning startups often need to demonstrate operational readiness and credibility before accessing certain services,” he said.

articles.title: Volant carré, style tranchant et clin d'oeil à la 205 : la future Peugeot 208 électrique se montre enfin
articles.text:
La future Peugeot 208 débarquera l’année prochaine avec des habits tout neufs. L’échéance approchant à grands pas, les premiers prototypes débutent ainsi leur mise au point sous d’épais camouflages. L’auto, qui inaugurera la nouvelle plateforme STLA One, s’inspirera du spectaculaire concept Polygon présenté en 2025. La face avant devrait adopter une calandre inédite flanquée de trois barres de LED traversantes.
Le capot s’allongera et deviendra encore plus plat pour équilibrer le profil du véhicule. Celui-ci abandonnera en revanche les incroyables portes papillon du concept pour des ouvrants plus traditionnels. Les rétroviseurs sont repris de la 308, alors que le vitrage devient plus rectiligne avec des angles plus prononcés au niveau de la portière arrière. La partie arrière plus verticale s’inspire pour sa part de la 205, avec un porte-à-faux plus court.
Le pari fou du volant Hypersquare sans liaison mécanique
Ajoutons que la poupe devrait adopter un bandeau lumineux composé de plusieurs segments illuminés cerclant l’inscription Peugeot rétroéclairée. Par rapport à la 208 actuelle, l’ensemble devrait être moins rondouillard et visuellement plus dynamique. L’histoire se répétera à bord avec une dalle flottante tirée droit du 3008. L’inédit se situe cependant à portée de main puisque la future citadine étrennera le volant Hypersquare.
Outre sa forme carrée, celui-ci sera dépourvu de liaison mécanique avec le train avant. Cela permettra un effort moindre pour diriger l’auto avec une direction ultra réactive qui s’adaptera à toutes les situations de conduite. Elle permettra alors de débloquer des capacités de conduite semi-autonome supérieures à celles de la 208 sortante. Reste à voir si le ressenti ne sera pas trop déroutant comparé à un volant classique.
Une citadine 100 % électrique pour tourner la page du thermique
La future 208 retiendra également le SLTA Brain, un cerveau centralisant toutes les fonctions du véhicule une seule et même unité pour une efficacité accrue. Suffisant pour inquiéter la dernière Clio ? Pas réellement, car la sochalienne s’adressera en réalité à un public complètement différent en faisant l’impasse sur les motorisations thermiques et hybrides. Car oui, la future citadine ne sera déclinée qu’en version électrique.
Il faudra plutôt voir la Renault 5 comme concurrente directe. Si Peugeot revoit le système d’infodivertissement et améliore sensiblement la partie technique, le triomphe de la lionne ne serait alors qu’une question de temps. La future 208 débloquera-t-elle enfin une plateforme 800 V pour une recharge enfin efficace ? La question reste en suspens, car cette architecture demeure encore coûteuse pour un véhicule du segment B.
Autonomie et prix : les défis majeurs de Peugeot
Côté autonomie, elle aura aussi fort à faire pour surpasser les 450 km de l’excellente Volkswagen ID. Polo. Enfin, gageons que ses prix soient maîtrisés pour faire face à la menace chinoise. Peugeot pourrait maintenir la 208 électrique actuelle pour proposer des tarifs plus attractifs. En parallèle, la 208 hybride ne sera pas remplacée et continuera à batailler avec la Clio.

articles.text:
Andhra Pradesh, PanIIT partner for Rs 500-Cr deeptech fund; An intralogistics business that serves 25 countries
Unveiled at the PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit in Vijayawada on Saturday, the deeptech-focused fund aims to back at least 25 local startups by 2030.
Dear Reader,
Industry experts argue India must develop its own AI safety framework tailored to its unique languages, scale, and application-focused ecosystem, rather than copy the newly signed White House Accord on Super Intelligence.
While top US tech firms such as OpenAI, Meta, Google, and xAI recently committed to voluntary internal controls, external audits, and oversight teams under the US pact, Indian leaders like Nasscom Chairman Srikanth Velamakanni emphasize that India needs a customised, multi-stakeholder approach.
Meanwhile, India’s top IT services firms are expected to post muted revenue growth (0.5–1% quarter-on-quarter) and stable margins for Q2 FY27 due to tight discretionary client budgets and prolonged decision cycles amid geopolitical tensions.
While UnearthInsight expects Q2 performance to mirror a sluggish Q1, Gartner sees a slight uptick driven by older contract wins transitioning into revenue. Overall, analysts say that market cautiousness persists, with key focus turning to conversion rates from deal pipelines to revenue and the deflationary impact of AI on traditional IT services.
Moving on to the world of electric vehicles, researchers are now looking at why some people feel motion sickness in an EV while others don’t. One of the possible reasons could be that humans have got accustomed to the sound of engines with movement. The silence in electric cars could trigger motion sickness, BBC reports. Other reasons include the braking mechanism in these cars as well as the way they accelerate and decelerate.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Andhra Pradesh, PanIIT partner for Rs 500-Cr deeptech fund
- ICYMI: An intralogistics business that serves 25 countries
Here’s your trivia for today: Which Japanese company was originally founded in 1946 under the name Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo before changing its name to a word derived from the Latin term for "sound"? (Scroll down for answer)
Deeptech
Andhra Pradesh, PanIIT partner for Rs 500-Cr deeptech fund
PanIIT Alumni India and the Andhra Pradesh government are partnering to launch the Rs 500-crore PanIIT Amaravati Venture Fund, targeting a first close by July 1, 2027. Unveiled at the PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit in Vijayawada on Saturday, the deeptech-focused fund aims to back at least 25 local startups by 2030 as part of a broader push to drive research, capital, and manufacturing into the state.
While the fund will draw capital from IIT alumni, industry figures, and institutional investors, the exact financial breakdown among the partners remains undisclosed.
Key takeaways:
- According to materials presented at the event, at least 50% of the companies the fund invests in will be expected to locate their principal R&D or manufacturing operations in Andhra Pradesh.
- The proposed fund seeks to address two pain points of the deeptech startup industry: access to patient capital and access to experienced operators and industry networks.
- Among the proposed initiatives is a permanent PanIIT Amaravati Council, which is expected to act as a coordinating platform for deeptech, research and innovation initiatives in the state.
In Focus
ICYMI: An intralogistics business that serves 25 countries
Over the past decade, Addverb has scaled from a five-member team into a global intralogistics player with over 1,000 employees, 300+ clients, and operations across 25 countries. The company offers end-to-end solutions combining hardware (AMRs, AGVs, general-purpose humanoids) with custom software across diverse industries including FMCG, electronics, petrochemicals, and energy.
Addverb is currently expanding its R&D into "physical AI" and aims to double its revenue while expanding its global presence to 100 countries over the next decade.
Key takeaways:
- Addverb operates manufacturing hubs in Noida and Greater Noida, serves over 300 clients across 25 countries, and generated about Rs 660 crore in revenue last year (targeting ₹1,300 crore this year). Half of its revenue comes from international markets.
- The company has expanded alongside the country’s logistics automation market that has grown to an estimated $2.1 billion and is projected to reach $8 billion by 2034.
- To support its expansion, Addverb has established offices across multiple regions. Its US office serves North and South America, while its Netherlands office covers Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.
News & updates
- Oil business: OPEC+, during a meeting on Sunday, agreed to keep oil production targets steady for November. Core members of the group are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman.
- AI ethics: David Robinson, who led the writing of safety reports that accompanied the ChatGPT developer’s product releases, has quit. He warned that OpenAI’s culture was broken and that AI firms were not being “careful enough” about developing the technology.
What you should watch out for

- Indian IT services company Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is scheduled to announce its Q2 FY27 financial results on Thursday, October 8, 2026.
