articles.title: Avengers: Endgame overtakes Avatar again to become the highest-grossing movie of all time
articles.text:
The big picture: Marvel Studios has put Avengers: Endgame back on top of the global box office chart, narrowly ahead of James Cameron's Avatar, following the theatrical release of an updated version of the 2019 film. The result shows how a major franchise can use an older hit to generate fresh attention at the multiplex. It also points to a shift in how studios are using rereleases to support their current theatrical pipelines.
The rerelease, titled Avengers: Endgame Encore, has pushed the movie's worldwide total to $2.9255 billion. That puts it just ahead of Avatar, which has earned $2.9237 billion globally.
The difference is slim, and the record could change again. Both films have relied on rereleases to extend their box office runs years after their original debuts. The latest Endgame release was timed to help promote Marvel's next major event film, Avengers: Doomsday, which opens in December.
Encore included about four minutes of additional footage spread across four scenes. The scenes preview Doomsday, giving audiences a reason to return to a film that has long been available on home video and streaming. The strategy turns an older hit into part of the marketing campaign for a new release.
 – Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) October 4, 2026
During the rerelease's opening weekend, Endgame Encore earned $86 million worldwide, making it the number 2 global rerelease opening of all time behind the 2012 3D rerelease of Titanic. It also opened at number 1 in North America with $26 million, outperforming new titles including Paramount's Heart of the Beast, A24's Primetime, and DreamWorks Animation's Forgotten Island.
Business slowed considerably in its second weekend. The film collected $4.4 million domestically and $14.4 million internationally, bringing its second-weekend global total to $18.8 million. It ranked seventh at the domestic box office.
Still, the first weekend provided enough of a boost to move Endgame past Avatar. The two films have traded the record before.
Avatar held the global box office title for about 10 years after its 2009 release. Endgame moved ahead in July 2019, shortly after its original run, when it passed $2.79 billion worldwide. Cameron publicly congratulated Marvel at the time.
The lead did not last. In 2021, Avatar returned to theaters ahead of Avatar: The Way of Water. That rerelease lifted the film's global total above Endgame and restored its place at the top of the chart.
Marvel is now using the same basic playbook. The Encore release was not simply an anniversary screening or a standard revival. Its new scenes centered on the next Avengers film, creating a direct link between the conclusion of the Infinity Saga and the next phase of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
For now, Endgame holds the record again. But given how close the totals are, Avatar could reclaim it with another rerelease.

articles.title: Así es la renovación del SUV compacto Kia XCeed: más tecnología, etiqueta ECO y menos de 20.000 euros
articles.text:
El Kia XCeed, el coche diseñado y fabricado en Europa y que sólo se vende en Europa, ha sufrido una renovación completa. Tanto estética, con un frontal que se adecua al resto de modelos de la marca, como de tecnología, con dos pantallas de 12,3 pulgadas desde las que podemos interactuar con el coche. Disponible en cuatro versiones y con cuatro motores de gasolina, uno de ellos con sistema de micro hibridación para conseguir la etiqueta ECO, su precio de salida, aplicando todos los descuentos, se encuentra por debajo de los 20.000 euros.
Un precio y unas características que buscan hacer frente a las marcas chinas que han llegado, literalmente, rompiendo el mercado. El nuevo Kia XCeed es de las últimas propuestas de vehículos de combustión y donde no vemos ningún híbrido enchufable.
Una renovación de diseño que ya tocaba
Es donde más llama la atención el nuevo Kia XCeed. Su última renovación estética fue en 2022 donde los cambios no fueron demasiado significativos. Ahora vemos una especie de armonización con otros modelos de la marca, sobre todo en la parte frontal con una nueva parrilla y faros verticales, estética muy similar al resto de lanzamientos de la marca de los últimos meses.
En cuanto a dimensiones, es un centímetro más largo que el modelo anterior, llega hasta los 4,38 metros de largo por lo que se mete de lleno a rivalizar el podio de los SUV compactos.
En su interior también vemos muchos cambios. Quizá la principal sea la aparición de dos pantallas de 12 pulgadas, una para el cuadro del conductor y otra donde vemos todo lo relacionado con la navegación, info entretenimiento y demás. Es un coche lleno de tecnología y donde apenas vemos botones físicos. De hecho, el menú de navegación tactil se puede personalizar en función de lo que estemos utilizando, si la radio o la climatización.
Las líneas, las llantas de 16 o 18 pulgadas, lo sitúan como un crossover compacto perfecto para el día a día, con un buen espacio de maletero superior a los 400 litros.
Ayudas a la conducción
Entre las ADAS que incluye el nuevo Kia XCeed podemos encontrar: asistencia integral para la conducción (control de crucero y seguimiento de carril) y el aparcamiento, distancia de seguridad, detección de ángulo muerto o asistente de prevención de colisión con tráfico trasero cruzado (RCCA).
Además, tiene una cámara interior que graba para supervisar el comportamiento del conductor, detectando síntomas como la distracción o la fatiga, recomendándole parar si lo necesita.
Etiqueta ECO
Aunque Kia viene apostando fuerte por la electrificación, el nuevo Kia XCeed se comercializa con cuatro motores de gasolina, uno de ellos con un sistema microhíbrido que no aporta más potencia y sólo baja un poco el tema de emisiones. Lo que sí genera es la etiqueta ECO, algo muy preciado sobre todo en grandes ciudades.
Los motores de 1.0 litro y 1.6l entregan potencias que van desde los 115 cv a los 180 cv. Todos ellos combinados con cajas de cambios manuales y automáticas donde destaca la de siete velocidades DCT, la configuración más cómoda y eficiente sobre todo en ciudades.
Precio
El nuevo Kia XCeed tiene un precio de salida, en el modelo base, de 27.990 euros pero aplicadas las ofertas y descuentos de la propia Kia, se queda en 19.860 euros, un precio muy atractivo y con el que espera seguir consolidando las buenas ventas de este modelo. Si queremos la versión básica microhíbrida, el precio sube mil euros.

articles.title: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s ‘rogue’ bots may be linked to a May outage
articles.text:
Following many recent disclosures about AI agents accessing third-party websites and services, the Wikimedia Foundation, which hosts Wikipedia, says that it “can confirm that we have discovered some activity” by “rogue” OpenAI agents on Wikimedia platforms.
Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s ‘rogue’ bots may be linked to a May outage
The Wikimedia Foundation believes OpenAI agents edited wikis, tried to ‘exploit’ a notetaking tool, and made ‘millions’ of automated API requests.
The activity includes edits to Wikimedia wikis, “unsuccessful attempts” to “exploit” the Etherpad note-taking tool that the Wikimedia Foundation hosts, and heavy traffic that the foundation says “may” have contributed to a partial outage that happened in May, according to a blog post. However, the Wikimedia Foundation says it didn’t find evidence that its systems were “used for coordination among agents” (recently, OpenAI bots reportedly hijacked a German wiki site to coordinate) or evidence of systems or data being compromised.
Here’s Wikimedia’s summary of what it saw:
Wiki editing: We’ve identified edits to Wikimedia wikis that we believe are from AI agents operated by OpenAI. These edits were not published to pages with visibility to general readers; almost all of them were testing edits in “sandbox” areas of the wiki. It also included a few edits to the configuration for a citation tool, which we believe were potentially malicious edits that were intended to misuse this tool as a proxy for fetching data from remote services. While Wikipedia policies allow bots to edit when they are disclosed and approved by the community, none of those approvals were sought in these incidents.
Etherpad probing and use: Agents we believe to be operated by OpenAI made some unsuccessful attempts to compromise our public Etherpad, a note-taking tool we host as a community service. Agents unsuccessfully tried to use it to fetch data from other websites as a proxy. Other agents also likely operated by OpenAI took notes about their tasks, though this did not appear to turn into coordination.
Excessive data downloading: Agents we believe to be operated by OpenAI made millions of automated requests to our public APIs to access the knowledge on Wikimedia projects, crawled millions of pages (mainly from our projects Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons), and made hundreds of thousands of data queries to the Wikidata Query Service (WQDS). This traffic may have contributed to a partial outage on WQDS in May.
“The open web is a public good,” the Wikimedia Foundation says. “We should not allow this behavior to become the ‘new normal’ for the people or organizations that maintain it.”
“We appreciate the detailed findings Wikimedia shared with us,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says in a statement. “We’re working with them as we review and analyze the activity they identified along with our overall investigation, and we’ll continue to share relevant information as that work progresses.” OpenAI’s investigation hasn’t been able to verify if its bots contributed to the May outage, according to Pusateri.
Update, October 5th: Added statement from OpenAI.

Researchers at Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, University of California, Santa Barbara, and National University of Singapore published a technical paper titled “Low contact resistance and high current density in ballistic p-type transistors based on oxygen-doped WSe2 monolayers.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“The development of high-performance p-type monolayer transistors is critical for extending two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors beyond silicon in sub 1-nm technology nodes for complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) circuits. articles.title: Desde hoy, las empresas tienen que explicar a sus trabajadores cómo funciona el algoritmo que gestiona su puesto de trabajo
articles.text:
Nuestras vidas cada vez están más supeditados a las decisiones que toma un algoritmo: decide qué noticias nos pueden interesar, cuál es la siguiente canción que te apetece escuchar o qué series te va a encantar. Sin embargo, lo que mucha gente no sabe, es que los algoritmos también deciden qué turnos de trabajo debes cubrir, qué tareas debes hacer e incluso cuál va a ser tu salario.
Lo malo es que nadie te ha contado cómo toma esa decisión el algoritmo. Hasta ahora. Hoy entra en vigor la nueva directiva sobre transparencia laboral con la que las empresas ahora deben contarte cómo decide el algoritmo todas esas variables que afectan de forma directa a tu puesto de trabajo.
Un mandato de Europa. Llevamos ya algún tiempo hablando de la necesidad de aplicar mayor transparencia a las decisiones que afectan al ámbito laboral. De hecho, la directiva europea 2019/1152 que regula la aplicación de esa transparencia laboral lleva cinco años de retraso en su trasposición a la legislatura española. El Real Decreto 723/2026 que entra en vigor hoy, es la materialización de ese mandato europeo haciendo que los empleos sean más previsibles para los empleados.
El artículo 3 de este Real Decreto obliga a las empresas a informar a los empleados de "la existencia de sistemas algorítmicos o automatizados de toma de decisiones". Es decir, si es un algoritmo quien decide tu carga de trabajo en función de la demanda, y eso puede afectar a tu salario.
Avisar no basta, hay que explicarlo. Si el sistema algorítmico o una IA fija la jornada, reparte tareas o calcula salarios, la empresa debe, además de avisarlo a los empleados afectados, explicar "las pautas, criterios y reglas de funcionamiento" del algoritmo para que el empleado sepa cómo afectan las distintas variables a sus condiciones laborales. Lo mismo se aplica para aquellas empresas que utilizan algoritmos para decidir quién asciende, en qué puesto trabaja o qué factores le convierten en candidato a un hipotético despido.
El objetivo es que el empleado sepa cómo afectan todas las variables del entorno laboral a su puesto de trabajo y así evitar sorpresas o discriminaciones. La información sobre el funcionamiento debe llegarle por escrito antes de comenzar a trabajar, en el contrato o en un documento aparte que el SEPE ya ofrece en su portal con el título de Documento informativo sobre los elementos esenciales del contrato de trabajo.
Una idea con nuevo destinatario. La normativa que entra hoy en vigor no es la única que cuenta con una cláusula que legisla sobre la transparencia de los algoritmos laborales en España. La Ley Rider ya daba al comité de empresa el derecho a conocer los "parámetros, reglas e instrucciones" de los algoritmos que afectan al puesto de trabajo de los empleados.
Aquella norma se aprobó con las plataformas de reparto de última milla en el punto de mira. El RGPD, el Reglamento de IA de la Unión Europea e incluso el artículo 64.4.d del Estatuto de los Trabajadores ya reconocía el derecho de los trabajadores de saber qué reglas, parámetros e instrucciones guiaban las decisiones del algoritmo, pero la nueva normativa le añade una nueva capa reconociendo el derecho individual a conocer esos detalles, no de carácter colectivo o en supuestos de algo riesgo, como especificaban las anteriores normativas.
El miedo a la caja negra. La hemeroteca nos da una explicación bastante clara del porqué de esta imposición de la Unión Europea a revelar qué tiene en cuenta el algoritmo para decidir sobre las condiciones laborales de los empleados. Según publicaba Reuters, Amazon descubrió en 2015 que su sistema de selección de personal no juzgaba igual a hombres y mujeres. Penalizaba los currículums con la palabra "femenino" y bajaba la nota a las graduadas de universidades solo para mujeres.
En Italia, el Garante de protección de datos sancionó con 5 millones de euros a Foodinho, filial de Glovo, porque había tratado de forma ilícita los datos de más de 35.000 repartidores. Entre los reproches que surgieron se hacía mención a las decisiones automáticas que los trabajadores no podían discutir porque no las había tomado una persona.
Lo que no te van a dar. De la misma forma que la normativa de transparencia salarial no publica salarios de personas concretas dentro de las empresas, sino que se hacen públicos los rangos salariales para un determinado puesto y experiencia, las empresas no tienen que hacer público el código de sus algoritmos. La normativa habla de pautas y criterios.
En declaraciones a ABC, Jonatan Amenedo, CEO de Welpay, lo confirmaba: "Nadie está obligado a entregar su modelo". Aunque sí deben ser suficiente para entender en qué criterios se basa la decisión y poder rebatirla. Tal y como dejaron muy claro compañías como Glovo durante la entrada en vigor de la Ley Rider, hacer públicos los entresijos de sus algoritmos podrían hacer que las empresas perdieran competitividad.

articles.title: OpenAI will show visual ads in ChatGPT while you generate images
articles.text:
OpenAI is expanding ads in ChatGPT, and one of the first new formats will show visual ads while you're generating images.
The company says it will begin testing the new ad format later this month in the U.S. with an initial group of advertisers.
According to OpenAI, these ads could use images to show product inspiration, how a product is used, or experiences associated with a service, which gives advertisers a more visual way to promote themselves inside ChatGPT.
"Initially, we'll test this new ad format during image generation in ChatGPT. Ads will be clearly labeled, and remain separate from the image being created," OpenAI explained.
OpenAI also reiterated that ads do not influence ChatGPT's answers.
The company says ChatGPT now reaches 1.2 billion people every week, and advertising is becoming another way for OpenAI to make money from users who may not pay for a subscription.
OpenAI is also getting more serious about measuring ChatGPT ads
Alongside the new visual format, OpenAI is adding more tools that allow advertisers to measure whether ChatGPT ads actually lead to purchases or other conversions.
It's integrating with Hightouch, Tealium, and LiveRamp for conversion data, while attribution partners now include AppsFlyer, Adjust, Branch, Triple Whale, Kochava, and several others.
OpenAI is also working with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science on brand suitability, which is particularly important for ChatGPT because ads appear around conversations rather than a traditional webpage.
The company says its safeguards are designed to prevent ads from appearing in emotionally vulnerable, sensitive, or otherwise unsuitable conversations.
OpenAI also says these independent partners will not get access to private user conversations while evaluating whether its advertising safeguards are working as intended.
For now, the visual ad experiment is limited to the U.S., but OpenAI clearly sees ads becoming a much larger part of ChatGPT as it tries to monetize its 1.2 billion weekly users.

Prime Day – Le téléviseur TCL 75C79K à 719,00 € (-22%)
Le téléviseur TCL 75C79K passe sous les 750 € chez Amazon Prime soit une baisse d'environ 22% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Le TCL 75C79K est un téléviseur Mini-Led 4K 144 Hz qui offre une alternative un peu moins onéreuse que l'excellent C89K. Il profite d'une bonne luminosité, de bon contrastes et de toutes les applications de Google TV.

- Consommation maîtrisée.

Points faibles

Grâce à son large choix de diagonales et son tarif attractif, il représente une alternative solide pour qui cherche un écran performant sans viser le très haut de gamme.

articles.title: Fuite de données à l'ANSSI : une enquête est ouverte
articles.text:
La semaine dernière, on a appris que l’Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d’information (Anssi) a été, à son tour, victime d’une cyberattaque. L’agence, chargée justement de lutter contre les attaques informatiques en France, a enregistré une fuite de données. Aux origines de l’offensive, on trouve une faille découverte cet été dans Metabase, le logiciel qui sert à analyser des données et à créer des tableaux de bord.
Dans la foulée, la Direction interministérielle du numérique (Dinum), le service de l’État français chargé de la transformation numérique et de la transmission de données entre organismes publics, a également été piratée en exploitant la même vulnérabilité.
À lire aussi : Cyberattaque contre la Région Hauts-de-France – les RIB de 700 000 Français compromis
Le parquet de Paris ouvre une enquête
Peu après l’annonce de l’ANSSI, le parquet de Paris a annoncé l’ouverture d’une enquête sur l’incident. Les investigations, menées par la section cybercriminalité du parquet de Paris, se portent sur des faits « d’accès, maintien et extraction des données d’un système de traitement automatisé de données mis en œuvre par l’État ». L’enquête doit évidemment permettre de mieux comprendre ce qu’il s’est passé, et de remonter jusqu’aux pirates à l’origine de la cyberattaque.
Dans le cadre de cette enquête, les enquêteurs vont vraisemblablement analyser les traces techniques laissées par les hackers, comme les journaux de connexion ou les adresses IP par exemple. Des responsables de l’ANSSI vont probablement aussi être entendus par les autorités.
La révélation de l’ANSSI fait partie du premier bilan de l’opération REACTIV. Cette équipe d’intervention d’urgence, mise sur pied à la demande du Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, a permis de lever le voile sur 99 fuites de données présumées dans les services de l’État depuis début août. Parmi les vulnérabilités dénichées par les agents, on trouve la faille de Metabase qui a abouti à la fuite de données de l’ANSSI.

articles.title: B&YOU glisse Amazon Prime ou Deezer dans ses forfaits mobiles, et le prix a de quoi surprendre
articles.text:
Bouygues Telecom lance deux nouveaux forfaits mobiles sans engagement B&YOU qui intègrent Amazon Prime ou Deezer Premium, dès 17,99 euros par mois. Ils rejoignent ainsi le Pack beIN SPORTS au sein d'une gamme baptisée Les Packs.
Depuis ce lundi 5 octobre, Bouygues Telecom propose deux nouveaux forfaits mobiles B&YOU sans engagement qui incluent directement un abonnement à Amazon Prime ou à Deezer Premium. Facturés respectivement 17,99 et 19,99 euros par mois, ils comprennent 170 Go de data en 5G et rejoignent le Pack beIN SPORTS lancé en juin, construit sur le même modèle. L'opérateur affirme être le premier à proposer ce type d'offre, une revendication discutable, et les conditions de souscription comportent plusieurs points à connaître avant de se lancer.
Amazon Prime et Deezer s'invitent dans les forfaits mobiles B&YOU
Les trois Packs désormais proposés par B&YOU partagent exactement le même forfait mobile. Chacun offre une enveloppe de 170 Go d'internet mobile en 5G par mois, dont 60 Go utilisables lors d'un séjour en Europe ou dans les DOM, ainsi que les appels, SMS et MMS illimités en France métropolitaine. Seul le service inclus change d'un Pack à l'autre, et il n'y a rien à souscrire ni à payer à part. L'abonnement est compris dans le prix du forfait, figure sur la même facture et s'utilise aussi bien sur le téléphone que sur les autres écrans. Pour démarrer, comptez 1 euro pour la carte SIM et 1 euro de frais d'activation, prélevé une seule fois sur la première facture. Et si l'on décide de partir, la résiliation coûte 5 euros, comme pour le reste de la gamme B&YOU.
Le Pack Amazon Prime, disponible dès aujourd'hui, ouvre le bal à 17,99 euros par mois, ce qui en fait le moins cher du trio. Le forfait embarque les avantages habituels de l'abonnement, à commencer par la livraison Premium gratuite sur des millions d'articles éligibles. On peut évidemment y ajouter les films et séries de Prime Video, dont les productions Amazon Originals, des offres réservées aux membres et un accès anticipé aux Ventes Flash sur la partie e-commerce. Les adeptes du clic du dimanche soir apprécieront.
Le Pack Deezer, à 19,99 euros, parle davantage aux amateurs de musique, proposée en illimité et en meilleure qualité, avec des recommandations signées à la fois par l'algorithme et par les experts de la plateforme. Ceux qui arrivent d'un autre service peuvent transférer leur ancienne bibliothèque en quelques clics, et le pack promet en prime des événements exclusifs et des places de concert à gagner. Lancé au mois de juin, le Pack beIN SPORTS donne quant à lui accès à la chaîne sportive sur tous les écrans, de la TV connectée au smartphone, ainsi qu'à plus de 180 chaînes via l'application b.tv, utilisable sur deux écrans en simultané au maximum. Son tarif a été fixé à 24,99 euros par mois.
Un forfait packagé vraiment malin, ou simplement bien emballé ?
Bouygues Telecom présente Les Packs comme une nouvelle catégorie d'offres et se décrit comme le premier opérateur à loger un service numérique au cœur du forfait mobile. Une primauté qui souffre d'un petit bémol toutefois puisque dès 2010, Orange incluait Deezer Premium dans son forfait Origami Style. Marc Laurier, le directeur marketing grand public de Bouygues Telecom, salue dans tous les cas, et il a raison de le faire, « une nouvelle étape » pour B&YOU, la marque dite à bas prix de l'opérateur. Ce dernier justifie le lancement de ses forfaits par le fait que 86 % des clients dits « digitaux autonomes » possèdent un abonnement SVOD, 31 % un service de streaming musical, et 52 % regardent ou écoutent chaque jour vidéos, TV ou musique sur leur mobile, selon une étude IPSOS datant de 2024.
Quoi qu'il en soit, est-ce une bonne affaire ? Dans la gamme B&YOU, le 200 Go Voyage, présenté comme le forfait du moment, s'affiche à 15,99 euros. Face à lui, le Pack Amazon Prime revient à s'offrir l'abonnement pour environ 2 euros de plus par mois, avec 30 Go de moins en France et 60 Go d'itinérance en Europe et dans les DOM, contre 40 Go valables dans plus de 160 destinations. Pour Deezer, l'écart monte à 4 euros. Pour qui paie déjà l'un de ces services à côté, il faudra bien calculer.
Attention toutefois aux petites lignes. Le service inclus disparaît en cas de résiliation du forfait, mais aussi au moindre changement d'offre, même vers un autre forfait B&YOU. Les Packs sont réservés à une première souscription, pour une nouvelle ligne ouverte sur bouyguestelecom.fr, et une fois l'enveloppe épuisée, l'internet mobile ainsi que les MMS hors France métropolitaine sont facturés aux tarifs en vigueur. Quant aux personnes déjà abonnées à Amazon Prime ou Deezer, l'opérateur évoque des « conditions » renvoyées vers sa FAQ, sans plus de précisions. Mieux vaut donc bien se renseigner avant et bien savoir à quoi vous êtes déjà abonné ou pas.
Et la concurrence, dans tout ça ? D'après nos recherches, ni Orange, ni SFR, ni Free ne proposent aujourd'hui de forfait mobile intégrant durablement un service tiers comme Amazon Prime ou Deezer. Le forfait Free Max mise sur des services maison, avec l'application Free TV+ et ses plus de 300 chaînes, un VPN intégré ou l'option eSIM Watch, et SFR inclut de son côté son propre service SFR TV. Orange et SFR proposent bien Deezer Premium à leurs abonnés mobiles, mais en option payante, avec des promotions ponctuelles (quelques mois offerts ou facturés 1 euro) avant un retour au plein tarif de 11,99 euros par mois. Quant à Netflix, Disney+ ou Prime Video, Free ne les inclut, dans leur version avec publicité, qu'avec sa Freebox Ultra, et non avec un forfait mobile seul.

articles.title: Supercharge regulated workloads with Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Supercharge regulated workloads with Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock
Please note that the following post is intended for informational purposes only. The approach detailed below may not be suitable for all organizations or compliance programs. It is important to evaluate this potential solution against the compliance requirements of your organization and any applicable regulatory obligations you may have.
The availability of Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions introduces an on-ramp for AI-assisted development for workloads with regulatory or compliance requirements, including International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Claude Sonnet 5 holds FedRAMP Class D (formerly High) certification and DoD Impact Level 4 and 5 (IL4/IL5) authorization, and Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 hold FedRAMP Class D certification on Amazon Bedrock (verify current model certification status).
In this post, we explore how to use these models on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US) with Claude Code, Anthropic’s agentic coding tool. With this solution, you can run AI-assisted workflows that speed up everyday development tasks while maintaining compliance alignment.
Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
AWS GovCloud (US) Regions are designed specifically for US customers with elevated compliance needs. You can deploy generative AI workloads to sensitive environments while maintaining compliance controls. Amazon Bedrock is built with security-focused features, including:
Built-in data protection where customer content isn’t stored, logged, or used to train AWS models or shared with third parties.
FedRAMP Class D (formerly High) certification and DoD Cloud Service Provider (CSP) SRG IL4/IL5 authorization pathways, supporting government agencies’ compliance requirements. See the Amazon Bedrock models compliance page for current model-level certification status.
Integration with existing security controls and compliance frameworks available in AWS GovCloud (US), maintaining the same high security standards as other AWS Regions while providing additional authorization pathways.
Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US) supports two endpoint surfaces, bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle, both powered by the same underlying Mantle inference engine with Zero Operator Access (ZOA) architecture. The bedrock-runtime endpoint uses the AWS SDK (InvokeModel and Converse APIs) and supports Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Agents, and invocation logging. This makes it the recommended choice for most new applications, particularly those requiring audit trails. The bedrock-mantle endpoint supports the Anthropic Messages API natively and provides access to capabilities currently available only on that surface, such as server-side tools, background inference, and Projects. Both endpoints are available for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5, with bedrock-runtime available in both AWS GovCloud (US) Regions (US-West and US-East) and bedrock-mantle available in AWS GovCloud (US-West).
Claude Code
Claude Code is Anthropic’s agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools. Powered by models such as Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US), it operates directly in your terminal, your preferred integrated development environments (IDEs) such as VS Code and JetBrains, and in the background with the Claude Agent SDK. Claude Code understands your entire codebase and can work across multiple files and tools to get things done. Claude Code can:
- Write code and fix bugs spanning multiple files across your codebase.
- Answer questions about your code’s architecture and logic.
- Execute and fix tests, linting, and other commands.
- Search through Git history, resolve merge conflicts, and create commits and pull requests.
- Connect to external tools and data sources with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), including the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), Terraform, and Kubernetes.
- Spawn sub-agents that work on different parts of a task simultaneously.
- Customize behavior with CLAUDE.md memory files, skills for repeatable workflows, and hooks for pre/post-action automation.
- Automate recurring tasks and integrate with continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) through GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD.
To learn more, see Anthropic’s articles: Claude Code tutorials and Claude Code: Best practices for agentic coding.
Solution overview: Try Claude Code with Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
This section provides step-by-step instructions for setting up and configuring Claude Code to work with Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US), including prerequisites, installation commands, environment configuration, and verification steps.
Prerequisites
Before you get started, make sure that you have the following in place:
- An AWS GovCloud (US) account with access to Amazon Bedrock.
- Appropriate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and permissions for Amazon Bedrock. At minimum, your IAM policy should include: 
         
  - For bedrock-runtime: bedrock:InvokeModel, bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream, bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles, and bedrock:GetInferenceProfile.
  - For bedrock-mantle (if using the Mantle endpoint): bedrock-mantle:CreateInference, bedrock-mantle:GetProject, bedrock-mantle:ListProjects, and bedrock-mantle:ListModels.
  - Alternatively, attach the AmazonBedrockMantleInferenceAccess managed policy.
- Amazon Bedrock model access to Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5 enabled in your AWS GovCloud (US) account.
- AWS CLI configured with valid AWS session credentials using short-term API keys or AWS SSO login.
Set up Claude Code with Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
After configuring AWS CLI with your credentials, install Claude Code using one of the following methods:
macOS, Linux, WSL:
Windows PowerShell:
Windows CMD:
Homebrew (macOS/Linux):
For additional installation methods, see Claude Code installation docs.
Option A: Interactive setup wizard (recommended)
- Navigate to your project:
- Launch Claude Code:
- Run through the login wizard:
At the login prompt, select 3rd-party platform, then Amazon Bedrock. Follow the wizard prompts to choose your authentication method, region (us-gov-west-1), and pin your models. The wizard saves configuration to your settings file automatically.
If you have previously configured Claude Code, run /setup-bedrock to reopen the wizard and update your credentials, region, or model pins.
Option B: Manual environment variable configuration
For scripted or enterprise deployments, set the following environment variables:
To use Claude Opus 5.5 as the primary model instead:
To pin specific model versions for consistent team deployments:
Then navigate to your project and launch Claude Code:
Option C: Using the Bedrock Mantle endpoint
Bedrock Mantle supports the Anthropic Messages API natively and is available in AWS GovCloud (US-West). To route Claude Code through Mantle:
When both bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle are needed in the same session:
Note: Guardrails and invocation logging are available exclusively through the bedrock-runtime endpoint. For deployments requiring these compliance features, use the bedrock-runtime endpoint (Option A or B).
Verify your configuration
Verify that Claude Code is running by checking for the Welcome to Claude Code! message in your terminal. Run the /status command to confirm your model and provider. The provider line should show Amazon Bedrock or Amazon Bedrock (Mantle) depending on your configuration.
To learn more about configuring Claude Code for Amazon Bedrock, see Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock.
Considerations when deploying Claude Code to your organization
With Claude Code now generally available, the next step is deciding how to deploy it across your organization. Consider your foundational architecture for security, governance, and compliance:
Use AWS IAM Identity Center to centrally govern identity and access to Claude Code. This verifies that only authorized developers have access. Additionally, using IAM Identity Center, developers can access resources with temporary, role-based credentials, alleviating the need for static access keys and helping enhance security. Prior to opening Claude Code, make sure that you configure AWS CLI to use an IAM Identity Center profile by using aws configure sso --profile <PROFILE_NAME>. Then log in using the profile you created: aws sso login --profile <PROFILE_NAME>.
Consider automated configuration of default environment variables. This includes the environment variables outlined in this post, such as AWS_REGION, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL. This will configure Claude Code to automatically connect to Amazon Bedrock, providing a consistent baseline for development across teams. Organizations can start by providing developers with self-service instructions, or use settings files to manage configuration centrally.
Consider implementing Guidance for Claude Code with Amazon Bedrock for large enterprise deployments. The guidance helps organizations deploy Claude Code while maintaining strict control over AI resource access, connecting to existing identity infrastructure and providing observability for developer productivity and usage patterns.
Review service quotas and set appropriate tokens per minute (TPM) and requests per minute (RPM) based on the number of active developers. Make sure that you have enough TPM and RPM quotas to support your team’s usage. For guidance, follow the rate limit recommendations.
Pin model versions for consistent team deployments. Without pinning, model aliases such as sonnet and opus resolve to Claude Code’s built-in defaults, which may change between releases. Claude Code defaults to Claude Opus 5.5 as its primary model, so an unpinned deployment is billed at the Opus per-token rate. To keep teams on Claude Sonnet 5.5, set ANTHROPIC_MODEL to its full model ID. Use ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL to control when your team moves to a new model. In AWS GovCloud (US), use the us-gov. prefix for cross-region inference profile IDs.
Implement cost monitoring and per-user token guardrails. Claude Code sessions can be token-intensive, particularly with Claude Opus 5.5, which carries a higher per-token cost than Claude Sonnet 5.5. According to Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 completes tasks using fewer tokens than Claude Opus 5, at a lower price per token. Consider the following:
- Implement per-user token guardrails to enforce daily token limits per developer, with alerting at 80% and 100% thresholds. This pattern uses Amazon CloudWatch invocation logging, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB to track and enforce limits in near real time.
- Use prompt caching to reduce costs and improve response times. Both 5-minute and 1-hour TTL options are available for supported models.
- Consider defaulting teams to Claude Sonnet 5.5 (lower cost than Claude Opus 5.5) and reserving Claude Opus 5.5 for tasks requiring deeper reasoning or longer autonomous runs. For workloads that require IL4/IL5 authorization, default to Claude Sonnet 5.
See the Claude Code Monitoring Implementation guide for additional observability patterns.
Consider permissions, memory, and MCP servers for your organization. Security teams can configure managed permissions for what Claude Code is and is not allowed to do, which cannot be overwritten by local configuration. In addition, you can configure CLAUDE.md memory files across projects to auto-add common workflows, style conventions, and coding standards to align with your organization’s preferences. Deploy your CLAUDE.md file into an enterprise directory so all developers inherit the same baseline. Use hooks to enforce pre/post-action automation such as auto-formatting or lint checks.
Choose the appropriate endpoint for your compliance requirements. The bedrock-runtime endpoint supports Guardrails, invocation logging, and cross-region inference within both AWS GovCloud (US) Regions (US-West and US-East). The bedrock-mantle endpoint supports the Anthropic Messages API natively and is available in AWS GovCloud (US-West). Guardrails and invocation logging are exclusive to bedrock-runtime today, so for deployments requiring comprehensive audit trails and content filtering, bedrock-runtime is recommended.
Conduct a thorough security assessment before deployment. Evaluate Claude Code’s capabilities against your organization’s security policies. Amazon Bedrock secures the inference layer, but Claude Code runs on local developer machines and requires separate evaluation and risk management. Apply controls such as managed permissions, invocation logging, and per-user token limits, as you would for other third-party software running in your environment.
Conclusion
The availability of Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US) provides organizations with a compliance-aligned path to AI-assisted development for regulated workloads. Claude Sonnet 5, with FedRAMP Class D (formerly High) certification and DoD IL4/IL5 authorization, offers the strongest compliance coverage for sensitive environments. Claude Sonnet 5.5, with FedRAMP Class D certification, is a step up from Claude Sonnet 5 on coding and knowledge work at a lower cost per task. Claude Opus 5.5, with FedRAMP Class D certification, brings deeper reasoning and longer autonomous task capabilities for workloads where that certification level is sufficient.
Combined with Claude Code, teams can adopt agentic coding workflows directly in their terminal, IDE, or CI/CD pipelines while data remains within AWS GovCloud (US) infrastructure. Whether you choose the bedrock-runtime endpoint for full Guardrails and logging support, or the bedrock-mantle endpoint for native Anthropic Messages API access, you can tailor the deployment to your organization’s compliance and operational requirements.

articles.title: Le jeu de course Star Wars Galactic Racer est déjà en promotion à un jour de sa sortie
articles.text:
Vous n’avez jamais vraiment fait le deuil de Burnout ou de Need for Speed ? Star Wars: Galactic Racer sort le 6 octobre sur PS5, Xbox Series et PC, et il est déjà proposé à 44,99 € sur Amazon, soit près de 20 € de moins que son prix de lancement de 59,99 €.
Un jeu de course signé par d’anciens de Criterion
Star Wars: Galactic Racer est développé par Fuse Games, un studio britannique créé en 2023, avec Lucasfilm Games, et édité par Secret Mode. Son équipe compte d’anciens de Criterion, le studio derrière Burnout et plusieurs Need for Speed. Cela ne fait pas de Galactic Racer un successeur officiel de ces séries, mais l’ambiance arcade, elle, est bien là.
Galactic Racer reprend les takedowns, ces éliminations obtenues en provoquant l’accident d’un concurrent. Dépasser proprement reste une possibilité, mais un adversaire un peu trop encombrant peut aussi finir contre un obstacle à éliminer. C’est précisément ce mélange de pilotage et d’agressivité qui devrait parler aux nostalgiques. Sebulba, le rival d’Anakin dans La Menace fantôme, aurait apprécié
L’histoire se déroule après la chute de l’Empire, dans la Galactic League, un circuit clandestin de la Bordure Extérieure où des syndicats sponsorisent les pilotes. La campagne fonctionne par « runs », à la manière d’un roguelite, et le jeu propose aussi des modes Scénario et Arcade, ainsi que des courses en ligne jusqu’à 12 pilotes, avec cross-play entre les plateformes. Le jeu est conçu avec l’Unreal Engine 5 et les décors font saliver.
Faut-il acheter Star Wars: Galactic Racer ?
Si vous trouvez Forza Horizon 6 un peu trop lisse, voilà de quoi reprendre de mauvaises habitudes de conduite. Avec sa campagne, ses modes Arcade et Scénario et son multijoueur, Galactic Racer semble avoir de quoi nous occuper. Les pièces à combiner pour bricoler son speeder pourraient aussi prolonger le plaisir : trouver un « build » efficace à utiliser en ligne, puis en essayer un autre, c’est une bonne raison de s’y pencher. À prix réduit, la tentation est là.

articles.title: Si votre téléphone Pixel plante et lag, vous feriez peut-être bien d’installer GrapheneOS — Frandroid
articles.text:
Il n’est pas rare que des mises à jour logicielles apportent, en plus des correctifs prévus, quelques problèmes inattendus. C’est notamment le cas pour la dernière mise à jour déployée sur les Pixel de Google. Android 17 QPR1 contient un bug qui provoque des ralentissements et des problèmes de réactivité sur certains mobiles made in Google.
Fait inédit cependant, la découverte de ce bug n’est pas à mettre au crédit de Google, mais des équipes derrière la ROM alternative GrapheneOS note Android Authority. Selon un long fil de messages postés sur les réseaux sociaux, le problème viendrait bien du code source d’Android 17, mais Google ne serait pas bien pressé de déployer un correctif. Contrairement à GrapheneOS, qui a déjà réglé le souci.
Pas de patch avant décembre ?
De manière parfaitement anecdotique, l’auteur de ces lignes peut témoigner que la mise à jour de mi-septembre a bien mis son Pixel 8 sous GrapheneOS à genoux avant que le correctif de début octobre ne vienne remettre tout en ordre. Il semblerait, par contre, que les utilisateurs et utilisatrices de l’Android de Google n’aient pas la même chance.
« Google met de plus en plus de temps à développer et déployer des correctifs pour les versions majeures d’Android », déplorent les équipes de GrapheneOS. « Google prend généralement quatre à six semaines pour déployer un correctif, même pour le plus sévère des problèmes touchant une version majeure d’Android. » Pour les mises à jour mineures, cela peut même prendre deux à trois mois, selon GrapheneOS. Selon le collectif, il ne faut donc pas s’attendre à trouver un patch salvateur avant décembre 2026 sans doute.
Le problème ne se situerait pas dans l’identification et la correction du problème, mais plutôt dans les processus de tests « complètement défaillants », affirme l’équipe de développement derrière l’OS ultra-sécurisé.
Une meilleure expérience sur GrapheneOS ?
Résultat, sur le papier, une version gratuite et alternative d’Android maintenue par une équipe de taille minime fait mieux que l’OS officiel de Google. « Nous devons désormais élargir notre champ d’action pour inclure la gestion des mises à jour de base », peste encore l’équipe de développement de GrapheneOS tout en expliquant que « nos ressources augmentent rapidement et nous saurons nous en charger. »
    Pour aller plus loin
Nouvelles applications, prise en charge du RCS, copier-coller amélioré : GrapheneOS va enfin se faire plus accueillant
            
La comparaison est cependant à prendre avec des pincettes, puisque les changements opérés par Google ont souvent la lourde tâche de fonctionner sur des millions de modèles de téléphones différents, alors que GrapheneOS ne fait que récupérer le code et l’améliorer pour ses Pixel. Reste que certains aspects de l’expérience sur un smartphone Google sont plus réussis sur un OS dégooglé. Un comble.

Regulation
In South Africa, serial spam callers could face up to 1 year in jail
Spam calling is a tricky cold outreach tactic. Get it right, and you may be lucky enough to win your business’s next customer. Get it wrong, and you can turn a stranger into an enemy. Now, the South African government wants to make it harder for businesses to use unsolicited calls.
Explain like I’m new here: South Africans have been dealing with spam calls from random numbers that interrupt their day, often with a salesperson on the other end. In 2019, a report found that South Africans received about 25 spam calls monthly, among the highest in Africa. The government had already tried to tackle the problem: South Africa’s Consumer Protection Act provided for an exclusion register as far back as 2011, while its data protection law later introduced rules restricting unsolicited electronic marketing.
State of play: But things got worse. In H1 2026, Truecaller, a call identity platform, said South Africans recorded 17.47 billion spam calls. Now, the regulators want to grow more teeth. New draft guidelines from the National Consumer Commission (NCC), the country’s consumer protection watchdog, say repeat or serious violations could lead to criminal prosecution, with offenders facing fines or up to 12 months in prison.
A year in prison for a spam call may sound excessive until you look at what the rule is trying to change. Most anti-spam systems put the work on the consumer. Block the number. Report it. Register your number on a do-not-call list. Download an app. When another number appears, do it all again.
Between the lines: South Africa’s proposal is now shifting some of that work to the businesses making the calls. Before sending out a marketing campaign, they would have to check their lists against the country’s opt-out registry—which businesses must register to use—and remove consumers who have opted out of receiving those calls. The registry would then charge R0.12 ($0.0072) per name check and return a cleaned list that remains valid for 30 days.
Zoom out: South Africa has had rules against unwanted marketing for years, with fines, but little has changed. Businesses were okay paying fines if the commercial gains outweighed the risks. A jail term is a more serious threat; it remains to be seen how often the government will actually enforce it and whether marketers comply.
Every business owner needs to watch this.
Ask a computer to add 0.1 and 0.2. It won’t give you 0.3. Now imagine that happening to your money, thousands of times a day. Fincra’s Engineering Lead breaks down why and how fintechs design around it. Watch the full breakdown.
Telecoms
Ghana awards 5G network licences to MTN Ghana and Telecel
In 2024, Ghana tried to make 5G a shared infrastructure project. It planned for one state-backed company to build and run the network, while private telecom operators would rent it and offer the service to customers. Two years into that plan, the rollout is falling below expectations. The country wanted to build 4,400 sites to reach 37 million customers by 2028. But as of March 2026, only 49 5G sites existed—about 43 in Greater Accra—leaving most Ghanaian telecom users without a 5G network to brag about. So, the government dropped the exclusivity and changed course.
What’s new? On October 2, Ghana awarded 5G spectrum and licences to MTN Ghana, the country’s largest telecom firm, and Telecel Ghana, the other major network operator, allowing both companies to build and operate their own 5G networks.
Explain like I’m new here: Ghana’s original 5G plan was centred on a single network that multiple telecom operators could use. Instead of MTN and Telecel each building their own 5G infrastructure, a state-backed company called Next-Gen InfraCo (NGIC) would build the network and lease capacity to them. The idea was to avoid duplicating expensive infrastructure while getting 5G to more people.
The Ghanaian government backed NGIC, with Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries involved through Radisys, which was selected to provide the network infrastructure. Ghana’s 1,200-site 2027 target was at risk due to slow progress. Now, the country has conceded to private operators building and running their own 5G networks.
What happens now? Telecel plans to launch its service in December on its own network. MTN Ghana secured spectrum in the different bands, paying about $100 million for each 15-year licence. For customers, having two major operators building their own 5G networks could mean more 5G coverage, more network capacity and less dependence on a single infrastructure provider. It could also give MTN and Telecel more control over how quickly they expand capacity in areas where customers use more data, underscoring the commercial benefits.
Zoom out: The move could leave Ghana with two major 5G networks, while giving private operators more control over the rollout. The government’s original model was meant to prevent that, keeping the telecom infrastructure under Ghanaian control. It is not clear yet whether giving MTN and Telecel their own networks will produce faster coverage, but both operators already have larger infrastructure footprints and investment plans. NGIC’s existing 5G sites are not being scrapped, either; it keeps its licence and spectrum rights, though it no longer has exclusive control of wholesale 5G infrastructure.

True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. Join us on October 28 & 29, 2026. Get your ticket.
AI
Ghana will centrally review all government AI purchases
Ghana does not want government agencies buying AI tools however they please. The country will now centrally review every AI system the public sector acquires, checking what happens to government data, whether different systems can work together, and whether Ghanaian workers can eventually operate the technology without depending permanently on its supplier.
Explain like I’m new here: Government technology contracts can last years. Once an agency builds its operations and data around one company’s software, switching providers can become expensive and difficult. This is called vendor lock-in. With AI, the stakes are higher because systems can process sensitive government and citizen data.
Under the new rules, Ghana’s Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations will coordinate requirements, while the National Information Technology Agency (NITA) will assess proposed systems for cybersecurity, data protection, interoperability, sustainability, and local skills transfer.
Why now? Ghana is preparing to spend heavily on AI infrastructure. Its ten-year National AI Strategy includes a planned $250 million AI Compute Centre and upgrades to the National Data Centre. Centralising procurement standards aims to set the rules before ministries start building separate AI systems that are difficult to connect later.
Between the lines: Ghana is using government procurement as industrial policy. Requiring skills transfer means a foreign company cannot simply sell software and leave Ghana dependent on it. Requiring interoperability makes it harder for one supplier to become indispensable.
Why this matters: Governments are potentially among the biggest early buyers of AI in African markets. Whoever supplies those systems could shape how public-sector AI develops for years. Ghana is trying to keep that relationship on its terms: foreign technology can come in, but control over public data, technical knowledge, and the ability to change suppliers should remain at home.
Banking
South Africans are replacing ATMs with supermarket tills
South Africans are finding a cheaper place to withdraw cash: the supermarket checkout. Retail tills now process about R326 billion ($19.6 billion) in cash-back withdrawals every year, across 663 million transactions, according to the South African Reserve Bank (SARB).
Explain like I’m new here: Instead of visiting an automated teller machine (ATM) to withdraw cash, a shopper can pay at a supermarket till and ask for extra cash. For shoppers, this pattern is also relatively cheaper. The SARB found the average withdrawal at tills to be R492 ($30). Processing R100 ($6) this way costs about 12 cents ($0.0072) compared with 68 cents ($0.041) through an ATM and R1.53 ($0.092) at a bank branch.
State of play: South Africa’s roughly 30,600 ATMs cost about R307,590 ($18,500) each to operate annually. Consumers then bear another cost: R17.7 billion ($1.1 billion) in withdrawal fees every year, plus billions more travelling to and queuing at cash points. Noticing the trend, several major South African banks have been reducing their ATM footprint.
Between the lines: Retailers also have one big advantage. They already handle large amounts of cash from shoppers every day. Instead of paying to transport that cash back to a bank, some of it can be handed directly to customers making withdrawals at the till. This keeps cash circulating while cutting the cost of transporting, storing, and eventually loading it into ATMs.
Nigeria saw a more extreme version of this during its 2023 cash crunch. As ATMs ran dry and bank withdrawals became difficult, cash-heavy businesses and point-of-sale (PoS) agents became alternative sources of physical money, often charging customers a premium to withdraw scarce notes. South Africa is not facing the same shortage, but the underlying lesson is similar. When accessing cash through banks becomes costly or inconvenient, businesses that already handle cash can become part of the distribution network.
Zoom out: Banks spent decades making ATMs the bridge between customers and physical cash. South Africa’s retailers are now deciding that alternative routes work better for them. If cash-back expands further, especially into informal retail, the future of cash access may depend heavily on how effectively these existing shops can double as neighbourhood cash points.

articles.title: Funcionários da Comissão Europeia criticam alternativa ao Microsoft Teams • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Funcionários da Comissão Europeia criticam alternativa ao Microsoft Teams
Comissão Europeia adotou Element Pro como opção de "backup" ao Microsoft Teams para reduzir dependência de tecnologias dos EUA.
A Comissão Europeia implementou uma ferramenta de nome Element Pro como alternativa ao Microsoft Teams. A medida faz parte de um plano de soberania digital que visa tornar a União Europeia menos dependente de tecnologias americanas. Só há um problema: a novidade tem sido fortemente criticada por funcionários da entidade.
Oriundo da Element, uma empresa com sede no Reino Unido, o Element Pro é uma solução de comunicação que inclui mensagens instantâneas, chamadas de voz ou vídeo, compartilhamento de arquivos e afins. Trata-se, de fato, de uma ferramenta que concorre com o Microsoft Teams, com o diferencial de permitir que a organização que a adota a hospede em servidores próprios.
Mas o site Politico constatou que funcionários da Comissão Europeia não estão satisfeitos com o Element Pro. O motivo principal aparenta ser uma insatisfação com o desempenho da ferramenta.
Em um fórum interno da Comissão Europeia, que permite postagens anônimas, um funcionário declarou: “eu não entendo o valor agregado disso aqui”. Outro, menos polido, classificou a ferramenta como “uma porcaria completa”. Um terceiro afirmou que, comparando o desempenho do Element Pro com o do Microsoft Teams, os Estados Unidos “venceriam a guerra instantaneamente”.
A julgar pelo tom dos comentários, o número de críticas só não é maior porque, nesta fase inicial, o Element Pro foi implementado como uma solução de “backup”, isto é, uma ferramenta de comunicação que deve ser usada quando o Microsoft Teams ficar indisponível. Este último continua sendo a ferramenta de comunicação padrão da Comissão Europeia.
A União Europeia vem planejando e adotando uma série de medidas para reduzir a sua dependência de tecnologias estrangeiras, especialmente daquelas oriundas dos Estados Unidos. Essa é uma forma de tornar os países do bloco mais tecnologicamente autônomos, reduzindo eventuais transtornos sob circunstâncias de conflito político ou econômico.
Esse movimento envolve tanto medidas locais, como o plano da Dinamarca de substituir o Windows e o Microsoft 365 por soluções abertas, quanto iniciativas que afetam todos ou a maior parte dos países da União Europeia, como é o caso da adoção do Element Pro pela Comissão Europeia.
Apesar das críticas, a Comissão Europeia não deu, até o momento, nenhum sinal de que pretende abandonar a ferramenta. Na verdade, como o Element Pro é executado dentro da infraestrutura tecnológica do próprio órgão, sem depender da nuvem de terceiros, tudo indica que haverá uma persistência sobre o seu uso.
Reforça essa possibilidade o posicionamento do CEO da Element, Matthew Hodgson. Ao Politico, o executivo deu a entender que mudanças de soluções tecnológicas sempre geram alguma resistência e que, portanto, as reações negativas sobre o Element Pro são esperadas: “a mudança é sempre dolorosa, principalmente se partir de um programa muito usado como o Teams”, frisou.
A Comissão Europeia em si não se manifestou sobre o assunto.

articles.title: Humanoid robots pummel YouTuber in cage matches, California tells startup to stop the fights
articles.text:
WTF?! You might think there are plenty of reasons why a real person shouldn't fight a humanoid robot in a cage match, but it happened anyway. The state of California wasn't pleased about this and has now sent a cease-and-desist letter to the robotics startup behind the event, telling it to stop holding these unsanctioned matches.
Last month, YouTuber Frankie LaPenna fought three different robots from REK, including a distinctly Terminator-like machine. At one point, the robot gave LaPenna a brutal kick to the face that sent him into the side of the cage, while another kick to the stomach sent the influencer flying onto his back. A different robot also put LaPenna on the ground with a fast series of punches to the face. It's all a bit concerning, really, though the child-like robot didn't put up much of a fight.
The California State Athletic Commission was also concerned about the event. It sent a cease-and-desist letter on September 30, demanding that REK stop hosting, promoting or sponsoring these fights.
REK CEO Cix Liv proudly shared the letter on X, writing that "we made it boys."
 – CIX 🦾 (@cixliv) September 30, 2026
The letter notes that any boxing or mixed martial arts contest, match, or exhibition, involving any human in the state of California, must first have approval from the California State Athletic Commission.
The letter adds that Business and Professions Codes section 18870 and 18878 make it a misdemeanor to promote or participate in a boxing or martial arts contest, match, or exhibition involving any human without a license.
Liv's unlikely to be too worried about the letter: don't be surprised if the fights simply move to another state or country. The free promotion will probably help, too.
Away from the legal ramifications, the fights illustrate just how quickly humanoid robots are advancing. It wasn't too long ago when a slight push from a human would have sent one of these machines sprawling to the floor and flopping around like a fish out of water. Video of the robots pounding the crap out of LaPenna looks like one of those pre-apocalypse news reports you'd find in an RPG about an AI that destroys the world.
There have been several reports recently about the military investigating use cases for humanoid robots. The US Army just named five companies as winners of the xTechHumanoid competition, which looks at ways these machines can be utilized in future military operations. One of the robots developed by a winner looks like it should be carrying a laser rifle and already has ballistic protection.
More recently, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the creation of a new military command designed to expand the use of autonomous and robotic capabilities across the US armed forces.
It's not just the US, either. China is preparing humanoid robots for combat as it moves them from labs to military training grounds.

articles.title: Dynatrace's $915M Arize deal bets AI agents are just another app to monitor
articles.text:
Dynatrace’s $915M Arize deal bets AI agents are just another app to monitor
Dynatrace closed its $915 million acquisition of Arize on October 1, joining Arize’s tracing and evaluation of AI agents to its own monitoring of the applications and infrastructure underneath them.
It also takes an independent AI observability vendor off the market, one Datadog had invested in.
I sat down with Sean O’Dell, a principal product marketing manager at Dynatrace, on September 25 at the WeAreDevelopers conference in San Jose, five days before the deal closed. Dynatrace was in a quiet period, so he kept his Arize comments general.
When I asked where Dynatrace is headed with Arize, his answer started from the premise that an AI app is still an app. When it breaks, the business needs to know what the outage cost, and the engineers on call need to know why it happened.
“We can ask a question, we can do natural language, we can have fantastic RAGs, we can do evaluations, but at the end of the day, it is an application,” O’Dell said.
Teams need to know whether a response is appropriate, whether it’s hallucinating, and what it cost, he said, and both Dynatrace and Arize already answer those questions. Those AI apps “are still a part of a broader ecosystem of legacy applications, mainframes in many cases,” he said.
Until now, that meant two tools. Arize co-founder Aparna Dhinakaran told The New Stack’s Paul Sawers that teams could debug the AI side in Arize, but a software problem sent them digging through separate traces to find the root cause.
Arize also brings Phoenix, its source-available tool for tracing and testing AI apps, and the developers who use it. O’Dell called that community “hard to find because it’s so early and so new.”
Both companies already have agents that act on the data. Dynatrace’s Bluebox, unveiled in June, reads a team’s code in GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, matches it against production data and proposes a fix, according to O’Dell. “So here is your PR,” O’Dell said. Arize’s Signal does the same for Alyx, Arize’s own AI assistant. Arize accepts roughly 65% to 70% of the pull requests Signal writes, Dhinakaran told The New Stack.
That leaves about a third for a person to catch. O’Dell said a team can step back as “a human out of the loop” on Bluebox’s fixes, but he still tells customers to validate a fix before approving it.
Ops has rarely let automation change production on its own. Back in the ITIL days, he said, an automated change came with “1,500 checks and balances.”
“I don’t trust everything that comes out of my [chatbot] or my agent,” O’Dell said. “So why would you?”
He’s right.

articles.title: Anthropic reports Florida woman’s Claude ‘diary’ threat to shoot up sheriff’s office, felony charge follows — it’s at least the third such conversation to reach police since August
articles.text:
Anthropic reports Florida woman’s Claude ‘diary’ threat to shoot up sheriff’s office, felony charge follows — it’s at least the third such conversation to reach police since August
Investigators say a message the following day mentioned a new gun.
A Lee County, Florida, woman was arrested on a felony charge after a threat linked to an Anthropic Claude AI chatbot conversation, or “diary,” by her account was reported to law enforcement via Anthropic’s human review team, according to WINK News. The arrest report includes a Sept. 26 statement from a user identified as “Carli” saying she would “shoot up” the Lee County Sheriff’s Office (LCSO), and allegedly a message the next day mentioned a new gun. The conversation was at least the third of its type to reach police since August.
Anthropic monitors chats for key phrases and content that could be deemed threatening, the arrest report says, and depending on severity, they can be elevated for human review. In this case, the team decided to report its findings to law enforcement. The Bonita Springs woman was detained at home without incident, and an LCSO intelligence detective took over the case from there. The arrest report is not yet in the court file, but our own check shows court records listing the Sept. 30 felony charge under Florida Statute 836.10: written or electronic threat of a mass shooting or act of terrorism.
No comment from Anthropic on the case is currently on record. Anthropic’s public privacy policy, effective Sept. 10, says that disclosure to law enforcement may occur where it has a good-faith belief “that disclosure is reasonably necessary to … prevent serious harm to any person or to property.” Its government requests report for the latter half of 2025 uses a narrower standard for emergency disclosures, the “danger of death or serious physical injury to a person,” and lists zero emergency requests from law enforcement in that period, though it doesn’t count referrals Anthropic makes on its own.
As booked, the charge is listed as “THREAT-TERRORISTIC-STATE OFFENSES-WRITTEN/ELEC THREAT MASS SHOOTING/TERRORISM ACT,” which covers the mass-shooting/terrorism half of the statute. The conversation with the chatbot may fall under the law as a threat sent, posted, or transmitted “in any manner in which it may be viewed by another person.” The messages found by Anthropic’s human review, including the next-day gun mention, are likely the supporting evidence for the arrest and charge. No attorney is named on the docket, and a public defender was appointed at the time of the charge.
The incident follows a string of recent cases tied to the use of chatbots from Anthropic and rival OpenAI. One incident, in San Antonio, involves Aug. 11 queries in “an Anthropic AI chat” about shooting at a nearby elementary school. The police, alerted by the FBI, arrested a 22-year-old man on a felony terroristic threat charge. Days later, in San Francisco, a user threatened Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in an Aug. 14 Claude chat, saying he had bought an AR-15. Anthropic notified police, but the user ended up not being arrested or charged. Both cases were detailed in regional news reports.
OpenAI has faced similar challenges in Florida over a message in March to its AI chatbot platform, ChatGPT, where user Darren Zhou spoke about killing his ex-girlfriend, and OpenAI reported him to the FBI, according to the Palm Beach Post. Zhou pleaded guilty in August to charges including written threats to kill, under the same statute, 836.10, and was sentenced to eight years’ probation.
The Florida attorney general also filed a lawsuit against the company in June, citing the 2025 Florida State University shooting, and last month asked a judge for a temporary injunction. OpenAI was also sued by British Columbia last month for not warning police about the Tumbler Ridge shooter, whose ChatGPT account, the lawsuit says, it had identified eight months before the attack. These incidents, and more, show a pattern where AI companies are expected to respect privacy while simultaneously being held responsible when they don’t report threats to law enforcement.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The increasing scrutiny on both privacy and security concerns related to AI products has led to calls for caution from experts such as Florida Gulf Coast University’s Chrissann Ruehle, who spoke to WINK News. This comes alongside demands for stricter, independently approved guidelines, such as those requested by Florida’s attorney general.
For users, it’s a reminder that what you share with your favorite AI companion is “never truly anonymous,” as Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno told WINK News. A marked conversation can act as a “diary” to human reviewers, and that can get you in trouble, as the woman identified as “Carli” discovered. More details about the case should be available after the arraignment on Nov. 2.

articles.title: Exploitation Hits Rejetto HFS Vulnerability Discovered by AI
articles.text:
Threat actors are exploiting a critical vulnerability in Rejetto HTTP File Server (HFS) to bypass authentication and gain remote code execution (RCE), VulnCheck warns.
Tracked as CVE-2026-61500 (CVSS score of 9.3), the flaw exists because the open source file server discloses outputs of its non-cryptographic session cookie generator to unauthenticated clients during login. It also derives the session-cookie signing key from the same generator.
The sensitive information leak allows an attacker to reconstruct the generator’s state and recover the signing key using a small set of collected login responses.
Using the recovered key, the attacker can then forge valid administrator session cookies to gain elevated access to the server and RCE via the server_code configuration feature.
The issue was that Rejetto HFS’s generator, Math.random(), was using the xorshift128+ algorithm to generate the ‘random’ value that was then passed to the server’s Node.js web framework Koa for signing session cookies.
Because the algorithm’s outputs are reversible, an attacker able to collect other numbers generated by Math.random() could determine other generated numbers and forge the authentication cookies, cybersecurity firm Horizon3 explained in a technical report.
Horizon3.ai researchers uncovered the flaw using Anthropic’s Mythos AI model, which used advanced mathematical reasoning to recognize that Math.random() PRNG outputs could be reversed to reconstruct the secret session-cookie signing key.
The security firm discovered the weakness in June, and Rejetto HFS version 3.2.1 was released on July 13 with the necessary patches.
“Multiple security vulnerabilities have been found in all previous versions, potentially allowing an attacker to gain administrative access to HFS,” Rejetto noted in its advisory.
On October 2, VulnCheck warned that hackers have begun targeting CVE-2026-61500 as part of small-scale reconnaissance originating from a China Telecom IP. The attempts hit canaries in Japan and the US.

When I reviewed the Sony 1000X The Collexion earlier in 2026, they impressed me in a few key areas. Of course, sound is one of them. I've already spoken about their expansiveness, but they also offer excellent balance across the frequency range, with impactful and dynamic bass output, rich and intricate mids, and expressive treble. If you have LDAC switched on for higher-res streaming — or if you're using a wired connection — The Collexion can also unearth some of the finest details in your favorite tracks, resulting in a highly insightful, engaging listening experience.
Something else that impressed me was their active noise cancellation. Although these headphones have a relatively relaxed fit, they still crush external sounds to impressive effect, and whether I was using them on public transport or just while working in the office, they kept me focused on my tunes with ease. There's also a transparency mode if you want to be more aware of your surroundings, something that you can trigger by placing your hand over the right earcup, or with a simple button press.
I also absolutely loved the look and feel of the Sony 1000X The Collexion.
