articles.title: German startups deepen Ukraine ties over weekend as innovation moves closer to the frontline | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Two German DefenceTech companies used Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s visit to Kyiv this weekend to deepen their links with Ukraine, in a sign of how the country is becoming an increasingly important development and manufacturing base for Europe’s next generation of autonomous defence systems.
As announced on Sunday, Munich-based drone company Quantum Systems is set to have several tens of thousands of interceptor drones financed by Germany under its winter 2026/2027 military assistance package, with the systems to be manufactured in Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Munich-based ARX Robotics and Ukrainian DefenceTech company Roboneers have expanded their existing relationship into a strategic partnership covering the integration and joint development of unmanned ground systems.
The agreements formed part of a broader push during Merz’s 4 October visit to increase German-Ukrainian cooperation in defence technology and production. Germany also announced around €1 billion in additional military assistance during the visit.
Andreas Flodström, co-founder and chairman of Ukraine-fcoused DefenceTech fund Varangians, shared his thoughts: “This aligns closely with how I think Europe should approach defence innovation: mobilising European production capacity while working much more closely with Ukraine on R&D.
“Ukraine has made an extraordinary leap in defence innovation for modern warfare. But to win the war, we also need to mobilise Europe’s industrial and R&D capacity. Structurally, this is an important step, and I hope we will see much more of it.”
Capital moves into defence
The two agreements also come against a substantial increase in capital flowing into German defence technology.
EU-Startups’ 2026 coverage includes more than €1.2 billion in disclosed funding across Quantum Systems and a group of European companies working in adjacent areas such as autonomous systems, drone operations, aerial intelligence, precision guidance and counter-drone technology.
Germany accounts for most of that total: Quantum Systems raised a €1 billion Series D in July, following a separate €150 million financing package in February, while Hannover-based INLEAP Photonics secured €20 million for laser-based drone defence and Berlin-based SPREAD AI raised €25 million to expand engineering software used across defence, aerospace and heavy industry.
EU-Startups has also followed both companies in the current agreements over several years: Quantum Systems previously raised €160 million and a further €180 million in 2025, while ARX Robotics’ funding history includes a €1.15 million pre-Seed round in 2023, a €9 million Seed round in 2024 and a Series A that reached €42 million in 2025.
The figures point to a German DefenceTech ecosystem in which autonomous platforms and the software, sensing and counter-drone technologies around them are attracting increasingly large pools of private capital.
Production shifts closer to the frontline
Founded in 2015, Quantum Systems develops autonomous aerial systems and accompanying software. Its Ukrainian footprint predates the latest order. Quantum Systems opened a production facility in Ukraine in April 2024, later expanding local manufacturing capacity and its Ukrainian workforce. By February 2025, the company said the site employed 80 people and was preparing to increase that number to 120 while producing locally manufactured Vector reconnaissance drones.
The newly announced interceptor programme pushes that localisation considerably further. The drones were developed by Quantum WIY Industries, part of Quantum Systems’ German-Ukrainian network, and are intended to counter increasingly capable Russian attack drones.
Sven Kruck, Co-CEO of Quantum Systems, said: “Ukraine needs interceptor drones at industrial scale. By expanding production in Ukraine, we can respond faster to the immediate threat while building an industrial capability that will also strengthen Germany and its allies.”
A similar development is taking place on the ground. Founded in Munich in 2022 by former Bundeswehr officers Marc Wietfeld, Maximilian Wied and Stefan Roebel, ARX Robotics develops unmanned ground vehicles and Mithra OS, its software platform for connecting and autonomising military vehicles.
Its partnership with Roboneers is also moving beyond supplying equipment into shared production and development.
In June, the two companies created ARX Industries, a joint venture designed to manufacture the Rys Pro unmanned ground vehicle in Ukraine and Germany. ARX said at the time that the venture aimed to produce several thousand systems in its first year before scaling towards tens of thousands annually.
The new agreement signed in Kyiv extends the relationship into deeper technical integration and joint development.
Marc Wietfeld, CEO ARX Robotics said: “Software-defined unmanned defence solutions are key for landforces on a modern battlefield where every action can be seen by the enemy. Together with Roboneers we provide the Ukrainian forces with a robust but smart UGV fleet at scale and at the same time ensure that the lessons learnt from the battlefield are incorporated into the landsystems development of other western armies.”
A wider innovation pipeline
These partnerships sit within a wider infrastructure being built around Ukrainian defence innovation.
In May, Germany and Ukraine launched Brave Germany, a programme run with Ukraine’s Brave1 defence innovation cluster to provide grants to German and Ukrainian startups working across unmanned systems, AI, communications, laser and missile technologies.
Brave1 said in September that it had awarded more than 1,000 grants since 2023, worth a combined €122 million (UAH 6.2 billion), including support for areas such as interceptor drones and ground robotics.
During his Kyiv visit, Merz explicitly described the relationship as one in which German defence companies learn from Ukraine’s wartime experience while German and Ukrainian businesses establish joint ventures and manufacturing capacity. “German and Ukrainian companies are jointly developing technologies that benefit both countries. That makes us safer and stronger,” he said.
From battlefield to European market
For startups, Ukraine is consequently becoming more than an end market for European defence technology. It is emerging as a place where systems can be developed, manufactured, deployed and iterated in unusually short cycles.
The Quantum Systems and ARX Robotics announcements show what that model can look like at industrial scale: European investment and manufacturing capacity paired with Ukrainian engineering and battlefield experience, with technologies developed for an immediate defence requirement feeding back into the wider European market.

articles.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
articles.text:
People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now.
Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI company. We don’t know if we really like what we’re doing.”
“I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist,” I replied. It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype, steered by zealots, inescapable.
The CEO of Springboards and I are far from alone. Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now.
On the one hand, public feelings are souring fast. According to the Pew Research Center, more adults in the US think AI will have a negative impact on them personally, and on society in general, than expect a positive one. The pessimism is strongest among the young.
More than half of people worldwide say that AI products and services make them nervous, according to a report from Stanford University. In a Gallup poll in May, 71% of US adults said they would oppose construction of a new AI data center in their area, far more than the 53% who said they would oppose a new nuclear power plant. And in an NBC poll in March, AI was less popular than ICE.
Yet the number of people using AI is still skyrocketing. ChatGPT hit a billion monthly users in May, according to the market analysis firm Sensor Tower. Google DeepMind’s Gemini is close behind, logging 950 million users in July.
According to Pew, half of US adults now say they use a chatbot, more than twice the number who said they did in 2023. One in four people say they do so every day. And it’s a global habit: More than a third of adults across all 38 OECD countries (a group of the world’s wealthiest democracies) report having used generative AI tools in the last three months.
All these surveys paint a picture of two contradictory truths: A lot of people really do not like AI and a lot of people cannot get enough of it. What’s going on?
It’s possible that these are two distinct groups, but I doubt it. The numbers don’t add up unless the Venn diagram is on its way to being a circle.
It’s also possible that the more people use AI, the more negative their opinions about it will be. There’s at least a correlation to back this up: The Global North, where adoption is highest, skews pessimistic. In the Global South, where adoption levels are lower, people are more optimistic.
But here’s what I really think is going on: When people say they hate AI it’s not the technology they dislike but, rather, the relentless drive of the companies behind it to push the tech upon us in as many ways as possible. They’re telling us to brace for the biggest social and economic upheaval in generations. How do they expect people to feel?
In many ways, we’ve been here before. We saw a similar dynamic play out with social media over the last 20 years. Billions flocked to Facebook and Twitter despite mounting techlash against the companies that ran those services. Ditto for Google search.
With social media there wasn’t much anyone could do. Quitting a platform meant losing all your content and connections, giving you the choice to suck it up or start over. But with AI there’s still a chance for people to have some sway. There’s certainly more political appetite for regulation this time around. All 50 US states have either passed or proposed laws governing the development and deployment of AI, creating a patchwork of more than 2,100 bills across the country—a tenfold increase in three years.
And with a number of top-class open-source alternatives to Google and OpenAI and Anthropic already on the market, there’s also (for now, at least) the potential for more consumer choice and the market pressure that goes with it.
I don’t want to be naïve. Trillion-dollar companies are hard to move. But what comes next is not as inevitable as those companies often imply. When I asked the Springboards CEO why his firm was developing a new model if he didn’t really like AI, he told me there was no walking back from LLMs—but you could still make them do something different.
Here’s hoping we see a lot more of something different: Clarity about what AI can and cannot do and, crucially, a technology that's not sold as if it’s about to take over the world.

articles.title: Wikimedia acusa agentes da OpenAI de ações não autorizadas
articles.text:
Agentes de inteligência artificial (IA) que a Fundação Wikimedia acredita serem operados pela OpenAI realizaram uma série de atividades não autorizadas em suas plataformas e podem ter contribuído para uma interrupção parcial de um de seus serviços em maio.
A entidade, responsável por manter a Wikipédia e outros projetos de conhecimento aberto, identificou milhões de requisições automatizadas, edições não autorizadas e tentativas de explorar uma ferramenta de anotações.
A investigação da Wikimedia não encontrou evidências de que os sistemas ou dados da organização tenham sido comprometidos. Também não foram identificados sinais de que os agentes tenham usado a infraestrutura da entidade para coordenar suas próprias atividades.
Mesmo assim, a fundação afirmou estar preocupada com o comportamento desses sistemas e com a dificuldade de identificar e atribuir esse tipo de atividade.
Milhões de páginas acessadas
- Segundo a Wikimedia, agentes que ela acredita serem operados pela OpenAI fizeram milhões de requisições automatizadas às APIs públicas da organização;
- Os sistemas também percorreram milhões de páginas, principalmente nos projetos Wikidata e Wikimedia Commons, além de realizarem centenas de milhares de consultas ao Wikidata Query Service (WDQS), ferramenta utilizada para pesquisar e consultar os dados estruturados do Wikidata;
- A Wikimedia afirma que esse volume de tráfego pode ter contribuído para uma interrupção parcial do WDQS em maio;
- O registro do incidente aponta que a instabilidade começou em 7 de maio e afetou o serviço por vários dias;
- Em determinado momento, mais de 50% das requisições ao endpoint externo do serviço apresentavam timeout, enquanto o sistema chegou a entregar dados desatualizados por mais de 20 horas em alguns servidores.
Agentes fizeram edições sem autorização
A investigação também encontrou edições em wikis que a Wikimedia atribui a agentes da OpenAI.
A maioria ocorreu em áreas de testes, conhecidas como sandboxes, e não chegou a páginas exibidas normalmente para os leitores. No entanto, alguns agentes fizeram alterações na configuração de uma ferramenta de citações.
Segundo a fundação, essas mudanças podem ter sido maliciosas e aparentemente tinham como objetivo utilizar a ferramenta como um intermediário para buscar dados em serviços externos.
A Wikipédia permite que bots façam determinadas edições, desde que sejam identificados e aprovados pela comunidade. De acordo com a Wikimedia, nenhuma dessas autorizações foi solicitada nos casos investigados.
Tentativa de explorar ferramenta de anotações
Outro alvo foi o Etherpad, ferramenta pública de anotações hospedada pela Wikimedia como serviço para a comunidade.
Agentes que a fundação acredita estarem ligados à OpenAI tentaram, sem sucesso, comprometer a ferramenta. Uma das estratégias identificadas envolvia tentar utilizá-la como intermediária para buscar dados em outros sites.
Outros agentes aparentemente ligados à OpenAI também usaram o Etherpad para registrar anotações sobre suas próprias tarefas. A investigação, porém, não encontrou evidências de que essas anotações tenham sido usadas para coordenar as atividades dos diferentes agentes.
Wikimedia diz que não houve invasão
Apesar das atividades identificadas, a investigação não encontrou evidências de comprometimento dos sistemas ou dos dados da Wikimedia. A entidade também não encontrou indícios de que sua infraestrutura tenha sido usada para permitir a comunicação ou coordenação entre agentes.
O problema, segundo a fundação, vai além de uma eventual invasão bem-sucedida. O volume de acessos automatizados pode consumir recursos de infraestrutura, aumentar custos e até impedir que usuários humanos consigam acessar os serviços normalmente.
A Wikimedia afirma que o comportamento de agentes autônomos representa desafio para plataformas construídas originalmente para interação humana e que ainda não existem soluções suficientes para lidar com esse tipo de atividade.
OpenAI já reconheceu comportamento imprevisível
A Fundação Wikimedia afirmou que empresas de IA precisam assumir responsabilidade pelos agentes que colocam em circulação e desenvolver mecanismos para monitorar e impedir danos a serviços públicos da internet.
A entidade também citou declarações da própria OpenAI sobre agentes que podem apresentar comportamentos “imprevisíveis”.
Para a Wikimedia, não é suficiente que organizações menores ou comunidades de voluntários tenham de identificar, investigar e corrigir as consequências dessas atividades depois que elas acontecem.
O episódio ocorre em meio a uma série de investigações sobre agentes de IA desenvolvidos pela OpenAI. A empresa já havia informado que estava investigando atividades não autorizadas de seus agentes e notificando organizações afetadas por comportamentos considerados indevidos.
No caso da Wikimedia, a fundação afirma que os episódios reforçam a preocupação com o impacto que agentes autônomos podem ter sobre a infraestrutura pública da internet — especialmente quando conseguem acessar serviços em grande escala sem autorização.
A organização defende que empresas que desenvolvem e colocam esses agentes em circulação também devem ajudar a evitar e reparar os danos que eles possam causar.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Prime Deal Days gegen Black Friday: Lohnt sich das Warten?
articles.text:
Prime Deal Days gegen Black Friday: Bei diesen Produkten lohnt sich das Warten
In den vergangenen Jahren hat Amazon das Jahresendgeschäft regelmäßig mit einem zweiten Prime Day im Oktober eröffnet – teilweise, wie auch in diesem Jahr, gleich an mehreren Tagen. Dahinter steckt gerade in Zeiten mit knappen finanziellen Spielräumen bei den Verbraucher:innen eine einfache Überlegung: Jeder kann sein Budget nur einmal ausgeben – und wenn Handelsunternehmen ihre Kund:innen möglichst früh mit als attraktiv empfundenen Angeboten erreichen, haben sie bessere Chancen darauf, dass das Geld in ihrer Kasse landet.
Doch genauso lange wie es die Konkurrenz zwischen den Prime Deal Days oder Prime Days im Oktober und den traditionellen Tagen rund um den Black Friday gibt, hält sich die Frage, wann mit den besseren Angeboten zu rechnen ist. Lohnt es sich anlässlich der Prime Deal Days am 6. und 7. Oktober zuzuschlagen – oder sollte man lieber bis Ende November warten?
Die Angebotsplattform Mydealz hat jetzt Daten ausgewertet, die zeigen, dass die Antwort auf diese Frage nicht eindeutig ist, es aber dennoch Anhaltspunkte für Kaufentscheidungen gibt. Im Rahmen der Analyse wurden 3.304 Deals aus dem vergangenen Jahr untersucht: 1.540 Angebote von den Amazon Prime Deal Days am 7. und 8. Oktober 2025 sowie 1.764 Angebote vom Black Friday am 28. November, der ja bei Amazon erst der Einstieg in die Black Week mit dem Cyber Monday ist.
Mydealz gehört zum Plattformbetreiber Atolls und ist eine der größten deutschen Communitys für Angebote und Rabattaktionen. Hier teilen die Nutzer:innen Informationen über Händlerangebote, Gutscheine und Preisaktionen und bewerten diese gemeinschaftlich. Die Auswertung ist deshalb also keine repräsentative Preisstudie für den gesamten deutschen Handel, kann aber angesichts der riesigen Community durchaus Aussagekraft besitzen, weil sie gut aufzeigt, wie sich Preise identischer Produkte zwischen zwei großen Shopping-Events entwickelt haben. Das Gute daran: Die Terminkonstellation ist im Vergleich zum vergangenen Jahr – bis auf die Verschiebung um einen Tag – nahezu identisch.
Bei gleichen Produkten gewinnt meist der Black Friday
Vor allem bei jenen Angeboten, bei denen exakt dasselbe Produkt rabattiert wurde. Hier wurden identische Modelle und Varianten als Neuware sowie jeweils der niedrigste auf Mydealz gepostete Preis betrachtet. 27 der 41 Produkte waren demnach am Black Friday günstiger, lediglich sieben während der Prime Deal Days. Weitere sieben kosteten bei beiden Aktionen gleich viel. Im Median lag der Black-Friday-Preis sechs Prozent niedriger. Deswegen macht gerade bei größeren Anschaffungen im Techniksektor das Warten oft einen Unterschied, weil eben der Black Friday sechs Wochen weiter im Produktzyklus liegt.
Die Untersuchung nennt hier zwei Beispiele: Die Playstation 5 Pro kostete während der Prime Deal Days 709,99 Euro, am Black Friday dagegen 679 Euro. Noch größer fiel die Differenz bei der Nintendos Switch 2 im Bundle mit Mario Kart World aus: 477,49 Euro im Oktober standen 389,54 Euro im November gegenüber. Auch bei Fernsehern und Haushaltsrobotern waren diesbezüglich die Unterschiede bemerkenswert groß. Der Samsung S90F mit 65 Zoll kostete am Black Friday 1.224,55 Euro statt 1.435 Euro während der Prime-Aktion. Beim Mova Z60 Ultra Roller sank der Preis sogar von 1.185 auf 849 Euro. Der Ecovacs Goat A1600 RTK wurde im November für 615,99 Euro angeboten, während er im Oktober noch 799 Euro gekostet hatte.
Prime-Rabatte wirken größer – sind es aber nicht unbedingt
Schaut man auf die gesamten Kategorien, spricht ebenfalls vieles dafür, bis zum Black Friday zu warten, der ja den gesamten Handel und nicht bloß Amazon betrifft. Bei Gaming-Artikeln, Fernsehern und Audiogeräten wurden stets mehr Deals als „heiß“ von der Community bewertet, die den Black Friday betrafen – und keines der sieben hier direkt vergleichbaren Angebote für Fernseher, Kopfhörer und Lautsprecher war im Oktober günstiger. Bei Saugrobotern und anderen Reinigungsgeräten gab es während der Prime Deal Days zwar etwa doppelt so viele Angebote, doch lediglich 16 Prozent wurden rund um den Oktober-Prime Day als heiß eingestuft – gegenüber 24 Prozent am Black Friday.
Ähnlich war das Bild bei Spielzeug und Lego sowie Sport- und Outdoor-Produkten, wo der Black Friday in der Auswertung besser abschnitt. Gerade Lego-Sets waren im November entweder gleich teuer oder günstiger, auch bei Sport- und Outdoor-Produkten gab es deutlich mehr besonders stark bewertete Deals. Keinen eindeutigen Gewinner sieht die Auswertung dagegen bei Computern und Elektronik, Küchen- und Haushaltsgeräten, Smartphones und Tablets sowie Produkten aus dem Bereich Wohnen.
Ein scheinbarer Widerspruch ist dabei die vermeintliche und die ausgewiesene Ersparnis. Denn zunächst wirkten die Prime-Angebote im Hinblick auf die ausgewiesene Ersparnis gegenüber dem jeweils nächstbesten Vergleichspreis attraktiver – diese betrug dort im Median 23 Prozent, während es am Black Friday „nur“ 20 Prozent waren. Doch der direkte Vergleich identischer Produkte zeigt, dass zahlreiche Artikel Ende November noch einmal günstiger angeboten wurden, sodass auch die Mitbewerber weniger teuer waren. Kaufinteressent:innen sollten sich deshalb nicht in erster Linie an der Ersparnis im Vergleich zum nächstbesten Preis orientieren, sondern auf den Vergleichsmarkt schauen.
Amazon-Geräte sind im Oktober häufig interessanter
Allerdings gibt es auch Warengruppen, bei denen die Prime Deal Days Vorteile haben. Das gilt vor allem für Amazons eigene Hardware von Echo, Fire TV, Kindle bis hin zu Ring und anderen Smarthome-Devices aus dem Amazon-Ökosystem. Hier zählte Mydealz 22 Deals, während es zum Black Friday nur vier waren. Das dürfte allerdings auch damit zu tun haben, dass Amazons Eigenmarken (bis hin zu den Amazon-Basics-Produkten) mehr Aufmerksamkeit erfahren als zum Black Friday, an dem die gesamte Branche mit Angeboten kommt.
Auffällig ist aber, dass die Prime Deal Days zuletzt stark von günstigen Alltagsartikeln geprägt waren. Mehr als jeder Dritte (36 Prozent) kostete weniger als 25 Euro. Zehn der zwölf Prime-Produkte unter den 20 populärsten Angeboten lagen unter 40 Euro. Auch bei Mode und Schuhen, Beauty und Körperpflege, Büchern, Filmen und Musik sowie Werkzeug und Garten schnitten die Prime Deal Days vergleichsweise gut ab. Bei Beauty-Produkten lag die mediane Ersparnis bei 27 Prozent, am Black Friday waren es 18 Prozent. Deutlich größer war das Angebot auch bei Vorrats- und Haushaltsartikeln.
Black Friday ist auch ein Gutschein-Event
Allerdings gehört zum Vergleich der beiden Shopping-Termine auch eine weitere Erkenntnis: Denn neben klassischen Produktschnäppchen waren es vor allem Rabattcodes und Gutscheine sowie Cashback-Aktionen, die am Black Friday eine Rolle spielen (458 solche Angebote listet Mydealz im Vergleich zu 13 zum Prime Day im Oktober letzten Jahres).
Wer also nicht nur auf bestimmte niedrige Angebotspreise wartet, sondern darauf hofft, Deals mit Rabattcodes, Bonuspunkten oder Cashback zu verknüpfen, sollte eher auf den Black Friday und die Woche Ende November schielen.
Etwas entspannt haben sich die Prime Days aber im Hinblick auf das Tagesgefüge. Die Mydealz-Zahlen zeigen, dass man nicht zwingend am ersten Morgen zuschlagen muss. Einerseits wurden am ersten Aktionstag des vergangenen Jahres 1.154 Deals beschrieben und am zweiten nur 372. Anteilig war der zweite Tag aber sogar erfolgreicher: Denn 44 Prozent der dort geposteten Angebote wurden als heiß eingestuft, am ersten Tag waren es 37 Prozent.
Für größere Anschaffungen ergibt sich daraus eine pragmatische Strategie: Wer nicht sofort kaufen muss, kann den Preis der Prime Deal Days zunächst als Orientierung nehmen und Ende November noch einmal vergleichen. Anders ist der Fall bei Amazon-Hardware und einigen außergewöhnlich starken Einzelangeboten zu sehen, insbesondere wenn es sich um Vorjahresware handelt, die hier abverkauft wird. Dennoch sollten Kund:innen einen kühlen Kopf behalten – denn auch und gerade bei den groß inszenierten Shopping-Events ist ein hoher Rabatt nicht automatisch ein guter Preis.

articles.title: Buscando entre las ofertas del Prime Day, encontré un mini PC con Windows 11 por menos de 400 euros
articles.text:
Los miniPCs se convirtieron en una gran alternativa para todas aquellas personas que no tienen mucho espacio en su escritorio. Pero en los últimos años, no es esa la única razón. Ocupan poco pero están de sobra preparados para rendir al máximo. Entre todas las marcas para comprar un mini PC, NIPOGI es una de las que mejor lo está haciendo, con equipos muy potentes y con precios bastante bajo.
De hecho, en cualquier modelo podemos encontrar componentes top tanto en procesadores como en gráficas. Y todos ellos cargados con sistema operativo, algo cada vez más difícil de ver en equipos de bajo precio.
Con la llegada del Prime Day de Amazon, que se celebra los días 6 y 7 de Octubre, NIPOGI ha bajado todavía más el precio a alguno de sus productos más vendidos. En este caso ellos han alargado la promoción hasta finales del 11 de octubre pero date prisa porque con estos precios, vuelan. Te los ordenamos según el precio, de mayor a menor.
NIPOGI ACEMAGIC K1 Mini PC, de 419 euros a 389 euros
Es el equipo más simple de los tres propuestos, pero es perfecto para la mayoría de personas. Para empezar, es súper compacto y se puede colocar en cualquier lugar. En cuanto a configuración, es el más sencillo pero te garantizamos que el procesador AMD Ryzen 5 no te va a dar ningún problema para tareas de ofimática o tareas sencillas. articles.title: Lola Vision Systems is trying to make it easier to run AI models on chips | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The story begins almost 12 years ago, when Tayo Adesanya started a career working with microchips and AI processors. He mainly helped large manufacturers decide which chips to use in their hardware. Those years, he told TechCrunch, gave him early insight into where demand in the AI computing market was headed. “Starting Lola Vision Systems was a bet on where the world was headed and what I was seeing,” he said.
In 2024, he launched Lola Vision Systems, an AI infrastructure company that builds software and chips for running AI models on devices. Its core product is software that translates AI models into instructions a specific chip can run. Adesanya calls this software a “compiler toolchain,” and he says it is a massive bottleneck: Manually setting up an AI model on new hardware can take “roughly 200 hours” just to begin testing. Lola Vision says it has rebuilt that software layer and is also developing its own semiconductor chips, with the goal of automating more of the process. A client provides its code and the AI model it wants to use, whether custom-built or open source, and the software translates both into instructions the client’s chip can execute.
“Speed is only part of it,” Adesanya said. He explained that faster setup gives aerospace and “other mission-critical companies” time to “run more accurate models on their own data, at a lower power.”
“For these customers,” he said, “accuracy and reliability aren’t nice to have. They determine whether a product passes regulatory review and whether it works reliably in the field.”
Lola Vision, based in Washington, D.C., is one of several startups trying to offer an alternative to Nvidia’s technology for running AI on devices. Right now, Adesanya said, many companies start with Nvidia’s Jetson, a line of compact computing modules for running AI on devices, or with open source AI models. Adesanya claimed these “often break or run poorly out of the box, so teams spend days or weeks getting them to run at all, then even more weeks debugging until the models are usable.”
“Even then,” he continued, “power consumption often blows edge computing budgets, or the board can’t deliver enough compute for the medium to large models the product actually needs to run successfully. This leads to the recognition models lagging behind targets or misreading objects.” (Edge computing means running AI directly on a device, such as a camera or drone, rather than in a remote data center. Recognition models are AI systems that identify objects.)
According to the company, a dozen corporate customers have signed letters expressing interest in buying Lola Vision’s chips once they are available, and it already has one signed customer. It has also partnered with SCALE, a microelectronics workforce development program, to work with more semiconductor labs. “To get revenue sooner, we will now license our software on existing hardware,” Adesanya said. (In other words, rather than waiting for its own chips, the company will let customers pay to use its software on chips that already exist.) He added that the company has raised just over $1 million in total funding to date.
Lola Vision was selected for this year’s TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 200, a group of 200 startups chosen for the program. “TechCrunch was a favorite when I was a student at Purdue,” he said. After about a year of building the product and signing its first customer, he said, he felt it was time to apply to Startup Battlefield and get the company in front of a wider audience.
As for what he’s most excited about when it comes to the event, it’s “making meaningful connections and learning as much as I can about what’s happening in and around our space,” he said. “And, to be direct, I’m looking forward to investors writing checks.”
To learn more about Lola Vision Systems and dozens of other highly vetted startups that are joining us at TechCrunch Disrupt next week (along with the VCs coming to check them out), join us in San Francisco, October 13-15.

articles.title: Hyundai CEO says only a ‘level playing field’ can minimize damage from China
articles.text:
There’s been a lot of doom and gloom from the auto industry lately when the subject of China comes up. Automaker CEOs, in particular, warn that allowing low-cost, high-tech Chinese electric vehicles to be sold in the US would effectively spell the end of their businesses.
Hyundai CEO says only a ‘level playing field’ can minimize damage from China
Hyundai CEO José Muñoz says the US could be overrun like Europe without protections in place.
Hyundai CEO José Muñoz is not as pessimistic as some of his counterparts. He says he’s confident the right mix of protectionist policies and improvements on the product side can keep China at bay. Even though his company is feeling the squeeze from China, Muñoz isn’t ready to throw in the towel. But he also acknowledges that China could flood the US with affordable imports without established protections in place.
“As long as there is a level playing field for everybody,” Muñoz said at the reveal of the new 2027 Hyundai Tucson in New York City last week. “That’s all we ask, right? We compete everywhere in the world, and then we have seen that in the markets where that position is respected, so it’s really good for us.”
Chinese automakers have expanded rapidly in Europe, gobbling up market share and damaging domestic brands like Volkswagen, Volvo, and Mercedes by offering vehicles at much lower prices. US automakers warn the same could be true for them if China were allowed to import its vehicles here.
“We compete everywhere in the world, and then we have seen that in the markets where that position is respected, so it’s really good for us.”
— José Muñoz
Steep tariffs and laws that prohibit the sale of cars with software from China have basically made it impossible to sell Chinese vehicles in the US. But in recent months, the dam appears to be weakening. President Donald Trump has said several times that he would be open to Chinese automakers building manufacturing plants in the US if they hire American workers. And experts across the board believe it’s only a matter of time before China finds a way to sell its cars in the US.
But if Chinese brands eventually set up manufacturing inside North America or enter via partner channels, it’s not clear whether Hyundai has a defensive strategy ready. I asked Muñoz whether his company had begun to plan for the eventuality of Chinese imports available in the US market. He said it had not.
“We don’t develop strategies specifically because of the Chinese or because of other types of consumers, or other types of competitors,” he said. “We are always trying to do better.”
If Hyundai has any strategy, Muñoz added, it’s vertical integration: bringing down costs by making its tech and components. “This allows us to be more competitive,” he said. “Better quality over cost.”
“We don’t develop strategies specifically because of the Chinese or because of other types of consumers, or other types of competitors.”
Muñoz cited Hyundai’s $5.8 billion investment in Louisiana to produce green steel as an example of the company’s efforts to vertically integrate in the US. Hyundai expects the investment to provide better, more competitive, and more environmentally friendly steel. He says the same philosophy applies to software and other technologies that Hyundai wants to develop internally.
“So there is always room to do better,” he continued. “So if the Chinese competitor were to enter in the market, we would see what would happen, but I don’t know, I don’t have a crystal ball. I just look around, for example, Europe, and see what has happened, and then you may expect similar type of behaviors.”
Chinese vehicles sold in Europe are on average about 30 percent cheaper than comparable European-made rival models, even when factoring in EU import tariffs. The US has already fallen behind the rest of the world when it comes to EV adoption, after Trump and Republicans in Congress eliminated federal subsidies. In Europe, EVs account for over 20 percent of sales; in China, it’s over 60 percent. In the US, it’s less than 6 percent.
Political polarization certainly plays a role in depressing sales, as does inadequate charging infrastructure. But the lack of affordable electric models is regularly cited as the biggest barrier to adoption in the US. On that front, Muñoz thinks the US can still catch up.
“I think the American market is the most competitive in the world,” he said, noting that Hyundai still records robust EV sales here. That may be true, but the company’s hybrids are what’s keeping its EV business afloat. Hyundai has added hybrids to a wide range of vehicles, including its top-selling Tucson.
Unlike other automakers, Hyundai hasn’t retreated from EVs. It continues to sell its Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 9 here in the US, as well as a growing number of hybrids. In fact, the Hyundai Group recently surpassed Honda to claim second place in US hybrid sales behind Toyota.
Muñoz acknowledged that the US was still catching up to China’s dominance in EV batteries. Hyundai operates a battery manufacturing joint venture with SK On in Georgia near its massive Metaplant, where it builds all of its EVs and hybrids.
“Obviously if you don’t have the critical mass, the volume, it’s very difficult to be competitive,” he said. “One of the biggest pieces of cost is the battery. That is the key element, right? But there is a lot of production of batteries in the United States with some of the best global manufacturers. So I’m not concerned.”

articles.title: Russia's uncrewed robot tank fails during debut military display in front of President Putin — vehicle repeatedly lost control links and eventually got stuck in the mud despite the switch to a human driver
articles.text:
Russia's uncrewed robot tank fails during debut military display in front of President Putin — vehicle repeatedly lost control links and eventually got stuck in the mud despite the switch to a human driver
Russia’s new Shturm uncrewed tank failed during its debut display at Tsentr-2026, a Russia-led strategic military exercise held from September 28 to October 3, 2026, losing its command-and-control (C2) link and eventually getting stuck in the mud. According to an October 3 Defense Blog post, the tank repeatedly lost its C2 radio link with its separate command vehicle, forcing organizers to abandon remote operations and switch to a human driver-mechanic for a demonstration in front of President Vladimir Putin.
Despite manual human control, the vehicle eventually got stuck in a muddy ditch beside a dirt track, with its tracks and front hull buried in the soil. The Shturm is a Russian heavy robotic, uncrewed assault tank system designed by Uralvagonzavod, a Russian machine-building company and the world’s largest tank manufacturer by output, primarily for urban combat
It is built on modified Soviet-era T-72 and T-90 tank chassis and features a shortened 125mm D-414 main gun, or alternative configurations such as twin 30mm 2A42 automatic cannons and thermobaric rocket launchers. Its defining feature — and the primary source of failure during its debut demonstration — is its control system, which allows the tank to be remotely operated from a separate crewed command vehicle within a radio link range of roughly 3 kilometers. It also has provision for a manual, on-board human driver.
According to Defense Blog, the Russian Defense Ministry initially said on Oct. 2 that Putin had been shown the new uncrewed combat vehicles, and that they provided fire support to assault units during the main stage of the drills. Reports of the failure emerged afterward. The vehicle has “several technical flaws, including an engine compartment and turret roof that are almost unprotected, areas drones most often target when attacking armored vehicles in Ukraine,” according to a Russian armor expert cited by Defense Blog. “The idea of this vehicle seems unsuccessful to me: dependence on a command post that has to be 3 to 4 kilometers away and in direct line of sight. Without proper communications like Starlink, or something similar, there is no point in such a vehicle,” he added. Starlink had earlier blocked russian drones from using its services in the country's ongoing four-year war with Ukraine.

articles.title: Row-Parallel DRAM Computing Cuts Data-Reorganization Overhead (Syracuse, FAU, TU Dresden)
articles.text:
Researchers at Syracuse University, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and TU Dresden published a technical paper titled “RAPID: Row-Parallel Arithmetic Processing in DRAM.”
Abstract Excerpt: “Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present RAPID, a Row-parallel Arithmetic Processing-In-DRAM architecture. RAPID augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. These primitives enable RAPID to operate directly on row-parallel, bit-parallel data, preserving CPU-compatible layouts while exploiting the massive parallelism of the DRAM subarray.”
Find the technical paper here. October 2026.
Tegge, William C., João Paulo Cardoso de Lima, Shouzhi Fang, Jeronimo Castrillon, and Alex K. Jones. “RAPID: Row-Parallel Arithmetic Processing in DRAM.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2610.02502 (October 2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.02502

articles.title: Microsoft: Windows KB5124010 update crashes some games and apps
articles.text:
Microsoft confirmed over the weekend that some games and applications using AC-3 (Dolby Digital) audio decoding will crash after installing the September 2026 KB5124010 Windows 11 preview update.
KB5124010 is an optional update that requires users to click the "Download and install" link, which should reduce the number of potentially affected Windows users. However, it installs automatically on devices running Windows 11 24H2, where the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" option is toggled on.
"In some cases the application can fail to launch, or close without warning. In other cases the application will work normally until certain features are used, such as playing music," Microsoft said in a Friday update to the Windows release health dashboard. "Affected applications may vary and can include games, media players, and certain productivity applications."
However, the company added that many modern apps don't use Windows for this type of encoding and aren't affected. Additionally, the code component that triggers these crashes is most commonly used in legacy applications that still use the Windows built-in audio decoding, while modern apps that use the legacy AC-3 codec often include their own audio decoding components.
Although it didn't provide an estimated timeline for a fix, Microsoft is working to resolve this issue and said it will share more information in a future update.
Last month, Microsoft released emergency updates to fix another known issue causing USB audio issues, as well as Remote Desktop Services failures and Hyper-V problems after installing the KB5124008 and KB5124012 September 2026 security updates.
Last year, the company addressed a similar issue in January that triggered audio playback issues and Code 10 errors on Windows 11 24H2 systems with USB audio device drivers, and lifted a safeguard hold that prevented upgrades and caused Bluetooth headsets and speakers to malfunction on systems with Dirac audio improvement software.
Two years ago, it also confirmed an issue that caused game audio to unexpectedly increase to full volume when using USB DAC sound systems and blocked Windows 24H2 upgrades on systems with incompatible Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio drivers because of blue screen of death (BSOD) issues.

articles.title: « C'était la seule façon »: Elon Musk fait une confidence sur le robot Tesla Optimus
articles.text:
Les puces maison de Tesla perdent une bonne partie de leur mémoire vive. Dans un message publié le 1er octobre, Elon Musk annonce que l’AI5 passe à 72 Go et l’AI6 à 144 Go, soit moitié et un tiers de moins que prévu. Objectif revendiqué : produire le robot humanoïde Optimus en très grande série.
 We cut our RAM in half for the Tesla AI5 chip (now 72GB of LP5) and 1/3 for AI6 (now 144GB of LP6).
This was the only way to get enough volume for Optimus production and greatly reduces cost.
As it turns out, we think this will have a negligible effect on Optimus performance,…
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 1, 2026
Un régime imposé par la cadence
« C’était la seule façon d’obtenir assez de volume pour la production d’Optimus », écrit le patron de Tesla, qui met aussi en avant des coûts « fortement réduits ». L’AI5 embarquera donc 72 Go de mémoire LP5, quand l’AI6 se contentera de 144 Go de LP6, les générations de mémoire basse consommation retenues pour ces deux puces.
Côté performances, le dirigeant balaie les inquiétudes et promet un effet « négligeable » sur le robot. Le goulot d’étranglement de ses puces se situerait dans la bande passante mémoire plutôt que dans la quantité embarquée : les modèles d’IA embarqués passent leur temps à lire la mémoire bien plus qu’à la remplir, et des gigaoctets inutilisés n’accélèrent rien.
Quelque 5 000 composants d’Optimus sont déjà en commande, et l’objectif affiché reste d’un million d’unités par an. À cette cadence, chaque gigaoctet retiré de la fiche technique se multiplie par un million d’exemplaires espérés.
À lire aussi : Tesla n’est plus un constructeur auto – pourquoi la fin des Model S et X change tout
Plus de 200 Go par robot, prédisait pourtant Micron
Plus de 200 Go de mémoire vive et plusieurs téraoctets de stockage par robot humanoïde : la projection vient du patron de Micron, Sanjay Mehrotra, qui comparait l’appétit d’un humanoïde à celui d’une voiture autonome, l’un des segments les plus gourmands du marché. Tesla prend le contre-pied avec ses 72 Go, et parie que l’optimisation logicielle comblera l’écart.
Les prix de la mémoire flambent par ailleurs depuis des mois : Samsung a enchaîné les hausses sur la RAM, et la pénurie déborde désormais jusque dans l’automobile. Musk ne relie jamais publiquement sa décision à ces prix, son argumentaire tient au volume et au coût de production.
Cet été déjà, le milliardaire qualifiait son robot de cauchemar industriel, au moment d’en justifier les retards. La coupe mémoire prolonge la même logique : simplifier la machine pour tenir la cadence promise, quitte à rogner sur la marge de confort technique.
Le test grandeur nature arrivera avec les premiers Optimus de série. Si 72 Go suffisent, Tesla aura montré qu’un humanoïde fonctionnel n’exige pas la configuration d’une station de travail, et son prix de vente pourrait suivre la même pente descendante. Dans le cas contraire, la mémoire économisée aujourd’hui se paiera en mises à niveau demain, sur des robots déjà livrés par milliers.

articles.title: Annulé ? Maintenu ? Que se passe t-il avec le prochain film Seigneur des anneaux ?
articles.text:
L’annonce de la fusion officielle entre Paramount et Warner Bros. Discovery, qui donne naissance à un nouveau géant baptisé Skydance et dirigé par David Ellison, a immédiatement déclenché une vague d’inquiétude sur les projets en cours.
Le projet le plus scruté s’appelle Le Seigneur des anneaux : Shadow of the Past, un film annoncé le 25 mars 2026 par Warner Bros. et New Line Cinema. Stephen Colbert, ex-animateur du Late Show et grand fan de J.R.R. Tolkien, est à l’origine du projet. Il écrit le film avec son fils, le scénariste Peter McGee, et avec Philippa Boyens, coscénariste de la trilogie de Peter Jackson. Peter Jackson le produit.
La fausse alerte qui a fait trembler les fans du Seigneur des anneaux
La panique a débuté le dimanche 4 octobre, quand le site Knight Edge Media a publié un article affirmant que le projet Seigneur des anneaux avait été « mis en pause » en raison des remaniements majeurs liés à la fusion Skydance-Paramount-WB. L’information a vite circulé, beaucoup y voyant un calcul financier ou un règlement de comptes après la suppression du Late Show, l’émission de Colbert, par CBS, une chaîne du groupe Paramount.
Warner Bros. a réagi en contactant plusieurs médias, dont World of Reel, pour assurer que le film n’était pas annulé et restait en développement.
Le projet poursuit sa phase d’écriture active chez New Line Cinema. Selon Rob Keyes, journaliste de Screen Rant, qui a contesté l’information de Knight Edge Media sur X ce lundi 5 octobre, rien n’a bougé depuis plusieurs semaines. Les scénaristes écrivent toujours, sans budget ni date de tournage confirmés, comme pour la plupart des films en développement.
David Ellison et Stephen Colbert, de la télévision au cinéma
Avec la fusion, David Ellison, patron du nouveau groupe, a désormais la main sur le film de Stephen Colbert, dont l’émission The Late Show a été supprimée par CBS, une chaîne qu’il contrôle aussi. CBS avait annoncé cette suppression le 17 juillet 2025, en parlant d’une décision « purement financière », trois semaines avant que Skydance ne finalise sa fusion avec Paramount, le 7 août 2025. La dernière émission a été diffusée le 21 mai 2026.
Warner Bros. n’a pas dit si la nouvelle direction comptait revoir ses ambitions pour la franchise, ni quand le tournage pourrait obtenir son feu vert.
Sur le plan créatif, Shadow of the Past vise d’abord les amoureux des livres. Le film se déroule quatorze ans après le départ de Frodon pour les Terres Immortelles. Sam, Merry et Pippin y refont les tout premiers kilomètres de leur quête, du Comté jusqu’à Bree.
Si le film de Colbert suit son cours sans calendrier précis pour le moment, le prochain rendez-vous majeur en Terre du Milieu reste inchangé : Le Seigneur des anneaux : The Hunt for Gollum, réalisé et joué par Andy Serkis, est toujours calé pour une sortie au cinéma le 17 décembre 2027.

articles.title: macOS : face aux agents IA, Apple va durcir l'accès complet au disque
articles.text:
Apple a annoncé de futurs contrôles supplémentaires sur « l’accès complet au disque » de macOS, un réglage qui donne à une app une vue sur l’ensemble du Mac. Le constructeur invoque les risques liés aux agents IA et n’a donné aucun calendrier.
Sur un Mac, certaines apps réclament une clé qui ouvre toutes les portes. Longtemps réservé aux logiciels de sauvegarde, ce passe-partout intéresse désormais une nouvelle génération d’outils, plus autonomes et plus bavards avec les serveurs distants. Apple vient de réagir publiquement, et le message ne laisse guère de place à l’interprétation.
Un passe-partout conçu pour les sauvegardes, détourné de son usage
L’accès complet au disque contourne en grande partie les protections habituelles de macOS. Apple l’a prévu pour que les applications de sauvegarde puissent copier tout le contenu de la machine, ce qu’elles ne pourraient pas faire autrement. Le constructeur reconnaît aujourd’hui que certains développeurs l’emploient d’une façon qui met les utilisateurs en danger.
Le risque, selon Apple, est d’exposer « tout ce qui se trouve sur le système, y compris les fichiers, les mails, les messages et même l’historique de navigation », sans que l'utilisateur n'en mesure pleinement la portée. Pour les applications de messagerie, la confidentialité des correspondants se trouverait elle aussi compromise.
La firme pointe surtout une menace à venir : à mesure que les agents IA, ces programmes qui agissent seuls pour le compte de l’utilisateur, gagnent en capacités et en autonomie, « les risques associés à ce niveau d’accès augmenteront considérablement ». MacRumors rattache cette annonce à l’essor d’agents toujours actifs, comme Muse de Meta et Dots d'OpenAI, qui ont déjà suscité des inquiétudes sur la vie privée.
Des garde-fous annoncés, mais sans calendrier ni détails
Apple a publié son message vendredi 2 octobre sur son site d’actualités destiné aux développeurs. Elle y promet des « contrôles supplémentaires » afin que seuls les utilisateurs qui souhaitent réellement accorder ce niveau d’accès puissent le faire, au moyen d’une action « très explicite ».
Le flou reste entier sur la forme de ces contrôles, sur la version de macOS qui les intégrera et sur la date de leur arrivée. On ignore aussi comment seront touchées les applications de sauvegarde, pour lesquelles le réglage a justement été créé.
En attendant, un contrôle rapide s’impose. Dans Réglages Système, rubrique Confidentialité et sécurité, puis « Accès complet au disque », vous voyez la liste des apps qui disposent déjà de cette autorisation. Retirez celles que vous n’utilisez plus ou que vous ne reconnaissez pas. Ce geste ne vous prendra que quelques secondes, mais est le plus efficace pour contrôler qui a le droit ou non d’accéder à vos informations les plus importantes.

articles.title: Apple vai dificultar acesso aos dados do Mac por causa da IA • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple vai dificultar acesso aos dados do Mac por causa da IA
Mudança no Acesso Total ao Disco busca reforçar a segurança diante de agentes de inteligência artificial.
A Apple vai reforçar os controles para aplicativos que exigem acesso aos dados armazenados em um Mac. A mudança mira a permissão conhecida como Acesso Total ao Disco (ou Full Disk Access, em inglês) e chega em meio ao crescimento de agentes de inteligência artificial capazes de interagir com arquivos e aplicativos no computador.
Em um comunicado para desenvolvedores, a companhia afirma que pretende garantir que essa permissão só seja concedida por uma ação “muito explícita” do usuário. A Apple ainda não detalhou como esses novos controles funcionarão nem informou quando a mudança será implementada.
O sistema da Apple utiliza diferentes mecanismos para limitar quais dados cada aplicativo pode acessar. O Acesso Total ao Disco é uma exceção criada para permitir que programas de backup consigam ler informações distribuídas pelo sistema. Quando ativada, a permissão pode liberar acesso a arquivos, e-mails, mensagens e até ao histórico de navegação.
Segundo a empresa, alguns desenvolvedores estão utilizando esse nível de acesso de maneiras que podem expor informações armazenadas no computador sem que os usuários entendam o que está acontecendo.
A ideia atual não é eliminar o recurso. A proposta é adicionar novas etapas para garantir que os usuários que realmente desejem liberar esse acesso façam isso conscientemente.
A Apple relacionou a mudança ao avanço dos agentes de IA. Esses sistemas não só respondem a perguntas, mas podem executar tarefas e utilizar informações armazenadas no disco do computador com maior autonomia. Na avaliação da empresa, conforme esses agentes se tornam mais capazes e independentes, os riscos associados ao Acesso Total ao Disco devem aumentar.
O tema ganhou atenção recentemente após uma divergência envolvendo o Muse, o agente pessoal de IA lançado pela Meta. Um jornalista afirmou que a ferramenta conhecia o conteúdo de suas mensagens privadas, mesmo sem uma autorização clara para isso.
A Meta contestou o relato e afirmou que o Muse só consegue acessar mensagens quando o usuário habilita as permissões necessárias, incluindo o Acesso Total ao Disco e uma conexão específica com o aplicativo Mensagens.
A discussão vai além do Muse. Ferramentas de IA para computadores estão recebendo recursos que exigem acesso cada vez maior aos dados. Em agosto, o ChatGPT ganhou o Computer History no macOS, função que registra atividades realizadas no computador para permitir que a IA encontre informações e ajude em tarefas futuras.
Outro caso recente reforça essa preocupação. Pesquisadores encontraram uma falha, já corrigida, no aplicativo do ChatGPT para macOS, que poderia permitir que um invasor assumisse o controle do app e acessasse conversas, sessões do navegador e outros dados sensíveis.
Ao mesmo tempo, casos de agentes ultrapassando limites definidos pelos usuários vêm aumentando. Em setembro, a própria OpenAI criou um protocolo para investigar e divulgar situações em que seus modelos agem sem autorização, acessam dados indevidamente ou burlam restrições.
A Apple afirma que os novos controles do macOS terão como objetivo deixar os riscos mais claros antes de um aplicativo receber acesso completo aos dados da máquina.
